# DESIGN.md — Clippet's architecture, as built

This is the design document of Clippet, a self-hosted clip server: upload a video, the server transcodes
it, and the share link unfurls as a playable card in Discord and on X. Sections 1–16 are the architecture
as it was fixed before the first commit (2026-08-31) — stack, topology, data model, API contract, pages,
transcode pipeline, sweeper, auth, security posture, testing — and **§20 is the binding decision log**:
every change since, numbered, dated and cited from the code as `§20 erratum N`. Where an earlier section
and a §20 entry disagree, the entry wins. Numbers are never reused or renumbered; the note at the end of
§20 says how they are allocated. Build plans and risk lists that were written before the code exist in
the private records, not here (§17–19 below is a pointer).

Provenance: Clippet is a clean-room rewrite from a written specification of a Streamable-like clip server.
No third-party clip server's source was read or copied; an earlier derivative was probed only as an HTTP
black box to learn what its users saw; every line here is original.

---

## 1. Decision summary

**Stack**: one static Go 1.27 binary (`clippet`) — stdlib `net/http` (Go 1.22+ method+pattern
`ServeMux`), `html/template` SSR from `embed.FS`, SQLite via `modernc.org/sqlite` (pure Go,
WAL, one-writer pool), `github.com/minio/minio-go/v7` for any S3-compatible bucket, static
ffmpeg/ffprobe **7.1.1** copied from `mwader/static-ffmpeg:7.1.1` into an `alpine:3.22` image,
one vanilla-JS file for upload progress/polling/forms. The same binary runs the HTTP server,
the transcode worker, the expiry sweeper, and an `admin` CLI. Compose in dev is
`app + minio + bucket-init`; production against R2/B2 is **one container**.

Direct Go dependencies, complete list: `modernc.org/sqlite`, `github.com/minio/minio-go/v7`,
`golang.org/x/crypto` (bcrypt), `golang.org/x/time` (rate). Everything else is stdlib.

**Why this shape (one paragraph)**: Clippet is a single-tenant tool one person runs for
years, so the design objective is *fewest things that can be down at 3am*: one process,
one data file, one bucket. SQLite removes a stateful container, a credential set and a
first-boot race; the write rate (state transitions, a handful of sweeper deletes per minute,
deduped view increments) is tens of writes per minute, and a one-connection write pool with
`BEGIN IMMEDIATE` makes `SQLITE_BUSY` a non-class. Go templates remove the Node toolchain and
the SSR-fetch-timeout class of failure entirely (pages read the local row in-process).
minio-go is S3-compatible-first and has no CRC32-trailer default to disable for R2/B2.
The panel's correctness grafts are all mechanism, not parts: a `deleting` tombstone plus a
blocking `worker.Cancel` plus a conditional finalize close the sweeper/worker race without
leases; a lazy `io.ReadSeeker` with DB-known size/ETag makes media serving one ranged GET
per request with zero `Stat` calls; a minimal `jobs` table keeps clip availability separate
from job state so Phase 4 trim/GIF never flips a `ready` clip to `processing`.

**Alternatives rejected**

| Alternative | Why not |
|---|---|
| Postgres (pgx/sqlc) | Buys concurrency and LISTEN/NOTIFY that one household never needs; costs a second stateful container, credentials, and a first-boot ordering race. `internal/db` hides all SQL so a port is a package swap if multi-node ever matters. |
| Next.js SSR + Go API | Two containers, a Node toolchain, the `HOSTNAME=0.0.0.0` footgun, and an SSR→API network hop that must be timeout-guarded. Seven pages do not justify a framework. |
| aws-sdk-go-v2 (Proposal 2) | Large module tree and a 2025 history of checksum-default regressions against MinIO/B2 that must be re-verified on every bump. `store.Store` is an interface, so this remains a one-package decision. |
| Direct client→S3 streaming ingest + worker re-download (Proposal 2) | Doubles bucket traffic, adds a `download` stage and an `uploading` half-row state with an abandon rule, and leaves incomplete multipart uploads on disconnect. Scratch-first ingest keeps "201 only after the original is durable" with none of that. |
| Full assets ledger + generic job registry (Proposal 3) | Six tables and a kind→handler registry are more machinery than "why is this clip stuck" should require. We take the *minimal* `jobs` table, per-attempt random output keys and the post-upload checkpoint — the three ideas that carry the extensibility — and leave the rest. |
| Processing leases + worker_id + renewal (Proposal 2) | In a single process the running-job set is known in memory; a blocking `Cancel` + conditional finalize gives the same proof with no lease columns. |
| `apk add ffmpeg` on alpine 3.22 | Ships 6.1.x while the host and E2E assert with 7.1.1; static 7.1.1 is pinned and identical across rebuilds. apk stays documented as the fallback only if the static image ever disappears. |
| argon2id passwords (Proposal 3) | 64 MiB per verify spikes memory under concurrent logins on a small VPS. bcrypt cost 12 with an 8–72 byte length rule is boring and sufficient. |
| `Cache-Control: immutable` on media routes (Proposal 3) | The stable-route indirection exists precisely so bytes can change under `/social.mp4` and `/video.mp4` (Phase 4 trim, deferred social rendition). Media uses `max-age=3600` with ETag revalidation. |
| An `uploading` row state (Proposals 1/2) | With scratch-first ingest the row is inserted only after the original is durable; there is no half-row to abandon, no unspecified card state, no source-less `failed` clutter. The clip state machine therefore has **no** `uploading` state (see §5). |

**Deliberate divergences from the earlier derivative (probed as an HTTP black box only)**: `/` and `GET /api/clips`
require a session here (it served both anonymously). Smaller trust surface; individual
clip pages/API/media remain public because the unguessable link is the auth. Recorded so
Phase 3 comparisons are not surprised; a `PUBLIC_INDEX` knob is *not* built (§19).

---

## 2. Compose topology

> Since §20 erratum 345 (2026-10-25) the default stack is the app alone on the folder store (`STORAGE_BACKEND=fs`,
> `compose.yaml`); a bucket is bring-your-own. The `minio` and `bucket-init` services below are the Phase 1 topology,
> kept as written.

```yaml
# compose.yaml (Phase 1). All tags pinned. `docker compose up -d --build` builds ./Dockerfile.
name: clippet
services:
  app:
    build: { context: ., dockerfile: Dockerfile }
    image: clippet-app:local
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports: ["${CLIPPET_PUBLISH:-127.0.0.1:8481}:8080"]   # AMENDED by §20 erratum 96: loopback by
                                              # default (host 8481)
    environment:              # AMENDED by §20 erratum 57: the repo's compose.yaml now interpolates
      CLIPPET_LISTEN: ":8080" # EVERY §4 variable as ${VAR:-<the §4 default>} (44 keys, SESSION_SECRET
      PUBLIC_BASE_URL: ${PUBLIC_BASE_URL:-http://localhost:8481}   # deliberately excluded), so `.env`
      DATA_DIR: /data         # is the single place an operator sets anything. The 15 keys listed here
      SCRATCH_DIR: /scratch   # resolve byte-for-byte as shown when no .env overrides them; compose.yaml
      S3_ENDPOINT: http://minio:9000                               # in the repo is the full list.
      S3_REGION: ${S3_REGION:-us-east-1}
      S3_BUCKET: ${S3_BUCKET:-clips}
      S3_ACCESS_KEY: ${MINIO_ROOT_USER:-clippet}
      S3_SECRET_KEY: ${MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD:-clippet-dev-secret}
      S3_FORCE_PATH_STYLE: "true"
      DEFAULT_CLIP_TTL: ${DEFAULT_CLIP_TTL:-never}
      REGISTRATION: ${REGISTRATION:-open}
      TRUSTED_PROXIES: ${TRUSTED_PROXIES:-}
      LOG_LEVEL: ${LOG_LEVEL:-info}
    volumes:
      - app_data:/data          # SQLite (clippet.db + -wal + -shm). NAMED volume, never a Windows bind mount.
      - app_scratch:/scratch    # transcode scratch disk (source copies + encoder outputs)
    stop_grace_period: 45s      # SIGTERM budget: Shutdown(15s) ∥ worker.Stop(20s) → sweeper → db.Close ≈ 25s max (§18.1); 20s headroom
    depends_on:
      minio:       { condition: service_healthy }
      bucket-init: { condition: service_completed_successfully }
    healthcheck:   # liveness = DB only; the listener is up before the storage ping loop starts (§8.7), so this never waits on storage
      test: ["CMD", "curl", "-fsS", "http://localhost:8080/healthz"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 10s

  minio:        # unchanged from Phase 0
    image: minio/minio:RELEASE.2025-09-07T16-13-09Z
    command: server /data --address ":9000"
    environment:
      MINIO_ROOT_USER: ${MINIO_ROOT_USER:-clippet}
      MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD: ${MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD:-clippet-dev-secret}
    volumes: [minio_data:/data]
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "mc", "ready", "local"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 12
      start_period: 5s
    restart: unless-stopped

  bucket-init:  # unchanged from Phase 0: one-shot, waits on minio HEALTH, mc mb --ignore-existing
    image: minio/mc:RELEASE.2025-08-13T08-35-41Z
    depends_on:
      minio: { condition: service_healthy }
    environment:
      MINIO_ROOT_USER: ${MINIO_ROOT_USER:-clippet}
      MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD: ${MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD:-clippet-dev-secret}
      S3_BUCKET: ${S3_BUCKET:-clips}
    entrypoint: ["/bin/sh", "-ec"]
    command:
      - |
        mc alias set local http://minio:9000 "$$MINIO_ROOT_USER" "$$MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD" >/dev/null
        mc mb --ignore-existing "local/$$S3_BUCKET"
        mc anonymous set none "local/$$S3_BUCKET" >/dev/null
        echo "bucket-init: bucket '$$S3_BUCKET' ready"
    restart: "no"

volumes:
  minio_data: {}
  app_data: {}
  app_scratch: {}
```

**Dockerfile** (`docker compose up -d --build` builds the final stage from local source;
`scripts/check.sh` builds `--target test` and `--target racetest`). The sketch below is the Phase 1
shape; §20 erratum 283 factored a `base` stage out above `build` and put the test passes on
`base → testdeps → testsrc → {test, racetest}`, so the fixed prerequisites sit above the source copy
and the two passes are siblings that can run at once. The `build` stage's instruction sequence, and
therefore the runtime image, are unchanged:

```dockerfile
# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1
FROM golang:1.27-alpine AS build
WORKDIR /src
COPY go.mod go.sum ./
RUN go mod download
COPY . .
ARG VERSION=dev
RUN CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -trimpath -ldflags="-s -w -X main.version=${VERSION}" -o /out/clippet ./cmd/clippet

FROM mwader/static-ffmpeg:7.1.1 AS ffmpeg          # verified on Docker Hub (amd64+arm64); static binaries

FROM build AS test                                   # unit + ffmpeg-tagged tests run here (check.sh)
COPY --from=ffmpeg /ffmpeg /ffprobe /usr/local/bin/
RUN test -z "$(gofmt -l .)" || (echo "gofmt needed:"; gofmt -l .; exit 1)
RUN go vet ./... && go test -tags ffmpeg ./...

FROM alpine:3.22
RUN apk add --no-cache ca-certificates tzdata curl \
 && addgroup -S -g 10001 clippet && adduser -S -u 10001 -G clippet clippet \
 && mkdir -p /data /scratch && chown -R 10001:10001 /data /scratch
COPY --from=ffmpeg /ffmpeg /ffprobe /usr/local/bin/
COPY --from=build /out/clippet /usr/local/bin/clippet
USER 10001
EXPOSE 8080
VOLUME ["/data", "/scratch"]
HEALTHCHECK --interval=10s --timeout=3s --start-period=10s --retries=3 \
  CMD curl -fsS http://localhost:8080/healthz >/dev/null || exit 1
ENTRYPOINT ["clippet"]
CMD ["serve"]
```

Notes:
- ffmpeg delivery is **decided**: static 7.1.1 in-image (matches host 7.1.1 used by E2E; flags
  below are 7.x: `-fps_mode`, `-update 1`, `out_time_us`). `apk add ffmpeg` (6.1.x) is the
  documented fallback only if the static image tag ever vanishes, and switching to it requires
  re-running the five-clip matrix. Never both.
- `/healthz` (DB liveness) is the compose healthcheck; `/readyz` (DB + storage) is what E2E
  waits on. A storage outage degrades readiness; it never restart-loops the container (§8, §12).
- `.dockerignore` must NOT exclude `web/` or `internal/db/migrations/` (both are embedded at
  build time). It excludes `.git`, `testclips/`, `scripts/`, `.e2e/`, `*.md`, `.env*`. `.gitignore`
  carries `.e2e/` (E2E scratch files, §16.3) and `testclips/`.
- Named volumes only. SQLite over a Windows bind mount breaks locking on Docker Desktop.
- `docker compose down -v` is the clean-machine reset (Phase 5 gate).

## 3. Repository layout

Module path `clippet` (existing `go.mod`). Owner stream in brackets (see §18).

```
cmd/clippet/
  main.go            [A]  subcommand dispatch: serve (default) | admin ... | migrate ; `runMigrate(cfg) int` ; `var version`
  serve.go           [A]  wiring: config → db → reconcile → LISTENER UP → background store ping → worker → sweeper; SIGTERM sequence (§8.7, §18.1)
  admin.go           [D]  `runAdmin(args, cfg) int`: expire|ls|stats|orphans (migrate lives in main.go [A])
internal/config/     [A]  Config struct, Load(getenv) with validation, DEFAULT_CLIP_TTL parser
internal/ids/        [A]  New() 12-char base62 slug; Valid(); Token() "ck_"+43 base64url; Rand(n)
internal/urls/       [A]  Builder from PUBLIC_BASE_URL: Page/Embed/Video/Social/Poster/Progress/Static/Abs/IsHTTPS/Origin
internal/db/         [A]  Open (two pools), Migrate, typed queries; migrations/0001_init.sql (embed)
internal/store/
  store.go           [A]  Store interface, ObjectInfo, PutResult, ErrNotFound
  keys.go            [A]  key layout (§6), SanitizeExt
  fake.go            [A]  in-memory Store for tests (fault injection: FailNext, Hook for latency/ordering, Calls, Deletes)
  seeker.go          [A]  NewSeeker: lazy io.ReadSeekCloser over GetRange (§8 media)
  minio.go           [D]  minio-go implementation incl. DeletePrefix with incomplete-upload abort
internal/httpx/      [A]  JSON envelope, WriteJSON/WriteError, SetLogField (request-scoped access-log annotations), middleware: Recover, RequestID, AccessLog, SecurityHeaders
internal/auth/       [B]  bcrypt, sessions, api tokens, Principal, Middleware, RequireUser/RequireSession/RequireScope, CSRF
internal/clientip/   [B]  Resolve(r, trustedPrefixes) netip.Addr
internal/ratelimit/  [B]  bounded per-key token buckets + Middleware
internal/views/      [B]  Deduper (bounded, TTL) + Key()
internal/httpapi/    [B]  NewHandler(Deps): router.go, dto.go, auth_handlers.go, clip_handlers.go, token_handlers.go,
                          upload.go, media.go, progress.go, view.go, health.go
internal/transcode/  [C]  Probe, ProbeOutput, VerifyMP4, MakePlan, EncodeArgs, Encode (progress+stall), Poster, progress parser
internal/worker/     [C]  DB-driven job loop, pipeline, in-memory progress registry, blocking Cancel, graceful Stop
internal/lifecycle/  [D]  Destroy(ctx, ...): tombstone → cancel → delete prefix → delete row → scratch rm
internal/sweeper/    [D]  ticker calling lifecycle.Destroy on SweepCandidates; session pruning; scratch janitor
internal/web/        [E]  templates (embed), page handlers (404/503 discipline), BuildMeta (card tags), static handler
web/templates/*.html [E]  base, index, login, register, tokens, clip, embed, notfound, unavailable
web/static/          [E]  app.js, app.css, card-placeholder.png (1200×630, committed binary)
scripts/
  check.sh           [D]  CI story, containers only (§16)
  e2e.sh             [D]  live-stack E2E (§16)
  testclips.sh       [exists] host-ffmpeg test-clip matrix generator
  lib/jget.py        [D]  tiny JSON path extractor for e2e.sh (no jq on host)
Dockerfile, compose.yaml, .env.example, .dockerignore   [A]
DESIGN.md (this)                                         [the design]
```

Import graph (acyclic, enforced by review): `config, ids, urls, httpx` ← `db` ← `store` ←
`transcode` ← `worker` ← `lifecycle` ← `sweeper`; `auth, clientip, ratelimit, views` ← `httpapi`
(imports everything above except `sweeper`, `web`); `web` imports `db, auth, urls, config, httpx`
only. `cmd/clippet` imports all. `httpapi` never imports `web`; `web` never imports `httpapi`.

## 4. Configuration

All configuration is environment variables, read once by `config.Load(os.Getenv)`; invalid
values fail the process at boot with a one-line reason each (fail fast, never guess). Durations
use Go syntax (`60s`, `5m`, `720h`). Booleans accept `true/false/1/0`. **Every** bad value is
reported, not just the first: `Load` returns a `*config.Errors` holding one error per variable and
`main` prints them one per line under a single `clippet: config:` header (§20 erratum 104).

| Env var | Default | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `CLIPPET_LISTEN` | `:8080` | no | Container-internal listen address; compose maps host 8481 → 8080. |
| `PUBLIC_BASE_URL` | — | **yes** | Absolute origin `scheme://host[:port]`, scheme ∈ {http, https}, no path, no trailing slash (a trailing slash is trimmed; any other path is fatal). Drives every absolute URL in cards/DTOs, the cookie `Secure` flag and `og:video:secure_url`. |
| `DATA_DIR` | `/data` | no | SQLite lives at `$DATA_DIR/clippet.db` (+ `-wal`, `-shm`). Must be a named volume. |
| `SCRATCH_DIR` | `/scratch` | no | Transcode scratch disk; per-clip dirs `$SCRATCH_DIR/{clipID}/`. |
| `STORAGE_BACKEND` | `s3` | no | `s3` (the default, and what every version before ROADMAP #37 did) or `fs`, a plain directory under `STORAGE_DIR` (§20 erratum 276). On `fs` the four bucket variables (`S3_ENDPOINT`/`S3_BUCKET`/`S3_ACCESS_KEY`/`S3_SECRET_KEY`) are REFUSED rather than ignored, each a boot error naming itself; `S3Config` then carries only the key prefix and the timeouts. Anything but the two values is fatal at boot. |
| `STORAGE_DIR` | — | conditionally | The absolute directory the media lives in on `fs` (§20 erratum 276) — required there, a boot error unset. Optional on `s3`, where it is what `admin storage migrate --to fs` copies into ahead of a switch. May not be `/`, and may not be, contain or sit inside `DATA_DIR` or `SCRATCH_DIR`. `compose.fs.yaml` pins the CONTAINER path to `/media` regardless of this value; only the compose-only `STORAGE_DIR_HOST` moves the host directory. |
| `S3_ENDPOINT` | — | **yes** | Full URL incl. scheme, e.g. `http://minio:9000`, `https://<acct>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com`, `https://s3.us-west-004.backblazeb2.com`. |
| `S3_REGION` | `us-east-1` | no | R2 uses `auto`; B2 uses its region string; MinIO ignores it. |
| `S3_BUCKET` | — | **yes** | Bucket name. Must already exist (compose `bucket-init` creates it in dev). |
| `S3_ACCESS_KEY` / `S3_SECRET_KEY` | — | **yes** | Credentials. Never logged. |
| `S3_FORCE_PATH_STYLE` | `false` | no | `true` → `minio.BucketLookupPath` (MinIO; compose sets it). `false` → DNS/virtual-host lookup (R2, B2 both work either way; `false` is the safe default off-compose). |
| `S3_KEY_PREFIX` | `` (empty) | no | Optional prefix to share a bucket (`clippet/`). If non-empty it must end with `/`; Load appends one if missing. |
| `STORAGE_OP_TIMEOUT` | `30s` | no | Per control-plane storage call (List, Remove, Stat, Ping) **and** the response-header wait of every GET/PUT (`http.Transport.ResponseHeaderTimeout`, §8.5). Never bounds a body stream. |
| `STORAGE_IDLE_TIMEOUT` | `2m` | no | **Progress-based** transfer timeout: a PutFile / Download / media body stream is aborted when no bytes have moved for this long (§8.5, §18.4). A 4 GiB original on a slow uplink is fine as long as bytes keep flowing. |
| `STORAGE_TRANSFER_MAX` | `6h` | no | Absolute cap on one PutFile / Download (belt-and-braces over the idle timeout). |
| `STORAGE_UPLOAD_THREADS` | `6` | no | How many 16 MiB parts one multipart PutFile uploads at the same time (`ConcurrentStreamParts`, §20 erratum 337); `1` is the sequential path, `1`–`32` or fatal at boot naming it. Memory ≈ N × 16 MiB per running upload. S3 only. |
| `STORAGE_PING_ATTEMPTS` / `STORAGE_PING_INTERVAL` | `10` / `3s` | no | The shape of the **boot** ping loop in `cmd/clippet/serve.go` (§8.7, §20 erratum 283). The listener is already open when it starts, so this is not a startup gate: it decides only how long the process keeps asking a store that is not answering before it logs `storage unreachable; serving degraded` and starts the worker and the sweeper anyway. Each attempt is capped at a non-configurable `pingTimeout` of 3s, so the defaults are ≈60s. Backend-agnostic (`fs` has a `Ping` too), which is why it is on `Config` and not `S3Config`. Under `1` attempt is fatal at boot naming the variable, per §4's never-guess rule. `/readyz` is unaffected — it pings live per request. |
| `MEDIA_DELIVERY` | `proxy` | no | HOW the media is delivered, as opposed to where it lives (ROADMAP #34 lane F, §20 erratum 278). `proxy` is byte-for-byte every version before it: the app streams every media byte itself. `redirect` answers the same URLs, after the same gates, with **302 to a freshly presigned URL on the bucket's own origin** — so no video byte crosses whatever sits in front of the app. The card tags, the share links and the route table are IDENTICAL in both, and `/original` is app-served in both, being the one object with an identity gate (erratum 207). `redirect` on `STORAGE_BACKEND=fs` is fatal at boot: a directory has no URL to redirect to. Anything outside the two words is fatal at boot naming both. |
| `MEDIA_PRESIGN_TTL` | `1h` | no | How long one of those signatures is valid, bounded `1m … 24h` and REFUSED rather than clamped outside them (§20 erratum 278). It bounds the window a copied media URL keeps working, not a clip's life: the link is minted per request, after the gate, and is never stored or written into a card tag. A short value is a trap rather than a tightening — a `<video>` keeps issuing ranged GETs against the SAME src for as long as its page is open, so a signature that expires mid-watch breaks seeking on a page nobody reloaded. |
| `MEDIA_PRESIGN_ENDPOINT` | *(= `S3_ENDPOINT`)* | no | The bare origin a VIEWER reaches the bucket at, validated exactly as `S3_ENDPOINT` is (§20 erratum 278). SigV4 signs the HOST, so a link minted for the origin this process uses is valid at no other — which is the case wherever the app reaches the bucket privately (the shipped MinIO is a compose service name) and a viewer reaches it publicly. On R2/B2/S3 one host serves both and it is left unset. Set while `MEDIA_DELIVERY=proxy` it is IGNORED, with a NOTE at boot and on `admin doctor`'s `media` row rather than an error — that is what `.env` looks like while an operator gets ready to switch. A plain-http value under an https `PUBLIC_BASE_URL` is fatal at boot: a browser refuses active mixed content, so the player would stay blank while the Discord card went on working. |
| `DEFAULT_CLIP_TTL` | `never` | no | Applied when `ttl_days` is absent/null on upload. Accepted: `never`, `0` (= never), `1d`, `7d`, `30d`, `90d`, or bare `1|7|30|90`. Anything else is fatal at boot. Stored as `DefaultTTLSeconds *int64` (nil = never). |
| `SWEEP_INTERVAL` | `60s` | no | Sweeper tick. |
| `SWEEP_GRACE` | `1h` | no | Clips in `processing` are swept only once `expires_at <= now - grace` (§12). |
| `SWEEP_BATCH` | `50` | no | Max clips destroyed per tick. |
| `MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES` | `4294967296` (4 GiB) | no | Operator limit on the video part, enforced via `http.MaxBytesReader` (+1 MiB slack for multipart framing) → 413. Documented as "no arbitrary caps — this is your disk". Bounded 1 … 2^62 at boot (§20 erratum 33). |
| `SCRATCH_MIN_FREE_BYTES` | `536870912` (512 MiB) | no | Ingest refuses (507) when `statfs(SCRATCH_DIR).free < 1.5 × Content-Length + this`. |
| `STORAGE_BUDGET_BYTES` | `0` (off) | no | An ADVISORY line the operator wants to know about crossing (ROADMAP #24, §20 errata 157 and 277). `0` is off. It is never a cap — no upload is ever refused because of it — UNLESS `STORAGE_BUDGET_HARD=1` below, the one opt-in that makes it one; README's "no tiers, no per-user quotas" stays literally true either way, because this is one line for one instance and there is still nothing per account. When the bytes the database says are in the bucket pass it: one WARN at the sweeper's next tick, `/healthz` grows a `storage_budget` object (present only once the sweeper has taken a reading), the library page carries one line, and the settings page's Storage panel leads with the `quota` row. |
| `STORAGE_BUDGET_HARD` | `0` (off) | no | Turns that line into a CAP (§20 erratum 277): a NEW clip is refused `507 storage_quota` once `db.StorageUsed` has REACHED the budget (`>=`, not the WARN's `>`), at one site — `httpapi.ingestCore`, which all three creating callers run through — so a replacement or a trim of an existing clip is not refused. The number is read live per upload and never from the sweeper's cache, so a delete makes room at once. `1` without a budget is fatal at boot: a cap of zero would refuse everything. |
| `STORAGE_PRICE_PER_GB_MONTH` | `` (unset) | no | What your provider charges to KEEP one GB for a month, as a plain decimal in your own currency (ROADMAP #39, §20 erratum 270): `0.015`, `0.36`, `0`. Optional, and UNSET means the cost line is ABSENT everywhere — not zero, because a 0.00 nobody configured reads as "this is free". At most six digits after the point and at most `config.MaxPricePerGB` (1000000) before it; a sign, an exponent, a separator or a currency symbol is fatal at boot naming the variable. The app never asks a provider anything (§15): it multiplies this by the bytes the database already counts, at 1 GB = 10^9 bytes, the unit providers bill in. |
| `EGRESS_PRICE_PER_GB` | `` (unset) | no | The same, for one GB SENT to viewers, against the per-day served-bytes counter migration 0017 added (§20 erratum 270). Either price may be set without the other — a friend on R2 prices storage and leaves egress unset, which is DEPLOY §31's worked example. |
| `STORAGE_PRICING` | `` (unset) | no | A dated PRESET of one provider's list prices instead of the two above: `local`, `r2`, `b2`, `s3` (§20 erratum 277). A table in `internal/cost/presets.go` — read off the provider's published page on the date each row carries and NEVER fetched, so §15's destination list is unchanged — carrying both prices, the currency that list quotes and the provider's free storage and free egress allowances as code. Either typed price OVERRIDES its half (both allowance rules stay). Unset is the custom case. A value outside the set is fatal at boot naming the four. |
| `CAPTURE_READY_WAIT` | `30s` | no | How long `POST /api/upload` holds its 201 waiting for the clip to be **CARD-ready** — `db.CardReady`: a poster plus the file `og:video` points at — so the URL a capture tool pastes unfurls as a player card (§20 errata 97, 212). `0` = never wait; hard ceiling 60s (`config.CaptureReadyWaitMax`), enforced at boot, and AT the ceiling the link is answered anyway with `card_ready: false`. The one §4 duration whose zero is a setting rather than a misconfiguration, so it has its own loader. It is the ONLY knob on that wait since erratum 212 — the request's own `wait` field is a 400 — and it never applies to `POST /api/clips`. |
| `LIGHT_TAG_TEXT` | `{light} preview · {best} on Clippet` | no | The one line burned into the LIGHT copy (§20 erratum 214), `{light}`/`{best}` substituted with that clip's real qualities ("720p30", "1440p60"). The word `off` switches it off; empty is the default rather than off, because `config.Load` reads through `getenv` and cannot tell an unset variable from one set to nothing (and compose's `${VAR:-default}` collapses the two before the process sees them). At most `config.MaxLightTagRunes` (80) runes, one line — a control character is fatal at boot. The FONT is not configured: serve.go resolves it from the image (`transcode.FindTagFont`) and clears this when it finds none. |
| `TRANSCODE_CONCURRENCY` | `1` | no | Simultaneous **ffmpeg runs**: the number of transcode loops, and the size of the semaphore every trim and gif encode also takes a slot from (§20 erratum 79). Bounded **1 … 16** (`config.MaxTranscodeConcurrency`, §20 erratum 104): every slot is a live encoder inside the process that also serves HTTP and runs the sweeper, so a typo must fail at boot rather than at the OOM killer. Sizing: ~0.5 GiB and one core per slot; rule of thumb `TRANSCODE_CONCURRENCY <= min(cores, RAM_GiB)`. |
| `TRANSCODE_PRESET` | `veryfast` | no | libx264 preset. **Measured (§20 erratum 215)**: `superfast` is 13–21 % faster and `ultrafast` 24–44 %, at +81 % bytes on the worst-case sample *at the same VBV ceiling* — so this default is not a guess. |
| `TRANSCODE_THREADS` | `0` (auto) | no | The `-threads`/`-filter_threads`/`-filter_complex_threads` value of every encode (§20 erratum 215). `0` = read this container's own CFS quota (`transcode.ResolveThreads`), because `nproc` inside a `cpus: 1.0` container reports every core the HOST has and x264 was then throttled at 25 % below its pinned speed. Bounded `0 … config.MaxTranscodeThreads` (128). The boot line prints the resolved number. |
| `TRANSCODE_HWACCEL` | `` (CPU) | no | `` or `cuda` (§20 erratum 216). `cuda` renders the NVENC argv — hardware decode, `scale_cuda`, `h264_nvenc` — and needs the Dockerfile's `gpu` target, which is the only image with an NVENC encoder; on the ordinary image it is FATAL at boot. It is read by the PLAN, not the build: `transcode.HWAccelFor` refuses it for any plan needing a CPU-only filter (tone map, deinterlace, pre-rotate, `setsar`) or `FULL_CODEC=av1`, and that clip silently renders the CPU argv on the same binary. The word `none` is accepted as a spelling of the empty value. |
| `TRANSCODE_CRF` | `23` | no | libx264 CRF (0–51). |
| `TRANSCODE_MAX_FPS` | `60` | no | Output fps cap. **Since §20 errata 202–203 it bounds the LIGHT copy alone** — which takes the minimum of it and its own 30 — and remains the sanity ceiling that keeps a container claiming 1000 fps from being believed; it can no longer lower a FULL tier below the rate its source actually ran at. |
| `TRANSCODE_MAX_WIDTH` / `TRANSCODE_MAX_HEIGHT` | `1280` / `720` | no | The fit box (long side ≤ W, short side ≤ H). Both must be **even** and ≥ 2 (fatal otherwise) so `MakePlan` can never exceed the box after even-rounding; keys do not encode the size, so changing them is safe. The H.264 level is not pinned (§10.3) so larger boxes need no other change. **Since §20 errata 202–203 this box is the LIGHT copy's and no other tier's**: a Full is encoded at the source's own size and a playable original is served at it, so lowering these makes smaller cards and changes nothing a viewer streams. |
| `TRANSCODE_STALL_TIMEOUT` | `5m` | no | No `-progress` line for this long while `out_time < 99%` of known duration → kill, permanent failure (§10). |
| `TRANSCODE_HARD_TIMEOUT` | `6h` | no | Absolute cap per ffmpeg invocation (also the only limit during the faststart remux tail and for unknown-duration sources). |
| `TRANSCODE_MAX_ATTEMPTS` | `3` | no | **Crash-class** bad endings (panic in the job, or found `running` at boot with no checkpoint — "the file might be what crashes us") before a job is `failed`. Backoff `min(30s·2^(n−1), 10m)`. |
| `TRANSCODE_MAX_TRANSIENT` | `10` | no | **Environment-class** bad endings (storage/scratch/DB/io errors during acquire, store, finalize) before a job is `failed`. Backoff `min(1m·2^(n−1), 30m)` — ten tries span ≈2.5 h, so a storage outage shorter than that fails nothing (§5, §11). Counted separately from crashes so an outage never burns the crash budget. |
| `JOBS_UNSTICK_AFTER` | `TRANSCODE_HARD_TIMEOUT` + `15m` (so `6h15m` by default) | no | How long a job may be `running` before the app repairs it ITSELF, applying exactly the repair `clippet admin jobs unstick` applies by hand (§20 errata 230-231, ROADMAP #12). `0` switches it off; a positive value under `config.MinUnstickAfter` (30 s) is raised to it. A job THIS process has claimed is never repaired, of any kind, whatever its age — that is what lets the age be SHORT, unlike the CLI's `--older-than`, whose floor is the hard timeout because a second process has no such knowledge (erratum 146). An age under `TRANSCODE_HARD_TIMEOUT` is therefore obeyed and WARNED about, at boot and in `admin doctor`: what it risks is a SECOND process on the same database, whose live job this one cannot see. The default is computed from another variable, so `compose.yaml` passes this one through EMPTY rather than spelling a literal that could drift. |
| `TRANSCODE_MAX_BITRATE` | `0` (off) | no | VBV ceiling of the **FULL tier** in **bits per second** (§20 erratum 202 — it is the one operator setting that can make a Full less than faithful), rendered as `-maxrate` with `-bufsize` = twice it (§20 erratum 124). `0` is a setting, not a bound: no `-maxrate` is emitted at all and CRF alone decides the bitrate, exactly as before. A non-zero value must be between 100000 and 2^34 — a value like `2500` (an operator thinking in kilobits) is fatal at boot rather than 2.5 kbps of video. |
| `SOCIAL_MAX_BYTES` | `26214400` (25 MiB) | no | The size at or above which a clip also gets the dedicated, smaller **LIGHT** tier for its card (§17 #3, §20 errata 121, 203). Since the quality tiers the rule has three terms and this is one of them: a file **larger than 1280×720** or **above 30 fps** gets a Light copy whatever its size. `0` turns the tier off entirely — no `social` job is ever enqueued and `/social.mp4` (and `/light.mp4`) serve the best playable tier through the same COALESCE, exactly as they did before the producer existed. The name is kept: renaming a variable breaks every `.env` in existence for a word. |
| `FULL_CODEC` | `h264` | no | `h264` \| `av1` — the encoder of the **FULL tier**, the one stored copy of a source no browser can play as it stands (§20 erratum 204). `h264` is the default because it is the only codec every browser, every Discord client and every embedded player decodes; `av1` (`libsvtav1 -preset 8 -crf 32`) roughly halves that file for the same picture, encodes considerably slower, and wants decoder hardware from about 2019. It bounds nothing else: a playable original is never re-encoded, a trim's cut is H.264, and the card's LIGHT copy is H.264 whatever this says. Anything but the two values is fatal at boot. |
| `FFMPEG_PATH` / `FFPROBE_PATH` | `ffmpeg` / `ffprobe` | no | Resolved via `exec.LookPath` at boot; missing → fatal. Version printed at boot and in `/healthz`. |
| `SESSION_TTL` | `720h` | no | Cookie `Max-Age` and DB `expires_at`; sliding (touched at most once per minute). |
| `SESSION_COOKIE_NAME` | `clippet_session` | no | RFC 6265 token (§20 erratum 28); a `__Host-`/`__Secure-` prefix requires an https `PUBLIC_BASE_URL` (§20 erratum 35). |
| `SESSION_MAX_TTL` | `2160h` (90 days) | no | The **ceiling** on the sliding window, measured from a session's CREATION (§20 erratum 105). A touch may slide `expires_at`, never past `created_at + SESSION_MAX_TTL`; `GetSession` refuses a row past it, and the re-issued cookie carries the row's remaining life, not a fresh `SESSION_TTL`. Below `SESSION_TTL` it also clamps a brand-new session. |
| `SESSION_SECRET` | — | **no (not used)** | Deliberately absent. Sessions are 256-bit random opaque tokens stored as `sha256(token)`; there is nothing to sign, so there is no secret to rotate or leak. Documented here so nobody adds one. |
| `REGISTRATION` | `first` | no | `open` \| `first` \| `closed` (§20 erratum 106). `first` is the DEFAULT: accepted only while the `users` table is EMPTY, so the first account bootstraps the instance and the door closes behind it. `open` accepts anybody, forever, and is what an operator sets deliberately while friends sign up. `closed` refuses everyone; `clippet admin users create` is how accounts are added then. A refusal is 403 `registration_closed` and `/register` renders a notice; `/login`'s "create an account" link and `/register`'s form follow the same resolution. The effective mode is on the boot line. |
| `LIBRARY_SCOPE` | `shared` | no | `shared` \| `own` (§20 erratum 113). `shared` is what every deployment did before this variable existed: the library and `GET /api/clips` list every account's `unlisted=0` clips plus the caller's own unlisted ones. `own` adds `AND owner_id = ?` to that one query, so an account's library is its own clips only. It narrows a LIST and changes nothing else — `GET /api/clips/{id}`, the share page, `/c/{id}`, the media routes and the Discord auto-post are all untouched, because the unguessable link is the authentication (§7). Anything but the two values is fatal at boot. |
| `INSTANCE_BADGE` | `` (the production instance) | no | One lowercase word this instance wears so a person cannot mistake it for the production one (§20 erratum 285): `dev`, `staging`, `lab-test`. Lowercase letters, digits and `-`, at most `config.MaxInstanceBadgeRunes` (12) of them — a set that needs no escaping in any of the places it is rendered; anything else is fatal at boot, naming the variable and the rule. Set, it renders `data-badge` on `<html>` (so one `:root[data-badge]` rule paints the wordmark's span, and a face's mouth with it, `--line-strong` grey instead of `--ok` green with the first byte of the page), a `<span class="instance">` beside the mark on every page but the embed, the `<title>` prefix, `og:site_name` / the oEmbed `provider_name` as `clippet <badge>`, and the manifest's `name`/`short_name` as `Clippet <badge>`. Empty is the default and changes NOTHING — an unbadged page is byte-identical to the one this app served before the variable existed, which a test pins by subtraction. Deliberately absent from `/healthz`: what it exists for is an eye, and the anonymous surface stays the size it was. |
| `TRUSTED_PROXIES` | `` (trust nothing) | no | Comma-separated CIDRs (`127.0.0.1/32,172.16.0.0/12`). Only when `RemoteAddr` is inside one of them are `X-Real-IP` / `X-Forwarded-For` honored (§13). |
| `VIEW_DEDUPE_TTL` | `30m` | no | Per-(clip, viewer) dedupe window. |
| `VIEW_DEDUPE_MAX` | `50000` | no | Hard cap on dedupe entries (§13). |
| `RATE_AUTH_PER_MIN` | `10` | no | Register/login attempts per client IP per minute (burst = same). |
| `RATE_UPLOAD_PER_HOUR` | `60` | no | Uploads per user (or IP when unauthenticated → 401 anyway) per hour. |
| `RATE_UPLOAD_PER_HOUR_PER_IP` | `120` | no | The second bucket both upload routes require, keyed on the resolved client IP; an upload must satisfy this **and** `RATE_UPLOAD_PER_HOUR` (§20 erratum 97). Deliberately looser than the per-user budget: it exists because accounts are free, not to bound a household behind one NAT. |
| `RATE_LIMIT_MAX_KEYS` | `10000` | no | Hard cap on limiter keys per limiter (§14). |
| `DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL` | `` (empty = off) | no | Phase 4 #4. Empty is the default: no `http.Client` is constructed for it and no `notify` job is ever enqueued — with the bot, Sign in with Discord and `CLIP_WEBHOOK_URL` off too, the binary makes **no outbound HTTP at all** beyond `S3_ENDPOINT` (§15). When set it must be `https`, its host exactly one of `discord.com` / `discordapp.com` / `ptb.discord.com` / `canary.discord.com` (no port), its path exactly `/api/webhooks/{numeric id}/{token}`, with no userinfo, query or fragment — anything else is fatal at boot with a reason that names the rule and never echoes the value. **The value is a secret** (the token is the last path segment): it is held as `config.DiscordWebhook`, whose `String`/`LogValue` render only `host/id`, and it appears in no log line, error, job row, `/healthz` or admin output. One INFO line at boot: `discord webhook configured host=… webhook_id=…`. See §20 errata 63–66. |
| `DISCORD_WEBHOOK_ROUTES` | `` (no routing) | no | Per-tag channel routing, ONE variable of ordered `<tag>=<url>` rules separated by `;` (ROADMAP #26, §20 erratum 158): a ready clip posts to the FIRST rule whose tag it carries, in the order written. Every URL is validated exactly as `DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL` is and is equally a secret; every tag follows the tag grammar (`^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,31}$`) and `default` is RESERVED (it already names `DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL`'s own channel). A rejected rule is named by its 1-based POSITION, never by echoing what was typed — a rule written backwards (`<url>=<tag>`) would otherwise print a live credential to `docker compose logs app`. |
| `DISCORD_WEBHOOK_UNMATCHED` | `default` | no | What happens to a ready clip no `DISCORD_WEBHOOK_ROUTES` rule matched: `default` posts it to `DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL` (and nowhere if that is unset — the pre-routing behavior, unchanged); `skip` posts it nowhere at all, which is how an operator says "only tagged clips are announced". `skip` with `DISCORD_WEBHOOK_ROUTES` empty and a live `DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL` is refused at boot (§20 erratum 160): with no rules to match, `skip` would announce nothing at all while the boot line still says a webhook is configured. |
| `DISCORD_APP_ID` / `DISCORD_PUBLIC_KEY` / `DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN` | `` (empty = the bot does not exist) | no | The Discord BOT (ROADMAP #33, §20 errata 253–256), a different feature from the webhook above: with all three set, `POST /api/discord/interactions` is registered and answers `/clip` for the servers `clippet admin bot bind` has connected. **All three or none** — any one of them alone is fatal at boot naming all three, because a half-configured bot boots and is silently dead. The app id is a snowflake (15–25 digits) and the public key is 64 hex characters; neither is secret (the key VERIFIES signatures and cannot make them). **`DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN` is a secret** and is used for exactly one thing, publishing the guild command: it lives behind `DiscordBot.Token()`, `String`/`LogValue` render `app <id>, public key <8 hex>… , token (redacted)`, and no rejection echoes it. Turning the bot on adds exactly two egress destinations to §15's list: `discord.com` (already the webhook's host) and the attachment CDN (`cdn.discordapp.com`, `media.discordapp.net`), which `config.ValidAttachmentURL` holds every fetched URL to. |
| `DISCORD_COMMAND_NAME` | `clip` (`config.DefaultCommandName`) | no | The slash command's name, without the leading slash (§20 erratum 284): 1–32 characters of lowercase letters, digits, `-` and `_`. Rides along as a fourth, OPTIONAL variable beside the three above — setting it with the bot off is fatal at boot, and so is any name but `clip` on a MANAGED bot (`DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN=managed`), which publishes one global `/clip` and forwards that command alone. Re-run `clippet admin bot register` after changing it: the name lives in the command Discord stores, and that call replaces the server's whole command set. |
| `DISCORD_LOGIN_CLIENT_ID` / `DISCORD_LOGIN_CLIENT_SECRET` | `` (empty = no Discord sign-in) | no | Sign in with Discord (ROADMAP #44, §20 erratum 302), a THIRD feature beside the webhook and the bot: the instance's OWN Discord application's OAuth2 client id (a snowflake; an own-bot instance may reuse `DISCORD_APP_ID`) and client secret (**secret**: 16–128 characters of the bot token's charset, behind `DiscordLogin.Secret()`, `String`/`LogValue` render `client <id>, secret (redacted)`, no rejection echoes it). **Both or none** — one alone is fatal at boot naming both. With both set, `/login` carries a "Sign in with Discord" anchor and three paths under `/api/auth/discord` exist; a Discord login opens an account that is LINKED (Settings, or `admin users link`) and never creates one, under any `REGISTRATION`. Egress: two paths on `discord.com`, a host already on §15's list. |
| `CLIP_WEBHOOK_URL` / `CLIP_WEBHOOK_SECRET` | `` (empty = off) | no | The clip webhook (ROADMAP #54, §20 erratum 319): every clip that becomes ready — unlisted ones included, marked — is POSTed once as a signed JSON document to the ONE URL the operator names. **Both or neither** (one alone is fatal at boot naming the missing one). The URL: `http` or `https`, a host, no userinfo, no fragment, a query allowed; **a secret** (receivers carry tokens in paths and queries), held with the key in `config.ClipWebhook`, whose `String`/`LogValue` render `<scheme>://<host>[/(path redacted)]`; no rejection echoes any part of either value. The key: 32 characters or more, no whitespace, the HMAC-SHA256 key of `X-Clippet-Signature`. Unset: no client, no `hook` job. |
| `SSR_TIMEOUT` | `5s` | no | Context deadline for the share/embed page's DB read (belt-and-braces; the read is local). |
| `LOG_LEVEL` / `LOG_FORMAT` | `info` / `text` | no | `debug|info|warn|error`; `text|json` (slog). |

**Compose-only knobs** (interpolated by `compose.yaml`, never read by the binary; they are in
`.env` because `.env` is the one place an operator sets anything): `CLIPPET_PUBLISH` (the host side of
the published port, §20 erratum 96), `CLIPPET_IMAGE` (the built tag, so a side-by-side lane stack
builds its own), `CLIPPET_GPU_IMAGE` (`clippet-app:gpu` — the same, for the `compose.gpu.yaml`
override of `app`, §20 errata 216/247), and — §20 erratum 104 — `CLIPPET_VERSION` (a **build arg**: it
reaches the Dockerfile's `ARG VERSION` and is baked in as `-X main.version`, so `/healthz` can say
which binary is live), `APP_MEM_LIMIT` (`2g`) and `APP_CPUS` (`1.0`), the app container's `mem_limit` /
`cpus`. The last two use compose's v2 single-host keys deliberately: a `deploy.resources.limits` block
is Swarm-only and `docker compose up` ignores it silently, which is worse than no limit at all.
`APP_CPUS` may never exceed the host's core count — the daemon refuses to *create* such a container —
which is why its default is one core and not two (§20 erratum 104(c)).

`.env.example` lists every variable in this table, commented out at its default with an explanatory
comment — the file is the complete list, not a curated subset. `PUBLIC_BASE_URL`, the bundled MinIO's
credentials and bucket (`MINIO_ROOT_USER`, `MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD`, `S3_BUCKET`, `S3_REGION`),
`DEFAULT_CLIP_TTL` and `TRUSTED_PROXIES` are the seven lines left uncommented; compose supplies dev
defaults for the rest.

Provider matrix (goes verbatim into Phase 5 README):

| Provider | `S3_ENDPOINT` | `S3_REGION` | `S3_FORCE_PATH_STYLE` |
|---|---|---|---|
| MinIO (compose) | `http://minio:9000` | `us-east-1` | `true` |
| Cloudflare R2 | `https://<account>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com` | `auto` | `false` (path-style also works) |
| Backblaze B2 | `https://s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com` | `<region>` e.g. `us-west-004` | `false` |

---

## 5. Data model

SQLite, file `$DATA_DIR/clippet.db`. All timestamps are `INTEGER` unix seconds UTC (rendered
RFC3339 UTC in JSON). All ids are TEXT: users/tokens use `ids.New()` (12 base62) like clips.
Nullable columns map to pointer fields in Go structs.

**Connection setup (`db.Open`)**: DSN
`file:$DATA_DIR/clippet.db?_pragma=busy_timeout(5000)&_pragma=journal_mode(WAL)&_pragma=synchronous(NORMAL)&_pragma=foreign_keys(1)`.
Two pools over the same file: `rw` with `_txlock=immediate` appended and `SetMaxOpenConns(1)`
(every write and every write transaction goes here — in-process writers queue in Go, so
`SQLITE_BUSY` between goroutines cannot occur); `ro` with `SetMaxOpenConns(4)` for reads.
The admin CLI is the only second-process writer (one statement, covered by `busy_timeout`).
`PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL` is verified after open (fatal if not `wal`).

**Migrations**: `internal/db/migrations/NNNN_name.sql` embedded via `embed.FS`; `Migrate`
creates `schema_migrations(version INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, applied_at INTEGER NOT NULL)` and
applies each unapplied file in ascending order inside one transaction per file. No down
migrations. `clippet migrate` runs it standalone; `serve` runs it at boot.

```sql
-- 0001_init.sql
CREATE TABLE users (
  id            TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  username      TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE COLLATE NOCASE,
  password_hash TEXT NOT NULL,                 -- bcrypt cost 12
  created_at    INTEGER NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE sessions (
  token_hash   TEXT PRIMARY KEY,               -- hex sha256 of the raw cookie value
  user_id      TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  created_at   INTEGER NOT NULL,
  expires_at   INTEGER NOT NULL,
  last_seen_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
  user_agent   TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT ''
);
CREATE INDEX sessions_expires ON sessions(expires_at);

CREATE TABLE api_tokens (
  id           TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  user_id      TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  name         TEXT NOT NULL,
  token_hash   TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,           -- hex sha256 of the raw token ("ck_...")
  prefix       TEXT NOT NULL,                  -- first 8 chars after "ck_", display only
  scopes       TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'upload', -- comma-separated; Phase 1 knows only 'upload'
  created_at   INTEGER NOT NULL,
  last_used_at INTEGER,
  revoked_at   INTEGER
);
CREATE INDEX api_tokens_user ON api_tokens(user_id, created_at DESC);

CREATE TABLE clips (
  id                  TEXT PRIMARY KEY,                       -- public share slug (§7)
  owner_id            TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  title               TEXT NOT NULL,
  description         TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  unlisted            INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  state               TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (state IN ('queued','processing','ready','failed','deleting')),
  failure_reason      TEXT,                                   -- set when state='failed'
  -- source (immutable after insert; "upload is sacred")
  source_key          TEXT NOT NULL,
  source_filename     TEXT NOT NULL,
  source_size         INTEGER NOT NULL,
  source_content_type TEXT NOT NULL,
  source_etag         TEXT NOT NULL,                           -- hex sha256 of the original (PutResult.SHA256 at ingest); ETag for /original
  -- rendition + poster (set at finalize; NULL until ready)
  rendition_key       TEXT,
  rendition_size      INTEGER,
  rendition_etag      TEXT,                                   -- hex sha256 of the object, computed while uploading
  poster_key          TEXT,
  poster_size         INTEGER,
  poster_etag         TEXT,
  poster_width        INTEGER,                                -- MEASURED from the JPEG (jpegStats, §20 erratum 92)
  poster_height       INTEGER,
  social_key          TEXT,                                   -- §17 #3; NULL = /social.mp4 serves COALESCE(social_key, rendition_key)
  social_size         INTEGER,
  social_etag         TEXT,
  social_width        INTEGER,                                -- MEASURED from the social mp4 (migration 0007, §20 erratum 123);
  social_height       INTEGER,                                --   og:video:width/height and twitter:player describe THIS file
  social_fps_num      INTEGER,                                -- MEASURED (migration 0012): the quality selector's "Light 720p30"
  social_fps_den      INTEGER,
  -- the quality tiers (migration 0012, §20 errata 200-206). The FULL tier's OBJECT
  -- is rendition_key: there is deliberately no second key for it, so every
  -- invalidation path that covers a rendition covers it (erratum 201).
  original_playable   INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,             -- the UPLOAD is web-playable as it stands
  original_remuxed    INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,             -- ...after a `-c copy` rewrite, which IS rendition_key
  original_width      INTEGER,                                -- the UPLOAD's own display dims, never a rendition's
  original_height     INTEGER,
  original_fps_num    INTEGER,                                -- the upload's average rate, exact
  original_fps_den    INTEGER,
  original_codec      TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',               -- as ffprobe named it: h264, hevc, av1, ...
  full_state          TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',               -- '' | skipped | encoding | ready | failed
  full_codec          TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',               -- which encoder produced the Full (FULL_CODEC)
  light_state         TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',               -- the same five values, for the card's copy
  -- measured media facts (from ffprobe of the OUTPUT, not the plan) — of the BEST
  -- PLAYABLE TIER, which is the file /video.mp4 serves (erratum 201)
  duration_ms         INTEGER,
  width               INTEGER,
  height              INTEGER,
  fps_num             INTEGER,
  fps_den             INTEGER,
  has_audio           INTEGER,
  -- counters + lifecycle
  views               INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  ttl_seconds         INTEGER,                                -- NULL = never; resolved at upload (request or DEFAULT_CLIP_TTL); kept for Phase 4 keep-alive
  expires_at          INTEGER,                                -- NULL = never; = created_at + ttl_seconds, fixed at upload; PATCH recomputes from now
  created_at          INTEGER NOT NULL,
  updated_at          INTEGER NOT NULL,
  ready_at            INTEGER
);
CREATE INDEX clips_owner_created ON clips(owner_id, created_at DESC, id);
CREATE INDEX clips_listed        ON clips(created_at DESC, id) WHERE unlisted = 0;
CREATE INDEX clips_expires       ON clips(expires_at) WHERE expires_at IS NOT NULL;
CREATE INDEX clips_state         ON clips(state);

CREATE TABLE jobs (
  id              INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
  clip_id         TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES clips(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  kind            TEXT NOT NULL,                              -- 'transcode' in Phase 1; Phase 4: 'trim','gif','notify','social','replace','poster'; the trim scrubber: 'filmstrip' (§20 erratum 220); quality tiers: 'full' (§20 erratum 206; retained but no longer enqueued since erratum 217)
  state           TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (state IN ('queued','running','done','failed','cancelled')),
  stage           TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',                   -- persisted at stage transitions (progress fallback after restart)
  attempts           INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,              -- CRASH-class bad endings (panic, interrupted w/o checkpoint); incremented ONLY in db.FailAttempt
  transient_failures INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,              -- ENVIRONMENT-class bad endings (storage/scratch/db/io); incremented ONLY in db.FailAttempt
  run_after       INTEGER NOT NULL,                           -- backoff gate for ClaimJob
  params_json     TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',                 -- Phase 4 (trim points etc.)
  checkpoint_json TEXT,                                       -- set after outputs are uploaded+verified (§10 step 8); NULL before
  last_error      TEXT,
  created_at      INTEGER NOT NULL,
  updated_at      INTEGER NOT NULL,
  started_at      INTEGER,
  finished_at     INTEGER
);
CREATE INDEX jobs_claim ON jobs(state, run_after, id);
CREATE INDEX jobs_clip  ON jobs(clip_id, id DESC);

-- The sweeper's per-clip Destroy-failure backoff, so a crash loop cannot hammer a
-- black-holing prefix (migration 0013, §12, §20 erratum 232). One row per FAILING
-- clip; the foreign key means a schedule cannot outlive the clip it describes.
CREATE TABLE sweep_failures (
  clip_id         TEXT PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES clips(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  failures        INTEGER NOT NULL,   -- consecutive failed Destroys, >= 1
  last_attempt_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
  next_attempt_at INTEGER NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE schema_migrations (version INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, applied_at INTEGER NOT NULL);
```

**Clip state machine (availability of the clip)** — there is no `uploading` state: the row
is inserted only after the original object is durable (§8 upload), so a clip row always has
a source.

```
            (ingest tx: clip row + transcode job, original already in bucket)
                                  │
                                  ▼
  ┌──────► queued ──ClaimJob──► processing ──FinalizeTranscode(1 row)──► ready
  │           ▲                    │
  │           │  FailAttempt       │  FailAttempt(FailPermanent || crash cap 3 || transient cap 10)
  │           └──(crash|transient, under cap; or ReleaseJob)──────────────► failed
  │                                │                                          │
  └──── POST /retry (failed→queued, job reset) ◄──────────────────────────────┘

  ANY state ──MarkDeleting (owner DELETE or sweeper)──► deleting ──DeleteClipRow──► (gone)
```

- `deleting` is a tombstone: every public route answers **404** for it immediately; it exists so
  a crash between "objects deleted" and "row deleted" is resumed by the next sweep tick, and so
  no new job can be claimed for the clip (`ClaimJob` skips clips in `deleting`).
- `failed` keeps the row AND the original forever (until TTL or owner delete). Retry is free
  because the source is still there.
- Phase 4 rule (written now, binding): **jobs of any kind other than `transcode` never change
  `clips.state`**. A trim/GIF/notify job runs against a `ready` clip that stays `ready`; when it
  succeeds it swaps `rendition_key`/`poster_key` (or fills `social_key`) in one UPDATE.
  Every kind but `transcode` is bound by this rule — the `jobs.kind` comment on the CREATE TABLE
  above has the current list (`trim`, `gif`, `notify`, `social`, `replace`, `poster`, `filmstrip`,
  `full`); two are worth detailing here: `notify`
  (§17 #4, shipped — §20 errata 63–67) and `trim` (§17 #5, shipped — §20 errata 68–72: it runs
  against a `ready` clip and commits with `SwapRendition`, ONE UPDATE that leaves `clips.state` alone).
  The rule is enforced in `db`, not by convention: the two
  claims are partitioned by kind (`ClaimJob` takes only `transcode`, `ClaimNonTranscodeJob` the rest —
  erratum 67) and `ClaimJob`, `FailAttempt` and `ReleaseJob` each guard their clip UPDATE with
  `kind = 'transcode'`;
  `CompleteJob` (the generic "job done" a notify uses) and `SwapRendition` (the trim's commit) **refuse**
  a transcode job outright so the coupling can only ever be written by `FinalizeTranscode`; `failAttemptTx` pins a non-transcode
  kind's ATTEMPT cap to its own constant (`db.NotifyMaxAttempts`, `db.TrimMaxAttempts`,
  `db.GIFMaxAttempts`) so `TRANSCODE_MAX_ATTEMPTS` cannot leak into one — while `trim` and `gif` keep
  the instance's `TRANSCODE_MAX_TRANSIENT` for the environment counter, which is nobody's file's fault
  (§20 erratum 89); and
  `orphanedProcessingClips` matches `kind = 'transcode'` so a leftover running `notify` cannot hide
  a `processing` clip from the boot repair. A failed announcement is not a failed clip.

**Job state machine (one row per attempt series)**: `queued` →(ClaimJob)→ `running` →
`done` | `failed`; `running` →(FailAttempt, non-permanent, under its cap)→ `queued` with a
backoff; `running` →(ReleaseJob on graceful shutdown, or `ReconcileOnStartup` for a job whose
`checkpoint_json` is set)→ `queued`, counters unchanged; `queued|running` →(MarkDeleting)→
`cancelled`. Bad endings come in **three classes** (`db.FailKind`):
- `FailPermanent` — the file is at fault (§11 classification) → `failed` immediately, no counter.
- `FailCrash` — panic inside the job, or found `running` at boot **without** a checkpoint
  (reason `interrupted by restart`) → `attempts++`; `run_after = now + min(30s·2^(attempts−1), 10m)`;
  `attempts >= TRANSCODE_MAX_ATTEMPTS` (3) → `failed`.
- `FailTransient` — storage/scratch/DB/io error → `transient_failures++`;
  `run_after = now + min(1m·2^(transient_failures−1), 30m)`; `transient_failures >= TRANSCODE_MAX_TRANSIENT`
  (10) → `failed`.
**Invariant: both counters are incremented in exactly one function, `db.FailAttempt`.** Graceful
shutdown never counts; a checkpointed job interrupted by a crash never counts either (the retry is
finalize-only and cannot be the file's fault). Both caps are finite → no infinite requeue; a storage
outage under ≈2.5 h fails nothing; a crash loop burns at most 3.

**Coupling rule for `kind='transcode'`** (implemented inside `db`, in the same transaction):
`ClaimJob` also sets `clips.state='processing' WHERE state='queued'`; `FailAttempt` sets
`clips.state='queued'` (requeued) or `'failed', failure_reason` (final) `WHERE state='processing'`;
`ReleaseJob` sets `clips.state='queued' WHERE state='processing'`; `FinalizeTranscode` sets
`clips.state='ready'` + all rendition/poster/measured columns `WHERE state='processing'` and
returns whether a row was affected (0 rows = the clip was tombstoned/deleted meanwhile → the
caller deletes its own outputs, §11). `RetryClip` sets clip `queued`, clears `failure_reason`, and
resets the latest transcode job (`queued`, `attempts=0`, `transient_failures=0`, `checkpoint_json=NULL`,
`run_after=now`).

**Views dedupe** is in memory only (§13); the `views` column is the persisted counter.

**Go types (contract; owner A)** — pointer fields for nullable columns:

```go
type User struct { ID, Username, PasswordHash string; CreatedAt int64 }
type Session struct { TokenHash, UserID string; CreatedAt, ExpiresAt, LastSeenAt int64; UserAgent string }
type APIToken struct { ID, UserID, Name, TokenHash, Prefix string; Scopes []string; CreatedAt int64; LastUsedAt, RevokedAt *int64 }
type Clip struct {
    ID, OwnerID, Title, Description string; Unlisted bool
    State string; FailureReason *string
    SourceKey, SourceFilename string; SourceSize int64; SourceContentType, SourceETag string
    RenditionKey *string; RenditionSize *int64; RenditionETag *string
    PosterKey *string; PosterSize *int64; PosterETag *string; PosterWidth, PosterHeight *int
    SocialKey *string; SocialSize *int64; SocialETag *string
    DurationMS *int64; Width, Height, FPSNum, FPSDen *int; HasAudio *bool
    Views int64; TTLSeconds, ExpiresAt *int64
    CreatedAt, UpdatedAt int64; ReadyAt *int64
}
type Job struct {
    ID int64; ClipID, Kind, State, Stage string; Attempts, TransientFailures int; RunAfter int64
    ParamsJSON string; CheckpointJSON *string; LastError *string
    CreatedAt, UpdatedAt int64; StartedAt, FinishedAt *int64
}
```

## 6. Storage key layout

One prefix per clip; delete-all-for-clip is a prefix operation. `P` = `S3_KEY_PREFIX` (empty or
ending in `/`). `{r8}` = 8 random base62 chars generated per **attempt** (`ids.Rand(8)`), so a
retry never overwrites a key a reader could be streaming, and a truncated object from a failed
attempt can never share a key with a servable one.

```
{P}clips/{id}/                                   ← ClipPrefix(P,id); DeletePrefix target
{P}clips/{id}/original/source.{ext}              ← the upload, immutable ("sacred"); ext = SanitizeExt(filename)
{P}clips/{id}/renditions/main-{r8}.mp4           ← the single progressive h264+aac rendition (RenditionKey)
{P}clips/{id}/poster/poster-{r8}.jpg             ← poster JPEG (PosterKey)
{P}clips/{id}/renditions/preview-{r8}.gif        ← on-demand preview GIF (GIFKey, §17 #6; gif_key)
{P}clips/{id}/renditions/social-{r8}.mp4         ← the card's own lower-bitrate mp4 (SocialKey, §17 #3; social_key)
{P}clips/{id}/filmstrip/strip-{r8}.jpg           ← the trim scrubber's sprite sheet (FilmstripKey, §20 erratum 220; filmstrip_key)
{P}clips/{id}/meta/probe.json                    ← {source: ffprobe JSON, output: ffprobe JSON, plan} written at finalize; overwrite OK; never served
later (deferred, same prefix, additive):
{P}clips/{id}/renditions/hls-{r8}/index.m3u8 ... ← if a ladder ever returns
```

Rules:
- `store.KeysFor / RenditionKey / PosterKey / GIFKey / SocialKey / FilmstripKey / ClipPrefix` are the **only** functions that
  build keys for writing. The DB stores the exact keys for reading (`source_key`, `rendition_key`,
  `poster_key`, `social_key`, `gif_key`, `filmstrip_key`), so a future layout change never breaks old clips. Every one
  of them is under the clip prefix, which is why `Destroy` needs no key list at all — and
  `db.KeysOf(clip).Keys()` is the ONE list of them for the callers that do (`admin ls --stat`,
  `admin orphans`).
- `SanitizeExt(filename)`: lowercase extension, `[a-z0-9]{1,8}`, else `bin`. Object
  `Content-Type` for the original = the multipart part's Content-Type if it begins with `video/`
  and is at most 127 bytes (§20 erratum 40), else by extension map (`mp4,m4v→video/mp4; mov→video/quicktime; webm→video/webm; mkv→video/x-matroska;
  avi→video/x-msvideo; ts→video/mp2t`), else `application/octet-stream`.
- Keys never contain user-controlled text except the sanitized extension; slugs are `[A-Za-z0-9]`
  only. Path traversal in keys is therefore impossible by construction (also asserted by a unit test
  that `KeysFor` output matches `^[A-Za-z0-9_./-]+$` and contains no `..`).
- Scratch mirrors the layout: `$SCRATCH_DIR/{id}/source.{ext}`, `$SCRATCH_DIR/{id}/out-{r8}.mp4`,
  `$SCRATCH_DIR/{id}/poster-{r8}.jpg`, `$SCRATCH_DIR/{id}/probe.json`.
- `DeletePrefix(prefix)` = paginated list → `RemoveObjects` in batches ≤1000 → list incomplete
  multipart uploads under the prefix and abort each (`ListIncompleteUploads` + `RemoveIncompleteUpload`)
  → re-list; non-empty → `ErrPrefixNotEmpty`. Incomplete multipart parts are invisible to a plain
  list and billed on R2/B2; aborting them is what makes "prefix empty" true.
- `DeleteKey(key)` = `RemoveObject` on that key + abort its incomplete multipart upload, with **no
  list anywhere in it**; a key that is not there is success. It is what removes an object whose key the
  caller already knows — every cleanup a run does of its own attempt — because a bucket's listing is an
  eventually consistent index and cannot be relied on to show a write of a millisecond ago, while a
  key-addressed request reads the object itself (§20 erratum 305). `DeletePrefix` is for finding
  everything; `DeleteKey` is for removing one thing you just wrote.

## 7. Share ids

**A clip's share URL is `{PUBLIC_BASE_URL}/{id}` — the id at the ROOT of the origin** (§20 erratum
248). `/clips/{id}`, the address until then, answers a permanent redirect to it; `/embed/{id}` and
`/c/{id}` are unchanged. `urls.Builder.Page` is the one renderer of that URL and `LegacyPage` the one
renderer of the old one.

There are **two id grammars**, chosen per upload with an account-wide default (§20 errata 249–250).
Both are minted in `internal/ids`, both are accepted by every `{id}` route, and which one an id is in
is read back off the id itself (`ids.Kind`) — there is no column on `clips`.

- **compact** — THE DEFAULT, and the only grammar before erratum 249. `ids.New()` returns **12
  characters** from the alphabet `A–Z a–z 0–9` (62 symbols, ≈71.4 bits), generated with `crypto/rand`
  using rejection sampling (draw a byte, accept if `< 248`, take `b % 62`) so the distribution is
  unbiased. Slugs are URL-safe without encoding and case-sensitive (SQLite TEXT PK compares byte-wise;
  `COLLATE NOCASE` is **not** applied to `clips.id`). It needs no rate limit of any kind.
- **memorable** — `ids.NewMemorable(n)` returns **n words** from the curated EFF long word list, each
  capitalised and joined without separators (`PurpleUpdateCharacter`), drawn from the same
  `crypto/rand` with the same rejection rule one width up (a two-byte draw, accepted below the largest
  multiple of the list length that fits in 16 bits). The list ships in the binary
  (`internal/ids/eff_large_wordlist.txt`, `go:embed`), curated by `^[a-z]{3,9}$` — which drops the four
  hyphenated entries of the published 7,776 and leaves **7,772**: **≈38.8 bits** for three words and
  **≈51.7** for four. **n is 3 for a listed clip and 4 when the clip is uploaded UNLISTED**, where the
  link is the only authentication (the owner's decision of 2026-09-09: three words are public-clip grade, four
  are unlisted grade). Word list: EFF large wordlist, CC BY 3.0 — credited in the package doc and beside
  the control on `/settings`; there is no LICENSE file in this repository.
- `ids.Valid(s)` is the UNION: `^[A-Za-z0-9]{12}$` OR `^(?:[A-Z][a-z]{2,8}){3,4}$`, scanned rather
  than matched (no regexp, no allocation). Every `{id}` route checks it first and answers 404 (JSON or
  page) on mismatch before touching the DB — this is also the cheapest scan defense — and both scratch
  janitors use it to tell a clip's working directory from anything else on the disk. The `.upload-{id}`
  spool stays outside it on its leading dot, exactly as before.
- **No minted id can equal a route.** `ids.Reserved` is the first path segment of every route the app
  registers, in ONE place: `ids.New` and `ids.NewMemorable` put back any draw that equals one
  (case-insensitively), and `internal/web`'s and `internal/httpapi`'s router tests walk the patterns
  their mux actually registered and fail when a segment is missing from that list. Neither grammar can
  reach the check with today's routes; it exists so "an id is never a route" is a property.
- **The two grammars overlap** on strings that are both twelve base62 characters and three or four
  capitalised words (about one draw in 3,000), so `ids.New` also puts those back — which makes
  `ids.Kind` exact for every id this build mints.
- Collision handling: the chance that a fresh id equals one of N existing ids is N/62¹² for compact
  (~10⁻¹⁵ at ten thousand clips) and N/7,772³ for three words (~2 × 10⁻⁸ at ten thousand clips — a
  once-in-fifty-million-uploads event, not a per-upload constant), but the code still handles it, for BOTH grammars: ingest picks
  the id before writing to the bucket (the key contains it) and calls `db.ClipExists(id)` first; if it
  exists, pick another (loop ≤3). If the final `INSERT` still hits `UNIQUE`, ingest deletes the
  just-written prefix, removes scratch, and answers 500 `id_collision` — the client simply retries.
  Users, tokens and collections use `ids.New` (their ids are internal or `/c/`-prefixed; collisions
  there are handled by the `UNIQUE` constraint → retry once).
- The id is minted AFTER the upload's `unlisted` is resolved, because the word count depends on it. A
  clip flipped to unlisted LATER keeps the id it has: an id is an address, and every link already sent
  names it (§20 erratum 251).
- The slug is the public id everywhere: URL path, JSON `id`, storage prefix, scratch dir. There is
  no separate integer id, so there is nothing to leak and nothing to re-salt.

## 8. API contract

**Conventions**
- JSON responses: `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8`. Timestamps RFC3339 UTC.
- Error envelope everywhere (also for 404/405/413/429/5xx produced by our handlers):
  `{"error":"snake_code","message":"human text"}`. Codes are stable identifiers listed per route.
- `{id}` path params must satisfy `ids.Valid` → else 404 `not_found` immediately.
- Auth column: `–` public; `user` = session cookie **or** `Authorization: Bearer ck_…` (token needs
  scope `upload` for uploads; any valid token for `me`); `session` = cookie only (tokens get
  403 `token_not_allowed`); `owner` = `user` whose id equals `clips.owner_id` (else 403 `forbidden`;
  unknown clip → 404 before the ownership check, so existence is not leaked... the id is public
  anyway).
- CSRF (§15): applies to cookie-authenticated mutating requests only.
- Rate limiting (§14): `429 rate_limited` + `Retry-After` seconds.
- DB unreachable on any route → `503 unavailable` + `Retry-After: 5`; storage unreachable where
  storage is needed → `503 storage_unavailable`. **Never** 404 for a backend failure.
- `http.Server`: `ReadHeaderTimeout 10s`, `IdleTimeout 120s`, **no** `ReadTimeout`/`WriteTimeout`
  (uploads and media streams must not be cut). `http.TimeoutHandler(15s)` wraps ONLY the JSON
  auth/clips/tokens/progress/view/health routes — the HTML pages are bounded by `SSR_TIMEOUT` on
  their HANDLER's DB read instead (§20 erratum 45; the auth Resolver's session lookup runs before the
  handler on the request context, there as on every `long` route) — never upload, never media,
  never `DELETE /api/clips/{id}` (it runs `Destroy` inline for up to 60s, §12), never anything that
  streams (it buffers and disables `Flusher`). No long-polling exists or may be added under it. The
  one handler that deliberately blocks — `POST /api/upload`'s ready wait, at most 60s (§20 erratum 97)
  — is on a `long` route for exactly that reason, and ends on client disconnect as well as on its
  own budget.
- Log levels (§12 doctrine): a green E2E run has **zero** `ERROR` lines, so handlers log expected
  conditions (client disconnects, cancellations, transient storage errors) at INFO/WARN only.

### 8.1 Route table

| Method & path | Auth | Request | Success | Errors |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /healthz` | – | – | 200 `{"ok":true,"version":"…","ffmpeg":"7.1.1","db":"ok","storage":"pending"\|"ok"\|"error: …","queue":{"queued":n,"running":n,"failed_24h":n,"oldest_queued_age_s":n,"longest_running_age_s":n},"uptime_s":n}` — `storage` is the **cached** last-Ping result (§8.7), never a live call. The last three `queue` fields are additive (§20 erratum 145): counts and ages in seconds only, never anything that names a clip, a user or a configured value. `repair` (§20 erratum 231) is the same shape once more — `{repaired,released,requeued,failed,errors}`, the automatic stuck-job repair’s lifetime counts, omitted when nothing is wired and never carrying `JOBS_UNSTICK_AFTER` itself | 500 `{"ok":false,"db":"error: …"}` only when DB ping fails |
| `GET /readyz` | – | – | 200 `{"ok":true}` when DB ping ok AND a **live** `store.Ping` (2s) ok | 503 `{"ok":false,"db":"ok","storage":"pending"\|"error: …"}` |
| `POST /api/auth/register` | – (rate: auth) | `{"username","password"}` | 201 `{"user":UserDTO}` + `Set-Cookie` | 400 `invalid_request` (username `^[A-Za-z0-9_]{3,32}$`, password 8–72 bytes); 403 `registration_closed`; 409 `username_taken`; 415 `unsupported_media_type` (non-JSON) |
| `POST /api/auth/login` | – (rate: auth) | `{"username","password"}` | 200 `{"user":UserDTO}` + `Set-Cookie` | 400; 401 `invalid_credentials` (same for unknown user; constant-time dummy bcrypt) |
| `POST /api/auth/logout` | session | – | 204, cookie cleared, session row deleted | 401 |
| `GET /api/auth/me` | user | – | 200 `{"user":UserDTO,"via":"session"\|"token"}` | 401 `unauthorized` |
| `PATCH /api/auth/password` (§20 erratum 108) | session (rate: auth) | `{"current_password","new_password"}` | 200 `{"sessions_revoked":n}` — the bcrypt hash is rotated and every OTHER session of the user deleted in ONE transaction; the caller's own session survives | 400 `invalid_request` (either field empty, `new_password` outside 8–72 bytes, or equal to the current one); 401 `unauthorized`; 401 `invalid_credentials` (wrong `current_password`); 403 `token_not_allowed`; 403 `csrf`; 415; 429 `rate_limited` |
| `GET /api/auth/sessions` (§20 erratum 107) | session | – | 200 `{"sessions":[SessionDTO]}` — the caller's LIVE sessions, newest first, `private, no-store` + `Vary: Cookie` | 401; 403 `token_not_allowed` |
| `DELETE /api/auth/sessions` (§20 erratum 107) | session | – | 200 `{"sessions_revoked":n}` — "log out everywhere but here": every session of the user except the one making the request | 401; 403 `token_not_allowed`; 403 `csrf` |
| `GET /api/auth/me/settings` (ROADMAP #22 and #35 — §20 errata 155, 250) | session (a token → 403 `token_not_allowed`, erratum 19) | – | 200 `{"default_ttl_days":null\|0\|1\|7\|30\|90,"default_unlisted":false,"default_link_style":"compact"\|"memorable","instance_default_ttl_days":0}` — the account's upload defaults. `default_ttl_days` is `null` for "no preference, follow `DEFAULT_CLIP_TTL`" and `0` for "this account chose keep-forever": different answers, different values. `default_link_style` is the opposite shape and has NO null: migration 0015's column is NOT NULL DEFAULT `compact` and there is no instance knob for a null to defer to; `private, no-store` | 401; 403 |
| `PATCH /api/auth/me/settings` (ROADMAP #22, #35) | session | `{"default_ttl_days":null\|0\|1\|7\|30\|90,"default_unlisted":bool,"default_link_style":"compact"\|"memorable"}` — every key optional, an ABSENT key leaves that preference alone and an explicit `null` CLEARS the TTL one (a `null` `default_link_style` reads as absent: there is no third state for it to mean) | 200 the same body | 400 `invalid_ttl` (outside the closed set, or not a number); **400 `invalid_link_style`** (§20 erratum 250); 401; 403; 415 |
| `GET /api/auth/me/stats` (ROADMAP #23 — §20 erratum 156) | session | – | 200 `{"clips","ready","collections","bytes_source","bytes_renditions","bytes_total","views_total","expiring_7d"}` — the CALLER's own tally, derived at read time, tombstones excluded. There is no `{user}` form of this route and never will be; `private, no-store` | 401; 403 |
| `POST /api/auth/tokens` | session | `{"name":"ShareX on desktop"}` (1–64 chars), optional `"scopes":["upload"\|"read"]` (§20 erratum 111; absent/null = `["upload"]`, `[]` is a 400) | 201 `{"id","name","prefix","scopes","token":"ck_…","created_at","sxcu":{…}\|null}` — raw token shown **once**; `sxcu` is the ready-to-import ShareX file (§20 erratum 59) and is **null for a token without the `upload` scope** | 400 `invalid_request` (name, or a scope outside the closed set); 401; 403 `token_not_allowed` |
| `GET /api/auth/tokens` | session | – | 200 `{"tokens":[{"id","name","prefix","scopes","created_at","last_used_at"\|null}]}` (revoked omitted) | 401 |

### 8.2 DTOs and the TTL wire format

```json
UserDTO  {"id":"…","username":"alice","created_at":"2026-08-31T23:59:00Z"}

SessionDTO {                             // ROADMAP #1, §20 erratum 107 — GET /api/auth/sessions only
  "created_at":"…","last_seen_at":"…","expires_at":"…",
  "current":true,                        // is this the session making the request?
  "user_agent":"Mozilla/5.0 …"          // what that browser sent, stored capped at 256 bytes
}                                        // NO id and no handle of any kind: see erratum 107

ClipDTO {
  "id":"aZ3kQ9xB2mLp","title":"…","description":"…","unlisted":false,
  "state":"queued|processing|ready|failed","failure_reason":null|"…",
  "views":3,                            // OWNER ONLY: key absent for every other caller (anti-feature: view counts are private)
  "source_duration_ms":30000,           // OWNER ONLY (§20 erratum 68): the ORIGINAL's length, the timeline every trim window is on
  "trim":{"start_ms":5000,"end_ms":9000}, // OWNER ONLY: the window this rendition was cut from; key absent when it is the whole original
  "tags":["clutch","gaming"],           // ALWAYS present, sorted, [] when none (never null); NOT owner-private (§20 erratum 81)
  "created_at":"…","updated_at":"…","ready_at":null|"…",
  "ttl_days":0|1|7|30|90,               // 0 = never (never null on output)
  "expires_at":null|"…",                // null = never
  "duration_ms":6000|null,"width":1280|null,"height":720|null,"fps":"30/1"|null,"has_audio":true|null,
  "poster":{"width":1280,"height":720}|null,
  "gif_url":null|"…/api/clips/{id}/preview.gif",   // null until a preview has been generated (§17 #6)
  "filmstrip":null|{"url":"…","tiles":24,"tile_width":160,"tile_height":90,"interval_ms":250}, // §20 erratum 220: null until made for the CURRENT rendition
  "source":{"filename":"clip.mp4","size":1234567,"content_type":"video/mp4"},
  "owner":{"id":"…","username":"alice"},
  "urls":{"page":"…/clips/{id}","embed":"…/embed/{id}","video":"…/api/clips/{id}/video.mp4",
          "social":"…/api/clips/{id}/social.mp4","light":"…/api/clips/{id}/light.mp4",
          "original":"…/api/clips/{id}/original","poster":"…/api/clips/{id}/poster.jpg",
          "progress":"…/api/clips/{id}/progress"},
  "tiers":[{"tier":"original|full|light","url":null|"…","width":null|1280,"height":null|720,
            "fps":null|"30/1","bytes":null|1234567,"codec":""|"h264",
            "playable":true|false,"state":"skipped|encoding|ready|failed|pending"},…], // ALWAYS 3 entries, best first (§20 erratum 205)
  "card_tier":"original|full|light|""     // which tier a crawler is actually served; "" for a clip that is not ready (DEPLOY.md §27)
}

CollectionDTO {                          // §17 #9, §20 erratum 82
  "id":"CoLLeCtIoN12","title":"Best of 2026",
  "url":"…/c/{id}",                      // absolute, from PUBLIC_BASE_URL: the link that is pasted
  "clip_count":2,                        // live members (a `deleting` tombstone is already gone everywhere else)
```
