(§20 erratum 300 (d)). The ORDER BY puts the untimed `deleting` tombstones LAST (§20 erratum 101).
(b) includes `queued` because nothing is in flight. (c) is the **grace period** (`SWEEP_GRACE`, 1h):
a clip mid-encode at its expiry gets up to an hour to finish; a clip stuck in `processing` because of
a crash is swept regardless once grace elapses (`ReconcileOnStartup` normally requeues it first, but
the rule holds even if reconciliation never ran). Since `Cancel` is safe, grace is a courtesy, not a
correctness need.

**`lifecycle.Destroy(ctx, deps, clipID)`** — used by the sweeper and by owner `DELETE`:
1. `db.MarkDeleting(id)`: `UPDATE clips SET state='deleting'`, `UPDATE jobs SET state='cancelled' WHERE
   clip_id=? AND state IN ('queued','running')`. `ErrNotFound` → already gone → return ok.
2. `worker.Cancel(ctx, id)` — waits, bounded by ctx, until the goroutine (if any) has exited (§10.1).
   `false` (ctx ended first) ends the sequence here with `lifecycle.ErrStillRunning`: nothing below runs,
   the `deleting` tombstone is all this call leaves, and rule (a) resumes it next tick (§20 erratum 300 (b)).
   A run that exits here has already removed, **by key**, every object its attempt wrote — including one
   whose `PutFile` this cancellation cut off, which the bucket may have committed anyway (§20 erratum 305).
3. `store.DeletePrefix(ClipPrefix(P,id))` — objects, then incomplete multipart uploads, then re-list
   must be empty (§6). Error → return it (row stays `deleting`, retried next tick; public routes 404).
   This step is LIST-driven and removes what the clip has **had**; it is not what removes what a run was
   writing an instant ago, because a listing is an index that lags (§20 erratum 305).
4. `db.DeleteClipRow(id)` (`WHERE state='deleting'`; **jobs, tags and collection memberships cascade** —
   `jobs`, `clip_tags` and `collection_clips` all carry `REFERENCES clips(id) ON DELETE CASCADE`, and
   `PRAGMA foreign_keys(1)` is in the DSN of BOTH pools, so this one DELETE is the whole story: a swept or
   owner-deleted clip leaves no tag rows and no membership rows behind, and drops out of every collection
   it was in without the sweeper knowing collections exist. The COLLECTIONS themselves are untouched — a
   list is not its links, §20 erratum 82). Error → return it (objects are
   gone; next tick re-lists an empty prefix and deletes the row — self-heals to no orphans).
5. `os.RemoveAll($SCRATCH_DIR/{id})` best-effort; `worker.Forget(id)` evicts the progress entry (and
   voids the clip's registered run, if one is still exiting, so it cannot write the entry back — §20
   erratum 49).

Objects are always removed **before** the row: a surviving row is a surviving pointer, so the system
converges to "no orphaned objects". A crash between 3 and 4 leaves a tombstone that rule (a) finishes.

**A candidate whose `Destroy` fails is backed off per clip** — `2m·2^(n−1)` capped at an hour, a free first
retry, two repeatedly-failing candidates a tick (§20 erratum 101(a)) — and that schedule is now WRITTEN DOWN
(`sweep_failures`, migration 0013, §20 erratum 232): one row per failing clip, read back once at the first
tick, deleted when a Destroy finally goes through, and removed with the clip by its foreign key. A crash loop
therefore cannot reset the schedule and hammer a black-holing prefix, which is the one case the "a restart
plausibly fixes storage" argument does not cover.

**Logging**: every tick logs `sweep checked=N destroyed=N failed=N dur=…` at INFO when `checked>0`
(DEBUG otherwise); every Destroy logs `destroy clip=… objects=N ok|err=… dur=…` (INFO on ok, WARN on a
storage error — it will be retried). Counters `sweep_destroyed_total`, `sweep_errors_total` are exposed
in `/healthz`.

**Log-level doctrine (process-wide; E2E step 16 fails on any `ERROR` line, so this is binding)**:
- **INFO** — every *expected* outcome, including the ones that look dramatic: cancellation-derived events
  (`reason=cancelled|shutdown`, a `PutFile` or ffmpeg aborted by `Cancel`/`Stop`, `lost_race`, a client
  disconnect mid-upload or mid-stream, `context.Canceled` anywhere), sweep/destroy successes, job
  state transitions, permanent transcode failures (`clip failed reason=…` — a bad file is a normal input).
- **WARN** — transient/environment trouble that the system retries or degrades around: any storage error
  (boot ping failures, `storage unreachable; serving degraded`, `storage_read_error` on media,
  `FailTransient` requeues, sweeper Destroy errors), scratch `RemoveAll` failures, `SQLITE_BUSY` retries.
- **ERROR** — only conditions the design says cannot happen or that need a human: panics (recovered or
  not), DB errors outside `busy_timeout`, row/object drift (`store.ErrNotFound` for a key the DB
  references), `bad_output` verify mismatch on our own encoder output, migration failures, `FinalizeTranscode`
  giving up after its retries, invariant violations (e.g. a `ready` row with NULL keys).
Handlers annotate the access log rather than emitting their own ERROR lines (`httpx.SetLogField`, §18.1).

**Also on each tick**: `db.DeleteExpiredSessions(now)`; scratch janitor every 10th tick — remove
`$SCRATCH_DIR/*` dirs whose clip row is missing, or whose clip is in `ready|failed|deleting` **and has
no `queued`/`running` job and no run registered in this process** (a trim and a gif work in that dir
while their clip is `ready` the whole time — `db.HasLiveJob` + `worker.Busy`, §20 erratum 89), or whose
mtime is older than 24h and whose clip is not `processing`.

**Boot** (`ReconcileOnStartup`, before the listener opens, §8.7): every `running` job **with**
`checkpoint_json` set → `ReleaseJob` (→ `queued`, `run_after=now`, **no counter touched** — outputs are
complete, only finalize remains); every `running` job **without** a checkpoint →
`FailAttempt(interrupted by restart, FailCrash)` (→ `queued` with the crash backoff, or `failed` at the
cap of 3); clips left `processing` with no `running` job → `queued`; expired sessions deleted; the
janitor runs once. Returns `(released, requeued, failed)`. Then the first sweep 10s later handles any
`deleting` tombstones.

**Owner `DELETE`** (`httpapi/clip_handlers.go`, **not** under `TimeoutHandler`, §8): after the 404/403
checks the handler builds `ctx := context.WithTimeout(context.WithoutCancel(r.Context()), 60s)` —
**detached from the client connection** so a dropped connection cannot abandon a half-run `Destroy`
(tombstone set, objects half-deleted; the sweeper would finish it anyway, but the handler must not
race it) — and runs `Destroy(ctx, …)`. `Result.RowDeleted` → 204. Any error, including
`context.DeadlineExceeded` from a slow storage backend (a single `STORAGE_OP_TIMEOUT` call is 30s, so
two slow calls exceed the budget) → 202 `{"state":"deleting"}`; the tombstone is already set, so every
public route 404s immediately and the sweeper finishes within a tick.

## 13. View counting (`internal/views`, `internal/clientip`)

- **Dedupe key**: `views.Key(clipID, ip) = clipID + "|" + hex(sha256(ip.String()))[:16]` — the ADDRESS
  alone (§20 erratum 103). The User-Agent used to be in it, so that two people behind one NAT each
  counted; but the header is written by the caller, so three POSTs from one address with three invented
  User-Agents counted three views and any link holder could run the owner's private counter up at the
  view limiter's 60/min. The count is bounded by addresses now, which a caller cannot mint; the price is
  the NAT case, and that is the right side to be wrong on for a number whose only job is to tell its
  owner roughly how a clip did.
- **Window**: `VIEW_DEDUPE_TTL` (30m). `Deduper.Seen(key, now) bool` returns true (and does not count) if
  the key is present and unexpired; otherwise records `expiry = now + ttl` and returns false (count it).
- **Bounded memory (hard cap, not just idle eviction)**: `map[string]int64` + a FIFO ring of `(key, expiry)`
  in insertion order. On every insert: pop expired heads; if `len(map) >= VIEW_DEDUPE_MAX` (50,000) pop
  heads until below the cap **even if unexpired** (oldest first). Worst case ≈ 50k × ~80 B ≈ 4 MiB. A
  scanner can therefore only shorten the dedupe window for the oldest entries, never grow memory.
- **Client IP** (`clientip.Resolve(r, trusted)`): parse `RemoteAddr`; if it is inside one of the
  `TRUSTED_PROXIES` prefixes: use `X-Real-IP` if present and parseable, else walk `X-Forwarded-For` from
  the **right**, skipping addresses inside trusted prefixes, taking the first untrusted one; if nothing
  usable, fall back to `RemoteAddr`. If `RemoteAddr` is not trusted, headers are **ignored** (default:
  trust nothing → the compose network's proxy-less setup counts each `RemoteAddr`; Phase 3 sets
  `TRUSTED_PROXIES` for cloudflared / a reverse proxy so all viewers do not collapse to one IP).
- Only the player's first `play` triggers `POST /view` (§8.6) — unfurl fetches and page loads never count.
- The same `Resolve` feeds the rate limiter.

## 14. Auth, sessions, API tokens, rate limiting hooks

**Registration**: `REGISTRATION=first` (default; §20 erratum 106) — accepted only while the `users`
table is EMPTY, so the first account bootstraps the instance and the door closes behind it.
`open` and `closed` are the two constants; `clippet admin users create` adds an account under any
of the three. The mode is resolved per request (one `COUNT(*)`, never cached) and is on the boot line. Username `^[A-Za-z0-9_]{3,32}$`,
unique case-insensitively (`COLLATE NOCASE`); password 8–72 **bytes** (bcrypt truncation guard);
`bcrypt.GenerateFromPassword(cost 12)`. Login failure for unknown users runs a dummy bcrypt compare so
timing does not reveal existence; both paths → 401 `invalid_credentials`.

**Sessions**: 32 random bytes → base64url (43 chars) is the cookie value; the DB stores hex `sha256`.
Cookie: `Name=SESSION_COOKIE_NAME; Path=/; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Max-Age=SESSION_TTL; Secure` iff
`urls.IsHTTPS()`. `GetSession` rejects expired rows; `TouchSession` extends `expires_at = now + TTL` and
`last_seen_at` at most once per minute per session (in-memory last-touch map, bounded 10k), **clamped to
`max_expires_at`** — a column fixed at creation to `created_at + SESSION_MAX_TTL` (90 days) that a touch
never moves, so an actively used cookie still dies on a schedule its holder cannot extend (§20
erratum 105). `GetSession` refuses a row past either bound, and the re-issued cookie's `Max-Age` is the
row's REMAINING life, not a fresh `SESSION_TTL`. Logout deletes the row and clears the cookie. Expired
rows pruned by the sweeper tick. `GET /api/auth/sessions` lists the caller's live sessions and
`DELETE /api/auth/sessions` ends every one but the caller's; `PATCH /api/auth/password` rotates the
bcrypt hash and sweeps the others in the same transaction (§20 errata 107–108).

**API tokens** (model ships in Phase 1; the capture-tool endpoint that consumes them ships in Phase 4):
`ids.Token()` = `"ck_" + base64url(32 random bytes)` (46 chars total); DB stores hex `sha256`, `prefix` =
first 8 chars after `ck_` for display, `scopes` default `upload`. The closed scope set is
**`upload` | `read`** (§20 erratum 111): `upload` is erratum 19's capture credential, `read` adds
`GET /api/clips` and `GET /api/collections` and unlocks the owner-private DTO fields of the caller's
own rows (erratum 112) — and nothing else. A mint with no `scopes` key is `["upload"]`; an empty array
is a 400. `auth.RequireSessionOrScope(scope)` is RequireSession widened by exactly one scope, and its
refusal keeps erratum 19's `token_not_allowed` code. Minted only from a **session**
(`POST /api/auth/tokens`), shown once; listed/revoked via session only; `last_used_at` bumped at most
once per minute. Revocation = `revoked_at` set; `GetTokenByHash` excludes revoked. Tokens are accepted
via `Authorization: Bearer ck_…` on `GET /api/auth/me` and `POST /api/clips` in Phase 1, and on
`POST /api/upload` in Phase 4. `RequireScope("upload")` guards upload routes now so later read-only
tokens need no migration.

**Middleware** (`auth.Resolver.Middleware`): resolves the Bearer token first (if present and valid),
else the cookie; stores `Principal{User, Via: "session"|"token", SessionHash, TokenID, Scopes}` in ctx
via `auth.WithPrincipal`; never rejects by itself. Field population is exact per `Via`:
`Via="session"` → `SessionHash` = hex sha256 of the cookie value, `TokenID=""`, `Scopes=nil` (a session
implicitly holds every scope; `RequireScope` passes); `Via="token"` → `TokenID` = `api_tokens.id`,
`SessionHash=""`, `Scopes` = the token's parsed scope list. `RequireUser` → 401 `unauthorized`;
`RequireSession` → 401, or 403 `token_not_allowed` when `Via=token`; `RequireScope(s)` → 403
`insufficient_scope` only for `Via=token` lacking `s`; `RequireOwner` is done inside clip handlers after
the 404 check.

**Sign in with Discord** (ROADMAP #44, §20 erratum 302): an OPTIONAL second key to an existing account, never a door. With
`DISCORD_LOGIN_CLIENT_ID`/`_SECRET` set, `GET /api/auth/discord/start` mints a browser-side flow cookie (the session cookie's
name plus `_discord`, so it inherits `__Host-`; `Path=/; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Secure iff https; Max-Age=600`) whose nonce is
the PKCE verifier and from which `state` and `code_challenge` are derived, and 302s to Discord's authorize URL with
`scope=identify`. `GET /api/auth/discord/callback` clears that cookie first (single-use: a replay is refused with no outbound
call), checks `state` in constant time, exchanges the code through `internal/notify` (the token endpoint and `users/@me`, the
secret scrubbed from any error), and issues **the same session `POST /api/auth/login` issues** for the account whose
`users.discord_user_id` matches — or creates nothing and lands on `/login?discord=unlinked`. Linking is `POST /api/auth/discord`
with the CURRENT PASSWORD (session + CSRF + JSON, the `auth` bucket) and the same callback in link mode; unlinking is `DELETE
/api/auth/discord` (session + CSRF). A Discord-issued session is indistinguishable from a password-issued one on purpose.

**CSRF stance** (resolves the judge concern about curl with a cookie jar): `SameSite=Lax` already blocks
cross-site POST cookie inclusion in modern browsers; the explicit check adds defense-in-depth **without
breaking non-browser clients**. For requests authenticated **by cookie** with method
`POST|PATCH|DELETE|PUT`: reject 403 `csrf` **only if** (`Origin` header is present AND its
scheme+host+port ≠ `urls.Origin()`) **or** (`Sec-Fetch-Site` is present AND equals `cross-site`).
Requests with neither header (curl, the E2E cookie jar) pass. Bearer-authenticated requests skip the
check entirely. JSON endpoints additionally require `Content-Type: application/json` (415 otherwise),
which HTML forms cannot send cross-origin without a CORS preflight. No CORS headers are emitted
(same-origin app), so browsers cannot read cross-origin responses.

**Rate limiting hooks** (`internal/ratelimit`): `Limiter{rate, burst, maxKeys}` holds
`map[key]*rate.Limiter` (`golang.org/x/time/rate`) with `lastSeen`; a janitor every minute evicts keys
idle > 10 minutes; **hard cap** `RATE_LIMIT_MAX_KEYS` (10,000) — at cap, evict the least-recently-seen
key before inserting (so a scan cannot grow memory). `Middleware(limiter, keyFn)` → 429 `rate_limited`
+ `Retry-After: <ceil seconds>`. Phase 1 wiring: `auth` limiter (`RATE_AUTH_PER_MIN`, key = client IP)
on register/login — and, since §20 erratum 108, on `PATCH /api/auth/password`, which takes a password and
runs a bcrypt compare, so it belongs in the same per-IP bucket rather than in a per-user budget a thief
holding the cookie already owns; `upload` limiter (`RATE_UPLOAD_PER_HOUR`, key = user id) on `POST /api/clips` — and,
since Phase 4, on `POST /api/upload` (erratum 58), `POST …/trim` (erratum 68) and `POST …/gif`
(erratum 75), every route that can queue work; `view` limiter (60/min, key = client IP) on
`POST …/view`, on `GET …/preview.gif` (erratum 75) and on `GET /api/collections/{cid}` (erratum 87).
**The two UPLOAD routes carry a second bucket** (`RATE_UPLOAD_PER_HOUR_PER_IP`, 120, key = client IP)
and an upload must satisfy BOTH (§20 erratum 97): the user-keyed budget bounds an *account*, and
accounts are free — `POST /api/auth/register` is held only by the auth limiter at 10/min/IP, so one
address can mint hundreds an hour, each carrying its own 60 uploads. The user bucket is listed first
so a caller over their own budget is refused without spending an address token. The trim and gif
routes keep the user-keyed limiter alone: they act on a clip that already exists and belongs to the
caller. Phase 2 tunes values, adds per-token limits and a global concurrent-upload cap; the middleware
and key functions are the hook.

---

## 15. Security posture

- **Zero telemetry / call-home**: the binary makes outbound connections only to `S3_ENDPOINT` and to what
  the operator turns on below — no outbound connection but the bucket's and the ones you set. The first:
  when the operator sets `DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL`, Discord — one of four allowlisted hosts on an `https`
  webhook path, validated at boot (§4, §20 erratum 63), never followed through a redirect. Unset (the
  default) there is **no outbound HTTP whatsoever**: no client is constructed and no `notify` job is
  enqueued. The Discord **bot** (ROADMAP #33, §20 errata 253–254) is the second, equally opt-in
  outbound feature: with `DISCORD_APP_ID`/`DISCORD_PUBLIC_KEY`/
  `DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN` set it calls `discord.com` (a host the webhook allowlist already names — the
  follow-up edit and the command registration) and fetches attachments from `cdn.discordapp.com` and
  `media.discordapp.net`, the closed set in `internal/config`'s `discordCDNHosts`. An attachment URL
  arrives in a request rather than in `.env`, so it is held to that allowlist before a socket is
  opened: "fetch what the interaction names" would be the server-side request forger ROADMAP refused
  "upload via URL" for. **Sign in with Discord** (ROADMAP #44, §20 erratum 302; `DISCORD_LOGIN_CLIENT_ID`/`_SECRET`) is the
  third opt-in outbound feature and adds NO host: two more paths on `discord.com` (the OAuth token endpoint and `users/@me`),
  through the same single construction function, never following a redirect. **The clip webhook** (ROADMAP #54, §20 erratum 319; `CLIP_WEBHOOK_URL` + `CLIP_WEBHOOK_SECRET`) is the fourth opt-in outbound feature and the only one whose destination is not on an allowlist: ONE URL the operator names in `.env`, `http` or `https`, through the same single construction function, never following a redirect. Unset (the default) nothing is built for it and no `hook` job is enqueued. No update checks, no analytics, no fonts/CDN, no third-party scripts. Two grep-level stages
  in `check.sh` keep this checkable rather than merely stated: no `http(s)://` literal outside tests and
  docs (§20 erratum 27), and no HTTP client, transport, request or dialer constructed outside
  `internal/notify` (§20 erratum 66). Both are **tripwires over the common call sites, not proofs** —
  the guarantee is the host allowlist in `internal/config` and the single construction site in
  `serve.go`; the greps are what makes a *second* one fail CI instead of passing unnoticed. Neither
  grep can see the **second potential egress path**, which is not a Go call site at all: `ffmpeg` and
  `ffprobe` are subprocesses, and a demuxer opens whatever its INPUT names — an HLS playlist's
  `http://` segment, a DASH manifest's, an ffconcat script's. That path is pinned by **our own**
  `-protocol_whitelist file` immediately in front of every `-i` (and in front of every ffprobe input
  path), rendered by `inputArgs`/`probeInputArgs` in `internal/transcode/exec.go` so a new argv builder
  cannot forget it, and backed by the container allowlist at the ingest gate (§8.3) which refuses those
  formats outright. The binary's own default (`file,crypto,data`) happens to agree today, but a vendor
  default is the vendor's to change on the next bump. A third `check.sh` stage is the tripwire for it:
  a non-test file under `internal/transcode` that spells an `-i` of its own must also name a whitelist
  (§20 erratum 91). **`MEDIA_DELIVERY=redirect` adds no destination to that list** (§20 erratum 278):
  a SigV4 query signature is local HMAC over the request line, minio-go contacts nothing to produce
  one (the region is pinned from configuration precisely so nothing is probed), and the second client
  a distinct `MEDIA_PRESIGN_ENDPOINT` builds exists only to carry the host that gets signed. What
  changes is not the app's egress but the VIEWER's: their client fetches the media from the bucket
  vendor instead of from this app, so the vendor sees their address — the privacy consequence, which
  DEPLOY §33 states plainly beside the recipe.
- **No CTAs / watermarks / tiers / social layer**: watch pages render the clip and nothing else (§9;
  amended for one wordmark each by §20 errata 244 and 246);
  limits are operator env vars, never per-user tiers; **view counts are private** — emitted only to the
  clip's owner (DTO `views` omitted otherwise; never on the anonymous share page or the embed, §8.2/§9.1).
- **No inline CSS/JS**: CSP `script-src 'self'; style-src 'self'` with no `'unsafe-inline'`; templates
  contain no `<script>`/`<style>` bodies and no `style=`/`on*=` attributes (asserted by tests, §16).
- **Cookies**: `HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Secure` (https); opaque random value; hashed at rest.
- **CSRF**: §14 rule. **CORS**: none.
- **Headers**: `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` everywhere; `X-Frame-Options: DENY` + CSP
  `frame-ancestors 'none'` on every page except `/embed/{id}` (`frame-ancestors *`, no XFO);
  `object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'self'` on both variants — the directives `default-src`
  does not cover, two of which have no fallback at all, so an injected `<base>` could otherwise have
  repointed every relative URL on the page and a rewritten form action could have posted the login
  off-origin (§20 erratum 94); `Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains` when and
  only when `urls.IsHTTPS()`, no `preload`;
  `Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin`; `Cache-Control: no-store` on all auth/token
  responses and on 503 pages.
- **Upload limits**: `MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES` via `MaxBytesReader` (413), metadata part ≤16 KiB, title/description
  length caps, scratch free-space precheck (507), ffprobe gate (415) so garbage never reaches the bucket.
  No global `ReadTimeout` (would cut large uploads); `ReadHeaderTimeout` guards slowloris on headers only.
- **Content-type discipline**: media routes set `Content-Type` from the DB (`video/mp4`, `image/jpeg`,
  original's stored type) + `nosniff`; the original's stored type is derived server-side (§6), never
  trusted blindly; the `original` route is owner-only and `attachment`.
- **Path traversal**: slugs are `[A-Za-z0-9]{12}`, extensions `[a-z0-9]{1,8}`, keys are built only by
  `store.keys.go`; scratch paths are `filepath.Join(SCRATCH_DIR, id, fixedName)`. `/static/` serves from
  `embed.FS` (no filesystem traversal possible).
- **Secrets**: `S3_SECRET_KEY`, passwords, raw tokens never logged; `/healthz` exposes no config
  values **beyond the storage backend's name, which is one of two words** (`s3` / `fs`, §20 erratum
  276): it names no endpoint, bucket, path, credential or directory, and it is the one fact an
  anonymous prober cannot otherwise establish about an instance whose storage is unwell. That is a
  deliberate amendment to the older absolute wording, made when the second backend shipped — a
  promise an operator cannot check is worse than a narrower one they can.
- **Process**: non-root uid 10001; static binary; ffmpeg invoked via argv (no shell); `-nostdin`.
- **Slug enumeration**: 71 bits of entropy + immediate 404 on malformed ids + the `view` rate limit.
  Accepted: no per-IP limit on `GET /api/clips/{id}` (crawlers must be able to fetch freely).
- **SQL**: parameterized everywhere; no string-built SQL.
- **Templates**: `html/template` contextual escaping; meta `content` attributes are attribute-context
  escaped; user text is never inserted into `<script>`.

## 16. Testing

### 16.1 `scripts/check.sh` — the CI story (containers only; host has no Go)

```sh
#!/usr/bin/env sh
set -eu; cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."; export MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1   # safe here: this script passes no host paths to native tools
echo "[check] compose config";      docker compose config -q
echo "[check] shell syntax";        for f in scripts/*.sh; do bash -n "$f"; done
echo "[check] unit + ffmpeg tests"; docker build --target test -t clippet-test:local .
echo "[check] runtime image";       docker build -t clippet-app:local .
echo "[check] OK"
```
(That Go line is the ORIGINAL. Since §20 erratum 283 it is two builds, `--target test` and
`--target racetest`, started together and waited on together, each `--output=type=cacheonly` and each
logged to its own file so the transcript reads the same every run; either failing fails the stage. The
runtime image line is the original too: since run 8 (lane `harness9`) its tag is the one compose would run,
`${CLIPPET_IMAGE}` from the shell or the checkout's `.env`, else `clippet-app:local`, so a lane's check never
retags the reference stack's image; since run 9 the Go stage is `scripts/lib/gocheck.sh` in one container,
DEPLOY §17.2.)

The `testsrc` stage runs `gofmt -l` (must be empty) and `go mod verify` (Phase 5: `go.sum` pins the
whole module graph by hash, and this re-checks the downloaded cache against it — DEPLOY.md §17.1);
`test` adds `go vet ./...` and `go test -tags ffmpeg ./...` with the
static ffmpeg 7.1.1 present, and its sibling `racetest` the cgo `go test -race ./...` pass (§20
erratum 41). Phase 2 appends the
unfurl regression test and the no-outbound-URL grep; Phase 4 appends the single-call-site grep beside it
(only `internal/notify` may build an `http.Client`, a transport, a request or a dialer — §20 erratum
66); the deep dive appends the protocol-whitelist stage beside them (a non-test file under
`internal/transcode` that spells an `-i` of its own must also name a `-protocol_whitelist` — §20
erratum 91). All three greps cover the common spellings — they are a tripwire, not a proof; the
allowlist in `internal/config`, the single construction site in `serve.go` and `inputArgs` in
`internal/transcode/exec.go` are the guarantee. Each carries a planted-file self-test so a broken
expression fails loudly instead of passing vacuously. The URL grep is LINE-based and does not skip
comments — a literal URL in prose fails it exactly as an egress would, which is deliberate and is
what its self-test plants in all four scanned languages (§20 erratum 189). The nit sweep adds one
stage of a different kind beside the `jget.py` self-test: `python scripts/lib/mkicons.py --check`
re-draws the companion mark's files — the two app icons, the four Discord icons and three SVGs under
`docs/brand/`, and the favicon `data:` URI on `base.html` and `embed.html` (§20 erratum 301) — and
compares the DECODED pixel rows of the committed PNGs against them (the SVGs and the favicon lines as
text), so a hand-edited or stale one fails the gate; like the `jget.py` stage it skips itself when the
host has no python. `scripts/lib/mkcard.py --check` does the same for the placeholder card (erratum 287). Lane `winexpose`
adds one more Docker stage beside the two Go ones, `[check] cross-compile: windows/amd64` (§20 erratum
308): `--target crosswindows`, a third SIBLING off `testsrc`, which is a
`GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -o /dev/null ./cmd/clippet`. It exists because
`go vet` and `go test` only ever see the host's `GOOS`, so the Windows-only files
(`freebytes_windows.go` in `cmd/clippet` and in `internal/worker`) are compiled by nothing else here —
about 10 s on a warm parent, and the one stage that would catch an `import "C"`, a syscall that is not
on that platform, or a build tag that stopped covering it.

### 16.3 `scripts/e2e.sh` — live-stack E2E (Git Bash; host curl + ffmpeg 7.1.1 + python3; no jq)

Preamble (Git Bash on Windows; each line is a rule, not a suggestion):
```sh
set -euo pipefail; cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
E2E_DIR="$PWD/.e2e"; mkdir -p "$E2E_DIR"            # ALL host files live here (jar, meta JSON, downloads); gitignored
W() { cygpath -w "$1"; }                             # EVERY host path handed to native curl goes through W(): -c/-b/-o/-F/-T
dc() { MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 docker compose "$@"; }     # path conversion is disabled ONLY for docker compose (in-container paths)
                                                     # — never `export MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1` globally: it would also stop W()-less
                                                     #   paths like /tmp/x from being converted and curl would write C:\tmp\x
PY=; for c in python python3 "py -3"; do             # `python` first: on this host `python3` may be the Microsoft Store stub
  if $c -c 'import sys; assert sys.version_info >= (3, 8)' >/dev/null 2>&1; then PY=$c; break; fi
done; [ -n "$PY" ] || die "no python >= 3.8 found (tried python, python3, py -3)"
jget() { $PY scripts/lib/jget.py "$1" "$2"; }        # reads a JSON file, prints a dotted path, null → empty
ENV_BASE=$(envfile PUBLIC_BASE_URL)                  # compose's .env, when present
BASE=${BASE:-${PUBLIC_BASE_URL:-$ENV_BASE}}; BASE=${BASE:-http://localhost:8481}; BASE=${BASE%/}
case $BASE in https://*) SECURE=1;; *) SECURE=0;; esac
JAR="$E2E_DIR/cookies.txt"; JARW=$(W "$JAR")         # curl -c "$JARW" -b "$JARW"
```
`BASE` is the origin under test and must MATCH the app's own `PUBLIC_BASE_URL` — every card tag is
absolute and is compared against `BASE` (the script warns when the two differ, §20 erratum 56).
Precedence: an explicit `BASE=https://… bash scripts/e2e.sh` (the Phase 3 public-origin run) wins, then
`PUBLIC_BASE_URL` from the environment, then `.env`, then `http://localhost:8481`. `SECURE=1` (an
`https://` base) turns ON the https-only assertions marked **https-only** below; an http base runs
exactly as it did before. The admin-CLI and bucket steps stay LOCAL (`dc exec` / `dc run`) whatever
`BASE` is: the script drives the public origin over HTTP and the stack from the host in the same run.
`curl` is invoked as `curl -sS -o "$(W "$E2E_DIR/resp.json")" -w '%{http_code}' …` so every response body
is a file under `.e2e/` and every status is captured; every step prints `[e2e] step N: …` and a failure
names the step (`die "step N: …"`). Steps:

1. `dc up -d --build`; wait ≤120s for `GET /readyz` → 200 (not `/healthz`). Then `e2e_sweep_own`
   (§20 erratum 272) clears whatever an ABORTED earlier run left — the clips of every account matching
   `^e2e_[0-9]{9,11}(_[a-z0-9]{1,3})?$` and nothing else, target list printed first — and is FATAL
   here, because a stack that cannot be swept is not a stack to test on.
2. `scripts/testclips.sh` (idempotent) → `testclips/*.mp4` (720p30, no-audio, vertical, 60fps, dual-audio + edges).
3. **Register** unique user `e2e_$(date +%s)` (`-c "$JARW"`) → 201; `GET /api/auth/me -b "$JARW"` → 200.
   **https-only**: the register `Set-Cookie` carries `Secure` and `HttpOnly` (§14: `Secure` iff
   `urls.IsHTTPS()`); then `POST /api/auth/login` with the same credentials into a second jar → 200 with
   the same two attributes, `GET /api/auth/me` on it → 200, `POST /api/auth/logout` → 204. This is the
   only place the E2E exercises the login route, and a returning viewer on a public origin is the path
   the cookie flag actually matters on.
4. **Upload A** `std-720p30.mp4` with `metadata={"title":"E2E std","ttl_days":1}` written to `$E2E_DIR/meta.json` →
   `curl -b "$JARW" -F "metadata=<$(W "$E2E_DIR/meta.json");type=application/json" -F "video=@$(W testclips/std-720p30.mp4);type=video/mp4"` → 201;
   assert `state=queued`, `ttl_days=1`, `expires_at` non-null. **Upload B** `noaudio-720p30.mp4` with
   metadata lacking `ttl_days` → assert `ttl_days=0` and `expires_at` null (default `never`).
   **Upload C** `vertical-720x1280.mp4` with `"ttl_days":0` → assert `expires_at` null (0-vs-missing proven
   on the wire). **Upload D** `hd-1080p60.mp4`, **Upload E** `dualaudio-720p30.mp4` (no ttl).
5. **Processing card**: immediately after upload E returns, Discordbot-UA `GET /clips/{E}` → 200; assert
   `twitter:card` = `summary_large_image`, `og:title` = real title, **zero** `og:video` / `twitter:player`
   substrings (if E is already `ready`, log "processing card not observed (fast encode)" and continue —
   the unit test covers it deterministically).
6. **Poll** `GET …/progress` for A–E every 1s ≤180s each: stop on `state=ready`; `state=failed` → die with
   `error`; HTTP 404 → die ("poller must not treat 404 as done"). Assert `percent` never decreases and ends 100.
7. **Metadata**: `GET /api/clips/{A}` → `width=1280 height=720 has_audio=true fps=30/1 duration_ms≈6000`;
   B `has_audio=false`; C `720×1280`; D `1280×720 fps=60/1`; E `has_audio=true`. Then A's SERVED
   rendition is downloaded and host-ffprobed for `color_space,color_transfer,color_primaries` — all three
   must be `bt709` (§20 erratum 93: an 8-bit yuv420p H.264 stream may never claim PQ/BT.2020). The
   download is removed again; no new step and no new matrix clip.
8. **Media**: for A: `curl -sI …/video.mp4` → 200, `Content-Type: video/mp4`, `ETag`, `Accept-Ranges: bytes`,
   `Content-Length`; `-H 'Range: bytes=0-99'` → 206 + `Content-Range: bytes 0-99/N` + 100 bytes;
   `-H "If-None-Match: $ETAG"` → 304; `-H 'Range: bytes=999999999999-'` → 416; `-H 'Range: bytes=-0'` → 416 and
   `-H 'Range: bytes=-100'` → 206 (§20 erratum 38); `-H 'Range: items=0-1'` → 200 with the full
   `Content-Length` (§20 erratum 44) and `-H 'Range: bytes=-0' -H 'If-Range: "stale"'` → 200 (§20
   erratum 43); `…/social.mp4` → 200 with the
   **same** ETag and `Content-Length` as `video.mp4`; `…/poster.jpg` → 200 `image/jpeg`.
   **Original**: `curl -sI -b "$JARW" …/original` → 200, `ETag` present, `Content-Disposition: attachment`;
   `-H "If-None-Match: $ETAG"` → 304; without the jar → 401/403 (never 200).
9. **Download + host ffprobe** (every `-o` path is `$(W "$E2E_DIR/<name>.mp4")`): `video.mp4` for A, B, C, D, E →
   exactly one `h264` video stream; audio: A/C/D one `aac` 2ch, B none, E **exactly one** `aac` 2ch; dims even,
   long ≤1280, short ≤720, equal to the DTO; D `r_frame_rate=60/1`; python byte-walk asserts `moov` offset <
   `mdat` offset. `poster.jpg` for A, B, C, D, E → host ffmpeg `signalstats` asserts `YAVG > 8`, i.e. the
   card image is not a black frame (§20 erratum 92), and A's `ffprobe` dims equal `poster.width/height`
   in the DTO.
   **E both-ears check** (merge, not drop, not pan): with host ffmpeg run the §16.2 bandpass+astats recipe for
   `c0/c1 × 440/880 Hz` on E's download; all four `RMS level dB` values > −40 and `|c0 − c1| < 1 dB` per tone.
10. **Discordbot-UA card sweep** (`-A 'Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; Discordbot/2.0; +https://discordapp.com)'`)
    on `/clips/{A}`: python `html.parser` extracts all `<meta>`; assert **every** §9.1 checklist tag is present
    with the expected value; every URL-valued tag starts with `$BASE`; `og:title` = "E2E std";
    `og:image:width/height` = poster dims; `og:video:width/height` = 1280/720; `og:video` and
    `twitter:player:stream` end with `/api/clips/{A}/social.mp4`; `twitter:player` ends with `/embed/{A}`;
    **`og:video:secure_url` absent** when `$BASE` is http, present when https. Repeat with a Twitterbot UA.
    `<title>` contains the title (visible text in initial HTML). The anonymous (no jar) share page body
    contains **no view count** (the `data-views` substring is absent; with the owner's jar it is present) and the HTML
    contains neither `style=` nor `<style` (CSP `style-src 'self'` would block them silently).
    **https-only**: every URL-valued meta tag is `https://` **and** on `$BASE` (one http URL makes the
    card mixed content and X drops the player); the anonymous page body contains no `http://` substring
    at all (the templates hold no absolute literals, so one could only come from a bad `PUBLIC_BASE_URL`).
    **https-only — PUBLIC RESOLVABILITY** (the Phase 3 gate condition "tag URLs publicly resolvable"):
    `card_urls` re-parses the ready share page and collects every URL a crawler or a player is handed —
    the URL-valued §9.1 tags, `<link rel=canonical>` and the `<video>` `src`/`poster`, the last two
    **root-relative in the body** and so absolutised against `$BASE` (`urljoin`) — deduped in document
    order; `data-view-url` is skipped (POST-only). The set must contain `/clips/{A}`,
    `/api/clips/{A}/poster.jpg`, `/api/clips/{A}/social.mp4`, `/embed/{A}` and `/api/clips/{A}/video.mp4`
    (≥5 URLs), each must be https on `$BASE`, and **each is fetched back from the public origin twice —
    once with the Discordbot UA, once with the Twitterbot UA — and must answer 200**. A tag URL that
    404s from outside turns a playable card into a bare link, and Discord caches that verdict per URL.
11. **Embed**: `curl -sI /embed/{A}` → 200, no `X-Frame-Options` header, CSP contains `frame-ancestors *`;
    body (`curl -s`) contains `<video`, no view count, no `style=`, no `<style`.
    **https-only**: the embed body contains no `http://` substring (it is what X iframes from an https
    page; mixed-content media is blocked silently inside an otherwise correct card), and the
    no-XFO/`frame-ancestors *` pair is re-asserted on a Twitterbot-UA `HEAD` through the public origin.
12. **Owner ops**: `PATCH /api/clips/{B}` `{"title":"renamed"}` (cookie jar, no Origin header → passes CSRF) →
    200; `PATCH {"ttl_days":7}` → `expires_at` set; `PATCH {"ttl_days":0}` → null again; `DELETE /api/clips/{D}`
    → 204; `GET /api/clips/{D}` → 404; mc prefix check (below) for D → empty.
13. **View dedupe + privacy**: `POST …/view` twice (no jar) → both 204; `GET /api/clips/{A} -b "$JARW"` (owner)
    → `views=1`; `GET /api/clips/{A}` without the jar → the `views` key is **absent** (jget prints empty).
14. **Forced expiry** (the documented mechanism, §8.8): `dc exec -T app clippet admin expire {A} --ago 2h`
    → prints the new `expires_at`. Poll ≤150s (≈2 ticks + margin) until `GET /api/clips/{A}` → 404 **and**
    `GET /clips/{A}` → 404 **and** the bucket prefix is empty:
    `dc run --rm --entrypoint sh bucket-init -c 'mc alias set local http://minio:9000 "$MINIO_ROOT_USER" "$MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD" >/dev/null && mc ls --recursive local/'"$S3_BUCKET"'/clips/{A}/ | wc -l'` → `0`.
    Also `dc exec -T app clippet admin ls {A}` prints `not found`.
15. **Expire-while-in-flight (best effort)**: upload F (`std-720p30.mp4`), immediately `admin expire {F} --ago 2h`;
    whatever state F is in (queued/processing/ready), it must be gone (404 + prefix empty) within 150s.
    Exercises `MarkDeleting → Cancel → DeletePrefix` on the live stack when the race is won; either way the
    assertion is identical. The resulting `lost_race` / cancelled-`PutFile` / killed-ffmpeg lines are INFO by
    doctrine (§12), so step 16 stays green.
16. `dc logs app` must contain no `panic` and no `ERROR` lines — **none**, not "none except expected": the §12
    log-level doctrine makes every event this script provokes INFO or WARN.
17. **Cleanup** (best effort, after the log gate — §20 erratum 36): `DELETE` B, C and E (the three clips
    the run leaves with no TTL) and `POST /api/auth/logout`; never fail the run on cleanup. Then the
    same `e2e_sweep_own` step 1 opened with (§20 erratum 272), best effort here: it force-expires
    anything the run's own accounts still own, waits for the sweeper, and prunes those accounts — so a
    passing run leaves NOTHING, where it used to leave four users. It replaces the `users prune` this
    step used to run; the bucket census follows it. Then print `E2E PASS` with a summary table.
18. **Capture tools** (§20 errata 58/59/60) — runs **between steps 15 and 16**, keeping steps 1–17 numbered as
    above: the step-16 log gate must cover this route's lines, and step 17 logs the session out while minting,
    deleting and revoking all need it. Mint a token from the session (`POST /api/auth/tokens`) and assert the
    `sxcu` object it returns IS the ShareX file — `RequestURL` = `$BASE/api/upload`, `RequestMethod` POST,
    `Body` MultipartFormData, `FileFormName` `file`, `URL` `{json:url}`, `ErrorMessage` `{json:message}`,
    `DestinationType` **`FileUploader`** (never an image destination, erratum 59), `Arguments` **absent or
    empty** with no `{filename}` anywhere in the response (erratum 60), and
    `Headers.Authorization` equal to `Bearer <the raw token just minted>`. Then the request ShareX actually
    sends, with **no cookie jar**: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOK" -F title=… -F ttl_days=7 -F unlisted=false
    -F who=cares -F "file=@testclips/std-720p30.mp4;type=video/mp4" $BASE/api/upload` → **201** with
    `{id,url,embed_url,state,expires_at}`, `url` = `$BASE/clips/{G}`, `embed_url` = `$BASE/embed/{G}`,
    `state=queued`, `expires_at` non-null, the unknown field ignored; `wait_ready {G}`; then a Discordbot-UA
    `GET {url}` re-runs the full §9.1 `card_check player` inventory — the point of the feature is that what a
    capture tool pastes unfurls as a player. Negatives: no credential → **401** `unauthorized` (a 1-byte file
    part, so the gate is the only thing under test); the file part sent FIRST → 201 with the title fallen back
    to the filename without its extension (the fields after it are never read); the token on a session-only
    route (`GET /api/clips`) → **403** `token_not_allowed` (§20 erratum 19). Cleanup inside the step: `DELETE`
    both clips with the owner session (204, or 202 for one still transcoding), `DELETE` the token, and prove
    the revoked token is dead (`GET /api/auth/me` → 401).
19. **TTL keep-alive** (§20 errata 61/62) — runs **between steps 18 and 16**, for the same two reasons step 18
    does: the step-16 log gate must cover this route's own access-log and sweep lines, and every request in it
    needs the session step 17 ends. Upload T (`std-720p30.mp4`, `ttl_days=7`) and its control U (identical), record
    T's `expires_at`, `wait_ready` both. Then: `POST …/touch` → 200 with `expires_at` ≈ `now + 7d` (±10 min) and
    never **earlier** than the upload's, `state`/`ttl_days` unchanged. That check is deliberately **not** a strict
    seconds-scale comparison against the upload's expiry: both values come from the app's clock, a container
    clock can step backwards under the host's time sync (observed on the dev host — the app 12s behind the host,
    stepping back ~8s mid-run), and the real gap here is only the second or two a 6s clip takes to transcode, so
    a strict comparison tests the clock rather than the feature. The "recomputed from now, **not** extended"
    claim is made at the rescue below instead, where one touch moves a backdated expiry **seven days** forward —
    a gap no clock jitter can fake. Negatives —
    anonymous → 401 `unauthorized`; a second registered user's session → 403 `forbidden`; a freshly minted capture
    token → 403 `token_not_allowed` (erratum 19), then revoked. A clip kept forever (C, uploaded `ttl_days=0`) →
    200 with `expires_at` still null. The share page: with the owner's jar it carries `data-touch-url`,
    `data-keep-forever` and `data-expires`; without it, neither the URL nor the button (erratum 62).
    **The rescue, against a control** — the point of the feature: `admin expire` **both** T and U `--ago 2h`, touch
    **only** T (→ 200 with an `expires_at` **seven days later than the backdated one** `admin expire` printed:
    the clock-proof "recomputed from now"), then poll until `GET /api/clips/{U}` answers **404** (cap 120s, ≈2
    ticks, `die` if it never does). What the step proves is precisely that: a touched clip **stops being a sweep
    candidate and survives a full tick**, and the control's destruction is what shows a tick actually ran and
    reached both clips — a fixed sleep cannot tell "survived a tick" from "no tick happened". T must then still be
    200 `ready` with the rescued `expires_at` and a non-empty bucket prefix, while U's prefix is empty. U needs no
    cleanup: the tick is what removes it. Note what this does **not** prove: a live touch lands ~200 ms after
    `admin expire`, long before the next `SweepCandidates`, so T is never on a candidate list and no
    `no longer expired; skipped` line is logged. Erratum 15's re-verification *inside* the tombstone write — a
    touch landing **after** candidate selection — is proven deterministically by
    `sweeper.TestTouchedClipSurvivesTheTick`, which drives that exact ordering. Finally keep-forever:
    `PATCH {"ttl_days":0}` → `expires_at` null, a further touch → still null, `DELETE` T and log the second user
    out. One control wait per run (~10–20s in practice), never a fixed sleep.

**Step 20 — Discord auto-post (#4)**, placed physically between step 19 and step 16 so the step-16 log
gate still covers its lines and so it runs before step 17 logs the session out. Two halves.
The **negative half always runs** and is the live proof of the §15 promise: with `DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL`
unset, `dc exec -T app clippet admin stats --no-storage` must print `notify=0` in its per-kind job line
(the enqueue is inside the ready transaction, so zero jobs across every state means no clip of the run
was ever queued for announcement), and the whole run's app log — the same `--since $START_TS` window
step 16 reads — must contain no `discord webhook` line at all. The **positive half runs only when
`E2E_DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL` is set** (`SKIP` printed otherwise, since only the operator has a real webhook):
step 1 then `export`s it as `DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL` so compose's shell
interpolation wins over `.env` (verified with `docker compose config` before the build), step 20 asserts
a `discord webhook delivered … clip=<id> … status=2xx` line for **every listed clip of the run** (A, B, C,
D, G, H, T, U — F is excluded, being force-expired the instant it is uploaded and possibly destroyed
before it is ready), asserts **no** such line for the unlisted clip **E**, asserts the boot line
`discord webhook configured` is present and that the webhook URL itself appears **nowhere** in the log,
and step 17 finally recreates the app **without** the variable so the shared stack never keeps a test
webhook. Matrix clip E is uploaded `unlisted:true` for exactly this control (§20 erratum 64).

**Step 22 — GIF export (#6)**, placed physically between step 21 and step 16 for the same two reasons
(a preview is made, regenerated, trimmed away and remade there, and every request needs the owner
session step 17 ends). It runs on **B**, the one ready clip step 21 does not trim, and it is the step
that proves **migration 0002 on the live volume** — a database created by 0001 alone — through
`clippet admin stats`'s `schema: applied=1,2` line. Then, in order: an ANONYMOUS `GET …/preview.gif`
answering 202 + `Retry-After: 5` while the DTO still reports `gif_url: null`; a poll to 200 with
`image/gif`, an ETag and `max-age=3600`; the HOST ffprobe measuring a real animated GIF (`-count_frames`:
codec `gif`, width ≤ 480, > 1 frame, ≤ 8 MiB); a second GET served at once and an `If-None-Match` 304;
`gif_url` absolute for the owner AND for an anonymous caller; the key present under the clip's own
prefix in `admin ls --stat`; 404 for a destroyed clip and for a malformed id; the owner's `POST …/gif`
answering 202 and then 409 `gif_in_progress`, with the regenerate landing under a FRESH `{r8}` whose
bytes (and ETag) are identical and whose predecessor is deleted; a trim dropping the preview
(`gif_url` null, the object gone, a fresh 202 on the next request); and finally `DELETE` B leaving an
empty prefix — which is why B is deleted **here** rather than in step 17's best-effort cleanup, since
"the preview goes with the clip" is a claim worth failing on. Step 11 carries #8 in the same run: the
plain embed has no `autoplay`/`muted`/`loop` and `preload="metadata"`, `?autoplay=1&loop=1` renders all
three attributes (muted included) with `preload="auto"`, and the share page ignores the same query.
23. **Tags + collections** (§17 #9; §20 errata 81/82) — runs **between steps 22 and 16**, for the same two
    reasons every Phase 4 step does. `admin stats` must report `applied=1,2,3,4` on the live volume, which
    is the migration proof. The subject is **C** (B is destroyed by step 22), and the filter assertions key
    on a tag no other run can have used (`e2e-<the run's timestamp>`), because the stack is shared.
    Tags: PATCH a mixed-case, duplicated, space-padded set on C and get back the normalised, deduped, sorted
    one; an illegal tag and eleven distinct tags are both 400 `invalid_tags` whose message NAMES the
    offending word (or the cap) and neither changes anything; `[]` clears and serialises as `[]`, not null;
    a title-only PATCH leaves the tags alone; a Bearer token gets 403 `token_not_allowed`. Tags at upload
    time through BOTH routes: `metadata.tags` on `POST /api/clips` (reported in the 201) and a
    comma-separated `tags` field on `POST /api/upload` (whose 201 stays erratum 58's five fields, with the
    set read back from the DTO); an illegal capture tag is 400. The filter: `?tag=` returns exactly the
    three tagged clips newest-first, an uppercase filter is the same filter, `limit=1` + cursor pages
    through all three, a cursor minted under the filter spent WITHOUT it is 400 `invalid_cursor`, and
    `?tag=BAD!` is 400 `invalid_tags` naming it. The pages: the owner's share page carries the pre-filled
    editor, the anonymous one carries no tag markup and not even the tag TEXT, the library renders chips
    linking to `/?tag=x` and says which filter is on, and an illegal `?tag=` on the library is a 303 to `/`.
    Collections: POST → 201 with `url` on the public origin; PUT a membership in a CHOSEN order (not the
    library's) with a duplicate in it → 2 members in that order; the anonymous GET shows them with their
    tags and NO `views` (nor for the owner); a third user's clip → 400 `not_your_clip` naming it, changing
    nothing; that third user's PATCH and DELETE → 404; a token's POST → 403. The card: Discordbot on
    `/c/{id}` → 200 with `og:type=website`, the title, the canonical URL, `og:image` = the FIRST ready
    member's poster, `twitter:card=summary_large_image`, **no** `og:video`, **no** `twitter:player`, no
    `data-views` and no inline style; the body links to each member's share page; the owner's page adds the
    controls, the membership picker with the current members preselected and the two-click delete; the
    library lists the collection. Unknown and malformed `/c/…` are true 404s with no card tags. Finally the
    cascade: deleting a member clip drops it from the collection (`clip_count` 2 → 1) with no membership
    step anywhere, and `DELETE` the collection → 204, then 404 on both the API and `/c/{id}`, with the
    surviving clip untouched. Step 17 also cleans up X (the capture upload).
24. **Janitor vs a live media run** (§20 erratum 89) — also between 22 and 16. A trim of a clip of its own
    (**Z**) runs to `done` while `admin ls --stat` reports its job and the clip never leaves `ready`, and
    the run's log carries no janitor removal and no requeued attempt for it. It asserts the GUARD, not the
    race: a janitor pass comes round only every tenth sweep tick.
25. **Chunked upload** (§20 erratum 90) — also between 22 and 16. A Bearer-authenticated
    `POST /api/upload` sent with `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` (no `Content-Length`, which net/http reports
    as −1) must still answer **201 with a JSON body** — not a proxy's HTML — and the clip must reach
    `ready` with no `failure_reason`; the clip and the token are removed afterwards. It proves the half a
    unit test cannot, that the new precheck did not break the streaming path; the REFUSAL is unit-tested
    (`httpapi.TestChunkedUploadIsGatedLikeAnyOther`), because nothing in the E2E may fill a disk.
26. **A playlist is not a video** (§20 erratum 91) — also between 22 and 16. A ~100-byte `.m3u8` naming
    an `http://127.0.0.1:1` segment, built inline and POSTed to `/api/upload` with a Bearer token, must
    answer **415 `not_a_video`**, and `admin stats`' clip count must be the same afterwards as before.
    Two curls, no polling; the token and the temp file are removed. It proves the WIRE half; the
    allowlist itself and a playlist reaching for a sibling clip's source are unit tests
    (`transcode.TestParseProbeContainerAllowlist`, `transcode.TestProbeRefusesACraftedPlaylist`).

**Since run 9 (lane `pool`) only steps 1–4, 6, 16 and 17 live in `scripts/e2e.sh`.** Steps 7–30 above
are pool bundles with their old numbers — `7-clip` (7–14), `15-ttl` (15, 19), `18-capture` (18, 29),
`20-pages` (20, 23, 27, 30), `21-trim` (21, 24), `22-gif` (22) — and steps 5, 25, 26 and 28 were cut after
the duplicates read (each one's proof that stayed is named in `scripts/e2e.d/README.md`, "The core in the
pool"). **Steps 27 onward have always lived in `scripts/e2e.d/`, not in this list.** `scripts/e2e.sh` runs every
`scripts/e2e.d/*.sh` file immediately before step 16 (the log gate) and step 17
(logout/cleanup) — so parallel work adds a FILE instead of contending for the same lines in the
script. One drop-in per bundle, named `<first step number>-<bundle>.sh` (e.g. `33-account.sh`); each
uses the same harness helpers (`step`/`expect`/`die`/`W`/`dc`/`upload`…), creates whatever clips it
needs (or reads the shared C/E/X, which live until step 17) and destroys anything step 17 would not
already clean up. The suite is **108 steps / 49 bundles**: 7 in the script itself (setup 1–4 and 6, then
16 and 17), the rest across the drop-ins (`7-clip`, `15-ttl`, `18-capture`, `20-pages`, `21-trim`, `22-gif`,
`31-nits`, `33-account`, `37-library`, `41-social`, `43-watch`, `47-upload`, `51-admin`, `55-owner`,
`61-nits2`, `62-tiers`, `67-capture`, `70-web`, `73-ops`, `77-design`, `80-front`, `82-links`, `85-bot`,
`87-storage`, `88-fsstore`, `89-quota`, `90-media`, `91-drop`, `92-setup`, `93-signin`, `94-instance`, `95-import`, `96-mint`, `97-hook`, `98-form`, `99-backup`, `100-inhook`, `101-autofetch`, `102-dedupe`, `103-audio`, `104-audiocard`, `105-migrate2`, `106-botsignin`, `107-snapshot`, `108-person`, `109-chunked`, `110-autohost`, `111-autobot`, `112-rotated`). A drop-in also adds its own clips to the closing summary table with
`summary_row`, and a `dc run` probe container that boots `clippet serve` on a private `DATA_DIR` MUST
carry a private `SCRATCH_DIR` beside it — see `scripts/e2e.d/README.md`, which records both conventions
and why the second one is not optional.

**The scheduling model (§20 erratum 245).** The drop-ins are no longer simply sourced in name order.
Each file declares in its own header how it may be RUN — `# e2e-schedule: parallel` or
`# e2e-schedule: exclusive` (the old fixed-lane form `parallel lane=<n>` is refused) — and **no marker
means exclusive**, which is the default a new drop-in keeps until somebody has shown otherwise. A file
may add `# e2e-schedule-after: <stem>[,<stem>]` to say it runs after another bundle (the harness checks
every such declaration before any bundle runs, §20 erratum 269(a), and the pool honours it by waiting)
and `# e2e-schedule-apart: <stem>[,<stem>]` to say the two must never overlap (four pairs today, each with
its reason in the file and in `scripts/e2e.d/README.md`: the `view` bucket — 70-web's filmstrip poll and
43-watch's GIF poll — the `claim` bucket, 67-capture's load sensitivity, and 91-drop/95-import).
`run_dropins` hands the parallel-safe bundles to a POOL of `E2E_LANES` slots, LONGEST FIRST by the last
passing run's seconds on the same origin (`.e2e/checkpoints/durations__<BASE>.txt`); each bundle runs in a
subshell with its own scratch context under `.e2e/ctx-<stem>/`, its own log and its summary rows written
to a file because a subshell's array would be lost. The harness then waits for the live queue to go idle
and runs the exclusive bundles one at a time in name order — since lane `excl` (erratum 245, amended
2026-10-06) that is `87-storage` alone. A bundle is parallel-safe only when it owns its clips and its
users, mutates no shared clip, restarts and reconfigures nothing, asserts nothing bucket-wide, log-wide or
instance-wide, and probes no rate limiter from the run's address (a drain fires from a throwaway
container instead, `burst_429 … apart`). `wait_ready` paces itself at a `POLL_SLEEP` the plan derives
from the number of polling bundles that can run at once, so the run stays at or under 1.5 progress
requests a second against the `poll` bucket's refill of 2 whatever the width.
The environment knobs that shape a run are none of them needed for the gate: `E2E_ONLY=<stems>` runs
only those bundles on the setup every run makes (steps 1–6: the owner, the second user, clips C, E and X) and ends in
`E2E PASS (PARTIAL)` listing everything that did not run; `E2E_SKIP=<stems>` is its complement;
`E2E_LANES=N` is the pool's width (default half the CPUs, at least 2 and at most 6; `1` runs the bundles
one at a time); and `E2E_RESUME=1` re-runs the setup plus only the bundles not yet recorded as passed
on this product tree (`E2E_OVERLAP`, which started the pool beside the core's last steps, is refused since
the core is in the pool). The knobs that override a SETTING for the length
of a run are listed in `scripts/e2e.d/README.md` — the three limiters, `E2E_SWEEP_INTERVAL`, and (§20
erratum 269(c)) `E2E_APP_CPUS`, `E2E_CLEAN_BUCKET` and `E2E_SELFTEST`. **`bash scripts/e2e.sh` with no
environment is still the whole suite.** Since run 9 it is the E2E stage of **T2**, `bash scripts/gate.sh`, on
the local `clippet-gate` stack. T2 is owed only at a release, a shape change, a nightly slot or the owner's word.

**The tiers (§20 erratum 331).**
- T0, `scripts/t0.sh`, on every commit, runs only the self-test.
- T1, `scripts/t1.sh`, once at a lane's end on the lane's own stack, runs `E2E_ONLY=$(scripts/select.sh)`. That is the
  bundles whose `# e2e-covers:` lines match the diff. A shape path stops it with "this diff needs T2".
- Every drop-in header declares its namespace (`# e2e-namespace:`) and its change map (`# e2e-covers:`), and the
  self-test refuses a collision or an uncovered product file.
- A pool bundle that fails on a classified transient is re-run once (`.e2e/retries.txt`).
- T3, `scripts/smoke-public.sh`, is the public origin's two-minute check after a deploy.

Everything the harness needs from inside the stack goes through `dc exec -T app clippet admin …` (the
DB, and — `admin objects` — the store) and the one helper `store_mc "mc …"` (planting and removing
objects, in the stack's OWN bucket with the stack's own credentials) — no host sqlite3, jq, or mc, and
no drop-in of its own (§20 erratum 281 (c) and (f)).

### 16.4 Test-clip matrix

`scripts/testclips.sh` (exists, host ffmpeg 7.1.1, lavfi `testsrc2` + `sine`) produces the five required
variants — `std-720p30`, `noaudio-720p30`, `vertical-720x1280`, `hd-1080p60`, `dualaudio-720p30` — plus
`rotated90-sidedata` (Display Matrix at side-data index 1 via `-display_rotation 90` remux),
`anamorphic-sar` (SAR 16:11), `fractional-2997`, `small-640x360`. The `-tags ffmpeg` Go tests regenerate
the same recipes inside the container so `check.sh` needs no host artifacts, and add two remuxes
`testclips.sh` does not ship — `rotated-89.4-sidedata` and `rotated-89.6-sidedata`, the pair straddling
ffmpeg's own autorotate boundary (§20 erratum 47). Git Bash quirk reminders:
`cygpath -w` (`W()`) for **every** host path given to native curl (`-c/-b/-o/-F/-T`), `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1`
scoped to `docker compose` invocations only (`dc()`), `python` before `python3` (Store stub), never
`Invoke-WebRequest`.

## 20. Errata & amendments after Stream A (binding; supersede earlier text where they differ)

Stream A (core) landed on `main` (commits `5763f71`…`d93ff13` plus the merge's `SweepTotals`
commit). While building, it found the contract drift below and resolved it; **B/C/D/E build against
the code on `main` as amended here**. `cmd/clippet/serve.go` is in its FINAL wiring form — streams
replace bodies inside their own packages and never edit `serve.go` (only `cmd/clippet/admin.go` is D's).

**Decisions taken at the merge**
- **Audio merge (spec §3 vs §10.3)**: the `aformat=stereo → amix=inputs=n:normalize=0 → alimiter`
  chain of §10.3 IS the binding mechanism. The spec's "amerge + `-ac 2`" is a mechanism suggestion for
  the requirement "merge, don't silently drop track 2"; `amerge` was measured on ffmpeg 7.1.1 to fail on
  layout-less mono inputs and to hard-pan when forced. `amix` meets the requirement (both tones at
  −24.1 dB in both channels on the fixture). Stream C builds §10.3 verbatim; goldens contain no `amerge`.
- **§12 sweep counters in `/healthz`**: `httpapi.Deps` gains an additive `SweepTotals func() (destroyed,
  errors int64)` (nil → field omitted); `/healthz` emits `"sweep":{"destroyed":n,"errors":n}`; `serve.go`
  passes `sw.Totals`. Already wired on `main`; B keeps it.

**Contract amendments (already implemented on `main`)**
1. `config.TranscodeConfig` gains `FFmpegVersion string` (never read from env; `serve.go` fills it from
   `ffmpeg -version` after `exec.LookPath`). `/healthz` reads `Cfg.Transcode.FFmpegVersion`. `httpapi.Deps`
   is otherwise byte-exact §18.2. `FFMPEG_PATH`/`FFPROBE_PATH` are resolved (LookPath, fatal if missing) in
   `runServe`, not `config.Load`; `cfg.Transcode.FFmpeg/FFprobe` are absolute paths after boot.
2. `sweeper.Sweeper.Start(ctx)` **blocks** until `ctx` is cancelled and the in-flight tick has finished;
   `serve.go` runs it in a goroutine and waits ≤5s for it on shutdown. `sweeper.New(lifecycle.Deps,
   config.Config)` starts no goroutine. D implements exactly this.
3. `db.CancelJob(ctx, jobID, now)` exists (idempotent; no error if the job is terminal/gone) — the
   lost-race path of §10.3 step 9. `db.JobStageQueued = "queued"` is the initial `jobs.stage` (set on
   insert, retry, requeue, release). `db.Backoff(kind, n)` and the state/kind constants
   (`db.ClipQueued … db.JobRunning`, `db.KindTranscode`) exist.
4. `db` semantics: `FailAttempt`/`ReleaseJob` require the job to be `running`; a job cancelled by
   `MarkDeleting` mid-run returns `db.ErrStateMismatch` with nothing changed — the worker treats that as
   "clip gone" (INFO), never an error. `db.Limits{}` zero values fall back to 3/10. `FinalizeTranscode`
   returns `(false, nil)` unless the clip is still `processing`. `RetryClip` → `ErrStateMismatch` when not
   `failed` (→ 409 `not_failed`), `ErrNotFound` when missing. `DeleteClipRow` → `ErrStateMismatch` unless
   `deleting`. `UpdateClipMeta`/`IncrementViews` → `ErrNotFound` for `deleting` rows. `MarkDeleting` is
   idempotent on `deleting`, `ErrNotFound` when gone. `ListClips` clamps `Limit` 1..100 (default 50),
   orders `created_at DESC, id ASC`, excludes `deleting`, garbage cursor → `ErrInvalidCursor`.
   `ErrConflict` is raised only for PRIMARY KEY / UNIQUE violations (FK violations are plain errors).
   `Ping` uses the ro pool only. `ForceExpire` sets `updated_at` from the wall clock.
5. `ReconcileOnStartup` is job-only and also repairs `processing` clips with no `running` job from their
   latest transcode job: `failed` → clip `failed` (+ `last_error`); `done`/`cancelled` → job requeued
   (checkpoint kept → finalize-only); `queued` → clip `queued`; no transcode job → clip `failed`
   ("orphaned at boot: no transcode job"; `RetryClip` creates one). `serve.go` calls
   `DeleteExpiredSessions` and a boot scratch janitor right after it. **D's every-10th-tick janitor must
   implement the full §12 rule** (dir name is a valid id AND (row missing or `ready|failed|deleting`, OR
   mtime > 24h AND state ≠ `processing`)) — mirror `cmd/clippet/serve.go`'s `scratchJanitor`.
6. `store`: `KeysFor(P, id, ext)` returns `Keys{Prefix, Original, Probe}`; rendition/poster keys take the
   per-attempt `r8`. There is no single-object `Remove`: delete an attempt's keys with `DeletePrefix(key)`
   (a key is its own prefix). `Fake` extras: `Put/Get/Keys`, `CallsSnapshot()`; `GetRange` errors on an
   unsatisfiable start, streams ctx-aware, `end=-1` → EOF; `Download` creates parent dirs. `NewSeeker`
   returns `io.ErrUnexpectedEOF` when the object is shorter than `size` and a sticky `store.ErrNotFound`
   on a missing key. `minio.go` already constructs the client (BucketLookup per `ForcePathStyle`,
   `DefaultTransport` + `ResponseHeaderTimeout=OpTimeout`, static V4 creds, region) and implements `Ping`
   (`BucketExists`); D replaces the file wholesale keeping that construction.
7. `httpapi`: `NewHandler` is mounted at `/api/`, `/healthz`, `/readyz` — register FULL paths. Keep
   `health.go` and the JSON-404 catch-all. The Go 1.22 mux never emits 405 once `/` is registered: wrap
   every route with `httpapi.Methods(h, "GET", …)` (HEAD implied by GET; `Allow` lists HEAD) to get
   405 + `Allow` + envelope. `Deps.Storage` is nil-safe. DTO structs with §8.2 tags exist; `ToDTO` panics.
8. `httpx`: `WriteJSON` sets `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8` and `X-Content-Type-Options:
   nosniff`. `AccessLog` logs `/healthz`,`/readyz` <400 at DEBUG, ≥500 at WARN, else INFO, and appends
   every `SetLogField`. `Recover` writes the 500 envelope only if headers were not sent; re-panics
   `http.ErrAbortHandler`. `SecurityHeaders(true)` deletes `X-Frame-Options` and sets `frame-ancestors *`;
   constants `httpx.CSPPage`/`httpx.CSPEmbed`; `httpx.Middleware` alias; `RequestIDFrom(ctx)`.
   `serve.go` applies `RequestID → AccessLog → Recover` at the root; **`SecurityHeaders` is per route**
   (httpapi and web apply it themselves; the web skeleton already wraps with `SecurityHeaders(false)`).
9. `config`: `config.ErrInvalidTTL` is exported (→ 400 `invalid_ttl`); `ParseTTLDays(nil, def)` returns a
   copy of `def`; `TRUSTED_PROXIES` accepts bare IPs as /32 or /128; `S3_KEY_PREFIX` is charset-validated
   and always ends in `/`; version `dev` yields buildID `dev-<unix36>` so `Static()` cache-busts per boot.
10. `auth`: `HashPassword`/`CheckPassword` are functional (bcrypt 12); `WithPrincipal`/`FromContext` and the
    pass-through `Resolver.Middleware` are tested; the 3-line `stubAuth` pattern is in
    `internal/auth/auth_test.go` for E. `transcode.Probe` returns a closure that panics when invoked
    (httpapi tests inject `Deps.Probe`); `ErrPermanent`/`IsPermanent` exist (`errors.As`).
11. Inert skeleton constructors (so `serve.go` boots on the skeleton): `worker.New` returns `NewNoop()`,
    `sweeper.New(...).Start` just blocks on ctx, `views.NewDeduper` returns a value whose `Seen` panics,
    `web.New` answers 503 text. Every other skeleton body panics `todo: stream X`.
12. Dockerfile: the trailing `# …` comments on `FROM` lines of §2 were moved to their own lines (Docker
    treats only line-leading `#` as comments). `0001_init.sql` ends with `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS
    schema_migrations (…)` and `Migrate` uses `IF NOT EXISTS` too.
13. Test loops (host has no Go). Per stream, from the stream's worktree (Git Bash):
    `export MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1; docker run --rm -v "$(pwd -W)":/src -v clippet-gomod:/go/pkg/mod -v clippet-gobuild:/root/.cache/go-build -w /src clippet-gotest:ffmpeg sh -ec 'test -z "$(gofmt -l .)" && go vet ./... && go test -tags ffmpeg ./...'`
    — `clippet-gotest:ffmpeg` = `golang:1.27-alpine` + static ffmpeg/ffprobe 7.1.1 at `/usr/local/bin`,
    `CGO_ENABLED=0` preset. **Streams never run `docker compose up`** (one live stack, one port; the
    merge gate runs it after merge) and never tag images `clippet-*:local`.

**Phase 2 hardening errata (binding; supersede earlier text where they differ)**

14. **Upload spool naming (fixes the janitor-vs-upload race)**: `POST /api/clips` spools the video to
    `$SCRATCH_DIR/.upload-{id}` (a name `ids.Valid` rejects; helpers in `internal/scratch`) and renames
    it to `$SCRATCH_DIR/{id}` only after `CreateClipWithJob` commits (a rename failure is WARN — the
    worker re-downloads). The §12 janitor rule is amended: `.upload-*` dirs are removed by the periodic
    janitor only when nothing inside them was touched for 24h (an in-flight upload is sacred, §11), and
    unconditionally by the boot janitor (no upload is in flight before the listener opens). The
    "row missing → remove" rule for plain `{id}` dirs stays immediate — with spools renamed only after
    commit, a row-less `{id}` dir is always residue.
15. **Sweeper re-verifies expiry at destroy time**: expiry-driven destruction goes through
    `lifecycle.DestroyExpired` → `db.MarkDeletingIfDue(id, now, grace)` — the tombstone UPDATE carries
    the same candidate predicate, so a TTL extension PATCHed after candidate selection wins and the clip
    is skipped (`Result.Skipped`, INFO, counted in the sweep line as `skipped`). Owner `DELETE` keeps the
    unconditional `MarkDeleting`. (A candidate the worker claimed instead of a TTL extension is skipped
    the same way but logged as deferred, not rescued — §20 erratum 51.)
16. **`store.Store.Download` carries a progress callback** (`func(done, total int64)`, nil ok) so
    §10.3 step 1's `frac = bytes downloaded / source_size` is real; acquire feeds it through
    `safeProgress`.
17. **Share-page cache headers**: `/clips/{id}` and the HTML 404 render principal-dependent content
    (owner view count, session nav), so they answer `Cache-Control: private, no-store` + `Vary: Cookie`
    — the HTML twin of §8.2's `privateJSON` — superseding §9.1's `no-cache` for those two pages
    (the principal-free embed keeps `no-cache`). The pages also check `auth.ResolveError` before
    trusting "anonymous" (index, tokens, clip, 404): a resolver DB error renders the 503 page, never a
    login redirect or an anonymous variant.
18. **Failure-classification symmetry in upload step 6**: `probeGate` answers 415 `not_a_video` only for
    `transcode.ErrPermanent` (bad file); a client disconnect is 400 `upload_interrupted` (INFO) and any
    other probe failure is 503 `unavailable` (WARN) — §8.3's "error → 415" is narrowed to the §11
    file-at-fault class. `POST /retry` evicts the stale terminal progress-registry entry
    (`Worker.Forget` before `Wake`), and a media `GetRange` NoSuchKey re-reads the row before logging:
    live row still referencing the key → ERROR drift; row gone/tombstoned/re-keyed → INFO lost race.
19. **API tokens are upload-only credentials in Phase 1** (`internal/httpapi/router.go`,
    `clip_handlers.go`): a `ck_…` Bearer token is accepted on exactly two routes – `GET /api/auth/me`
    (any valid token) and `POST /api/clips` (`RequireScope("upload")`). Every other user/owner route
    (`GET /api/clips`, `PATCH`/`DELETE /api/clips/{id}`, `POST /api/clips/{id}/retry`,
    `GET /api/clips/{id}/original`) runs `RequireSession` and answers a token with 403
    `token_not_allowed`, so a leaked capture-tool token cannot list the library, read private fields,
    edit, delete, retry or download originals. A token never reveals the owner-private `views` count
    either: `clipDTO` computes `isOwner` as `Via == "session" && User.ID == owner_id`, so
    `GET /api/clips/{id}` – the one owner-relevant route a token still reaches, because it is
    public – renders the public DTO even to the owner's own token (the 201 of `POST /api/clips` still
    carries `views:0` for the uploader: a fresh clip has nothing to reveal). This supersedes the §8.1
    auth column for those routes (`user` on `GET /api/clips`, and `owner` – "`user` whose id equals
    `owner_id`" – on the four owner routes, now read `session` / session-owner) and the §8.2 `isOwner`
    definition ("session or token principal whose id equals `owner_id`" → session principal only);
    §14's list of the routes that accept `Authorization: Bearer` is now exhaustive. Phase 4's
    `POST /api/upload` keeps the token model of §8.1 (token with scope `upload`, or a session).
20. **Public `failure_reason` has scratch paths redacted** (`internal/worker/pipeline.go`
    `redactPaths`): before `FailAttempt` stores the reason (§10.3's `stage: message`), the worker
    replaces the clip's scratch dir and, defensively, the scratch root with `…` – ffmpeg/ffprobe
    stderr echoes the input path (`$SCRATCH_DIR/{id}/source.ext`), and `failure_reason` is public to
    any clip-id holder via `GET /api/clips/{id}` and the progress `error`. The stderr tail (bounded by
    `transcode`'s `failureTail`) is otherwise stored verbatim, and the worker's failure log line
    (`clip failed` / `attempt failed; requeued`, keyed by clip id) carries the same text, so the
    operator loses nothing: the scratch layout is fixed and reconstructible from the id.
21. **`id_collision` cleanup is key-scoped** (`internal/httpapi/upload.go`): when `CreateClipWithJob`
    returns `db.ErrConflict` the clip prefix already belongs to the upload that won the id, so the
    loser's `abortUpload` removes only the object it wrote (`DeletePrefix(keys.Original)`; a key is
    its own prefix, §20.6) instead of `DeletePrefix(keys.Prefix)` – §8.3 step 8's "same cleanup" is
    narrowed to that. The winner's row and original are untouched when the extensions differ; when
    they coincide the loser's `PutFile` has already overwritten the winner's object (last writer wins)
    and only a conditional put could have prevented it – accepted at 71 bits of id entropy behind
    the `ClipExists` pre-check. `newClipID` (unexported, `= ids.New`) is the test seam that pins the
    id an upload draws.
22. **Share-page `IsOwner` is session-only** (`internal/web/server.go` `clipView`) — the HTML twin of
    erratum 19. `/clips/{id}` still runs the Resolver (the page is public and the header nav needs the
    session, so a Bearer token becomes a principal there too), but `IsOwner` — which gates the
    owner-private view count and the owner controls in `clip.html` — is computed from the **session**
    principal only (`sessionUser`), never from a token, mirroring `httpapi.clipDTO`. The §8.2 "session or
    token principal whose id equals `owner_id`" definition is superseded for the page exactly as erratum 19
    superseded it for the API; "a token never reveals the owner-private `views` count" now holds on every
    surface. E2E step 10 mints a token and asserts the share page shows it neither `data-views` nor
    `data-owner-controls`.
23. **Multi-range requests are capped at 8 range-specs** (`internal/httpapi/media.go` `maxRanges`,
    `rangeCount`): `serveObject` counts the non-empty range-specs of the `Range` header before
    `http.ServeContent` and answers more than 8 with **416** `range_not_satisfiable` (`Content-Range:
    bytes */size`, `no-store`, the §8 envelope, message "at most 8 ranges per request") — zero storage
    calls, GET and HEAD alike, on all four media routes. §8.5's "multi-range → one GET per range (accepted
    cost)" is amended to "accepted up to 8"; the §19 open item (a hostile client listing thousands of
    one-byte ranges to turn a kilobyte of header into thousands of sequential `GetRange` calls on the
    anonymous, un-rate-limited routes — reproduced at ~1.3 ms per range against local MinIO, a billed
    transaction each against R2/B2) is closed by exactly the remedy it named. RFC 9110 §14.2 permits
    rejecting "many small ranges"; real clients send one range (a seek) or two.
24. **The step-16 log gate keys on the level field** (`scripts/e2e.sh`): the §12 doctrine binds the
    *process's* log levels, and the gate that enforces it must read them, not hunt for a substring.
    `AccessLog` echoes the request path (quoted and escaped by slog, so no record is ever split or given a
    second `level=` token) into an INFO line, and any anonymous client can request
    `/x%20level=ERROR%20msg=y` or `/panic` — under the old `grep -E 'level=ERROR|"level":"ERROR"|panic'`
    that failed the gate, and on the shared stack a concurrent prober could fail another run's E2E at
    will. The gate now matches `(^|\| )time=… level=ERROR ` (slog's text handler always emits `time`,
    `level`, `msg` first; `(^|\| )` skips compose's `name | ` prefix), the JSON twin
    `{"time":"…","level":"ERROR"`, and the Go runtime's own `panic: ` / `fatal error: ` line starts
    (an unrecovered crash prints those with no slog record — the recovered ones log at ERROR and are
    caught by the level anchor), and self-tests the expression against planted and real samples before
    reading the log. Operators alerting on the log should key on the same field. The app is unchanged.
25. **The session cookie slides with the row** (`internal/auth/auth.go` `Resolver.Middleware`): §4 and
    §14 promise a sliding session ("Cookie `Max-Age` and DB `expires_at`; sliding"), but only `expires_at`
    slid — `SetSessionCookie` was called from register/login alone, so a browser discarded the cookie
    exactly `SESSION_TTL` after login however active the user was, and the DB slide was dead work for
    browser clients. When `resolveSession`'s once-a-minute touch extends `expires_at`, the Middleware
    re-issues the cookie on that same response — same value, `Max-Age = SESSION_TTL`, the §14 flags
    (`Secure` from `PUBLIC_BASE_URL`'s scheme, as at login) — at most once per minute per session and
    never for a token or anonymous request. `ClearSessionCookie` first drops a refresh queued on the
    same response, so logout never re-issues what it clears. Every route under the Resolver already
    answers `no-store` or `private` (§20.17; `/original` is `private` + `Vary: Cookie, Authorization` —
    true of its own 403/404 exits only from erratum 55, which closed that gap), so the header reaches no
    shared cache; `/static`, `/embed` and the public media routes bypass the Resolver and are unchanged.
26. **`source_filename` is capped at 255 runes** (`internal/httpapi/upload.go` `stripPath` →
    `truncateName`): §8.3 stores the "sanitized filename", and sanitising now includes a length bound.
    Go's `mime/multipart` accepts part headers up to 10 MiB, so one authenticated upload could store a
    multi-MiB `source_filename` that every `ClipDTO` echoed — the shared `GET /api/clips` library for
    every user, buffered whole by `TimeoutHandler` — and that `GET …/original` put into a
    `Content-Disposition` curl (exit 100) and browsers (256 KiB header limit) refuse, so the owner could
    not download that original. The stored name keeps its last path segment, drops controls and
    surrounding space as before, and is cut to 255 runes with a plausible extension (≤16 runes)
    preserved at the end; `defaultTitle` (200 runes) and `attachmentName` inherit the cap through
    `stripPath`. §8.1's `filename="<sanitized>"` and the §8.2 `source.filename` field are unchanged in
    shape.
27. **`check.sh` runs the §15 no-outbound-URL grep** (the stage §15 and §16.1 promised for Phase 2,
    which round 1 did not land): before the container build it greps every non-test `*.go`, `*.html`,
    `*.js` and `*.css` under `internal`, `cmd` and `web` for an `http(s)://` literal and fails on any
    hit, after a self-test that the expression flags a planted `a.go` and skips `a_test.go`. Tests,
    docs, `compose.yaml`, `Dockerfile`, `.env.example` and `scripts/` stay out of scope (they legitimately
    name `http://localhost:8080/healthz` and `http://minio:9000`, the self-healthcheck and the
    `S3_ENDPOINT` §15 permits). There is no allowlist today because nothing needs one (no `ogp.me` /
