242. **The theme is a cookie, read by the page handlers and rendered as `data-theme` on `<html>`**
    (**amended by erratum 288**: the top bar carries a second control for this cookie — a light/dark glyph — so `POST /settings/theme` is now ANONYMOUS and comes back to the page it was pressed on rather than to Settings; everything else below stands.)
    (`internal/web/theme.go`, `server.go` `page.Theme`/`basePage`, `pages.go` `embedPage.Theme`,
    `web/templates/base.html`, `embed.html`, `settings.html`, `app.js` `setupTheme`; DEPLOY.md §28;
    API.md "Pages"). Both themes are first class and the default is the operating system's, read by the
    stylesheet's `prefers-color-scheme` block; a person who wants the other one says so in Settings
    (System / Light / Dark) and the answer is the `theme` cookie — `light` | `dark`; absent or anything
    else = follow the system — `Path=/`, `SameSite=Lax`, `Secure` iff the public origin is https, one
    year, deliberately NOT `HttpOnly` because `app.js` writes it too, and no column and no migration: it
    is a fact about this browser, like the muted/loop preferences in localStorage. Server-rendering the
    attribute is what makes the choice paint with the first byte — no flash, and no inline script,
    which the CSP has no room for. The no-JavaScript half is `POST /settings/theme`
    (`theme=system|light|dark`, session-only, form-encoded, `form-action 'self'`): it sets or deletes
    the cookie and `303`s to `/settings#theme`; a value the control never writes is a 400; `GET` is a
    405. A cross-site POST could at worst change a theme. E2E steps 78–79.

243. **`font-src 'self'` joins both CSP strings** (`internal/httpx/middleware.go` `cspBase`,
    `httpx_test`). `default-src 'self'` already covered fonts by fallback; naming the directive is what
    makes the promise explicit now that the product ships faces of its own — Spline Sans and Spline
    Sans Mono, two variable latin-subset woff2 files under `web/static/fonts/` with the OFL text beside
    them, embedded by `web/static/embed.go` (`fonts` directory pattern) and served by the static handler,
    which now walks the embedded FS (`fs.WalkDir`) and sets `font/woff2` itself because the container
    has no mime table. `@font-face` with `font-display: swap` sits at the top of `app.css`; the fallback
    stacks are close enough that no layout depends on the webfont, and the wordmark's span is
    positioned in em so it survives a fallback face within a pixel. The running app never fetches a
    font from anywhere; E2E step 77 pins the stylesheet to no `http(s)://` and the faces to
    `/static/fonts/` with the static cache policy.

244. **"Delete after" is the grammar of every lifetime CHOICE, and a stranger's watch and collection
    pages carry the wordmark alone** (the owner's feature walk, 2026-09-10 — two reactions; `internal/web/server.go`
    `ttlOptions` and `page.Wordmark`, `pages.go` (the clip and collection handlers), `web/templates/base.html`,
    `index.html`, `settings.html`, `clip.html`, `app.css`, `web/STYLE.md`, E2E steps 47 and 77, DEPLOY §10/§20/§23,
    README; amends 240's "the visitor's watch page is … and nothing else" and §9's "no CTAs, no 'powered by'
    links on watch pages").
    (a) The owner's reading: "keep for … never" is not a sentence — it is keep forever or never delete, so the
    row should say "delete after". Wherever a lifetime is CHOSEN the
    row now reads `Delete after` and its options complete that sentence. The table, old → new: the upload form's
    row label `Keep for` → `Delete after`, its first option `Default (server: never)` → `server default · never`;
    Settings "Upload defaults" `Keep new clips for` → `Delete after`, `Server default (7 days)` → `server default
    · 7 days`; the bulk bar's unlabeled select (`aria-label="Keep for"`) + `Set lifetime` → a visible `Delete
    after` label, the select, a `Set` button; the owner's row `Lifetime` → `Delete after`, its no-op `Keep
    current` → `no change`; and the shared option list `Never (keep forever) · 1 day · 7 days · 30 days · 90
    days` → `1 day · 7 days · 30 days · 90 days · never` — `never` is the word, and it is LAST now, the far end
    of the scale (the bulk bar rests on its own `no change`, below). The wire contract
    is untouched: `ttl_days` absent = the server default, `0` = never (§8.2, §8.3), and the owner's first option
    still carries no `selected` (95(b)). Statements of FACT keep their own grammar where it already reads right:
    `expires <date>`, `expired <date> (pending deletion)`, `kept forever`, `23 days left`, the facts list's
    `Lifetime` line, the library row's line, and the trim readout's `keeps 3.3 s of 6.0` — a length, not a
    lifetime, and not in this change; `Keep forever` stays an action.
    (b) The owner's reading: the share page as a visitor sees it is good, but it carries no Clippet branding that
    leads to the site providing it; a simple logo pointing at the homepage, so people know who made it, is fine.
    §9's rule is amended by the owner for exactly this and nothing more: the share page and the collection page
    render `<header class="top">` with the wordmark ALONE — `cli<span class="pp">pp</span>et`, live text, the
    green span, 21 px, `href="/"` — for a session-less visitor (`page.Wordmark`, set by the two handlers;
    `base.html` renders the header when there is a viewer OR the flag, and the nav only for a viewer). Placement:
    the header slot, top-left above the player, not a footer line under the facts, because (1) it is where the
    wordmark is on every other page of the product, so a visitor who later has an account finds it where they
    left it, and a logged-in stranger already sees that band there — an anonymous page and a non-owner's page
    now differ only by the nav; (2) a line under the facts is the "made with" credit STYLE.md forbids — a header
    says "this is clippet", a footer says "made with clippet"; (3) above the player it is read before the clip
    plays and competes with nothing once the eye is on the player. No nav, no "sign up", no text beside it. The
    embed carries none (an iframe is someone else's page — superseded by erratum 246, which gives the embed
    the overlay); the card inventory (27 http / 28 https) is unchanged;
    nothing owner-private moves. Proven by `web_test` (the anonymous share page), `collection_test`,
    `watch_test` (the embed has none), E2E step 77 (which asserted the inverse before) and `visual.sh`.
    Amendments by name: 95(b)'s "Keep current" is now the option `no change` (same value "", same
    absence of `selected`, same rule); §7's route table reads the new option list. The fix pass after
    the verification changed two things: `.watch` is `align-content: start`, because it is on
    `<body>` (BodyClass) with `min-height: 100vh` and the new header made two grid rows that shared
    every spare viewport pixel (a 158 px band at 1280×900, 408 at 1512×1400); `visual.sh` now measures
    `header.top` on every shot (fails above 64 px) and adds a tall 1512×1400 shot of the stranger's
    page. And the bulk bar's select rests on its own `no change` option (value ""), which `app.js`
    refuses to send — `Number("")` is 0, and 0 is never — so a stray Set schedules nothing.

245. **The E2E harness schedules its bundles instead of sourcing them in order** (`scripts/e2e.sh`,
    `scripts/e2e.d/*.sh` headers, `scripts/e2e.d/README.md`; §16.3 amended). 79 serial curl steps took
    **1270 s** locally and 18–21 minutes over the tunnel, and every one of those minutes was spent one
    request at a time on a suite that is mostly independent bundles. The gate command does not change:
    `bash scripts/e2e.sh` with no environment is the whole suite, and it now runs the parallel-safe
    bundles concurrently.

    (a) **The scheduling model.** Every drop-in declares in its own header how it may be RUN:
    `# e2e-schedule: parallel lane=<n>` or `# e2e-schedule: exclusive`. **A file with no marker is
    exclusive**, and the harness prints a NOTE saying so — that is the default a new bundle keeps until
    somebody has read it. `run_dropins` starts one process per LANE (its bundles in name order, each in
    a subshell with a scratch context of its own under `.e2e/ctx-<stem>/` and a log of its own under
    `.e2e/bundle-<stem>.log`), waits for every lane, prints the per-bundle logs into the transcript in
    BUNDLE order so the record reads the same whichever lane finished first, waits for the live queue to
    go idle, and then sources the exclusive bundles one at a time into the harness's own shell exactly
    as it always did. `summary_row` writes to a file rather than to an array, because an array a
    subshell appended to is discarded with the subshell and the bundle's clips would vanish from the
    closing table.

    (b) **The safe/exclusive rule.** A bundle is `parallel` only when it creates its own clips and its
    own users and deletes them; reads the shared clips (A–E, W, X) and mutates none of them; restarts,
    recreates and reconfigures nothing (no second app process against this database, no account-wide
    setting); asserts nothing bucket-wide, log-wide or instance-wide (`admin stats`' clip and object
    counts, `admin orphans`' summary line, a listing of the whole of `/scratch`, the absence of a line
    over the whole app log); and probes no rate limiter. Six of the fourteen bundles fail that test and
    are exclusive: 33-account (it revokes every other session of the shared account and counts what
    went), 37-library (step 38 boots a SECOND app process against this database and may only do so while
    the queue is idle), 47-upload (step 47's cancel probe takes an instance-wide census of clips,
    objects and `/scratch`), 51-admin (a live `unstick` sweep, a throwaway instance, plants under the
    shared clip C and a bucket-wide orphans report), 55-owner (it drains the `view` limiter, changes the
    account's upload defaults and asserts a global notify count), 62-tiers (it drains the `poll`
    limiter) — and 61-nits2, which is safe in fact but asserts an absence over the whole app log and so
    keeps the default. **Seven run alone, seven run in lanes** (31-nits, 41-social, 43-watch,
    67-capture, 70-web, 73-ops, 77-design).

    (c) **Lanes, not a work pool.** Two bundles can each be safe and still fight over something neither
    is about. `internal/httpapi`'s `viewsPerMinute` (60) and `pollsPerMinute` (120) are per client
    ADDRESS and are compile-time constants no environment can raise, and every lane reaches the app from
    the same address: 70-web's filmstrip poll spends one `view` token a second and 43-watch's
    preview-GIF poll one every two, so they share lane 2 and never overlap. A lane is a promise about
    what does NOT run together, which a pool cannot make. `wait_ready` polls at `POLL_SLEEP`, which the
    scheduler sets to the number of lanes, keeping the whole run near one progress request a second
    whatever the width.

    (d) **The knobs**, all off or at their default unless asked for. `E2E_ONLY=<stems>` runs only those
    bundles on the minimal setup every drop-in depends on — steps 1–6, plus the second user and the
    shared capture clip X that steps 19 and 23 would otherwise have left behind — and ends in
    `E2E PASS (PARTIAL)` listing the steps and the bundles that did not run, because silent truncation
    reads as covered. `E2E_SKIP=<stems>` is its complement. A name in either that matches no drop-in is
    fatal before step 1. `E2E_LANES=N` (default 4) sets the width; `E2E_LANES=1` is the old serial order
    exactly. `E2E_SWEEP_INTERVAL` (default `15s` for a run, shipped default 60s) and
    `E2E_RATE_AUTH_PER_MIN` (default 120, shipped 10) join the upload limiters step 1 already raised, by
    the same mechanism and for the same reason: steps 14, 15 and 19 each wait for a sweeper TICK and
    assert what the sweeper DESTROYS rather than how often it looks, and nothing in the suite asserts
    the auth ceiling while four bundles logging in inside one minute would trip it. Step 17 hands all of
    them back.

    (e) **Two harness corrections that came with it.** Step 54's bucket-WIDE summary assertions
    (`extra=2 extra_bytes=`, `extra_deleted=1`) became a floor plus a per-key check — the report prints
    each key and then, indented, what it did with it, so the step now asserts that ITS rendition was
    deleted and ITS planted original was refused, which is stronger than the counts and immune to an
    aborted run's leftovers (the sweep recipe exists because those equalities failed on
    somebody else's litter). And `get`/`page`/`head_` retry ONCE, after 3 s and with a line saying so, on
    curl exits 7/28/35 — the three that mean no answer came back — while `http` does NOT, because those
    are the writes and a timed-out POST may have landed. `dc` retries once on exit 125, docker's own
    failure code, which no `clippet` exit can be confused with.

    (f) **What did not move.** Not one assertion was weakened, and the `has_file`/`expect`/`die` site
    count across `scripts/e2e.d/` is unchanged in twelve of the fourteen files. Two moved, and both are
    accounted for. **51-admin** gained three (two bucket-wide `has_file` equalities out, five scoped
    checks in — see (e)). **41-social** LOST three, which is not a loss: `wait_social` moved bodily into
    `scripts/e2e.sh` and took its two `expect`s and its `die` with it, so the SUITE's total is unchanged
    and those assertions now run for 62-tiers as well. That move, and two like it, are why: a bundle
    that runs in a lane runs in a subshell and its definitions go with it, so `wait_trim` left step 21
    (41-social and 47-upload call it, and a filtered run does not execute step 21) and `wait_social` and
    `prefix_names` left 41-social.sh (62-tiers calls both, which worked only while every drop-in was
    sourced into one shell in name order). A helper a second file needs belongs to the harness; the rule
    is in `e2e.d/README.md`.
    73-ops's step 73 is the ONE step content the schedule forced, and it is a poll replacing an
    assumption. Its second half — "the repairer left its OWN live encode alone" — needs that encode to
    be BOTH past the 30 s repair age and still running at the moment it is read, and the step read it
    whenever the loop watching the OTHER process's repair happened to exit. On an idle box that is 28 s
    into the repairer's encode (under the age, so the assertion proves nothing) and on a busy box it is
    after the encode has finished (so there is nothing to read); both were observed on this machine, in
    that order, and each failed loudly and correctly. The probe now polls its own age past the floor,
    waits one further repair tick, and reads the answer then — and encodes at `placebo` rather than
    `veryslow`, which the comment had described as "minutes of work" while it finished in 29 s. The
    encode is killed a few lines later, so the slower preset costs the run nothing. `expect_prefix_count`'s fixed `sleep 3` became a bounded poll, and
    73-ops's `sleep 22` for a second sweep tick became a poll for that tick. The remaining fixed sleeps
    are deliberate and stay: the `sleep 1.2` in steps 23 and 37 (a courtesy that makes two `created_at`
    values differ, documented as not a guarantee), 47-upload's `sleep 3` for a handler cleanup that has
    no observable, 70-web's `sleep 6` for an object to age past `--min-age` (the fact is not readable —
    a REFERENCED object is not reported at any age), 51-admin's `sleep 25` for the unstick floor, which
    is a wait for a threshold and not for a state, and the `sleep 9` step 73 gained, which is a wait for
    an EVENT NOT to happen — a whole repair tick (`every=7.5s`) during which the repairer must leave its
    own past-the-age job alone. There is nothing to poll for the absence of a thing; the wait IS the
    assertion's window, and it is bounded by the tick it is derived from.

    **Measured**, same box, same stack: **1270 s** before the pass, **1339 s** with this harness at
    `E2E_LANES=1` (the control), **1163 s and 1143 s** on two consecutive default runs, and **79 s** for
    one bundle (`E2E_ONLY=70-web,77-design`, which is what the filter is for). Against its own control
    the schedule is −186 s (−14%): the parallel phase is 253 s and does what those seven bundles need
    445 s to do one at a time. What it cannot touch is the exclusive phase, ~680 s, and two lines
    dominate that: 62-tiers's step 66 and 55-owner's step 56 each hammer a route until a rate limiter
    refuses — 125 s and 86 s, a sixth of the run, spent proving two ceilings — while 73-ops (255 s) fills
    a lane on its own. Every one of those is a step's own design and not the scheduler's to fix.
    The ceiling on the rest is the deployment, not the harness: `compose.yaml` ships `cpus: 1.0` and
    `TRANSCODE_CONCURRENCY: 1`, so every live transcode in the suite runs one at a time on one core
    whatever the lane width. Parallelism buys back the host-side work — fixture builds, container
    spawns, `dc exec` round trips, page and media assertions — and not the encoder.

    (g) **At four cpus** (2026-09-10; the owner's call: at least four cpus on the reference box even though
    the shipped default is 1 — `APP_CPUS=4` in the reference stack's `.env`, the shipped default unchanged,
    `TRANSCODE_CONCURRENCY` still 1, `TRANSCODE_THREADS=0` resolving to 4). **Measured on the reference
    stack over the quick tunnel: 772 s** against 859 s at one cpu on the same harness and origin (the
    parallel phase 245 s against 256 s; the 150 s 720p60 sample's Light copy 22 s, the capture link back
    `card_ready: true` in 26 s — DEPLOY §27). The suite moved by a tenth because it is mostly requests;
    the encodes inside it moved by four, and THAT broke three steps that had passed every gate at one
    cpu, none of them a product bug: (1) step 21 fires eight "simultaneous" trims at a 6 s clip, and
    they arrive through a tunnel staggered over ~0.5 s while the trim now re-encodes in 0.4 s, so a
    late loser is refused as "the cut this clip already has" — a 400, not the 409 the step demanded of
    every loser. The step now accepts that as the second honest shape of losing (its message pinned)
    and still demands exactly one 202, which is what the guarded INSERT promises; it prints the split
    and a NOTE when no loser saw the trim in flight. (2) Step 72 needs two clips in flight and used a 15 s
    720p60 mp4 as "a real encode on one core": at four cpus it was repacked and its card copy encoded in
    under three seconds, and the second clip's 24 MB upload alone took half of that — its POST landed
    40 ms before the first clip went ready. The fixture is now 30 s of 10-bit 720p60 (a pixel format no
    browser plays, so the server owes a Full re-encode at the source's own resolution AND the Light
    copy, on any core count) capped at 1.5 Mbps (≈6 MB, so the wire is not the wait), and the two POSTs
    fire from two background curls at once so the second clip is queued for the whole of the first
    encode; both halves were then seen on the first poll. (3) Step 53's probe slept a fixed 25 s between
    the too-young refusals and the sweep, and the Docker VM clock stepped BACKWARDS by 27 s inside that
    sleep (the seconds-scale clock trap; the offset then held steady), so the sweep's own `now` put
    the killed job's `started` in the future and repaired nothing — the clock's verdict, not the
    repair's. The probe now polls the age the CLI itself prints (`running_for=`) past the 20 s floor,
    bounded at 120 s, before it sweeps: this erratum's polls-not-sleeps rule applied to the one sleep
    that hid inside a `sh -c` script. Two more attempts died on the tunnel, not the stack (a known trap:
    an early 4xx on a POST whose body is still in flight comes back as a tunnel-made 5xx; the tunnel was
    recreated after the second). Not one assertion was weakened: step 21's winner count and step 72's
    two observations are unchanged, and step 53 asserts the same repair against the same floor.

    **Amended 2026-09-15 — checkpoints, `E2E_RESUME`, and a bundle that fails without ending the run** (`scripts/e2e.sh`,
    the owner's two questions: why a run re-proves the first sixty steps when the code has not changed between runs, and
    why one failed block stops the whole suite).
    The SEVENTH GATE's public E2E died six times on six different things — four harness assumptions of the bundled-MinIO shape
    surfaced one at a time by the R2 switch, two edge transients — and each attempt re-ran up to 89 passed steps to reach the
    one that had changed, because the gate was "one uninterrupted run" and the run stopped at the first failure. Three changes,
    none of which weakens an assertion: (1) **checkpoints** — every bundle that passes is recorded (`.e2e/checkpoints/<key>__<origin>.txt`,
    one `<stem>	PASS	<utc>` line) under a key naming the PRODUCT tree — `git ls-tree HEAD` over `internal cmd web go.mod go.sum
    Dockerfile compose.yaml`, what the binary and the image are built from; a harness edit does not move it, an uncommitted change
    under those paths makes it `-dirty` and records nothing — and the origin under test; (2) **`E2E_RESUME=1`** runs the core
    (steps 1–30, which make every fixture) and only the bundles NOT recorded as passed on that key at that origin, and its banner
    reads `E2E PASS (RESUMED)` naming the bundles credited from earlier runs — **the union is the gate** when nothing the binary is
    built from changed between those passes and this run, which the key proves; a full run is owed only when the product tree
    moves; (3) **a failed bundle is recorded, its checkpoint forgotten, and the run goes on** — lane bundles already ran in
    subshells, the exclusive ones now do too (`( . bundle; step_close_ )`; nothing a bundle sets in the shell is read by a later
    one, which the README's conventions and check.sh's helper scan keep so) — so one run reports EVERY failed bundle in its
    closing `E2E FAIL … bundle(s) failed:` banner and exits 1, after step 16's log gate and step 17's cleanup have still run.
    The core's own steps stay fatal: a fixture that was not made cannot be worked around. Proven the same night: the SEVENTH
    GATE's leg 2 became attempt 6's 19 passed bundles + the step-90 partial + one resumed run (core + `31-nits` in a lane +
    `85-bot` exclusive, 442 s) on product tree `e3831c3c16d0`, `E2E PASS (RESUMED)`, zero ERROR/panic.

    **Amended 2026-10-05 — lane `speed2`: the lanes become a pool that scales to the box** (`scripts/e2e.sh`, the drop-in headers,
    `scripts/e2e.d/README.md`; the owner's ask: every stage as parallel as it can be, scaled to the resources available).
    (c)'s fixed lanes made two promises with one number — "these never overlap" and "these queue" — and the second capped the
    phase at four whatever the machine (lane 4 queued eleven bundles, 219 s, while lanes 1-3 idled). The width is now `E2E_LANES`,
    defaulting to half the CPUs within 2..6 and printed at step 1; the parallel bundles are handed out LONGEST FIRST from
    `.e2e/checkpoints/durations.txt` (the last passing run's seconds; one file per origin since lane `nits7`,
    `durations__<BASE>.txt`, so a lane stack's seconds never order a clippet.gg run — an old unkeyed file is simply not read) by a
    pool that starts each the moment a slot frees and nothing
    it is declared apart from is running; the overlap promise is spelled `# e2e-schedule-apart: <stem>` (four pairs — the `view`
    and `claim` buckets, 67-capture's load sensitivity, 91-drop/95-import; still four after lane `excl`, whose `burst_429 … apart`
    is a different thing that shares the word: a limiter drain fired from another ADDRESS, not a scheduling pair), `after` is
    honoured by waiting, `lane=<n>` is refused.
    `wait_ready`'s pacing comes from the number of polling bundles (≤ 1.5 progress requests a second). `E2E_OVERLAP=1` starts the
    pool after step 26 — the core's last instance-wide assertion, so no earlier start is correct — and is opt-in because it measured
    nothing (775 s against 774/774/775). Measured on a lane stack at `APP_CPUS=4`: the full E2E 880 s → 774/774/775 s (three green
    runs; parallel phase 221 → 155 s, the core 244 → 210-228 s from polls that wait on the event at 0.5-1 s instead of 2-5 s);
    the width curve 162/155/157/151 s at 4/6/8/12, floored by 73-ops alone. No assertion changed.

    **Amended 2026-10-06 — lane `excl`: the exclusive phase shrunk to one bundle** (`scripts/e2e.sh`, eight drop-in headers and
    bodies, `scripts/e2e.d/README.md` "The exclusive phase, read bundle by bundle"; the owner's ask carried from lane `speed2`). The
    nine exclusive bundles were read for WHY and each reason was removed where it could be without weakening anything: (1) an
    ACCOUNT-WIDE change of the run's owner (33-account's password and sessions, 55-owner step 57's upload defaults, 82-links
    step 83's default grammar) is done to an account of the bundle's own — `bundle_account <suffix>` registers
    `${E2E_USER}_<suffix>` (a name erratum 272's sweep admits; the helper refuses any other) and the harness's `upload`
    honours `UPLOAD_JARW`; (2) a LIMITER DRAIN (55-owner's `view`, 62-tiers' `poll`) is fired by `burst_429 … apart` from a
    throwaway container of the stack's compose project at the live app's service address — the same process, ceiling, route
    and query, from an address nothing else in the run uses, since every bucket is keyed by the client's address; (3) a second
    `serve` on the LIVE database or an instance-wide CENSUS (37-library step 38, 47-upload's cancel, 55-owner steps 59-60)
    moves onto an instance of its own (its own DATA_DIR, SCRATCH_DIR, S3_KEY_PREFIX and STORAGE_DIR, media pinned to proxy;
    89-quota's shape), which makes the census and 55-owner's notify count EXACT on every stack; (4) a shared clip a bundle
    planted under (51-admin step 54's C) becomes a clip of its own; (5) 61-nits2's log-wide absence is of a BOOT line of the
    stack's process, which no parallel bundle restarts. 87-storage stays exclusive: its subject is the stack's one
    served-bytes counter behind its own origin, which a probe instance cannot stand in for. The marker → phase rule is a pure
    function (`dropin_phase_`) and the self-test pins it on planted files, pins that every drop-in declares a phase and that
    the exclusive set is exactly `87-storage`, and pins the `apart` address mapping and `bundle_account`'s refusal. One
    timing-shaped assertion the wider pool exposed was fixed: 67-capture's crawler hold judges each answer AFTER reading the
    clip's `card_ready` (it only goes false → true). Measured on a lane stack at `APP_CPUS=4`, warm durations: the full E2E
    1006 s (core 321 | parallel 175 | exclusive 510) → 581 s on the same box state (core 268 | parallel 281 | exclusive 31), and 380 s on the final tree after a PC reboot (187 | 164 | 29); E2E_RESUME green (181 s, every bundle credited); `E2E_LANES=8` once 557 s, not
    shipped (inside one run's noise, every large bundle slower, and the race above). The default width stays half the CPUs, 2..6.

    **Amended 2026-10-08 — run 9: T2 is the one full run** (erratum 331). Where this erratum and its amendments say the
    whole suite is the gate and "a full run is owed only when the product tree moves", read instead: **T2 is the one full
    run, owed at a release, a shape change, a nightly slot or the owner's word**. It is `bash scripts/gate.sh` on the local
    `clippet-gate` stack, never per lane and never per merge. A lane's proof is T1 (`scripts/t1.sh`, `E2E_ONLY` sized to its
    diff by `scripts/select.sh`), and the public origin's is T3 (`scripts/smoke-public.sh`) after a deploy. The union rule
    of the 2026-09-15 amendment stands inside T2.

246. **A front door for strangers at `/`, and the wordmark on the embed player** — **the overlay is
    AMENDED by §20 erratum 287(d) (2026-09-15): it now reads this instance's own public host**, as
    the lockup on `clippet.gg` and any subdomain of it and as plain text anywhere else; its one shadow
    became two layers so it survives a white frame; and it moved to the top-LEFT, because 287(e) put
    the clip's duration in the top-right of every poster and at 400 × 225 the two printed on top of
    each other. Its size and its 10 px / 12 px insets are untouched, as is everything about the front
    door. (ROADMAP #36, the owner's
    walk reactions of 2026-09-10 and the four answers; `internal/web/server.go` (`pageNames`),
    `pages.go` (`frontPage`, `front`, `index`), `web/templates/front.html` (new), `embed.html`,
    `web/static/app.css` (`.front`, `.embed-mark`, `body.embed[data-playing]`), `app.js`
    (`setupClipPage`'s embed branch), `web/STYLE.md`, E2E steps 80–81 (`scripts/e2e.d/80-front.sh`,
    new) and 77 (amended), `scripts/lib/visual.js`, DEPLOY §17.3/§20/§28, API.md "Pages", README).
    the owner's three questions: whether the homepage, which may be the sign-in page for now, should link
    anywhere; whether a simple homepage with a login endpoint would solve it; and whether the embed could
    carry some simple branding, so that someone
    likes our embed they'll know who to try / use?" — and, to the four-point summary: "1) lgtm yeah",
    "2) defer repo link for now, it's a private link anyway", "3) cool do that", "4) fine for now".
    (a) **The front door.** `GET /` without a session is a **200** now, not `303 /login?next=/`: a page
    in the auth layout (`<section class="auth front">`) carrying the display wordmark (40 px, the same
    `<span class="wordmark display">` `login.html` renders), ONE line — "Upload a clip. Get a link." (the
    third clause, "It plays in Discord.", was dropped by erratum 264) — one ink button **Log in** →
    `/login`, and **Create an account** → `/register`
    only while `registrationOpen(r)` is true, read exactly as `login` reads it. Nothing else: no feature
    list, no screenshots, no marketing voice, no header slot (`page.Wordmark` stays false: the page IS
    the front door, and a wordmark linking to `/` on `/` is noise), no card meta (it is not a clip), no
    `noindex` (it is the one page a stranger may be sent to). `<title>` is the product name. The
    response carries the headers the redirect it replaced carried — `private, no-store` + `Vary:
    Cookie` (erratum 37): WHICH page `/` renders depends on the cookie, and a shared cache that stored
    the stranger's page would hand it to a session. A session lands on the library exactly as before;
    `/login` and `?next=` are untouched; `HEAD /` works and `POST /` is still 405; a resolver failure is
    still the 503 page (`resolved` runs first). Why a page and not the login form: the stranger's
    wordmark of erratum 244 pointed at `/`, which then bounced to a form — the one page the brand led to
    said nothing about the brand. This amends erratum 106 only in what the page shows (`Create an
    account` follows the same flag on one more page) and §9's route table (one row for the no-session
    case). (b) **The embed overlay.** §9's "no CTAs, no 'powered by' links on watch pages" is amended
    by the owner for the embed the way 244 amended it for the share page, and for exactly this much:
    `/embed/{id}` renders, after the player (or the `.embed-status` frame — a poster-less black box is
    exactly where a viewer wonders whose player it is), ONE link, `<a class="wordmark embed-mark"
    href="/clips/{id}" target="_top" rel="noopener" aria-label="clippet">cli<span class="pp">pp</span>et</a>`
    — the same live-text lockup as every page, 16 px, **top-right** (`position: absolute; top: 10px;
    right: 12px`), relative href (it resolves against the embed document's own origin, which is ours,
    and can never be mixed content), `target="_top"` because an iframe cannot navigate itself out; the
    share page then carries 244's wordmark to `/`, so two clicks reach the front door. **Visible on the
    poster and while paused, hidden while playing** (the owner's default; no low-opacity variant until
    asked): `app.js` sets `data-playing` on `body.embed` from the video's own `play`/`pause`/`ended`
    events — starting from the player's real state, because an autoplaying embed may be playing before
    the deferred script runs — and one rule, `body.embed[data-playing] .embed-mark { display: none }`,
    does the rest; no style attribute, no timer, the CSP untouched. Why top-right: the native controls
    own the bottom band (48 px at Discord/X sizes, ≥ 400 × 225) and the top-left is where a browser's
    own status text and the "Processing…" line sit, so the top-right corner is the one that is clear of
    both by construction; at 400 × 225 the mark's box ends 26 px down. Colour: the ground here is always
    the player's black whatever the page theme, so the mark uses the dark palette's text and green
    outright (`#ECE9E2`, `#4CD69A` — STYLE.md's colour law, green = the wordmark's span) and a
    one-pixel `text-shadow`, the one shadow in the system, because the ink rule cannot apply on top of a
    poster's pixels. No text beside it, no play count, no "sign up". UNCHANGED, and asserted rather than

    stands: no watermark on any tier beyond the Light tag (214), no analytics on the front page, no CTA

    … an iframe is someone else's page") and `TestEmbedReady`'s `<a ` are now "the overlay and nothing
    else" (exactly one `<a `, no `<header`, no `<nav`, no absolute href); `TestEmbedNonReadyStates`

    `<nav`); step 11's "no inline style" holds; `visual.js`'s "no face is ever fetched on the embed"
    exemption flipped (Spline Sans MUST load there now), the embed is shot at 400 × 225 as well as the
    two widths with a DOM assertion that the mark's box lies inside the frame and above the bottom

247. **The GPU flavour, proven in a container: the `video` driver capability, and an override file instead
    of a profile (2026-09-10; amends 216).**

    **The proof ran** (the owner's GPU proof, after a reboot): `nvidia-smi -L` in a CUDA container lists
    the RTX 5090, and the 60 s 1080p60 sample through the app's own CUDA argv inside the `gpu` image —
    hardware decode, `scale_cuda`, `h264_nvenc`, the `h264_metadata` stamp, no override of any kind —
    completes: Full (1920×1080@60, `-cq 22`) **12.25 s, 229.6 MB**; Light (1280×720@30, `-cq 34`)
    **8.26 s, 12.3 MB**; both probe `bt709` on all three colour fields; the bytes match 216's calibration.
    The same sample in the ORDINARY image at four cpus (libx264 veryfast, `-threads 4`): Full **29.0 s**,
    Light **12.65 s**. So the card is **2.4× / 1.5×** against four cores in a container, not the 9–11×
    erratum 216 measured host-native at one cpu: Docker Desktop's WSL2 GPU path (a paravirtualised device)
    costs more per frame than a native driver, and the hardware decode plus download alone is ~6.5 s of
    the Light figure. The one-ffmpeg dual output (217) pays that decode once for both tiers. Live through
    the app on the reference stack: see the line DEPLOY §27's table carries for the 150 s 720p60 sample
    at `APP_CPUS=4` + cuda.

    **What blocked it was not the driver update.** Erratum 216 blamed "a stale WSL driver injection …
    cured by a Docker Desktop restart"; after the reboot the failure was identical: `Cannot load
    libnvcuvid.so.1`. The cause: the CUDA base image sets `NVIDIA_DRIVER_CAPABILITIES=compute,utility`,
    and the container runtime injects ONLY those driver libraries; NVDEC/NVENC (`libnvcuvid.so.1`,
    `libnvidia-encode.so.1`) are behind the **`video`** capability. `nvidia-smi` passes (utility), the
    `ffcaps` boot check passes (ffmpeg LISTS `h264_nvenc` whether or not the library it dlopens at run
    time is present), and every hardware decode dies at the first frame. The `gpu` Dockerfile target now
    sets `ENV NVIDIA_DRIVER_CAPABILITIES=compute,utility,video`; the run above used the rebuilt image
    with no `-e` override. A boot check cannot catch this class (the listing is static); DEPLOY §27
    names the failure line an operator would see instead.

    **The profile became an override file.** `compose.yaml`'s `app-gpu` (an `extends` sibling in profile
    `gpu`, sharing `app`'s port and volumes) could not be a long-lived deployment: every plain
    `docker compose up -d` — the E2E's steps 1 and 17, §16's upgrade checklist, an operator's habit —
    starts `app` back against it, and the two fight for the port and `/data`. Now **`compose.gpu.yaml`
    overrides the ONE `app` service** (build target `gpu`, tag `CLIPPET_GPU_IMAGE`, `gpus: all`), selected
    in `.env` by `COMPOSE_FILE=compose.yaml:compose.gpu.yaml` plus `COMPOSE_PATH_SEPARATOR=:` (so the line
    reads the same on Windows, whose default separator is `;` — verified both ways on Docker Desktop, and
    from `.env`). Every command, script and log name stays `app`; without the line nothing GPU is resolved
    or pulled. `.env.example`, DEPLOY §27 and §4's compose-only knobs carry the recipe; the `app-gpu`
    service, the `gpu` profile and the `--profile gpu up app-gpu` recipe are gone.

    **the reference stack runs it** (`.env`: `APP_CPUS=4` + the three lines; boot line `hwaccel=cuda`;
    `docker inspect` shows the device request and the 4-cpu quota — the owner's call for that box, the shipped
    defaults stay CPU at 1.0). The gate that follows this erratum proves the 81-step E2E, `check.sh` and
    the visual pass on the CUDA path, fallbacks included (216: interlaced/HDR/rotated/anamorphic sources
    take the CPU argv on the same binary).

    **One more fallback, found by the same proof: what NVDEC cannot decode.** `-hwaccel cuda` on a source
    the hardware decoder does not take (a 10-bit High 10 H.264 — exactly what E2E step 72's fixture and a
    capture card write — ProRes, DNxHD, FFV1, any 4:4:4) is not an error: ffmpeg decodes it in software
    without a word, the frames sit in system memory, and `scale_cuda` fails the run with a zero-byte file
    (proven in the gpu image). `Plan` now carries `SourceCodec`/`SourcePixFmt` from the probe and
    `HWAccelFor` refuses with `hwWhyDecoder` unless the codec is one NVDEC decodes AND the pixel format is
    8-bit 4:2:0 (`yuv420p`, `yuvj420p`, `nv12`); empty fields (a plan built without a probe) are unknown,
    not refused, so no CPU argv changes. A 10-bit HEVC/VP9/AV1 source could take the card with a device
    format conversion; not built (a cleanup row). Live through the app on the reference stack the 150 s 720p60
    sample's Light copy took **14 s** (22 s at four cpus on the CPU image); DEPLOY §27's table has the row.

    **The harness on the GPU flavour.** E2E step 73's probe slows the repairer's own encode with
    `TRANSCODE_PRESET=placebo` so it outlasts the 30 s repair age, and step 53's with `veryslow` past a 20 s
    hard timeout; a `compose run` probe inherits the service's `TRANSCODE_HWACCEL=cuda` and the card, NVENC
    knows no x264 preset, R's encode took 7 s, and step 73 died on the empty `running_for` it exists to read.
    Both probes now pin `TRANSCODE_HWACCEL=` (the CPU argv) — they are about the repairer and the CLI, not
    the encoder. The 245 (g) lesson again: a faster encoder breaks a timing assumption the harness never
    knew it had.

248. **The share link is the id at the ROOT of the origin, and `/clips/{id}` is a permanent redirect**
    (ROADMAP #35, the owner's decision of 2026-09-09 after buying `clippet.gg`: a share link is
    `clippet.gg/{id}`, the id at the ROOT, with no `/clips/` and no `/share/`). A share URL is
    `{PUBLIC_BASE_URL}/{id}`, rendered by `urls.Builder.Page` and by nothing else — so every place that
    emits one moved together: `ClipDTO.urls.page` and `UploadDTO.url`, `og:url` and the canonical link,
    the copy-link control, the library and collection rows, the embed overlay's href (erratum 246 had
    hard-coded `/clips/{id}`; it takes `embedPage.PageURL` now), `notify.Content`'s Discord post, the
    `.sxcu` reply's `{json:url}`, and the phone share target's 303. `GET /{id}` serves exactly what
    `/clips/{id}` served — the same handler, the same owner/stranger/crawler-hold/`NoIndex` rules, the
    same headers — and `HEAD` with it. **`/clips/{id}` answers 308**, not 301: 308 is method-preserving,
    a 301 permits a client to turn a HEAD (which the unfurlers and every uptime checker send) into a
    GET, and Discord, X, Slack and Facebook all follow permanent redirects when they unfurl, so a card
    link pasted a year ago still resolves to the page with the tags on it. The redirect reads NO row:
    every `ids.Valid` id redirects whether or not a clip exists, so it cannot be used to probe which
    ids do, and the hop lands on the same 404 the root form gives directly (E2E step 84 compares the
    two bodies byte for byte). It preserves the query string and is `public, max-age=3600` — a pure
    function of the path, with no session, no row and no clock in it — EXCEPT on a response carrying a
    `Set-Cookie`, which is `private, no-store` + `Vary: Cookie`: the route runs under the Resolver so a
    logged-in caller's 404 still has its nav (§9's rule for the catch-all), and the Resolver's sliding
    touch writes the refreshed cookie onto whatever response it is on — a shared cache storing THAT
    publicly would hand one person's session to the next caller. Erratum 207 made the same call on
    `/original`, for the same reason. `/embed/{id}`, `/c/{id}` and every
    `/api/…` path are UNCHANGED (ROADMAP #35 says so; a collection is not a clip and the two spaces stay
    separate). **Precedence.** `/{id}` matches every single-segment path, so what keeps `/login` a login
    form is the Go 1.22 mux's specificity rule, and what keeps THAT true is a test:
    `internal/web`'s `TestRootIDDoesNotShadowALiteralRoute` is a table over every pattern the page mux
    registers — checked against the patterns the mux actually recorded, so adding a route without adding
    a row fails. A single segment that is NOT an id is the 404 page for every method, deliberately
    including POST: `getOnly` would have answered 405 `Allow: GET, HEAD` for `/nope`, telling a scanner
    that every one-segment path is a route and changing an answer `/` had always given (`server.share`
    checks the id before the method for exactly this, and says so). **Reserved words at mint time.**
    `ids.Reserved` is the first path segment of every route the app registers — `api c clips embed
    favicon.ico healthz login manifest.webmanifest oembed readyz register robots.txt settings static` —
    in ONE place that both the minter and two router tests read; `internal/web` and `internal/httpapi`
    each record what their mux registered and assert every literal segment is in it. Neither grammar can
    reach the check today (no route is twelve base62 characters or three capitalised words), so it is
    proven with a rigged generator instead. **`robots.txt`** was `Disallow: /clips/ /c/ /embed/` +
    `Allow: /$`, which with the id at the root would have closed nothing at all; it is now
    `Disallow: /` plus `Allow` for `/$`, `/login`, `/register` and `/static/`, with the four unfurler
    groups' empty `Disallow` unchanged. It reads as a closed site because this IS one — everything else
    here is somebody's private link — and neither mechanism is a security control, exactly as erratum
    94 said.

249. **A second id grammar: memorable ids from the EFF long word list** (ROADMAP #35). `internal/ids`
    now mints two shapes. **compact** is unchanged and remains THE default: twelve base62 characters,
    ≈71.4 bits, and the owner's rule that it needs no rate limit at all. **memorable** is three or four
    words from the curated EFF long word list, each capitalised and joined without separators
    (`PurpleUpdateCharacter`), drawn with `crypto/rand` and rejection sampling exactly as the base62
    sampler is — one width up, because 7,772 needs thirteen bits: a two-byte draw is accepted below
    62,176, the largest multiple of the list length that fits in 16 bits, then reduced modulo it. The
    list ships inside the binary (`go:embed` of `internal/ids/eff_large_wordlist.txt`, one word per
    line) and is CURATED by `^[a-z]{3,9}$`, which drops the four hyphenated entries of the published
    7,776 (`drop-down`, `felt-tip`, `t-shirt`, `yo-yo`) and leaves **7,772** — so the entropy this
    build actually ships is **log2(7772³) ≈ 38.77 bits** for three words and **log2(7772⁴) ≈ 51.70** for
    four, which is what ROADMAP #35's "39 bits / 52 bits" meant. Word list: EFF large wordlist,
    CC BY 3.0; the credit is in the package doc and beside the control on `/settings`, and there is
    **no LICENSE file in the repository** (the owner's decision of 2026-09-08: all rights reserved for now; erratum 353 records the licence chosen since).
    `ids.Valid` is now the union `^[A-Za-z0-9]{12}$` OR `^(?:[A-Z][a-z]{2,8}){3,4}$` — scanned, not
    matched: an uppercase letter opens a word and the lowercase run closes it, so the split is unique
    and one pass decides it with no regexp and no allocation. Every `{id}` route, both scratch janitors
    and `db.ClipExists` accept both shapes by construction, and `.upload-{id}` stays outside `ids.Valid`
    on its leading dot exactly as before (`scratch_test` now draws both grammars).
    `ids.Kind(id)` reports which grammar an id is in and **nothing is stored** — the id is the fact, and
    a column that could disagree with it would be a second, worse one. The two grammars OVERLAP:
    `AbcAbcAbcAbc` is both twelve base62 characters and four capitalised triples. Exactly eleven
    twelve-character shapes qualify (3+3+3+3, and the ten ways three words of 3-9 characters sum to 12),
    each drawn with probability (26/62)^12, so a random compact draw hits one about once in 3,000;
    `ids.New` puts such draws back — costing the compact grammar 0.0005 of a bit — and `Kind` is
    therefore exact for every id this build mints. An id minted BEFORE this erratum is compact and
    carries that same one-in-3,000 chance of reading as memorable; the only consequence is one
    true-but-irrelevant line on its owner's own page.

250. **`link_style` — per upload, with an account default, mirroring `ttl_days`/`unlisted`** (ROADMAP
    #35). Migration **0015** adds `users.default_link_style TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'compact'` — 0011's
    shape with one difference: two states and no NULL, because there is no instance knob for a null to
    defer to and "no preference" and "compact" would be the same answer if there were.
    `GET/PATCH /api/auth/me/settings` gain `default_link_style`; a value outside the closed set is
    **400 `invalid_link_style`**, the one code every route that takes the field answers with, and a JSON
    `null` reads as absent like `default_unlisted`'s. `POST /api/clips` takes `link_style` in its
    metadata JSON and `POST /api/upload` takes it as a text field before the file part, under the same
    rules `ttl_days` has had since erratum 58 (any order, ≤ the field caps, an EMPTY value means "not
    sent", the form field is trimmed and the JSON one is not). The resolution order is the house one,
    in the one place both routes run: **FIELD SENT > ACCOUNT DEFAULT > `compact`** (`applyDefaults`).
    **The capture endpoint and the phone share target therefore FOLLOW THE ACCOUNT** — the shipped
    `clippet.sxcu` has no argument for the field and sends none. The word COUNT is a product rule and
    lives in `httpapi.newClipID`, not in `internal/ids`: three words for a listed clip, **four when the
    clip is uploaded unlisted**, where the link is the only authentication (the owner's rule: compact needs no
    rate limit at all; three words are public-clip grade; four are unlisted grade — and so **no new
    rate limit was added**). The id is therefore minted AFTER `unlisted` is resolved, which is why
    `pickClipID` takes the resolved meta; the §7 collision loop (`ClipExists` ≤3, then 500
    `id_collision`) covers both grammars unchanged. The upload form and `/settings` each get one
    two-option control in the `label | control | state` row grammar (`.seg` radios, so the
    no-JavaScript form posts the field like every other), the upload one starting on the account's own
    default — which is also what silence would resolve to, so changing nothing changes nothing.

251. **A memorable clip flipped to unlisted keeps its id** — and, until erratum 264 withdrew it,
    **its owner got one line** (ROADMAP #35). **The second half is WITHDRAWN by erratum 264**
    (the owner's rejection of that copy): no page renders that sentence for anybody now, and `clipPage`
    carries no `LinkStyle`. The FIRST half — an id is an address and a later flip re-mints
    nothing — stands, and so does `ClipDTO.link_style`, which is now a wire fact no page spends.
    What 251 shipped, for the record:
    An id is an ADDRESS: every link already sent names it, so `PATCH {"unlisted":true}` re-mints
    nothing — a three-word id stays three words. What changes is one plain line on the OWNER's share
    page, in the facts list: `Link — Memorable links are easier to guess.` It is rendered only when the
    id is memorable AND the clip is unlisted; a stranger never sees it (the whole row is owner-only),
    and it carries no warning colour, because nothing has gone wrong — four words is what an unlisted
    memorable link is worth and the owner is entitled to know the number is smaller. A memorable clip
    that is LISTED carries the row `hidden`, so `app.js` reveals it the moment Save flips the switch
    without a reload; a COMPACT clip has no such element at all, so the sentence is absent rather than
    merely hidden. `ClipDTO` gains **`link_style`** for that: derived from the id (`ids.Kind`), always
    present, never null, not owner-private — anyone holding the link can read the id it describes.
    (The row, its element and its client handling were all removed by erratum 264; the DTO field,
    which costs nothing and names a fact a client may want, was kept.)

252. **What the harness and the docs record, and what deliberately did NOT change** (ROADMAP #35).
    E2E: the share-URL assertions moved to the root form everywhere they appear (`$BASE/{id}`,
    `og:url` in `card_check`, the oEmbed `url=`, the embed overlay's href in steps 77 and 81, the
    notify content, the sxcu `url`, the share target's 303, the public-URL sweep's want-list), each
