    redirect has a truth of its own it is asserted there (the crawler's ranged GET is 302 then 206
    **from the bucket**; the conditional GET is 302 then 304; an unsatisfiable range is 416 from the
    bucket, its ENVELOPE being the vendor's and not ours); otherwise the assertion stands down with
    a printed line — `[e2e]   (redirect: <what> is the bucket's; the app's <what> is proven by step
    90)` — and never quietly. (c) *`/original`, `preview.gif` and `filmstrip.jpg`* are app-served in
    every mode (erratum 278(a)) and their sites are untouched; three assertions now SAY so on a
    redirect run rather than leaving it assumed — the owner's `/original` at the detection block,
    `preview.gif` at step 22 and `filmstrip.jpg` at step 71 each assert an empty `Location` on the
    200 they already fetch.

    **(e) The served-bytes step is the one place the two modes disagree about a number, and it says
    so.** `87-storage.sh`'s ranged reads now measure the body that actually ARRIVED (in `redirect`,
    `%{size_download}` off the app hop would read zero — precisely the silent lie erratum 270 was
    written to prevent). Its LOWER bound — the counter counted at least what the viewer received —
    holds in both modes and on every origin. Its UPPER bound, "nothing bodyless was charged", is
    *meant* to be exceeded in `redirect`: erratum 278(i) charges every 302 its whole object, so two
    150 KB ranged reads of a 1 MiB rendition cost about a mebibyte each. It therefore stands down
    with a NOTE naming that erratum, beside the edge-origin NOTE it already had. In exchange the
    step gains two assertions it could not make before: the Storage panel says `estimated
    (redirect)` in `redirect` and must NOT in `proxy`, and `admin stats`' `served:` line reads
    `bytes a viewer was redirected to fetch … estimated (redirect)` rather than `bytes sent to
    viewers`. That is erratum 278(i)'s promise — the over-count is never silent — checked on a live
    stack instead of only in a unit test.

    **(f) A probe container must not inherit a mode it cannot run — two rules, the second found by
    the proof.** compose interpolates `MEDIA_DELIVERY` and `MEDIA_PRESIGN_ENDPOINT` for every
    container of the project, so a throwaway `clippet serve` inherits both. Usually that is harmless
    — a presign makes no network call, so a bucket-backed probe signs happily for an origin nothing
    in its container could reach, and none of them fetches media. Two shapes are not harmless, and
    both are boot errors by design:

    - **A probe on `STORAGE_BACKEND=fs`.** `redirect` on a directory is erratum 278(e)'s refusal, so
      on a redirect stack `88-fsstore.sh` would never have started, over a rule that is nothing to do
      with what it tests. The three `MEDIA_*` variables now travel with the four `S3_*` ones it
      already unsets: in the container's boot script, in `fs_sh`, and on the two `docker exec`s that
      supply bucket variables.
    - **A probe that INVENTS its own `PUBLIC_BASE_URL`, and invents an https one.** `61-nits2.sh`
      (`https://clippet-warn.invalid`, the shipped-credential warning) and `85-bot.sh`
      (`https://bot-probe.example`, the interactions endpoint) both do, deliberately: a fabricated
      origin is how they keep their assertions the same on a lane stack and on the reference stack
      (a known trap). But the inherited presign origin was chosen to match the STACK's base, and a
      plain-http one under an https base is erratum 278(e)'s mixed-content refusal — so on a lane
      stack in redirect mode over the bundled MinIO, both probes died at boot. **The redirect proof
      of this erratum found it at step 61, which is exactly what it was run for.** Both now pin
      `MEDIA_DELIVERY=proxy` with the presign variables blank. Note the shape of the miss: on
      clippet.gg the presign origin is R2's own https host, so the reference gate would have passed
      and left the trap for the first person to run redirect mode locally. The rule is in
      `scripts/e2e.d/README.md` as a convention, beside the private-`SCRATCH_DIR` one it rhymes with:
      **a probe that invents a base invents a mode to go with it.**

    **Step 90 is unchanged** except for its header, which used to say the stack under test must stay
    on `proxy`; it is still the only place where BOTH modes run against the SAME database and the
    same objects, which is what makes "the bytes behind the redirect are the bytes proxy mode serves"
    an assertion rather than an assumption, and every stand-down line above points at it.

    **(g) A local redirect stack, so this is testable without R2.** `compose.e2e-minio.yaml`
    publishes the bundled MinIO on the host (`MINIO_PUBLISH`, loopback by default) — the one
    deployment where the app's origin for the bucket and a viewer's differ, which is the whole reason
    `MEDIA_PRESIGN_ENDPOINT` exists. Four lines in `.env` (`COMPOSE_FILE`, `MEDIA_DELIVERY=redirect`,
    `MEDIA_PRESIGN_ENDPOINT`, the published port) and the whole suite runs against a redirect stack
    on a laptop. DEPLOY §33.6 carries it, labelled as the development aid it is: a real redirect
    instance points at R2, B2 or S3 and leaves `MEDIA_PRESIGN_ENDPOINT` unset.

    **(h) What did not change.** The gate command (`bash scripts/e2e.sh`, no variables), the step
    count (90), the bundle count (21), the schedule, the sweep, the self-test's checks, `visual.sh`,
    and every non-media assertion in the suite. A `proxy` run executes the same curl invocations it
    always did, because in that mode each helper IS its plain counterpart — which is deliberate: the
    lane stacks, `E2E_ONLY` runs and any future self-hoster's local stack must not pay for a mode
    they are not in.

281. **`clippet admin objects <id>`: the harness asks the STACK what is in the store, never a MinIO**
    (`cmd/clippet/admin_objects.go`, `cmd/clippet/admin.go`, `cmd/clippet/admin_objects_test.go`,
    `scripts/e2e.sh`, `scripts/e2e.d/{47-upload,70-web}.sh`, `scripts/e2e.d/README.md`; DEPLOY.md §24
    and §24.4; **no migration, no new step number, no new doctor check** — 90 steps, 21 bundles and 14
    questions, exactly as before).

    **Why.** The SEVENTH GATE's public run on clippet.gg died at step 19: `the rescued clip's bucket
    prefix is empty`. `scripts/e2e.sh`'s two prefix helpers — `prefix_count` and `prefix_names` — ran
    `mc ls` inside a one-off `bucket-init` container against the BUNDLED MinIO, by service name and
    with the compose root credentials. That is this stack's store only while this stack keeps its
    media there, and clippet.gg had moved to R2 the same day (erratum 278); the compose MinIO was
    empty. Twenty-nine assertion sites in eight files go through those two helpers.

    **The failure was the lesser half of it.** A count that is always 0 makes
    `expect_prefix_count <id> 0` PASS. In that same run steps 12, 14 and 15 each reported an "empty
    prefix" for a bucket they had never looked at, and `wait_gone`'s bucket clause — the one that
    proves a destroyed clip's objects are really gone, and the reason this suite can claim a delete is
    a delete — was answered by a bucket nothing had ever written to. A harness pointed at the wrong
    store does not merely fail; it agrees with you. That is also why the fix keeps no fallback (c
    below): the helpers were never wrong until today, they were right for exactly as long as the
    store happened to be where they were hard-coded to look, and a fallback would rebuild that.

    **(a) One new verb, and it is a BUCKET question.**

    ```
    clippet admin objects <id> [--count]
    ```

    lists every object under `clips/<id>/` through `store.Open` and `S3_KEY_PREFIX` — the same store
    and the same keys the app itself writes — as one `<key> <size> <modified RFC3339>` line per
    object, sorted by key, then a `<n> object(s)` line. That count line is printed for an empty prefix
    too (`0 object(s)`), so "nothing is there" is never indistinguishable from "the command printed
    nothing". `--count` prints the number alone. An id that fails the id shape is a USAGE error (exit
    2) rather than a `not found`: every other answer this verb gives is a fact about the store, and "0
    objects under a prefix that could not exist" would read as one. A store failure is exit 1 with the
    store's own sentence — no credential, signature or webhook is ever in one. It honours
    `STORAGE_OP_TIMEOUT` through `withAdminTimeout` like every other bucket verb, and it is
    indifferent to `MEDIA_DELIVERY` (erratum 278): where the bytes live is a different question from
    how a viewer is handed them. On `STORAGE_BACKEND=fs` it lists the directory and the answer has the
    same shape, which is the claim the harness now rests on.

    **(b) It never opens the database, and that is the requirement rather than an optimisation.** It
    is routed past `db.Open` in `runAdminWith` beside `doctor` and `restore-check`, because the
    question worth asking most often is "did destroying this clip actually remove its objects" — and
    by then there is no row to open a database for. A verb that needed one would be useless in exactly
    the case it exists for, which is `wait_gone`'s: it asks after the 404.
    `TestAdminObjectsNeedsNoRowAndNoDatabase` pins both halves — the fixture's row-less orphan prefix
    answers, and so does a configuration whose database file has never been created (with `stats` as
    the control, refusing that with exit 2) — and that no database is created by the attempt.

    **(c) The two helpers become the verb, and the mc path is GONE.** `prefix_count <id>` is
    `dc exec -T app clippet admin objects <id> --count`; `prefix_names <id>` is the key column of the
    listing. Both keep their old outputs exactly — a bare number, and the names one per line — so all
    29 call sites are unchanged; and both die rather than hand a caller output they could not parse:
    `prefix_count` on anything that is not a number, `prefix_names` on a listing with no count line or
    one whose count disagrees with the lines it parsed. A short list handed back quietly is what
    `lacks_file` would read as proof.

    `exec` rather than `run`: the app container is already up, these two are POLLED (by
    `expect_prefix_count` and by `wait_gone`), and the verb opens no database — so the extra process
    cannot contend with the one serving the run, and no call costs a container. `dc run`'s
    cookie-name override is for probes that boot `serve`; this boots nothing. `bucket-init` itself —
    the SERVICE, its image and its command — is untouched: it still creates the LOCAL bucket for local
    stacks. The four drop-in helpers that PLANT or REMOVE objects (`51-admin`, `73-ops`, `89-quota`,
    `90-media`) were left alone by this half of the work, on the reasoning that a read-only listing
    verb cannot do their job and they are the bundled MinIO's by nature. The first half of that is
    true and the second is not: **(f) records what they became.**

    **(d) Two private copies of the same mistake went with them.** `47-upload.sh`'s `up_names` and
    `70-web.sh`'s `w1_sheets` were the same `mc ls` against the same MinIO, written locally so that a
    bundle would not depend on another bundle's file being present. `prefix_names` is a harness helper,
    so there is nothing left worth copying: the first is deleted and its one call site calls
    `prefix_names`, and the second narrows `prefix_names` to `clips/<id>/filmstrip/`, which is the
    count step 70 is actually about. Neither was in the 29 sites this lane was briefed on, and both
    would have failed the very gate the change exists to unblock.

    **(e) What did not change.** The 29 call sites, the gate command, the step count (90), the bundle
    count (21), the schedule, the sweep, `bucket-init`, the doctor's 14 checks, and what every
    assertion means. What changed is which store answers them — and it is now the one under test.

    **(f) THE WRITE SIDE — `store_mc` (2026-09-14, lane `mcstore`; `scripts/e2e.sh`,
    `scripts/e2e.d/{51-admin,73-ops,89-quota,90-media}.sh`, `scripts/e2e.d/README.md`, and one stale
    sentence in DEPLOY.md §7 that this pair of errata finally makes false; no Go change, no migration
    and no new step — still 90 steps, 21 bundles and 14 doctor questions).**

    (c) left the four helpers that PLANT or REMOVE objects alone because no read-only verb can do their
    job. That is true, and it is not why they were wrong. Each carried its own copy of

    ```
    dc run --rm -T --no-deps --entrypoint sh bucket-init \
      -c 'mc alias set local http://minio:9000 "$MINIO_ROOT_USER" "$MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD" && …'
    ```

    — the BUNDLED MinIO, by service name, with the compose ROOT credentials — which is the same
    hard-coded store the read side had just been taken off, and it fails in the same two ways. On
    clippet.gg, whose media is in R2: step 54 plants two objects into a bucket nothing will ever read
    and then dies on its own report (the SEVENTH GATE would have stopped there), step 75 counts an empty
    prefix and would have called a Destroy failure it never proved a success, and 89-quota's and
    90-media's EXIT traps sweep a bucket they had never dirtied while reporting that they had tidied up.

    **One helper.** `store_mc "<shell command line>"` runs `mc` in a one-off `bucket-init` container
    against the STACK'S OWN bucket, with the STACK'S OWN credentials. It derives them from the stack's
    `.env` through the harness's existing `envfile`, each falling back to compose.yaml's own documented
    default — `S3_ENDPOINT` → `http://minio:9000`, `S3_ACCESS_KEY`/`S3_SECRET_KEY` → `MINIO_ROOT_USER`/
    `MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD` → `clippet`/`clippet-dev-secret`, `S3_BUCKET` → `clips` — which is exactly the
    derivation `88-fsstore.sh`'s migrate probe already does for its four, so a checkout with no `.env` at
    all still gets the dev MinIO it always had and an `.env` pointing at R2, B2 or S3 is followed there.

    **The credentials are ENVIRONMENT, never argv.** `-e S3_SECRET_KEY` with no `=value` passes the value
    exported in the harness shell through, so the secret is in no command line that `ps`, `docker
    inspect` or an echoed failure could show, and it is not in the `-c` string either: the shell inside
    expands `"$S3_SECRET_KEY"` itself. The exports are made inside a SUBSHELL, so they cannot leak into
    the harness's own environment, where `docker compose` would interpolate them into `compose.yaml` for
    every later call. An mc failure is a `die` carrying mc's own stderr with anything credential-shaped
    taken out (`X-Amz-` lines dropped, the key and the secret substituted) — by parameter expansion and a
    `case`, so that neither is an argument to `sed` or `grep` either.

    **Two placeholders, because this suite plants in two places.** `$SM_B` is
    `store/<bucket>/<S3_KEY_PREFIX>`: a key written after it is byte-for-byte the key the app would
    write, which is the only kind `admin orphans` and `prefix_count` can see (51-admin's two extras under
    clip C). `$SM_ROOT` is `store/<bucket>/`, the bucket root, for the three probe bundles — a probe
    container is given `-e S3_KEY_PREFIX=<its own>/` and that flag REPLACES compose's value rather than
    nesting under it, so its objects sit beside the stack's key space and not inside it. `$SM_PREFIX` is
    that key prefix alone, NORMALIZED as `internal/config`'s `keyPrefix` normalizes it (leading slashes
    off, exactly one trailing slash, empty stays empty): the store joins nothing, the app concatenates —
    so the raw `.env` value 51-admin used to paste made `fooclips/…` out of the perfectly legal
    `S3_KEY_PREFIX=foo`, a latent bug this fix removes. Path style mirrors the app's rather than mc's own
    `auto`: `S3_FORCE_PATH_STYLE` true → `--path on` (the bundled MinIO), false → `--path off` (the
    DNS-style R2/B2/S3 of DEPLOY.md §7 and §33.3).

    **A stack with no bucket says so.** On `STORAGE_BACKEND=fs` there is none — `bucket-init` is behind a
    compose profile and the four S3_* variables are deliberately empty (`compose.fs.yaml`) — so
    `store_has_bucket` (asked of the RUNNING container with `printenv STORAGE_BACKEND`, because that
    value comes from the override and not from `.env`) is the first thing each of the four sites calls,
    and each stands down with a printed line: step 54 skips the plant-and-report half and keeps its
    backup rotation, step 75 skips the count-and-remove, the two EXIT traps simply return. `store_mc`
    itself dies rather than plant into a MinIO that is not the store.

    73-ops's two READS stay `mc ls` rather than becoming `prefix_count`: what they count is a whole
    throwaway INSTANCE's key space at the bucket root, whose clip id belongs to a database that no longer
    exists, so there is nothing to ask the app about. The four private helpers (`mc_run`, `o1_mc`,
    `qo_mc`, `md_mc`) are gone, and `scripts/e2e.d/README.md` now says the rule out loud: planting and
    removing go through `store_mc`, the credentials come from `.env` through `envfile`, and nothing else
    in the suite runs `mc`.

282. **The visual pass reads both media-delivery shapes: one sheet, two shapes** (`scripts/lib/visual.js`,
    `scripts/visual.sh`; `web/STYLE.md`, DEPLOY §33.6; **no Go change, no migration, no new shot** — 90
    shots, exactly as before).

    **Why.** clippet.gg went to R2 with `MEDIA_DELIVERY=redirect` (erratum 278) on 2026-09-14, and the
    visual pass is one of the three legs of every gate. On that stack it answered **90 shots, 52
    failing**, every failure the same shape: `foreign requests: …/clips/<id>/poster/… |
    …/renditions/….mp4?X-Amz-…`. `visual.js`'s no-telemetry tripwire — `web/STYLE.md`'s "a request to
    any origin but the stack's" — counts every request off `$BASE` as foreign, and in `redirect` mode
    the watch page's `<video>` and the embed's poster follow the app's own 302 to the bucket's origin:
    ONE legitimate second origin, which the app's own CSP names (erratum 278(j)). Erratum 278(k) listed
    `visual.sh` among the things that do not change; that was wrong, and this is the amendment, exactly
    as erratum 280 is the E2E's. **Two faults, not one.** The pass could not read half of what the
    product ships — and its failure message printed the whole signed link, `X-Amz-Credential` (which is
    the access key id) and `X-Amz-Signature` included, into a log file on disk.

    **(a) The mode is DETECTED, from the stack, once, and printed — before the first shot.** It is never
    read out of `.env`: a run against somebody else's origin has none, and a lane's is what an operator
    MEANT rather than what the process booted with (erratum 280(a) for the identical rule
    in the E2E). **"Before the first shot" is a requirement and not a preference**, and finding out why
    is what this erratum's first draft was for: the E2E asks its question of a ready clip, and the first
    version here copied that, detecting the mode after the pass's own upload. But `LIBRARY_SCOPE=shared`
    is the DEFAULT (erratum 113) — the library lists every listed clip on the instance — so the
    `library-empty` shot of a brand-new account is not empty on any populated stack, and on the reference
    stack it fetched four other people's posters from the bucket four shots before any clip of the run's
    existed. A mode known too late is a tripwire that fires on the very pages it was taught to read.
    So the question is asked of the app's own **policy**, which every page carries: `cspBase` writes
    `media-src 'self'` in `proxy` and appends the ONE media origin in `redirect` (erratum 278(j)), so the
    login page answers it before a clip exists. The line is
    `[visual] media delivery: <mode> (<host>) — the policy the app serves`.

    **(b) …and CONFIRMED on the wire, which is erratum 278(j) proven from outside the binary.** The moment
    the run's own clip is ready, one anonymous GET of its `video.mp4` with redirects NOT followed: a
    declared `proxy` must answer **200**, a declared `redirect` must answer **302** with a SIGNED
    `Location` on **exactly** the origin the policy named, and the watch page must declare the same shape
    as the login page did. Neither half is worth as much alone. A policy naming an origin the media
    routes never redirect to would have this pass allowing requests to a host the product does not use;
    a 302 to an origin the policy does not name is erratum 278(j)'s silent failure itself, where the
    Discord card goes on working while our own CSP blocks the player on our own page — and a pass that is
    allowed to let the media origin through (below) must never be the thing that hides that. Both are
    read from the ANSWER on the wire, never from configuration.

    **(c) The tripwire is converted, not weakened.** A request is not foreign when **all three** hold:
    its origin is the run's media origin, its URL carries `X-Amz-Signature=`, and its path is under
    `clips/` (matched anywhere after the origin — `S3_KEY_PREFIX` and a path-style bucket both put more
    in front of it). A bare, unsigned request to the bucket origin is still a fault — it would be a media
    URL this app did not mint — and so is a signed request to anywhere else. In `proxy` the media origin
    is empty, the exception can never match, and the filter is byte-for-byte the one it has always been.
    The fonts rule, the console rule and the CSP-violation rule are untouched.

    **(d) No signature reaches a log.** One `redact(u)` replaces a query carrying `X-Amz-` with
    `?<signed>`, keeping the path, which is what a post-mortem needs; `redactText(s)` does the same to
    every URL inside a MESSAGE — a console line, a CSP violation's blocked URI, an exception's text —
    and every failure a shot records passes through it once more at the single point where it is printed
    and written to `results.json` and the contact sheet. A message nobody thought to redact is therefore
    not a way out for a credential. (Erratum 280(b) is the same rule, and the same reason, for the E2E's
    transcript.) A green run prints no request URL at all, so a `grep` of its log for a signature would
    be zero whether the redaction worked or not; the pass therefore SELF-TESTS the three rules before
    the browser starts — the allow rule in all five of its answers, the redaction in four — over a
    fixture carrying an invented 64-hex signature, and prints that fixture redacted. The grep then has
    something real to be zero about, and the rule most likely to rot is pinned on every run.

    **(e) The assertion the other mode cannot make.** In `redirect`, the watch and embed shots must have
    made at least one signed media request to the media origin: a page whose every request stayed on
    `$BASE` would mean the 302 was never followed, the tripwire would say nothing about it, and the shot
    would be photographed as though the stack were proxying. In `proxy`, zero requests leave `$BASE`, as
    always. The `embed-paused` NOTE (the pinned Chromium has no H.264, so that shot cannot be taken here)
    is unchanged, and a skipped shot asserts nothing.

    **(f) What does not change, and the one thing a LOCAL redirect stack needs.** The shot list, the two
    widths and the two themes, the DOM tests (`domFollow`, `domFaces`), the contact sheet, the `visual_%`
    sweep, and every other assertion. The browser runs INSIDE the Playwright container, which is why
    `visual.sh` already rewrites a loopback `BASE` to the host as that container reaches it — and the
    media origin gets no such rewrite, because it is the APP that signs that origin and a rewritten host
    is a signature that verifies nowhere. So a local redirect stack has to SIGN for an origin the
    container can resolve: `MEDIA_PRESIGN_ENDPOINT` naming the host's docker-internal name and the
    published MinIO port, rather than loopback. DEPLOY §33.6 carries the sentence. A real redirect
    instance points at R2, B2 or S3, where one public host serves everybody, and the question does not
    arise.

283. **The three gates, faster — and two of them proving more than they did** (`internal/config`,
    `cmd/clippet/serve.go`, `Dockerfile`, `scripts/check.sh`, `scripts/e2e.sh`, five drop-ins,
    `scripts/e2e.d/README.md`; DEPLOY §2, §4, §17.1, §33.6; **no migration, no new E2E step, the doctor
    stays at 14 checks**).

    **Why.** Measured on the last green public gate (`8b9f705`): `check.sh` 409 s, the E2E 763 s, the
    visual pass 274 s — and a lane pays one or two of those before the gate pays it again. A read-only
    research pass took every one of those numbers out of the harness's own records rather than
    guessing, and found that the largest single cost in each of the first two was **not the product
    being tested**. The E2E's slowest step was a retry loop against a port the step had closed on
    purpose; `check.sh`'s second-slowest stage was pure shell text processing over 21 files. Nothing
    here weakens an assertion: every clause below either keeps the same assertion and pays less for it,
    or adds one.

    **(a) The boot ping loop is configuration** (`STORAGE_PING_ATTEMPTS` = 10, `STORAGE_PING_INTERVAL`
    = 3s; `internal/config/config.go`, `cmd/clippet/serve.go` `pingLoop`; DEPLOY §2, §4; **−106 s of the
    E2E**). `serve.go` opened its listener, then pinged the store ten times three seconds apart before
    starting the worker and the sweeper — about a minute, hard-coded. For every real operator that is
    the right behaviour and it is unchanged: the two defaults are what every release before this did,
    and `internal/config.TestDefaults` now pins both so they cannot drift. But the E2E's step 75 boots
    a probe with `S3_ENDPOINT` pointed at a **closed port on purpose**, twice, to prove that a failed
    `Destroy` is remembered across a restart — and each of those two boots spent the full sixty seconds
    failing to reach it before the sweeper it is actually testing had ticked once. The three recorded
    runs agree to the second (`failsecs=74/74/73`, `s3firstsweep=69/69/69`). `73-ops.sh` now passes
    `-e STORAGE_PING_ATTEMPTS=2 -e STORAGE_PING_INTERVAL=1s` to that one container: the same loop with
    the same outcome — every attempt fails, the process serves degraded and logs `storage unreachable`
    — reached in about seven seconds. **Nothing step 75 asserts is about the ping loop**, and the
    change makes its central assertion STRONGER rather than weaker: the claim is "the restarted process
    did not re-attempt while its two-minute backoff still held", and a boot that no longer burns
    seventy seconds leaves the ticks it counts well inside that window instead of near its edge, where
    erratum 245 had already had to stop comparing wall clocks. The knob is defensible on its own
    merits, which is why it is a product change and not a harness one: an operator whose NAS is slow to
    appear after a reboot raises the attempts, and one whose bucket is always up lowers them so a dead
    endpoint is named in the log in seconds rather than a minute. Under one attempt is a boot error
    naming the variable, per §4's never-guess rule. `/readyz` is untouched — it pings live per request,
    whatever these say.

    **(b) The test image's fixed prerequisites move above the source, and the two Go passes become
    siblings that run at once** (`Dockerfile`, `scripts/check.sh`; **−45…−60 s of `check.sh` every
    run**). The stage graph is now `base → build` for the binary and
    `base → testdeps → testsrc → {test, racetest}` for the checks.

    Two separate faults, and both were measured before they were touched. First, `test` inherited
    `COPY . .` from `build` and only THEN copied in the static ffmpeg (14.5 s), installed `font-dejavu`
    (≈13 s) and — inside the race RUN itself — `gcc musl-dev` (≈5 s). None of the three depends on
    anything in the tree, so all three re-ran on every source change; they are now in `testdeps`, above
    the copy, where the layer cache keeps them. Second, the two passes ran one after the other as a
    chain, 75.3 s then 228.9 s. They are **complementary and neither may be dropped** — `-tags ffmpeg`
    runs only in the first (`internal/transcode` is 66.8 s with the tag and 4.2 s without) and `-race`
    only in the second (`internal/httpapi` is 48.7 s without it and 218.8 s with) — but they share
    nothing, so as siblings off one `testsrc` parent the short one now hides inside the long one.
    Everything they DO share — the source copy, `gofmt -l`, `go mod verify` — sits in `testsrc` and is
    done once.

    **Coverage: none.** The same two commands, the same flags, the same packages, the same gofmt and
    `go mod verify`. The two things concurrency costs are both closed explicitly: each build's output
    goes to its own file and both are printed after both finish, in a fixed order, so the transcript
    reads the same every run; and BOTH exit statuses are captured and checked, so either failing fails
    the stage with its own log above the line that names which. `--output=type=cacheonly` on both (the
    driver is buildx and it was proven on this host before it was relied on) drops the 17.5 s export of
    `clippet-test:local`, an image nothing in this repository has ever consumed — `check.sh` was
    the only thing that made one. The RUN steps still execute; what changes is what is written at the
    END of a solve.

    **The runtime image is byte-for-byte what it was**, which is the one thing a Dockerfile refactor
    owes. `build`'s instruction sequence is unchanged — the two layers `base` factors out are the two
    it began with — and the proof is in the report: the same `RootFS.Layers` list from a build of the
    old file and the new one against the same source.

    **(c) The cross-drop-in helper scan strips each file once instead of once per helper name**
    (`scripts/check.sh`; **−53 s of `check.sh` every run**, measured on this box at 58.2 s → 5.4 s).
    Erratum 234's stage — "no E2E drop-in calls a helper another drop-in defines" — was written as a
    triple loop: for every defining file, for every helper name in it, for every other file, run a
    `sed` to strip comments and quoted strings and then a `grep`. Twenty-one drop-ins now define
    seventy-six helpers between them, so that is about 1,500 `sed`+`grep` pairs, roughly three thousand
    process starts, and **the second-slowest stage in `check.sh`** after the Go passes — 46 s of a
    433 s run, all of it process start, none of it work. It was not in the speed research's ranked
    levers because the per-stage timing that made it visible was added the day after.

    The strip now happens ONCE per file, into a temp copy, and each helper name is asked about ONCE
    with a single `grep -l` across every stripped copy at a time: ~97 processes instead of ~3,000.
    **Coverage: none lost.** The same `helper_strip` sed, the same command-position expression
    (`(^|[;&|(]|[[:space:]])name([[:space:]]|;|\)|$)`), the same skip of the defining file, the same
    message, the same order — and the stage's OWN self-test, three planted files that must yield
    exactly one hit (a bare call flagged; quoted prose, an assignment and a hyphenated word ignored;
    the defining file never flagged), is unchanged and is what pins that. The one new thing is a
    basename→path map, because the message must name the file the reader knows and the stripped copies
    have names of their own; reading it costs one `sed` per HIT, which on a green run is zero.

    **(d) The retry pause is a variable, so the self-test stops sleeping through its own proof**
    (`E2E_RETRY_PAUSE`, default 3; `scripts/e2e.sh`, the three retry sites and the `E2E_SELFTEST` block;
    **−18 s of `check.sh`**, measured 21 s → 2.6 s for that stage). `dc`'s exit-125 retry, `curl_`'s
    7/28/35 retry and `http_refused`'s edge retry each waited a hard-coded three seconds. In a run that
    is right and it is unchanged. In `E2E_SELFTEST=1` — which runs those branches against a stub, with
    no daemon and no network, and is the ONLY thing that ever executes them — seven branches × 3 s was
    twenty seconds of `check.sh` asleep, and the stage's own description had to warn about it.

    **Coverage: not lost, ADDED.** What the self-test proves is that a wrapper retries once and that a
    write whose success is asserted, a non-125 docker failure and an exit-22 curl are not retried;
    a wrapper that paused for nothing would satisfy every one of those. The pause itself had never been
    asserted anywhere. It is now: the block reads `E2E_RETRY_PAUSE` **before** it sets it to zero and
    checks that the default is 3 — one new check, 50 → 51 — so the value that was previously protected
    only by being felt is now protected by a failure.

    **(e) Four self-contained probe bundles move into lane 4** (`85-bot`, `88-fsstore`, `89-quota`,
    `90-media`; `scripts/e2e.d/README.md`'s table; **−30 s off the exclusive phase, absorbed by the
    quietest lane**). Each was read against erratum 245(b)'s list before its marker was touched, and
    each failed it for a reason that was about COST rather than about a shared thing — 85-bot's own
    header said so out loud ("Neither is parallel-unsafe on today's bundles"). All four bring their own
    instance: their own `DATA_DIR`, their own `SCRATCH_DIR`, their own database, and — for the three
    that write objects — their own `S3_KEY_PREFIX` at the bucket root, removed by the probe and again
    by an EXIT trap. None creates a clip or an account on the stack under test, mutates a shared clip
    or an account-wide setting, runs `dc up`, starts a second process against THIS database, probes a
    rate limiter, or asserts anything bucket-, log- or instance-wide about it. 88-fsstore's published
    port is `CLIPPET_PUBLISH` + 200 and the only other two bundles that publish one (37-library,
    55-owner) are exclusive, so they can never be concurrent with it.

    One thing genuinely IMPROVES by the move, and it is worth writing down because it is the opposite
    of what a reader would assume. `run_lane` sources each bundle in a **subshell of its own**, while
    the exclusive phase sources them into the harness's own shell (since erratum 245's 2026-09-15 amendment the exclusive phase runs each bundle in a subshell as well, so the comparison is historical). So the host-side `trap … EXIT`
    that 89-quota and 90-media use to guarantee their bucket prefix is removed is now scoped to the
    bundle that armed it, instead of living in the shell every later bundle also runs in. 73-ops has
    relied on exactly that since erratum 245.

    Lane 4 did 9 s of work in a 230 s parallel phase. It now does about 45 s at the time of writing, still far inside lane 1.
    The nine bundles that stay exclusive stay so for reasons that are about the stack: a shared account
    (33-account, 82-links), an idle queue or a global census (37-library, 47-upload, 51-admin), a
    rate-limiter drain (55-owner, 62-tiers), an absence over the whole app log (61-nits2), and an
    instance-wide served-bytes counter with a flush window (87-storage), which is correctly exclusive
    and is the thing under test.

    **(f) The two rate-limiter drains fire from one `curl` process per chunk** (`burst_429` in
    `scripts/e2e.sh`; `62-tiers` step 66, `55-owner` step 56; **−20…−60 s**). Proving a ceiling means
    reaching it, and both steps reached it with a `while` loop that forked a `curl` per request: 203
    processes in the last public gate (145 progress + 58 oEmbed) and 361 on a lane stack, each one a
    fork, a fresh connection and — through an edge — a fresh TLS handshake. Measured on this project's
    own loopback: forty requests are 9.8 s as forty processes and 0.29 s as one.

    **Coverage: none.** This is deliberately the cheap variant of the lever, not the probe-container
    one. The ceiling is still reached on the LIVE stack, at its own shipped value, by the same
    requests; every answer before the refusal is still asserted 200; the refusal is still required
    inside the same bound (400 and 200 respectively); and the 429's `error: rate_limited` and
    `Retry-After` are still read off a real refused response. What changed is how many processes make
    the requests — `E2E_BURST_CHUNK` (25) of them share one `curl --next` invocation.

    Two details the helper owes the reader. The chunked requests discard their bodies, so the envelope
    is read by a request of its own afterwards — and because the bucket refills while a chunk finishes
    (the `poll` one at 2/s), that read ASKS UNTIL IT IS REFUSED, bounded at fifty — five bursts of ten — with no pause,
    rather than assuming the very next request is refused; assuming would have been asserting the speed
    of `curl`, which is the thing 62-tiers' old comment warned against. And the burst goes through
    `curl_`, so a chunk whose connection dies is re-fired once like every other read in this suite;
    a re-fire can only make the printed count smaller than the number of requests actually sent, and
    nothing asserts that count.

    **(g) Four of the nine redirect stand-downs become assertions on the BUCKET** (`media_head` in
    `scripts/e2e.sh`, step 8, `31-nits` (b), `62-tiers`; **≈ 0 s, and the highest value per second in
    this lane**). Erratum 280 converted what it could and stood the rest down with a printed line,
    proving each inside step 90's own probe — **against the bundled MinIO**. clippet.gg has served its
    bytes from **R2** since 2026-09-14, so from the SEVENTH gate on, the range, conditional and
    validator behaviour of the origin that actually serves viewers was asserted nowhere at all. These
    four ask the origin the app just signed for.

    * **`Accept-Ranges: bytes`, a satisfied single range, and the byte behind it.** `media_head`'s
      redirect branch already asks the bucket for `Range: bytes=0-0` and reads the total off the
      answer; it now also asserts that the answer says `bytes 0-0/<total>`, that exactly one byte came
      back, and that the object's own origin advertises `Accept-Ranges: bytes`. All three are
      a MAY in RFC 7233 that every S3-compatible store this app targets sends on a 206 (asserted for that reason, not as a protocol guarantee), and this runs on EVERY media HEAD the
      suite makes, not once. The two `media_skip "Accept-Ranges"` lines (step 8 and 31-nits) are gone:
      the claim is made one hop along instead of stood down.
    * **The suffix range says WHICH bytes.** Step 8 checked that `Range: bytes=-100` returned a
      hundred bytes and never checked the `Content-Range`, so an implementation answering the FIRST
      hundred satisfied it. New in BOTH modes.
    * **The unsatisfiable range is refused BY THE BUCKET.** The app's 416 envelope is replaced by a 302
      and still stands down — `Content-Range: bytes */<len>` on a 416 is a SHOULD in RFC 7233 and not
      every S3 implementation sends one — but the half that is not optional is now asserted at both
      sites: the refusal carried none of the object's bytes, and it came from the media origin the app
      signed for. A store that answered a crawler's past-the-end range with the whole file would put a
      rendition on the wire to Discord in place of an error.
    * **The validator belongs to the OBJECT, not to the link.** 62-tiers' one cross-source ETag
      equality legitimately cannot hold in redirect mode. In its place: a SECOND `media_head` of the
      same route mints a fresh signature — a different URL, a different query, a different signing
      instant — and the bucket must answer with the same ETag. A store whose validator moved with the
      link would give every viewer a cache that never hits and every crawler a conditional GET that
      never matches.

    Nine stand-downs become six, and two of those six now carry a bucket-side assertion beside them.
    What genuinely stays stood down is what a 302 really does replace: the app's own range PARSER
    (erratum 44's unknown unit, erratum 43's stale `If-Range`), the headers its 304 carries, its
    `Vary`/`Cache-Control` on the object, and its `If-Match` 412 — each still proven by step 90 in both
    modes on an instance of its own.

    **(h) The two `doctor` rows nobody checked, and the four media helpers nothing self-tested**
    (`51-admin`, `88-fsstore`, the `E2E_SELFTEST` block; **≈ 0 s; 50 checks → 63**).

    51-admin asserted `doctor: 14 checks` and then looped over **twelve** names; 88-fsstore over
    thirteen. The missing ones were `media` and `bot` — the two newest rows, and therefore exactly the
    two whose silent disappearance the summary line would have covered for. Both loops now name all
    fourteen.

    And `E2E_SELFTEST` ran fifty checks over the retry wrappers and the sweep's guards while pinning
    **nothing** of the media helpers. Two of the four are security functions that a green run cannot
    exercise: `media_redact_` (and `md_redact_` for the step-90 probe's own output, added at the merge) is what keeps `X-Amz-Signature` and `X-Amz-Credential` out of a
    transcript that lives on disk — and a redaction that did nothing would look identical on a run
    where no message was printed — and `media_no_cookie_` is what keeps the session cookie out of a
    third-party bucket, a guard whose own comment says it "can only ever fire on a harness mistake",
    which is to say it was dead code nobody could watch rot. The other two decide the origin every
    signed Location is compared against (`media_origin_`) and the size every redirect-mode comparison
    rests on (`media_total_`, split out of `media_head` for exactly this reason). All four are pure
    string or argument functions; all four are now pinned against planted text, with no daemon, no
    network and no stack, including that a planted 64-hex signature and its access key id do not
    survive the redaction.

    **(i) A failure names the last five requests, and a run prints every step** (`scripts/e2e.sh`:
    `ring_`/`ring_show_`, `die`, the ERR trap, the closing tables; **0 s**). Two diagnosis costs, both
    paid repeatedly.

    The closing table printed `head -10` of the step times, and `e2e_ctx` empties the per-context files
    at the start of the next run — so of ninety steps, eighty measurements were discarded and then
    destroyed, every run. The 2026-09-14 speed research had to rebuild a step table out of three runs'
    top-tens plus a per-bundle residual, and still could not say where most of the time went. Every row
    is printed now, slowest first, and the merged table is also WRITTEN to `.e2e/step-times.txt` in step
    order so it outlives the transcript. Beside it, the **phase split** — `serial main | parallel |
    exclusive`, with the total — which had to be derived by subtracting one table from another and is
    the one number that says whether a lane rebalance would buy anything.

    And a `FAIL` line named the step and the assertion, never the traffic. Both of the last two gate
    failures were diagnosed by reading hundreds of lines backwards for the request that had actually
    gone wrong — the G6 attempt whose log is named `e2e-attempt1-step73-cookie.log`, and the proxy and
    redirect runs that died on probes inheriting the `__Host-` cookie name. `http`, `http_refused`,
    `get`, `page` and `head_` now append `METHOD url -> status` to a five-deep ring, and `die` and the
    ERR trap print the tail of it under the FAIL line. The ring is a FILE, for the reason the
    self-test's stub counter is one: every wrapper runs inside a command substitution and a variable it
    set would go with the subshell. It lives in `$CTX_DIR`, so a bundle that dies in lane 3 prints lane
    3's own requests. A signed Location goes through `media_redact_` on the way in — this file is on
    disk — and an ordinary URL keeps its query, which is what makes an `?format=json&url=…` line worth
    reading. Each wrapper still returns exactly what it returned before: the status on stdout and
    curl's own exit code, which callers rely on under `set -e`.

284. **`DISCORD_COMMAND_NAME`: the slash command's name is configuration** (`internal/config/discordbot.go`,
    `internal/notify/bot.go`, `internal/httpapi/discord.go`, `cmd/clippet/serve.go`, `cmd/clippet/doctor.go`,
    `cmd/clippet/admin_bot.go`, `compose.yaml`, `.env.example`; DEPLOY §7, §24, §30.2, §30.7, §30.8; API.md;
    `scripts/e2e.d/85-bot.sh`; **no migration, no new E2E step, the doctor stays at 14 checks**).
    **Amended by erratum 315 (2026-10-05):** `DISCORD_COMMAND_NAME` names the LINK command `/clip` now; its twin
    `DISCORD_UPLOAD_COMMAND_NAME` (default `upload`) names `/upload` under the same rules, the two must differ,
    and `DISCORD_ENRICH_COMMAND_NAME` (default `Enrich`, length only) names the message command.

    **Why.** The owner, 2026-09-15, planning a dev instance on a second application beside clippet.gg, asked for
    the command's name to carry a dev marker, because one server only ever has one of each command name.
    §30.8's last paragraph already said an instance serves ONE Discord application, and that the way to run both
    paths is two instances. What it did not say is what happens when those two instances are invited into the
    same **server**: the name was `const botCommandName = "clip"` in `internal/httpapi` and `botCommand = "clip"`
    in `internal/notify`, so both boxes published `/clip` there and the second registration replaced the first.
    One of them then answered nothing, or — worse, because it looks like it worked — the wrong one answered and
    uploaded into the wrong library. A name is the only thing that distinguishes them, and it was not a setting.

    **(a) The variable.** `DISCORD_COMMAND_NAME`, default `clip`, validated at boot by Discord's own rule for a
    CHAT_INPUT command name: 1–32 characters, each a letter, a digit, `-` or `_`, and **no uppercase anywhere**
    (spelled as "the rune is its own lowercase", so a titlecase rune is refused too). This is not decoration:
    Discord REJECTS a registration that breaks it, and the operator meets that minutes later, from the wrong
    side, as "the command never appeared in the picker" — §4's class of misconfiguration, moved to boot.

    It is a FOURTH variable and deliberately NOT part of erratum 254's "all three or none" rule, because it has a
    default and is therefore never required. But it is meaningless without the bot, so setting it while the three
    are unset is a boot error of the same family, naming itself and them. With one of the three set the
    THREE-variable error is reported alone: the operator's next action is the missing pair, not a second sentence
    about the same mistake.

    **(b) The managed constraint.** On an instance that answers the OFFICIAL bot (`DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN=managed`,
    erratum 279) the name must be `clip`, or unset. That application publishes ONE global `/clip` and its
    forwarder relays that command and no other, so a renamed managed instance would publish nothing, be reached
    by nothing, and answer "Clippet does not know that command" to the one interaction that did arrive — silence
    with extra steps. It is the twin of 279's `admin bot register` refusal, moved to boot time because nothing
    later could ever say it. A malformed name is refused by the SHAPE rule first: the operator is told what is
    wrong with what they typed before they are told it is the wrong word for this deployment.

    **(c) One value, read by both halves.** `config.DefaultCommandName` is now the single spelling of the
    default; `internal/notify` keeps its own `botCommand` and `internal/httpapi` reads
    `cfg.DiscordBot.CommandName()`, because §3 forbids the import that would make them one constant. The
    three-way pin is `TestClipCommandNameMatchesTheRegistration`, which now also asserts that a bot configured
    with no name of its own answers the default — the loader being the third spelling and the one the other two
    are useless without. `BotDeps.CommandName` is injected for exactly the reason `APIHost` is: the RULE lives in
    `internal/config` and is tested there, so `internal/notify` validates nothing and an empty value means the
    default rather than an empty command.

    **(d) The three refusals that NAME the command stopped being constants.** "Run /clip in a server, not in a
    DM.", "Attach a video to /clip, or give it a link." and "Give /clip a video or a link, not both." are built
    from the configured name now. An instance renamed to `/clip-dev` must not send the person in the channel to a
    `/clip` it does not answer — which is precisely the confusion a rename exists to remove. On a default
    instance every one of them is the byte-identical sentence it was, which is what lets the harness and API.md
    keep pinning the exact strings. A FOURTH sentence names the command from outside `internal/httpapi`: the
    reply a job cancelled by a restart is edited into ("Clippet was restarting — run /clip again.", `internal/notify`)
    is built by `sentenceRestart(command)` the same way; `SentenceRestart` stays the default instance's exact text
    (the verifier's find; fixed at the merge).

    **(e) What the operator sees.** The boot line gains `command=/clip`; `admin doctor`'s `bot` row prints
    `command: /clip` on the row that already carries the application, and the check COUNT is untouched (14) —
    a new fact about a configured thing belongs on that thing's row, not in a new check the E2E would have to
    re-count. `admin bot bind`/`register`/`unbind` and `admin bot`'s own usage print whichever command this instance
    publishes, so `--no-register`'s "…was NOT published" names the thing that was not published. The name lives
    in the command DISCORD stores, so changing it needs `admin bot register` again — the same sentence
    `PUBLIC_BASE_URL` already had, now with a second reason and a §30.7 row for the symptom (the command is in
    the picker and every use answers "Clippet does not know that command").

    **(f) What the E2E can and cannot prove.** `85-bot.sh` gains a third probe container renamed to `/clip-dev`:
    its boot line and `admin doctor` name the command, `bind --no-register` prints it, the renamed interaction is
    answered by the binding, and the DEFAULT `/clip` is refused as an unknown command — which is the half that
    matters for two instances in one server. A fourth container, managed AND renamed, refuses to boot; step 86
    gains the orphan's twin (a name with no bot). The REGISTRATION BODY is NOT proven here, on purpose: this
    suite reaches Discord for nothing (erratum 257) and has no fake Discord to register against, so what
    `Register` PUTs is pinned against an httptest server in `internal/notify`
    (`TestRegisterPublishesTheConfiguredCommandName`), where the body can actually be read. Step count 90,
    bundle count 21, self-test count unchanged.

    **(g) Three corrections (2026-09-17, lane `misc`, from this lane's own cleanup rows).** The log
    field is the command this instance ANSWERS: `discord.go` set `discord=clip` as a literal, so a
    renamed instance logged a command nobody could have sent — and that field is the one line an
    operator greps to see the rename took. `DISCORD_COMMAND_NAME` is now read UNTRIMMED and a value
    with content and whitespace around it is refused by name (`l.raw` trims, so `clip ` was accepted as
    `clip`: fine until the day the space was the typo and the name was not); a whitespace-ONLY value is
    still "unset", as it is for every variable this loader takes. And the NAME is resolved before the
    application id and the public key are checked, so a bad name is reported BESIDE a bad id or key
    instead of behind it — the loader collects every fault and prints them together (§4), and until
    this an operator who mistyped both fixed one, restarted the container, and met the other. Pins:
    `TestInteractionsLogTheCommandThisInstanceAnswers` (a renamed instance logs `discord=clip-dev`, an
    unknown command still logs `unknown_command`, the shipped instance is unchanged),
    `TestDiscordCommandNameRefusesSurroundingWhitespace` and
    `TestDiscordBotCoReportsABadNameWithABadIdOrKey`; all three fail with the three changes reverted,
    verified on this lane. DEPLOY §30.2's rule list carries the whitespace rule as its own bullet,
    beside Discord's charset rule rather than inside it: "no spaces" there is about the characters
    IN the name, and the refusal points an operator at §30.2 by name, so the rule has to be findable
    where they land.

285. **`INSTANCE_BADGE`: a dev instance wears the monochrome mark** — **one clause SUPERSEDED by §20
    erratum 287(a) (2026-09-15): the badge no longer reaches `og:site_name` or the oEmbed
    `provider_name`.** That line is the instance's own HOST now, which tells `dev.clippet.gg` from
    `clippet.gg` exactly, with no variable set, and does it on a self-hoster's box too. Everything a
    BROWSER shows is unchanged: `data-badge`, the grey span, the word beside the mark, the `dev · `
    title prefix and the manifest's `Clippet dev`. On an instance whose host does not carry the
    wordmark the embed's grey span has nothing to paint (287(d)) — no loss, since that overlay names
    the box itself. (`internal/config/config.go`,
    `internal/web`, `internal/httpapi/oembed.go`, `web/templates/*`, `web/static/app.css`, `compose.yaml`,
    `.env.example`, `web/STYLE.md`, DEPLOY §7.1 + §7 + §30.8, `scripts/e2e.d/77-design.sh`,
    `scripts/lib/visual.js`; 2026-09-15, lane `badge`). The owner, on running a dev box beside clippet.gg:
    a visual indicator on everything the dev instance renders, to prevent accidental cross-environment
    use — the monochrome underline, and the pick: dev is monochrome.

    The rule the two Discord application icons already set, made the product's: **a green span is
    production, a grey span is dev.** Erratum 284 gave two instances in one Discord server two different
    slash commands; this is the same problem one layer up — a person with two tabs open, two cards in one
    channel, two apps on one phone — and the answer is the same shape: one variable, the instance says
    which it is, and the production instance is untouched.

    **(a) The variable.** `INSTANCE_BADGE`, empty by default, is one word a person READS: lowercase
    letters, digits and `-`, at most `config.MaxInstanceBadgeRunes` (12). `dev`, `staging`, `lab-test`.
    Anything else — an uppercase letter, a space, a dot, an underscore, a non-ASCII rune, a quote, a
    thirteenth character — is fatal at boot naming the variable and the rule (§4), never a silent trim and
    never a silent lowercasing: an operator who wrote `Dev` meant something, and a page that quietly
    disagrees with the file that configured it is precisely the confusion this exists to remove. The
    charset is narrow on purpose rather than by accident: the value lands in an HTML attribute, in element
    text, in a `<title>`, in a `<meta content>` and in two JSON documents, and a set that needs no escaping
    anywhere is a property held by construction instead of by five correct call sites.

    **(b) The mark goes monochrome, and that is the whole visual change.** `data-badge` is rendered on
    `<html>` beside `data-theme`, by the server, for `data-theme`'s own reason: four rules in `app.css`
    (`:root[data-badge]` before each of `.wordmark .pp::after`, `.wordmark:not(.sad) .eyes .mouth`,
    `.embed-mark .pp::after` and `.embed-mark:not(.sad) .eyes .mouth`) then paint the span and a face's
    mouth `--line-strong` instead of `--ok` with the FIRST BYTE of the page — no flash of production
    green, no script, nothing for the CSP to allow. It is **colour only**: the geometry, the weight, the
    tracking, the pupils, the eight faces, the entrance and the embed overlay's box are byte-for-byte
    what they were, so the visual pass's rest frames are unmoved and the favicon — which is drawn, not
    styled, and belongs to the tab rather than to the instance — is untouched.

    **`:not(.sad)` is load-bearing, and the verifier found out why.** `sulk` keeps `--danger` everywhere
    — red is loss, and a failed clip is not something an environment recolours — but the first build
    wrote the rule as `:root[data-badge] .wordmark .eyes .mouth`, which at (0,5,0) beats
    `.wordmark.sad .eyes .mouth` at (0,4,0): on a badged instance every failed clip frowned GREY, and the
    one recorded exception to the colour law was silently repealed (measured in a browser: a badged sad
    mouth stroked `rgb(167,171,179)`). The selector excludes `.sad` now, so when the class is present it
    does not match at all and the red rule stands. `domBadge` toggles `sad` on a synthetic mouth on both
    marks and asserts `--danger`, which is the only way to see a rule that otherwise exists for the
    few hundred milliseconds of an animation.

    **The embed's overlay spends one spelled-out grey, and it is `--faint`, not `--line-strong`.** Its
    ground is the player's own black whatever the page theme says, so it takes a fixed value exactly as
    it already takes the dark palette's green and text (erratum 246). The first build used that
    palette's `--line-strong`, `#514D47` — about 2.5:1 on black, which at 16 px over a poster reads as a
    MISSING span rather than a grey one (the owner and the verifier, independently). It is `#837F77` now, the
    dark palette's `--faint`, about 5.2:1: still unmistakably not green, and actually visible. The
    overlay's MOUTH takes the same value and needs a rule of its own: without one it inherits the PAGE
    theme's `--line-strong` from the mark rule above, and one lockup carries two different greys.

    **(c) One word AFTER the mark, and never a tile.** `<span class="instance">dev</span>`: mono, 11 px,
    500, uppercase with a touch of tracking, `--muted` on `--surface-2`, 3 px radius, 2 px 6 px of
    padding. **One placement, everywhere: the tag follows the word**, on the same line, 8 px after it,
    vertically centred on the mark's box — the header's arrangement, at 21 px and at 40 px alike.

    The first build put it UNDER the display mark and the owner refused it on sight: centred under the
    logo, the underline under the Ps is centred on neither the word nor the Ps, so it looks off. That
    describes the mark's own geometry — the span is centred on the double p,
    which is not the centre of the word — so anything centred UNDER the word has two axes to disagree
    with and picks a fight with the one thing the logo is. Beside the word there is no axis to disagree
    with, and the 8 px is the gap the header has always used.

    The thing that makes it possible without moving the mark is a wrapper that exists **only on a badged
    page**: each display template emits `<span class="lockup">` and the closing tag inside
    `{{with .Badge}}`, so an unbadged page's markup is byte-identical to the one that shipped before this
    feature (the subtraction test below removes the two sequences). `.lockup` is
    `grid-template-columns: 1fr auto 1fr`, the mark in the MIDDLE column and the tag in the third
    (`justify-self: start; margin-left: 8px`), and `width: 100%`. The two outer `1fr` columns are equal,
    so the middle column's centre IS the container's centre and the mark stays exactly where
    `.auth`/`.message`'s own `justify-items: center` had put it — a flex row with a gap would have
    shifted the word left by half the tag. `domBadge` asserts both halves of that (the mark's centre
    against the lockup's, within a pixel; the lockup's width against its container's) on the front door,
    the auth card and the 404, and again at 390 where the mark is 32 px, together with "the page does not
    scroll sideways".

    It is `.instance` and not `.badge` because `.badge` is already the state chip on a poster frame, and
    one class name with two meanings is how a stylesheet starts lying about itself. In the header it is
    centred rather than baseline-aligned for one reason: giving either it or the mark
    `align-self: baseline` would move the MARK down the band, and the mark's geometry may not move.
    **At 390 px the header bar is already full**, and the tag costs it about 43 px: two badge-scoped
    rules in the phone block make `Log out` unwrappable (the username is the elastic thing in that row
    and already ellipsises) and let the TAG itself ellipsise at the extreme, because a bar that scrolls
    the page sideways is worse than a shortened word and a two-line bar is worse than both — the visual
    pass caught the 67 px band the first build produced, and the band is 45 px again. Never on the embed
    — the overlay is 16 px of live text over a picture on somebody else's page, "no text beside it"
    (erratum 246) is older than this feature and outranks it, and the grey span is the whole signal
    there.

    **(d) The four strings.** `<title>` gains `dev · ` as a prefix on every page (`docTitle` in
    `internal/web/server.go`, which the embed handler uses too), so twenty tabs sort themselves out.
    `og:site_name` and the oEmbed `provider_name` become `clippet dev` — the wordmark's spelling plus the
    word — because Discord renders that line as TEXT and that line IS the logo there (erratum 241): it is
    the one place a card can carry the badge at all, since the poster is a frame of the clip and the player
    is the clip. The manifest's `name`/`short_name` become `Clippet dev`, the product in PROSE like the
    document titles, so two installed apps on one phone are two names under two identical tiles.
    `theme-color`, the favicon, the CSP, the routes, the DTOs and the wire values are all untouched, and
    **`/healthz` gains nothing**: what this exists for is an eye, and the anonymous surface stays the size
    it was.

    **(e) Proven by subtraction.** `TestBadgedPageIsTheUnbadgedPagePlusTheBadge` renders eleven pages twice
    from ONE fixture — same rows, same ids, same clock — with the badge on and off, removes the badge's own
    seven byte-sequences from the badged page, and requires what is left to be BYTE-IDENTICAL to the
    unbadged one. That is a stronger statement than any list of things to look for, and it is the statement
    that matters: this feature exists to be invisible on the instance where it is off. (One of the seven
    is the oEmbed discovery `<link title=…>`, which carries `DocTitle` too — the test found it, not a
    reviewer; two more are the display lockup's open and close, and the close is removed FIRST because the
    header's form of the tag is a substring of it.) Beside it: the config rule (valid, invalid, the two
    refusals' wording), the tag's presence on every mark and its absence on the embed,
    `siteNameOf`/`providerNameOf` as functions, and the manifest's name.

    **(f) What the harness proves.** E2E step 77 gains a throwaway `INSTANCE_BADGE=dev` container of its
    own (`STORAGE_BACKEND=fs` into its own directory, its own database and scratch, `--rm`, nothing of this
    stack touched — the README's third convention): the attribute, the tag, the title prefix, the
    monochrome CSS rules as SERVED, `og:site_name`, the oEmbed `provider_name`, the manifest's name, the
    embed's attribute-without-a-tag, and a bad value refused at boot by name. Step count 90, bundle count
    21, doctor's 14 checks, the self-test count: all unchanged. `scripts/lib/visual.js` reads the badge off
    the stack's OWN DOM before the first shot and prints it; on a badged stack it adds `domBadge` — the
    attribute, the tag's metrics and its 8 px after the word, the lockup keeping the mark on the
    container's centre (at 1280 and at 390, with "the page does not scroll sideways"), the span's and a
    synthetic mouth's computed colour against the token, the same mouth with `sad` on it against
    `--danger`, and the embed's one grey with no tag — and the two frames `badge-header` and
    `badge-front`; on an unbadged stack it skips both and the pass is the 90 shots it has always been.

    **(g) The subtraction counts, and the visual pass reads `/register` too (2026-09-17, lane
    `misc`).** (e)'s proof is a SUBTRACTION, and it used `strings.ReplaceAll`: a page that rendered one
    of the badge's sequences TWICE — a tag emitted twice, a title prefixed twice — had both copies
    removed, the reconstruction succeeded and the test passed. A subtraction that removes more than was
    added proves nothing about what was added. `unbadge` now counts each sequence first and fails the
    test on more than one, removing exactly one; not every page carries every sequence (the display
    lockup is on four pages, the header tag on the others), so the rule is "at most one". Demonstrated
    by emitting the header tag twice in `base.html`: the counting form fails five subtests, the
    `ReplaceAll` form passes. And `domBadge` measured `/`, `/login`, the 404, the share page and the
    embed — but not `/register`, the third display container and the page a stranger is most often
    sent to; it is in the loop now, at the same three assertions the other two get.

286. **`/clip` takes ONE option, and it is required: the `link` option withdrawn** (the owner,
    2026-09-15: `/clip link` is useless and a worse experience than nothing — a user who uploads on
    the web page has a link to copy and paste already, and one who uploads in the server
    upload from in-server then they already will have the link dropped when it's avail exactly where
    they uploaded."*; lane `nolink`. Changed: `internal/notify/bot.go`, `internal/httpapi/discord.go`,
    `internal/urls/urls.go`, the tests beside all three, `scripts/e2e.d/85-bot.sh`, DEPLOY §30.2/§30.4/
    §30.5/§30.6/§30.7, API.md, README. No configuration, no migration, no route, no new E2E step: step count
    90, bundle count 21, self-test count 63, doctor 14 — all unchanged.)
    **Amended by erratum 315 (2026-10-05):** the one-option upload command stands (renamed `/upload`), and a `link`
    option returns on a command of its OWN, `/clip link:` — why that is not the shape withdrawn here is 315(b).
    Erratum 268(b) added a second option so that a file Discord refused to attach could come back into
    the channel by its link. The owner used it and found the premise wrong at both ends: the person who
    uploads on the site is holding the link already, and the person who uploads in the server gets it
    dropped where they ran the command. The option only ever asked somebody to type a link back at the
    place it had just come from — so it is withdrawn. **268(b) is withdrawn by this erratum; 268(a)
    (the command description naming this instance's host) and 268(c) (the `{title} · {m:ss}` reply)
    stand**, and the description's pointer stands with them: where to put a file Discord will not take
    is still the one thing worth saying before it refuses to take it.

    **(a) What the command is now.** One option, `file`, ATTACHMENT (type 11), **`required: true`** —
    and the `required` is the whole of what the withdrawal buys. "Exactly one of these two" was a rule
    Discord's command definition could not express, which is why 268 left BOTH options optional and
    made the endpoint say the two mistakes in a line each. With one option there is nothing to express
    but "this one is needed", which Discord can: an empty `/clip` is now refused in the CLIENT, before
    a request exists, instead of being answered a second later by an ephemeral sentence nobody enjoys
    reading. Three sentences go with the option — `msgBothInputs`, `msgLinkForeign` and `msgLinkUnknown`
    — and a fourth loses half of itself: `msgNoInput` is *"Attach a video to /{command}."*, the command
    name still built from `DISCORD_COMMAND_NAME` (erratum 284(d), which listed three such sentences and
    now owns two).

    **(b) The endpoint keeps its own refusal, and it is ONE answer.** `msgNoInput` is not dead code
    because `required` lives in the definition Discord STORED when a server was last registered: a
    guild whose `/clip` was published by an older build still offers a `link`, and somebody there can
    still fill it in. That body reaches this endpoint and is answered the way any `/clip` with no
    usable attachment is — `clipAttachment` finds the attachment by TYPE and skips every other option
    in silence, so an option this build does not know reads as "no attachment". No crash, no oracle,
    and no second vocabulary: a `link` naming a real clip of this instance and a `link` naming nothing
    get the identical line, which is the cheapest possible version of the anti-enumeration rule 268
    needed two paragraphs to keep. A stale definition carrying an attachment AS WELL is simply an
    ordinary `/clip`; the operator's fix for the picker is the sentence DEPLOY §30 already had —
    re-run `clippet admin bot register`.

    **(c) What went with it.** `discordClipLink`, `botAwait`, `clipLink`, `botLinkOptionName`,
    `notify.botLinkOption`, `optionTypeString` (both copies), `notify.ClipLinkOptionName`/`ClipLinkOptionType`, the
    `notify.Await` type and `ClipJob.Await`, and `Bot.work`/`jobKind` — the last two because a job has
    one shape again, which also removes the `how=` field from the bot's two log lines (an operator
    reading "/clip failed" no longer needs telling whether a fetch was involved: there is always one).
    **`urls.Builder.ParseShare` goes too, with its three tests**: the bot's `link` option was its only
    caller in the binary — it was written for it at 268(b) and widened for it at 275(b) — so nothing in
    this app now turns a URL somebody typed into a clip. That is a §15 property, not a tidy-up:
    erratum 268 had to argue at length that a link option is not a fetch option, and the argument is
    retired along with the thing it defended. `urls.Builder.Host()` STAYS — the command description is
    its caller, and always was. Erratum **275(b)** (`/embed/{id}` accepted, Discord's `<…>`/`||…||`
    wrappers trimmed) is moot with `ParseShare`: it is history, kept for the record.

    **(d) What the tests and the harness prove.** `internal/httpapi` pins the new rule where 268's was
    pinned: a body carrying the withdrawn option and no attachment gets the attach sentence and hands
    over NO job — for a ready clip of this instance named by every spelling 275(b) had taught
    `ParseShare`, for a clip on its way out, for an id nobody minted and for another host entirely,
    all answering the same line — and a body carrying it BESIDE a real attachment uploads normally.
    `internal/notify` pins the registration BODY, which is the only place `required: true` can be seen
    at all (erratum 284(f): this suite reaches Discord for nothing, so the PUT is proven against an
    httptest server): exactly one option, named `file`, type 11, required. `85-bot.sh` loses the three
    `link` refusal probes and gains one — the withdrawn option, signed, in the bound guild, answered by
    the same line an empty `/clip` gets, on the three-second response with no outbound call.

    **(e) The forwarder.** `clippet-forward`'s `scripts/deploy.sh register` builds the GLOBAL command
    body for the official application, and that body carries the `link` option too (one line, the
    `register` verb). It is a separate repository and a separate deploy; the two must be published
    together, or a server on the official bot offers an option every instance answers with the attach
    sentence — correct, but pointless. The operator action is `deploy.sh register` after this ships.

287. **The card Discord draws: the site line, the description's budget, the bar, the overlay, the
    poster's duration and the placeholder** (the owner, 2026-09-15, on a real card in a real channel; the
    measurement is recorded in the run's notes). Six calls, in the owner's words where they matter.
    Nothing here moves §9.1's tag COUNT: the inventory is 27 tags on http and 28 on https, exactly as
    it was, and everything below is a value, a template-level tag outside the inventory, or a picture.

    **(a) The site line is the instance's own public HOST.** *"the grey line … maybe should be
    'clippet.gg'"*. `og:site_name` and the oEmbed `provider_name` are now `urls.Builder.SiteName()` —
    the hostname of `PUBLIC_BASE_URL`, with no scheme, no port and no base path: `clippet.gg`,
    `dev.clippet.gg`, a self-hoster's `clips.example.com`. Discord renders that line as text above the
    title and nobody can click it, so the best thing it can say is the one thing a reader could type.

    This SUPERSEDES erratum **241**'s "the wordmark's spelling", and 241's head now says so. It also
    supersedes erratum **285**'s `clippet dev` on the same line, and 285's head says so: a host already
    tells the dev box from production, exactly and with no variable set, and it does it on a
    self-hoster's instance too. The badge keeps everything a BROWSER shows — `data-badge`, the grey
    span, the word beside the mark, the `dev · ` title prefix and the manifest's `Clippet dev`.

    The HOST has ONE home (`internal/urls`), which both `internal/web` and `internal/httpapi` already
    hold; what stays duplicated is only the FALLBACK for a builder with no host at all — `siteName` and
    `oembedProvider`, still the product's own spelling, still pinned against each other by check.sh's
    stage, because a blank provider line is a grey empty row above the title. `ClipView.Badge` and
    `CollectionView.Badge` are gone: `og:site_name` was their only reader.

    **(b) The description leads with the length, and the quality clause can no longer be cut off.**
    *"desc. is fine, capping desc so clause always shows is good"*, *"clip length there is fine too"*.
    `og:description` / `twitter:description` / `description` are now
    `{m:ss} · {the owner's words, clamped} · {the quality clause}`, each part dropped when it has
    nothing to say, and §9.1's default sentence only when all three do.

    The DURATION goes first because it is the one fact a reader wants before clicking and the one
    Discord renders nothing for — `video:duration` is emitted, is correct, and produces no field in the
    embed (measured 2026-09-14) — and because it is already the bot reply's own grammar. The clamp
    AMENDS erratum **214**, whose head says so: 214 put the owner's words before the clause on purpose
    and that ordering is unchanged; what changes is that the owner's half is now clamped to what is left
    of a 200-rune budget instead of taking all 2000 of it, so the clause 214 exists for — the one thing
    standing between a Light card and a reader concluding the product is a 720p product — is no longer
    the first thing a wordy clip loses. 200 is a safe target and not a measured limit: Discord's visible
    cut is undocumented (discord-api-docs#1593, open since 2020) and the community numbers have no
    first-party source; 200 is under the lowest of them, about two lines of an embed, and leaves the
    clause's worst case (~50 runes) room it cannot lose. The cut is one `…`, at a word boundary where
    there is one within the last quarter of what is kept, and it counts RUNES — a byte-wise cut would
    put a replacement character on every card in a language that does not space its words.

    **(c) The bar down the left edge of the unfurl follows the clip's state.** *"changing color for
    status would be AWESOME"*, and it is: `web.CardColor` gives a ready clip `#0E7C4F` (light `--ok`),
    a queued or encoding one `#D98E12` (light `--time`) and a failed one `#F0665C` (dark `--danger`) —
    web/STYLE.md's colour law ("green = you can paste this", "amber = happening", "red = loss") on the
    one surface it had never reached. The three are chosen from the palette's two columns on ONE
    criterion, the better worst case across Discord's light and dark grounds; no palette value clears
    3:1 on both, so the honest bar is Discord's own blurple (2.99 / 4.15) and `#0E7C4F` (2.64 / 4.71)
    clears it. No token is added: STYLE.md's palette stays closed.

    The MECHANISM is an ordering, and it is measured rather than documented (2026-09-15, eight variants
    against a real channel): **Discord takes the LAST `<meta name="theme-color">` on the page and does
    not evaluate `media` at all**, while a browser takes the FIRST candidate whose media matches (HTML,
    "obtain a page's theme color"). The two consumers read opposite ends of one list. So `base.html`
    renders ONE unqualified tag AFTER the existing light/dark pair, from a `page.CardColor` field, and
    the phone's browser chrome is unchanged in all three of that block's branches — including the two
    cookie-pinned single-tag ones, whose tag is still first. Every client is served byte-identical HTML
    and nothing anywhere looks at a User-Agent: a media-less `theme-color` is the specification's own
    fallback for a consumer that cannot evaluate media queries, and Discord is such a consumer.

    It is emitted by the TEMPLATE and deliberately not through `meta.go`'s inventory, for two reasons
    that compose: `{{range .Meta}}` runs near the top of `<head>`, so an inventory tag would land FIRST
    — painting the phone chrome green and leaving Discord on the pair's `#191816`, both halves broken at
    once — and §9.1's count is an exact set pinned in three places that this must not move. It is set on
    the pages that CARRY a clip's card, which is the share page in both its shapes, and nowhere else:
    the front door, the library, Settings, the auth pages and the collection page emit the pair alone
    and are byte-identical to what they served before. A collection is a list of several clips and has
    no state to paint. **The risk, recorded:** the last-wins rule is undocumented; if it ever flips to
    first-wins a card's bar becomes `#ECEDEF` — visible, wrong, harmless, and detectable by re-running
    the same probe. Neither rule breaks a card.

    **(d) The embed overlay reads the host.** *"change to clippet.gg on the baked in part of the vid …
    make sure that text follows the clippet design language and is readable on any background, without
    making it too much more obtrusive"*. The 16 px overlay of erratum **246** now spells this instance's
    own public host, and 246's head says so. On `clippet.gg` and any subdomain of it the host CONTAINS
    the wordmark, so the lockup is intact — `{sub.}` + `cli<span class="pp">pp</span>et` + `.gg`, one
    face, one size, the green span still under the two stems. On ANY other host it is the host as plain
    text in the same style and there is no span: a self-hoster's `clips.example.com` is not this
    product's wordmark, and painting the brand's green under two letters of somebody else's domain
    would be the logo claiming a name it does not have. The corner it sits in moved: see below. The suffix test is on `.clippet.gg` and not on
    the bare domain, so `notclippet.gg` is somebody else's host. Two consequences, both accepted and
    both read off the stack by the harness rather than assumed: the plain form has no `.pp`, so app.js
    injects no living mark there and that instance's embed wears no face; and erratum 285's grey span —
