    the badge's one embed signal — has nothing to paint, which is no loss, because such an overlay
    already says which box this is, by name.

    **The overlay moved to the top-LEFT corner, and that is the one thing in this erratum the brief did
    not ask for.** It has been top-right since 246; clause (e) below puts the clip's DURATION in the
    top-right of every poster, which is where every video site has put one for twenty years and where
    The owner asked for it. At a card's own size (400 × 225) the video FILLS the frame, so the overlay's
    corner and the poster's corner are the same corner and the two print on top of each other — seen on
    the visual pass's own `embed-card` shot, not reasoned about. Something had to move, and it is the
    overlay: it is ours, it is two CSS values, and the label is burned into a picture that is also the
    library's thumbnail, the collection picker's and Discord's card image. LEFT and not lower, because
    the bottom band is the native controls' (246's reason, unchanged) and a fixed vertical offset cannot
    clear the label at all — the overlay is positioned against the FRAME and the label lives in the
    PICTURE, so the two align only when the video fills the frame and drift apart when it is
    letterboxed. Nothing of ours was in the top-left: the non-ready frame's status line is centred. It
    is reversible in one value if the owner would rather keep the mark on the right and move the label.

    **Readable on any background, without a box and without growing.** The rest of erratum 246's
    geometry is untouched: 16 px, 10 px down, 12 px in, clear of the native controls at 400 × 225. What
    changed is the shadow, which is now two layers, and the numbers are computed rather than asserted
    (a contrast script in the run's notes). `#ECE9E2` on white is **1.21:1** — over a bright poster the letters
    are not carried by their own colour at all, they are carried by the dark edge under them. The added
    `0 1px 2px` at 60 % deepens and widens that edge: the pixel directly under a glyph goes from about
    `#494949` (7.6:1) to `#2B2B2B` (**11.8:1**) and the dark band reaches a pixel further, which is what
    holds the letter shapes together on a bright frame. Over black it is invisible, there being nothing
    left to darken.

    **And what it does not do, stated rather than glossed.** Both layers are offset DOWNWARD, so on a
    white frame the TOP edge of a glyph is still about 1.1:1 and the sides about 1.7:1. A mark that read
    at full contrast on any frame at all would need a scrim, a plate or a text-stroke, and all three are
    ruled out here — this is a LOGO, and a logo is recognised rather than read. The one thing on a
    picture that must be READ is the duration in clause (e), and that is exactly why it gets a plate.
    A text-stroke is the option if the owner ever wants the mark itself to clear a bright frame outright;
    it is a cleanup row. No scrim, no plate, no size change; still the ONE shadow the system allows.

    **(e) The poster carries the clip's duration, burned into its top-right.** *"Can you just bake a big
    length text in the top right of the thumbnail? as it's only useful before clicking play anyway"* —
    and that last clause is the whole specification. `{m:ss}` in Spline Sans Mono 500 (web/STYLE.md
    gives that face exactly this job: "things a machine measured", timecodes among them), sized at
    4.5 % of the poster's height with a 14 px floor, on a plate of the dark palette's ground at 72 %,
    inset 12 px at 720p-equivalent and scaled with the picture. TOP-right: the bottom-right is the LIGHT
    tag's corner and the bottom band is where a `<video>`'s native controls live.

    **It is NOT a watermark and the anti-features list is not bent for it.** A watermark is a brand mark
    that exists so an artefact advertises its maker; this carries no brand, no name and no logo — it is
    one measurement of the file it is drawn on, in the same relationship to the picture as the "3:42" a
    video player prints over its own thumbnail. Only `poster.jpg` carries it: the video, the Original,
    the Full, the Light copy, the GIF, the filmstrip and the frames an owner picks from are untouched,
    and it is gone the moment anybody presses play.

    The plate is what makes it legible on ANY frame rather than on most of them, and its numbers are
    why it is a plate and not a shadow: composited over white the ground is ≈`#595957` and the text
    reads **5.8:1**; over black it is ≈`#121110` and reads **15.5:1**. Both clear 4.5:1 on the two worst
    frames a clip can have. (drawtext draws a rectangle and cannot round a corner; a rounded plate would
    need a second filter graph or an overlay PNG, which is not worth it for a corner chip.)

    Every path that writes a poster draws it, because the drawing is INSIDE `transcode.Poster` and
    `transcode.PosterAt` rather than at their callers: the pipeline, a replace, a trim and the owner's
    "Use this frame" all get it, and a ranged poster gets it too. It is drawn ONCE, on the frame the
    pass settled on, and AFTER every measurement — that order is load-bearing, because the near-black
    rule (erratum 92) rejects a candidate by the luma of the frame it decoded, and a bright plate burned
    in first would lift every candidate past the test and the rule would stop rejecting anything. It can
    never fail a poster: no font in the image, no measured duration, an unwritable scratch file, an
    ffmpeg that refuses the filter or a cancelled context all leave the unlabelled picture exactly where
    it was, which is the poster this function returned before this erratum existed. A zero or negative
    duration draws nothing rather than claiming `0:00`. The pass cannot resize, so the measured
    `og:image:width/height` the row already holds stay true.

    **The font.** `web/static/fonts/spline-sans-mono.ttf`, a 24 KB static instance at weight 500 — the
    same family and weight the browser already loads as woff2, beside the `OFL.txt` that covers all
    three files. It is under the SIL Open Font License 1.1 and carries its own copyright and licence URL
    in its name table; DEPLOY §27 records it beside DejaVu's. The Dockerfile installs a copy of it (and
    the licence) into both runtime images at `/usr/local/share/clippet/fonts/`, and
    `transcode.FindPosterFont` searches for it there the way `FindTagFont` searches for DejaVu, falling
    back to the LIGHT tag's own list for an operator who built their own image. There is no variable and
    nothing to configure: an image with none of those fonts draws no label, exactly as an image with no
    DejaVu draws no tag. `transcode.FormatDuration` is the third spelling of `m:ss` in this repository
    and is pinned against the same one table, `testdata/duration.tsv`; `internal/web`'s is no longer a
    copy but a delegation to it, since that package already imports `internal/transcode`.

    **(f) The link-out placeholder, redrawn — and what the measurement could not settle.**
    `web/static/card-placeholder.png` was a flat `#1F2833` slab with nothing on it, in no palette this
    product has; it predates the 2026-09-09 design pass. It is now the Kept dark ground `#191816` with
    the display wordmark centred on it (Spline Sans 600, the letters `#ECE9E2`, the green span
    `#4CD69A`) and NO text: the card's own title already says `Processing…` or `Processing failed`, and
    repeating that in the picture would be the one place in the product where a message is stated twice.
    Same name, same 1200 × 630, so `internal/urls`'s three facts, the oEmbed document's thumbnail
    dimensions and every assertion that names the file are untouched. It is DRAWN by
    `scripts/lib/mkcard.py` — dependency-free like `mkicons.py`, whose rasteriser, PNG writer and PNG
    reader it imports rather than copies — and check.sh gained the stage `mkicons.py` already had, over
    DECODED pixel rows and never the compressed bytes. It costs ≈0.4 s, because the mark occupies a
    fifth of the card and the rest is one flat colour that needs no scanline pass.

    The 2026-09-15 measurement also found the link-out card coming back from Discord as a `thumbnail`
    rather than the wide `image` its 1200 × 630 and its `twitter:card=summary_large_image` were drawn
    for. **The brief's hypothesis — that the probe page lacked something the app emits — is refuted:**
    that page (a throwaway server in the run's notes, `linkout_page`) reproduces `linkOutMeta`'s fourteen tags byte
    for byte (sixteen since erratum 294, which added the two alt tags after this measurement), `og:type=website`, `og:image:width/height` and `twitter:image` included. Nothing is
    missing and nothing is ours to fix in the tags; the remaining candidates are all Discord-side and
    none can be separated without posting to a real channel, which is not this lane's to do. What the
    finding DOES settle is a constraint on the redraw, and the redraw honours it: the mark is 54 % of
    the card's width, so it survives being scaled into a small thumb as a word with a green rule under
    it. The next measurement, if the owner wants one, is one webhook post of a processing clip from the
    reference stack and one read of `embeds[0]`.

    > **Amended by §20 erratum 301 (2026-09-17).** The placeholder is redrawn once more: the
    > companion mark large on the left (340 px, 54 % of the card's HEIGHT — the same share this clause
    > gave the word of its width) with the display wordmark small under it at 64 px, on the same dark
    > ground, still with no text. Same name, same 1200 × 630, same generator (`mkcard.py`, which now
    > imports the mark's geometry from `mkicons.py` beside its rasteriser), same check.sh stage; the
    > thumbnail finding above is unchanged and still unmeasured.

    **(g) What the tests and the harness prove.** `internal/web` gains `card_test.go`: `CardColor` per
    state; the rendered share page carrying exactly three `theme-color` tags with the pair FIRST and
    qualified and the card's LAST and unqualified, on all three clip states; the front door, the
    library, Settings, the auth pages, the collection page and the 404 carrying the pair ALONE; the
    clamp keeping the clause, cutting on a rune and on a word, and the floor that would drop the owner's
    words being unreachable by the fixed parts; `markOf` over eight hosts including `notclippet.gg`; and
    the overlay through the real template in both its shapes. `internal/transcode` gains
    `posterlabel_test.go` (the argv, the metrics at seven frame heights, the corner arithmetic, the
    golden table, and every way the label can fail leaving the poster and its directory untouched) and
    `posterlabel_ffmpeg_test.go`, which draws on a WHITE clip and measures the corner's darkest pixel
    (255 → 80 — the plate, not a tint), proves the other three corners do not move, repeats it on a
    vertical and a tiny frame, proves the near-black rule still rejects an all-black clip WITH a label on
    it, and proves a chosen frame carries the clip's length. `internal/worker` pins that the owner's
    chosen frame is told the CLIP's duration and not the moment it was taken at. In the harness,
    `SITE_HOST` is DERIVED from `BASE` once and every site-line assertion reads it; `card_check` asserts
    the site line and that the description begins with a timecode; 77-design asserts the tag ORDER on
    the share page and on a cookie-pinned one, the pair alone on the collection page, and the overlay in
    whichever of its two forms this origin earns; 67-capture measures the poster's own top-right corner
    on the black fixture (the one clip in the suite whose picture is black end to end); and the visual
    pass reads the host off `PUBLIC_BASE` — never off `BASE`, which names `host.docker.internal` inside
    the container — asserts the overlay's text, its form and its accessible name on every embed shot, and
    says out loud when an instance's host cannot carry a mark for the embed's one smile to play on.

    **(h) The overlay cannot reach the plate, and the poster stage budgets for both its files
    (2026-09-17, lane `misc`, from this erratum's own cleanup rows).** (d) moved the overlay to the
    top-LEFT and cleared the collision (e)'s plate had created, but it did not bound the plain form's
    WIDTH: 16 px of host text from 12 px in runs to roughly 47 characters at a Discord card's own
    400 × 225, so `clips.averylongsubdomain.example.com` has a few characters of clearance and nothing
    fails if the two merely touch — the visual pass fails only when the box leaves the FRAME.
    `.embed-mark:not(:has(.pp))` now carries `display: inline-block; max-width: calc(80% - 12px);
    padding-bottom: 5px; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis`. Both halves of that selector are
    load-bearing: the branded form is a `*.clippet.gg` host with the wordmark inside it — short by
    construction, and it carries the green span, which `.pp::after` draws BELOW the text box, so an
    `overflow: hidden` on it would cut the span off the mark — while the plain form is one text node
    and can be a block container that ellipsizes properly. 80 % of the width less the inset ends the
    text at 0.8 × the width; the plate's own left edge is at about 0.87 for the longest duration a clip
    can carry, and both scale with the picture. A browser without `:has()` gets the overlay exactly as
    it was.

    **The `padding-bottom` is this lane's fix pass** (2026-09-17), and it is the half the bound
    shipped without. `overflow: hidden` clips at the PADDING box, so the clip ended exactly where the
    TEXT's content box ends — `.wordmark` is `line-height: 1`, so at 16 px that is 16 px — while the
    mark PAINTS 21. Measured in Chrome against the served sheet: the descenders of p, q, y, g and j
    reach 2 px below the content box (`scrollHeight` 18 against `clientHeight` 16 in the DOM, before
    any shadow is counted), and the shadow reaches 3 px below THEM, its deeper layer being offset
    1 px and blurred 2. A pixel scan of `clips.pygmy-quay.example.jp` drawn with the element's own
    face and both shadows agrees to the row: the last row carrying ink is the 21st, and the three
    rows the clip took hardest (16, 17, 18) are the darkest ink the mark has, #AE, #6E and #5B on
    white. So the bound was cutting off every descender tail and the whole drop shadow under the
    line — and on this mark the shadow is not decoration, it is the readability (#ECE9E2 on white is
    1.21:1; web/STYLE.md's overlay paragraph and app.css's own comment both say so), which made a
    WIDTH bound something paid for in INK. It landed on the plain form alone, which is every
    self-hoster's embed and every stack the E2E and visual passes run on, those being `localhost`.
    5 px is 2 + 3 and nothing more; the box is transparent, so the room costs a viewer nothing.
    `overflow: clip` with an `overflow-clip-margin` does the same job where both exist and is not what
    is used: the margin is the younger half of that pair (Firefox took `clip` at 81 and the margin at
    102) and an engine with one and not the other clips at the padding box again, which is the bug.

    `TestEmbedOverlayIsBoundedOnTheHostForm` pins the served rule (and that `.embed-mark`'s own rule
    still clips nothing), and now also that the clip leaves that ink room: it reads `text-shadow` OFF
    the served sheet, adds the measured 2 px of descender to the deepest layer's offset-plus-blur and
    fails if `padding-bottom` is under the sum, so DEEPENING the shadow fails the test rather than
    quietly costing the mark its bottom; a side padding fails it too, the insets of errata 246 and
    287 being where the mark sits. Both halves were proven by reverting them on this lane: with the
    padding gone it reports "the box leaves 0 px under the text and the mark paints 5 px below it",
    and with the padding kept and the shadow deepened to `0 2px 4px` it asks for 8. It is a CSS unit
    test because the measurement would need a browser and `VISUAL_DRY` — the only half of that pass a
    lane may run — stops before one exists; the pass's own `mark.bottom` is the union of the anchor
    and the green span and still does not count the shadow, which is a cleanup row and not a fault
    here (it is compared against a 48 px controls band, and 3 px cannot reach it). Separately,
    `drawPosterLabel` holds TWO full-size JPEGs for the length of the label pass (`poster.jpg` and the
    `poster.jpg.lbl` it renames over it) while the scratch reservation budgeted for one:
    `posterScratchBytes = 2 * posterMaxBytes` now says what the stage actually holds.
    `TestPosterReservesScratchForBothFilesTheLabelPassHolds` gives the disk exactly the old budget and
    asserts the requeue with `msgFrameDisk` (the clip stays `ready` and keeps its card image), then the
    same job with room for both goes through; it fails with the constant back at one picture, verified
    on this lane.

288. **A light/dark glyph at the end of the top bar, and the auth panel's rows stacked** (the owner,
    2026-09-16: a light/dark glyph in the top bar; and, looking at the register page, a question whether
    the field hints' placement was intentional — the
    username field's mono hint was drawn OVER the right half of the input, spilling past its border;
    lane `theme`. Changed: `web/templates/base.html`, `web/static/app.css`, `web/static/app.js`,
    `internal/web/theme.go`, `internal/web/server.go` (`page.Path`, the route), the new
    `internal/web/theme_test.go`, `scripts/lib/visual.js` (`domTheme`), `scripts/e2e.d/77-design.sh`
    (steps 77 and 79), `web/STYLE.md`, API.md, DEPLOY §28. No configuration, no migration, no new
    route and no new step: step count 90, bundle count 21, self-test count 63, doctor 14, visual shots
    90 — all unchanged.) Two unrelated things the owner saw in one pass, both in the one grammar's world.

    **(a) The glyph: one form, two buttons, and the stylesheet draws exactly one.** At the far end of
    `header.top`, last in the bar, on every page that HAS a bar — the library, Settings, the owner's
    and a stranger's share page, a stranger's collection page, a signed-in 404. It is a 16 px inline
    SVG in the Kept line style (1.5 px strokes, `currentColor`, `--muted`, `--text` on hover, the
    standard focus ring), no button chrome, no label text: a sun and a moon, each carrying
    `aria-label` and `title` naming **the theme it hands you** — `Light theme` on the sun, `Dark theme`
    on the moon — because a toggle labelled with the state it is in is a toggle half its readers press
    the wrong way. The page renders BOTH buttons, always, and four rules in `app.css` decide which one
    exists, in the same three states and the same order as the token blocks at the top of that file:
    the bare `.theme-glyph [data-theme-to="light"] { display: none }` is the complete light answer,
    `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) { :root:not([data-theme="light"]) … }` is the system's, and
    `:root[data-theme="dark"] …` is the cookie's. A `[data-theme="light"]` block would be dead; the
    bare rule already is it. **That is what makes the glyph correct without JavaScript in all three
    states**: the server stamps `data-theme` only when the cookie decided (erratum 242) and never
    learns what the visitor's operating system prefers — `prefers-color-scheme` answers for everybody
    else, in the stylesheet, with the first byte and no flash. app.js enhances the same form the way
    it enhances the Settings picker: one `applyTheme` now does the writing for both, the click is
    cancelled rather than the submit (so nothing navigates and nothing reloads), and the swap to the
    other glyph is the attribute's own doing. Pressing the glyph while the cookie says `system` PINS
    the theme it gives you, and the radio in Settings moves with it if that page is the one you are on
    — **`System` is reachable from Settings alone**, deliberately: there are two states to swap
    between in a bar, and a third that says "ask the machine" is a preference, not a toggle. The
    FOCUS moves with the swap (verifier): the button that was pressed is the one the stylesheet then
    hides, and an element that becomes `display: none` while it holds the focus drops it to `<body>`
    — the next Tab would start again at the top of the document and a keyboard user could not press
    the glyph twice. The other button stands in exactly its place and takes the focus, and only when
    the press carried it, so a mouse click on an engine that does not focus buttons grows no ring.

    It sits in a new `.bar-end` slot and NOT inside the `<nav>`: it navigates nowhere, and a
    stranger's share page has no nav to put it in. `header.top` is `space-between`, so one slot at the
    end is one placement in both states — the nav and the glyph with a session, the glyph alone
    without one. The badge lockup (erratum 285) still sits at the left on its `margin-right: auto`,
    and neither the wordmark's position, its spacing (271) nor the display mark's tracking (273)
    moves. **Erratum 244's rule for a stranger's page is unchanged in substance and narrowed in
    words**: that page carries no nav, no sign-up, no CTA and no brand but the wordmark — a control
    that changes how THIS BROWSER paints is none of those, and a viewer watching somebody's clip at
    midnight is exactly the person who wants the other theme. The E2E's whole-slot assertion still
    says "anything else in here is a diff"; it cuts the glyph's form out first, the way
    `badge_test.go` cuts the badge out of its byte-for-byte comparison. **The pages that have no bar
    by design keep none** — the front door, login, register and the message pages are their own front
    door (errata 244, 246) — so the theme on those follows the system or a cookie set elsewhere, and
    `<meta name="theme-color">` is untouched here. On a phone the bar is already full, so erratum
    285's `Log out` nowrap rule is now UNSCOPED (the glyph is on every instance; the tag is on no
    production page at all) and the 28 px the glyph costs comes out of the username, which already
    ellipsises and may shrink to nothing.

    **(b) `POST /settings/theme` is anonymous, comes back where it was pressed, and the security
    reading.** The route loses its `authed` wrapper — it is now the one page route outside the
    Authenticator, for the reason `/static` and the embed are outside it: its answer does not depend
    on the principal. `setTheme` drops the session check with it. It writes ONE cookie about ONE
    BROWSER and reads no row, no session and no database, so there is nothing for a principal to
    change and nothing for a resolve error to say; `postOnly`, the 303, the cookie's attributes
    (`Path=/`, `SameSite=Lax`, a year, `Secure` iff the public origin is https, never `HttpOnly`) and
    the 400 on a value no control writes are all exactly as erratum 242 left them. The redirect
    target is new: `page.Path` — this request's path, no query, normalised by `safeNext` — is rendered
    as the form's hidden `next`, and `themeNext` puts whatever comes back through `safeNext` again,
    because the value that arrives is the client's and not necessarily the one rendered; a form with
    no field at all is the Settings picker, and still lands on `/settings#theme`. **The reading:** a
    cross-site POST can at worst flip a visitor's theme in their own browser, once — which is what
    242 already said about the same route, and what the cookie's own comment has said since it was
    written. The route has no CSRF token because there is nothing to protect: no row changes, no
    money, no state anybody else can observe. `form-action 'self'` in both CSP strings
    (`internal/httpx/middleware.go` `cspBase`, the one directive line carrying
    `base-uri 'none'; form-action 'self'`) already bounds where this app's own forms may post, and
    `SameSite=Lax` means a cookie written by a cross-site POST does not accompany the cross-site
    request that wrote it. The one thing anonymity adds over 242 is that the same nuisance now works
    against a signed-out visitor as well as a signed-in one, and the nuisance is a repaint.

    **(c) A control never leaves its own row, and the auth panel stacks.** Two fixes for one report.
    `.rc > input, .rc > textarea` gain **`min-width: 0`**: a flex item's automatic minimum size is its
    CONTENT's, and an input's content width is its `size` — about 260 px — so without it an input
    refuses to shrink below that and is painted outside its own track whatever the grid says. The rule
    is global because the failure is: any row whose control column is narrower than that does it, and
    the visual pass reads every page's frames to say no other control moved. Then `.auth .row` takes
    the **stacked grammar** — the same four rules the ≤780 px breakpoint already writes (one column,
    the label above, the state cell left-aligned with `max-width: none`, `.rs:empty` hidden) — applied
    to that one container at every width. The arithmetic is why: `.auth` is 460 px, and `9rem` of
    label plus a 12 px mono state cell of up to 26ch leaves the control about 70 px of track. The one
    grammar does not fit there, and the honest answer is the one the grammar already has for a narrow
    box rather than a special case invented for this one. Login's rows read identically (its state
    cells are empty and disappear exactly as they do on a phone); register's hint now sits under the
    field it describes, which is where the owner was looking when asking.

    **(d) What the tests and the harness prove.** `internal/web/theme_test.go`: the bar carries
    exactly the two buttons with those values, labels and tooltips, in the end slot and not in the
    nav, on every page with a bar and on none without one; the nav is still the session's alone; the
    hidden `next` is the page's own path and never its query; `data-theme` renders from the cookie
    exactly as before; the anonymous POST is a 303 with the cookie and NOT a bounce to `/login`; nine
    `next` values, four of them hostile, resolve the way `safeNext` says; a bad value is 400 with no
    cookie signed in or out; and the Authenticator runs zero times for a theme POST. `domTheme` in
    `scripts/lib/visual.js` is the half no test in Go can make: a real browser in each of the three
    states on a light system AND a dark one, on a stranger's share page and on the library, asserting
    that exactly one button is drawn, that it is the one the ground the page actually painted calls
    for, and that a pinned cookie beats the machine — plus the glyph's slot, its `--muted`, its

    sideways, and every control on both auth panels inside its own `.rc` and its own `.row` at 1280
    and at 390. E2E step 79 gains the form's markup, the stranger's page carrying it, the login page
    not, the four visibility rules as SERVED, the anonymous POST with its cookie and its `next`, a
    `next` that is not a path on this origin becoming `/`, and the 400 with no session; step 77's two
    header-slot literals — this stack's and the badged probe's — grow the empty end slot, and both cut
    the glyph's form out before comparing. The visual pass takes no new frame: the `library`,
    `register`, `front` and `notfound` shots it already takes in both themes are all four subjects.
    One thing this lane's verification found in the harness rather than in the product: `domFaces`'
    first-ambient-face band (erratum 274) pinned BOTH ends to boot, while app.js's accumulator does
    not start counting until the 5 s guard after the 404's arrival gasp has ended — so any draw above
    about 83 s failed the 404, and one did (94500 ms against a 90500 ceiling). Both ends are measured
    from the moment the timer starts counting now — 0 on the front door, the gasp plus the guard on
    the 404 — and nothing about the mark or the timer moved.

    **(e) The display mark's green span had one pixel of air under it** (the owner, 2026-09-16, on the
    live 404: the Not Found heading sat very close to the logo). Measured: the heading's box began **1 px**

    is the same shape as (c)'s: `.wordmark .pp::after` is an ABSOLUTELY POSITIONED pseudo-element
    hanging `0.265em` below the mark's own border box (erratum 271), so it is in no box a grid can
    measure — every `.auth` and `.message` stack was spacing from an edge 11 px above the lowest ink
    the reader sees, and at 12 px of row gap the green line read as an underline on "Not found"
    instead of as part of the logo. **The fix is on the container and not on the mark**:
    `.auth > .wordmark.display, .auth > .lockup, .message > .wordmark.display, .message > .lockup`
    take `margin-bottom: 0.5em` — the mark's grid CELL, and on a badged page the `.lockup` that holds
    it. Nothing about the mark moves: the geometry, the tracking and the span's placement are erratum
    271's, `domBadge` measures the mark's own box, and a padding on the mark would have pushed
    erratum 285's instance tag off the line it shares with the word. In `em`, so it scales with the
    lockup (20 px at 40, 16 px at the 32 px phone size). The air below the span is then **21 px on the
    404, 27 on the front door and 31 under both auth panels** — the containers keep their own rhythms
    (12 / 18 / 22 px of row gap), which is right: the 404 is dense and the auth page is not. Checked
    on all four pages that stack under the display mark, in both themes and at both widths; the 503
    page is a `.message` and takes it with the 404. `domTheme` pins the floor at 12 px on each of them,
    measured off the span at rest — a face's mouth is the same band redrawn and is in motion, so
    measuring that would make the check a race about the ambient timer rather than a claim about the

289. **The classifier reads the WHOLE captured stderr; only the REASON is a tail** (2026-09-16, from
    the first `/clip` that ever ran through the official bot — clip `NCrggyXXNUpT`, job 6191 on
    clippet.gg. Amends **265**, whose mechanism is otherwise unchanged. `internal/transcode/encode.go`,
    `exec.go`, `hwfallback.go`, `hwfallback_test.go`; lane `hwtail`. No configuration, no migration, no
    route, no new E2E step: step count 90, bundle count 21, self-test count 63, doctor 14 — all
    unchanged.)

    **(a) The bug: the fallback could not see the refusal it was built for.** The owner's first `/clip`
    through the official bot was a 2560×1440 H.264 yuv420p 30 fps ShadowPlay-class capture, 37.9 MB,
    19.7 s — erratum 265's proof shape, one size and one frame rate apart — and it came back
    **"Processing failed"**, which is the single ending 265 exists to prevent. NVDEC had refused it at
    set-up with exactly 265's signatures (`cuvidCreateDecoder … CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_VALUE`, `Failed setup
    for format cuda: hwaccel initialisation returned error.`) and the CUDA graph had said `Impossible to
    convert…` after them. What was new was not the refusal but what followed it: ffmpeg 7.1.1's shutdown
    after one prints `Error reinitializing filters!`, a `Task finished` / `Terminating thread` pair for
    each of `fc#0`, `vost#0:0/h264_nvenc` and `aost#0:1/aac`, a `Could not open encoder before EOF` for
    each output stream, and the muxer's `Nothing was written into output file…` — **973 bytes of trailer
    on a 1,204-byte capture**, measured on the fixture that reproduces it below; the owner's own was 990,
    which is arithmetic its own reason gives away (`ed error.` + a newline + 990 = 1000).
    `runInstrumentedRefusal` handed `hwInitRefusal` that 1000-byte `failureTail` — the tail meant for the
    failure REASON — and on a capture like this one the tail opens INSIDE the word
    `initialisation`: the recorded reason begins **`ed error.`** and then `Impossible to convert…`. Not
    one of the three signatures survived the cut, `hwInitRefusal` returned `""`, the NVENC-only re-run
    never happened, and the clip failed permanently for the operator's hardware. 265's own proof capture
    was short enough to fit a kilobyte, which is how a mechanism proven in the gpu image, tested six ways
    and green in every gate since could still lose the first real clip it ever met. (Interim on the
    reference stack while this lane built: `TRANSCODE_HWACCEL=` empty and `admin retry`, which landed the
    clip on the CPU; the card goes back on when this merges.)

    **(b) The fix: two readings of one buffer, each sized for what it is FOR.** The captured stderr lives
    in a ring of `stderrRingSize` (8 KiB) and is read twice at the end of a failed run. The **reason** is
    `Tail(failureTail)` — 1000 bytes — because a reason is a log line and is allowed to open mid-word.
    The **classification** now reads `Tail(stderrRingSize)`, the whole ring, because the signatures it
    looks for are printed while the decoder is being SET UP, which is the earliest thing in a run, and
    everything a refusal prints afterwards pushes them out of any tail. Nothing else moves: the reported
    reason is byte-for-byte what it was, the three signatures are what they were, and `runHWFallback`
    acts on the answer only for a CUDA graph — so an install without a card computes the same value it
    always did and discards it, and the CPU path is unchanged by construction.

    **Why 8 KiB is enough, measured rather than assumed.** Every argv in this package that ENCODES
    carries `-hide_banner -nostdin -loglevel error -nostats`, and no argv here runs above error level at
    all (the poster's three leave out `-nostats`, which error level suppresses anyway; ffprobe spells it
    `-v error`), so nothing below an ERROR is written: no banner, no per-frame stats, no warnings. The
    refusal that cost the clip is ≈1.2 KB in total (231 bytes of signature lines with their newlines,
    973 of shutdown), and the longest shape this package can render is the two-output tier pass of
    erratum 217, whose four output streams and second muxer add their own shutdown lines — ≈2 KB, still
    a quarter of the ring. The ring therefore stays at 8 KiB. Raising it to
    32 KiB would have been nearly free (one ring per RUNNING ffmpeg, and `APP_CPUS` bounds those, so tens
    of kilobytes either way), which is exactly why it should not be done on a guess: the number that was
    wrong here was never the ring, it was which of the two numbers the classifier was handed. The "first
    line naming a signature" rule stands with it — even 8 KiB can open mid-line, and a whole line naming
    the cause is what an operator's WARN wants. On this capture that line is NVDEC's own
    `cuvidCreateDecoder … CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_VALUE`, the first of the three; the `Failed setup for format
    cuda` line DEPLOY §27 prints as its example is what leads an install with **no device at all**, which
    has no cuvid line to lead with.

    **(c) The test** (`internal/transcode/hwfallback_test.go`). The fixture is named after the shape that
    found it, `shadowplay-1440p30-long-trailer`, and its shutdown lines are not invented: they are ffmpeg
    7.1.1's own, captured on this host by failing a filter negotiation under the same four flags every
    encode argv here carries. `TestHWInitRefusalReadsTheWholeRing` asserts **the bug first** — the fixture
    written through a real `newRing(stderrRingSize)`, its `Tail(failureTail)` naming no signature,
    opening mid-word rather than on a whole line, and still carrying the CONSEQUENCE (`Impossible to
    convert`) that made the failure look explained — because a fixture that quietly stopped reproducing
    it would leave everything after it proving nothing; then the fix: `Tail(stderrRingSize)` returns the
    refusing line, and that line is one the tail never carried. Two more assertions guard the argument
    rather than the code: that the capture still FITS the ring (the sizing above, as a test that fails if
    a future ffmpeg prints more), and that the reason an operator sees is still bounded by `failureTail`
    — widening the classification must not widen the log line. `TestEncodeHWFallbackLongTrailer` runs the
    same capture through a real `Encode` on a fake ffmpeg that prints it and exits 218 having written
    nothing: two runs, the second with no `-hwaccel` and the card's encoder (`hwAccelNVENCOnly`) on the
    same output, ONE warning carrying the refusing line, 100 % published once, and the encode **succeeds**
    where the owner's clip failed. That run-level test is the one that FAILS on the code as it was — verified
    by reverting the one expression and re-running it, where it ends "the clip failed although the decode
    could have moved to the CPU". Its unit half cannot fail there and is not meant to: it calls
    `hwInitRefusal` directly, and what was wrong was never that function but which reading of the buffer
    the call site handed it — which is precisely why the pair had to include a run-level test.

    **(d) The same trap, closed at the other capture (2026-09-17, lane `misc`).** (b) gave
    `runInstrumentedRefusal` its two readings, but `runCapture` — the function behind every ffprobe,
    every poster pass, every remux and the filmstrip — still returned `ring.Tail(failureTail)` and
    dropped the ring. Nothing classifies those failures today, so nothing was broken; what was left in
    place was the shape this erratum is about, waiting for the next caller that wants to ASK a question
    of that stderr and is handed a kilobyte that can open past the line naming the cause. `runCapture`
    now returns a `stderrCapture` — `Reason()` (the last `failureTail` bytes, the log line) and `All()`
    (the whole ring) — and `exitReason` takes the capture and spends `Reason()` itself, so a caller
    cannot hand the log line the wrong reading. `runInstrumentedRefusal` is byte-identical through the
    same helper (`captureOf`): `se.All()` IS `stderr.Tail(stderrRingSize)` and `se.Reason()` IS
    `stderr.Tail(failureTail)`. Pins: `TestRunCaptureHandsOverTheWholeRing` (a trailer whose first line
    the reason cannot carry) and `TestRunCaptureOfARealProcess` (a real non-zero exit: the whole
    capture keeps the first line, the reason does not, and `exitReason` stays a log line); both fail
    with `All()` reverted to the short reading, verified on this lane.

290. **The scripts' destructive edges, guarded and pinned** (2026-09-16, lane `guard`, from the audit —
    ROADMAP #41's pass-2 list: items #2, #3, #4, #7, #11, #18, #24, #28 and additions A1, A2. Files:
    `scripts/lane-teardown.sh`, `scripts/e2e.sh`, `scripts/e2e.d/51-admin.sh`, `73-ops.sh`, `89-quota.sh`,
    `90-media.sh`, `scripts/visual.sh`, `scripts/testclips.sh`, `cmd/clippet/admin.go` (+ test). No
    configuration, no migration, no route, no new E2E step: step count 90, bundle count 21, doctor 14 —
    unchanged; the self-test grows from 63 to 105 checks. The house rule that every one of
    these serves: nothing on a shared stack is removed without a printed list, and nothing is removed by
    a selector that could be empty.)

    **(a) The E2E hands the reference stack back on ANY exit (A2 — the one that mattered).** Step 1
    exports the run's overrides into compose's environment (`RATE_*`, `SWEEP_INTERVAL=15s`,
    `REGISTRATION=open`, the test webhook, `APP_CPUS`) and recreates the app with them; the ONLY place
    that dropped them again was the end of step 17. Every run that died before it — a core `die`, a
    killed shell, a Claude process exit — left clippet.gg accepting registrations and posting to
    the owner's test channel until a person typed `docker compose up -d`, which happened several
    times over. Now: `e2e_handback_` is one function (the `unset …; dc up -d` step 17 did),
    `e2e_handback_arm_` sets a flag and `trap … EXIT` immediately before step 1's `dc up -d --build`
    (the first moment the overrides can reach the app), step 17 calls the same function as its last
    act, and the flag makes it run ONCE whichever reaches it first. Bash resets caught traps in every
    subshell, so no bundle — a lane's `( … ) &` or an exclusive `( . file )` — inherits or fires it;
    `E2E_SELFTEST=1` exits before step 1 and never arms it; every command in it is guarded, so it can
    neither change the exit status it runs under nor trip the ERR trap. What no trap sees is SIGKILL
    and host death: after one of those the NEXT run's step 1 hands back, as before. Pinned in the
    self-test: no trap armed under E2E_SELFTEST; a subshell armed and exiting 4 keeps status 4 and
    recreates once, naming the step; step 17 first → once, the trap then silent; a nested subshell's
    exit fires nothing. "A died E2E leaves registration open" is history from this commit.

    **(b) `lane-teardown.sh` (#2 + A1).** `dev` joins `main|master` on the refuse-list (the dev
    instance's worktree is fast-forwarded to main, so "merged" was always true of it and its two
    running containers were the only thing refusing the teardown). A worktree whose `.env` does not
    carry the exact line `COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME=clippet-<lane>` is refused (read through `tr`/`grep -x`
    only — its other lines are credentials and are never printed): compose resolves the project from
    the directory it runs in, `compose.yaml`'s `name:` is the REFERENCE project, so a lane with no
    `.env` `down`ed clippet.gg's app, minio and tunnel — A1, verified in a scratch directory. The
    `down` now names the project with `-p "$proj"` as well, so the file is never what decides which
    stack goes. A DIRTY worktree now `continue`s like every other refusal (it printed DIRTY and then
    OK). `--check` runs the check loop alone, prints OK/REFUSED per lane and exits 0/1 — the mode the
    self-test drives in a scratch repo (a copy of the script, its own `git init`, a real worktree with
    `.env` gitignored): `dev` refused by name; no `.env` refused; an `.env` naming ANOTHER project
    refused; the exact line (CRLF tolerated) passes, and a planted secret on the line above it never
    reaches the transcript. The permission rule `Bash(bash scripts/lane-teardown.sh:*)` is unchanged.

    **(c) `E2E_CLEAN=1` keeps what is not the run's (#3).** It was `rm -rf .e2e/`. `.e2e/backups/`
    holds the earlier instance's archives (the only copies), `checkpoints/` is
    E2E_RESUME's state, `logo/` and `bot/` are exploration files, `demo-user.txt` and `webhook.txt` the
    operator's. `e2e_clean_` removes every top-level entry NOT on the keep-list `backups logo bot
    demo-user.txt webhook.txt checkpoints`, and prints the removal list and the kept list before it
    acts. Pinned on a scratch directory: `backups/x`, `checkpoints/y`, the two files survive;
    `logs/`, `ctx-main/`, `app.log` go; the removal line is printed first.

    **(d) `admin orphans --clip <id>` (#4).** The listing becomes that one clip's prefix instead of
    the whole of `clips/`, the rows that one row or none, so the row-less report, the missing report,
    the extras report and `--delete` are bounded by the prefix by construction; a `scope` line names
    it; a `--clip` that is not an id, or a positional beside it, is usage (2). Step 54 passes
    `--clip "$C"` on BOTH loops — until now the delete loop was a bucket-wide `orphans --delete
    --min-age 5s` run unattended on production R2 every gate, the one standing exception to the house rule —
    and plants a STRANGER (`clips/e2eStrangerA/original/stranger.bin`, a row-less prefix under a fixed
    id so a died step leaves at most one, overwritten and removed by the next run) that must survive
    the scoped delete, be absent from the report, and be removed before any assertion can die.
    `TestAdminOrphansClipScopesEveryReportAndTheDelete`: extras under X and a finalized Y, the
    fixture's row-less Z; `--clip X --delete` removes X's extra alone, counts `extra=1 … prefixes=0
    foreign=0`, mentions neither Y nor Z nor the foreign key; `--clip Z --delete` takes the prefix and
    nothing of Y's. The sweeper is untouched; `ClipIDsWithLiveJobs` still runs first.

    **(e) `E2E_KEY` folds `.env` and every `COMPOSE_FILE` member (#7).** The resume key named the
    product tree only; a changed `MEDIA_DELIVERY`, `STORAGE_BACKEND`, cookie name or compose overlay
    changed what a bundle had proved without moving it. The sha256 of `.env` (contents, never printed)
    and of each file `COMPOSE_FILE` names (the shell's value, else `.env`'s, split on `:` or `;`) are
    hashed into the key; `-dirty`/`nogit` unchanged. Every checkpoint recorded before this commit is
    therefore stale by construction — the first run after the merge is a full one. Pinned: twelve hex;
    stable across two reads; `MEDIA_DELIVERY=proxy` ≠ `redirect`; a `COMPOSE_FILE` overlay differs.

    **(f) Stale probe containers swept at step 1 (#11).** Three bundles boot a NAMED second app
    container (`clippet-e2e-scope-…`, `-owner-…`, `-fsstore-…`) and remove it from an EXIT trap, which
    fires on `die`, INT and TERM (measured) — only SIGKILL/host death leaves one running. Step 1 now
    reads the compose project's name off `dc config`, lists `docker ps -a` filtered by the label
    `com.docker.compose.project=<this project>` AND the name prefix `^clippet-e2e-`, prints them, then
    `stop -t 20` + `rm`; with no project name it calls docker not at all. `INT TERM HUP` were NOT added
    to the traps (no effect, as the auditor measured). Pinned with a stub `docker` that records its
    arguments: the label filter is present, only the e2e-named containers in the listing are stopped
    (the app container beside them is not), and an empty project name makes no call.

    **(g) `testclips.sh` writes through `.part` and trusts ffprobe, not `-s` (#18).** Every fixture is
    written to `.<name>.mp4.part` (`-f mp4`, since the name has no extension) and renamed into place
    only when ffmpeg exited 0, so the final name is either absent or whole; "exists" is now "ffprobe
    reads a duration out of it", so a 1-byte plant or an interrupted write is regenerated with a `!`
    line. `TESTCLIPS_ONLY=<name>` limits a run to named fixtures (the self-test's pin generates one
    clip: a 1-byte plant beside a stale `.part` is regenerated, the `.part` is gone, the final file
    probes, the next run keeps it).

    **(h) `visual.sh` tidies only its own stack (#24).** `prune_visual_` and `rm_visual_collections_`
    run through `docker compose exec` in the checkout, i.e. against the LOCAL project; with a foreign
    `BASE=` that project is not the stack photographed. `ENV_BASE` is resolved as e2e.sh resolves it and
    both tidy-ups run only when `BASE` equals it, with a NOTE otherwise; `VISUAL_DRY=1` prints the
    decision and exits before the sheet is removed or the image built (pinned with a stub `docker` on
    PATH: a foreign BASE runs no `compose exec`; the default BASE keeps the tidy-up on).

    **(i) The `mc rm --recursive --force` traps ask a guard first (#28).** `store_rm_prefix_ok_`
    refuses an empty prefix, `/`, a dot-path and anything not of the harness's own minted shape
    `^e2e-[a-z0-9]+-[0-9]+/$`; the three trap functions (`o1_rm_prefix2`, `qo_rm_prefix`,
    `md_rm_prefix`) return before `store_mc` when it refuses, and `store_mc_derive_` dies on an empty
    `S3_BUCKET` before building `SM_ROOT` from it. Pinned: the minted shape passes; empty, `/`, `.`,
    `clips/` and the shape without its trailing slash are refused.

    **(j) Three more edges of the same kind (2026-09-17, lane `misc`, from this erratum's own cleanup
    row and the Gate 10/12 harness notes).** (b) made `lane-teardown.sh` strict about what it removes,
    but not about WHERE IT IS RUN: `$0` decides which checkout the script thinks it is in, so a copy
    run from inside a lane worktree resolved `REPO` to that worktree, looked for `<worktree>-<lane>`,
    found nothing, and reported "already gone" — an OK for the tree it was standing in, with the
    branch trivially an ancestor of main before its first commit. It now refuses unless the cwd IS the
    main worktree, which git can answer whatever the cwd is (`git rev-parse --git-common-dir`, whose
    parent is the main checkout). The self-test runs the SAME copy from the scratch repo's lane
    worktree and asserts the refusal; it reports OK without the guard, verified on this lane.

    Second, (d)'s own pin. The stranger — the object outside `clips/$C/` whose survival proves the
    `--clip` scope — was planted just before the delete loop, so on the first pass it was seconds old
    and would have survived because it was younger than `--min-age`, whatever the scope did. An object
    store has no `touch`, so it is now planted FIRST, before the two extras the report loop already
    waits to age, and the step then asks `admin orphans --clip <the stranger> --min-age 5s` — a
    read-only report scoped to its own prefix, which lists nothing else and removes nothing — and
    requires the `orphan ` line rather than the `recent … (skipped: younger than …)` one before the
    delete runs. This is the audit the Gate 10 note asked for, over every drop-in that plants an object
    a report or the sweeper must SEE: `88-fsstore.sh` already gives both its plants a 2020 mtime
    (a directory has `touch`); `51-admin.sh`'s backup plants already stamp the stale one and leave the
    fresh one fresh, deliberately; `73-ops.sh`, `89-quota.sh` and `90-media.sh` remove prefixes and
    plant nothing; `70-web.sh` and `62-tiers.sh` read a report about objects a real job wrote and
    assert an ABSENCE that age cannot fake. The stranger was the one that plants "now" and asserts on
    it.

    Third, the transcript. 61-nits2's `warn-probe:` lines are its own throwaway container's — the
    shipped-credential warning it asserts, and a `storage ping failed … 400 Bad Request` from a probe
    booted with credentials that cannot authenticate by design — and a reader scanning a run for WARN
    meets them first with no way to tell an asserted one from a stack fault. A NOTE now says so, above
    them. Along with it, three stale harness comments: `85-bot.sh` said THREE throwaway containers
    (four since erratum 284) and "the two probe containers" that take its fabricated origin (three),
    and still explained the link option's origin as though something read it back — nothing has since
    erratum 286; `77-design.sh` counted "the four rules" its stylesheet block asserts (it names each of
    them now, and the one spelling that must NOT be in the file), said its in-container script is "a
    FILE rather than an inlined `-c`" when it is written to a file and then handed to `sh -c` as one
    argument, and printed the upload status twice inside one `expect`, which prints it already.

291. **The checkpoint carries the tier decision, and the three job-row writes a run makes on its own
    behalf are pinned to its attempt** (2026-09-16, the audit's #1 and #12, lane `worker`;
    `internal/worker/pipeline.go`, `internal/db/jobs.go`, the seven sibling runs' `setStage`).

    **(a) A finalize-only retry committed blank tier columns.** `checkpoint()` marshals `j.ready`
    (§10.3 step 8), and the ONLY assignment of `j.ready.Tiers` was inside `finalize()` — AFTER it. So
    every checkpoint this program ever wrote carried the zero `TierFields`, and the one path the
    checkpoint exists for — a released job (`ReleaseJob` keeps the checkpoint: a shutdown, a boot
    reconcile, `admin jobs unstick`, the automatic repair) retried finalize-only, with no probe — read
    it back and committed `original_playable = false`, `original_codec = ''`, `full_state = ''` and
    `light_state = ''` on a clip whose every file was in the bucket. Finalize's own comment said the
    checkpoint "is where this very struct wrote it", which was the intention and not the fact; erratum
    206's `TestTierFieldsSurviveAFinalizeOnlyRetry` round-trips a hand-built struct and could not see
    the order of two calls. The decision now runs ONCE, between `store` and the checkpoint
    (`settleTiers`): the columns first, then the instruction — `playSize()` reads
    `Tiers.OriginalPlayable`, so the order is load-bearing — and the checkpoint carries all of it.
    `finalize` derives nothing from a probe any more; the one thing it still decides is `QueueSocial`,
    which is an INSTRUCTION rather than a column and rides on no checkpoint, and it decides it from
    `j.ready` alone (`settleLight`), so a fresh run repeats its own answer and a retry asks the
    checkpoint's fields the same question. `TestCheckpointCarriesTheTierDecision` reads the checkpoint
    the RUN wrote and then commits a second clip from exactly those bytes; both halves fail on the old
    order (proved by reverting the one call). A checkpoint written BEFORE this pass still carries the
    zero struct — a row that was `running` with a checkpoint across the upgrade — and such a retry
    commits as it did before; the window is the seconds between a checkpoint and its commit.

    **(b) `SetJobStage`, `SaveCheckpoint` and `CancelJob` matched on the id alone.** Every other
    writer of a running row tests `state = 'running'` (`FailAttempt`, `ReleaseJob`,
    `RequeueWithBackoff`, `CompleteJob`), and none of them tests WHOSE attempt the row is; these three
    did not even test the state. The scenario is not this process racing itself — the automatic repair
    skips every job in its own `live` set (erratum 231) — but a SECOND hand on the database: the CLI's
    `admin jobs unstick` on a live job (DEPLOY §24.3 said in so many words that "the older run then
    cancels the job row underneath it"), a second instance's automatic repair, or a stale probe
    container of a died E2E. After such a repair the row is `queued` again or a NEWER attempt's, and
    the old run kept writing: its stage over the new attempt's, a `cancelled` over a row it did not
    hold, and — the one that matters — a checkpoint naming ITS keys onto a row whose next finalize
    would then publish objects another attempt never made. The three writes now carry the run's claim
    stamp (`AND state = 'running' AND started_at = ?`; `claimStamp(j.job)`, which `ClaimJob` always
    set), a miss says why (`ErrNotFound` for a missing id, `ErrStateMismatch` for a row that is not
    this attempt's), and two claims can never share a stamp: an unstick needs ≥ 30 s of age and the
    stamp is whole seconds. The run treats a mismatch as a LOST ATTEMPT, never as a failure: a stage
    that will not write is abandoned at INFO and the run goes on; a checkpoint that will not write
    ends the run through `lostAttempt` — the uploads it made are discarded (nothing references them:
    the checkpoint is what would have), its scratch outputs go, the source stays, the progress entry
    is forgotten, and the row is NOT touched, because `FailAttempt` there would spend the current
    owner's counter. One window moved: `MarkDeleting` cancels a clip's jobs as it tombstones the clip,
    so a tombstone that lands mid-run is now met at the checkpoint rather than at finalize's
    conditional flip; `checkpoint()` re-reads the clip on a mismatch and a `deleting` or missing clip
    takes the lost-race ending it always took (`lostRace`, `CancelJob` answering "already ended under
    another hand" at INFO, the same three keys removed). `CancelJob` no longer takes a `queued` row and
    is no longer silent over a row that has ended; its only production caller is a run cancelling the
    claim it holds, and the test callers that cancelled queued trim jobs now claim them first.
    `TestAttemptPinnedWritesRefuseAStaleHandle` (claim, unstick, re-claim, the old handle refused on
    all three and the row byte-for-byte unchanged) and `TestARunWhoseRowWasRepairedEndsAsALostAttempt`
    (an unstick from inside the encode; the row keeps the repair's ONE crash attempt, no transient
    failure, no checkpoint; the bucket holds the original alone) both fail on the unpinned statements.
    The four state-only writers named above are still unpinned — a `FailAttempt` from a run whose row
    a newer attempt holds would still count against that attempt — and that is recorded as a cleanup row
    rather than widened here: every one of them is reached only through an ending the pinned
    checkpoint now precedes on the transcode path, and the media kinds' endings are a lane of their
    own.

    **(c) What an operator sees.** Three new INFO lines, all expected endings: `job row is no longer
    this attempt's; stage not recorded` (per stage, after a repair under a live run), `job row is no
    longer this attempt's; outputs discarded, row untouched` (the lost attempt), `job already ended
    under another hand; nothing to cancel` (a lost race whose job `MarkDeleting` had already
    cancelled). DEPLOY §24.3's sentence about the older run cancelling the row underneath a second
    worker is corrected: it cannot, now, and what it does instead is the second of those lines.


292. **Four operator-facing knobs that were not what they said: the compose shape audited** (2026-09-16, lane
    `knobs` of the audit run — items #14, #10, #27 and #6; `compose.yaml`, `compose.tunnel.yaml`,
    `compose.tunnel-local.yaml`, `Dockerfile`, `scripts/check.sh`, `internal/clientip`).

    **(a) `STORAGE_PING_ATTEMPTS` and `STORAGE_PING_INTERVAL` reached no container.** Erratum 57 made
    `compose.yaml`'s `environment:` block the one path from `.env` to the process — every §4 variable
    interpolated with its documented default — and DEPLOY §7 and `.env.example` both described these two as
    settable. Neither had a row. `config.go` read them (`l.intMin`, `l.duration`, with a boot error for a
    bad value), so the code was right and the documentation was right and an operator who set
    `STORAGE_PING_ATTEMPTS=40` for a NAS that is slow after a reboot got the default ten, silently. The
    audit computed the diff — 67 names read, 75 keys passed, exactly these two on the left and not the
    right — and the fix is the two rows. What keeps it fixed is a `check.sh` stage that recomputes that
    diff on every run: every `l.<kind>("NAME"` in `internal/config`'s non-test files against every key
    under the `app` service's `environment:`, a self-test with a planted config file and a planted compose
    (a name passed only to the `minio` service must still be flagged), and a floor of 50 names so a regex
    that rots to nothing fails rather than passes. The lane's own first cut of that regex could not see
    a helper with a digit in its name (`l.int64Min`, four names) nor the four Discord names, which reach
    the loader as `Env…` constants — found by asking why compose passed eight names config "did not
    read"; the stage takes the union of both spellings now and its self-test plants one of each. With
    that, the two lists are the same 75 names. The stage is one-directional on purpose: an extra row
    would be harmless, a missing one is this erratum.

    **(b) The production ingress ran a moving tag.** Both tunnel files named `cloudflare/cloudflared:latest`,
    so every `docker compose up -d` after a registry push — the E2E's own step 1 included — was an
    unreviewed upgrade of the one process every viewer's bytes cross, while §17.1 pinned every other image
    and said so. The tag is now `2026.8.3`: not the registry's newest (`2026.9.1`, pushed 2026-09-11) but
    the version the reference and dev tunnels were actually running (`docker image inspect`'s
    `RepoDigests`, `sha256:51c9cef…`, built 2026-08-31), because a pin records what was verified and a bump
    is a separate, reviewable edit — §17.1's new row says how. The index digest sits beside the tag as a
    comment, the way the Dockerfile keeps its bases' (an anchor, not a pin). A second `check.sh` stage greps
    `compose*.yaml` for `:latest`, comments included — on the lane's own first run it caught the lane's own
    comment, which is the stage doing its job: a spelled-out `:latest` in a comment is a recipe somebody
    will paste. DEPLOY §3's two quick-tunnel recipes and the operator notes' `cloudflared` invocations name the
    same tag; the recipes are documentation, so the stage does not cover them, and drift there costs a
    reader nothing worse than a version.

    **(c) The GPU stage's digests.** The Dockerfile's `gpu` stage had, since 2026-09-08, a comment saying
    "digests … recorded for the same reason as the three above" followed by two image names and no
    digests. They are recorded now, dated, from `docker buildx imagetools inspect`: `jrottenberg/ffmpeg:
    7.1-nvidia` is a SINGLE `linux/amd64` manifest (`sha256:8cf5440…`), not a multi-arch index, which is
    the platform erratum 247 proved and the only one it claims; `nvidia/cuda:12.6.2-runtime-ubuntu24.04`
    is an index (`sha256:16411bb…`, amd64 + arm64). §17.1 gains the two rows; its "three digests" sentence
    now counts five and names the tunnel's as the sixth of the same kind.

    **(d) An IPv6 client is keyed by its /64.** `clientip.Resolve` returned the whole address, and both
    callers key on it: `ipKey` for the auth and view limiters (§14) and `views.Key` for the dedupe
    (erratum 103's "a count is bounded by ADDRESSES, which the caller cannot mint"). That sentence was
    true of IPv4 and false of IPv6: an ISP hands a household or a phone a /64, inside which the host
    picks the low 64 bits itself — privacy extensions rotate them hourly — so one machine could present
    2^64 distinct addresses to a limiter that gave each a fresh budget and to a dedupe that counted each a
    viewer. `Resolve` now folds an IPv6 result to `netip.PrefixFrom(a, 64).Masked().Addr()`; every caller
    inherits it and none needed the exact address (the access log prints `RemoteAddr` from the request,
    not this). The fold is applied to the RESOLVED client and after the trusted-proxy test, which still
    runs on the exact peer: a proxy trusted as `fd00::1/128` is matched by `fd00::1`, not refused because
    its /64 base is not in the prefix — `TestResolveFoldAfterProxyCheck` pins that order, with the
    X-Forwarded-For walk's per-hop test covered too. IPv4, a v4-mapped address (already unmapped by
    `parseAddr`) and the invalid zero `Addr` are unchanged. The cost is the same one erratum 103 accepted
    for a NAT: a household is one auth budget and one view per window; the right side to be wrong on for
    a limiter and a private counter. Pins: `TestResolveFoldsIPv6ToSlash64` (one /64 → one `Addr`, two
    /64s → two, IPv4 and a zoned link-local as expected), `TestAuthRateLimitIPv6Slash64` (a second address
    in the exhausted /64 is 429; a neighbouring /64 and an IPv4 neighbour are not) and
    `TestViewDedupeIPv6Slash64` (one view per /64 per window; a second /64 is a second view) — all three,
    and two rows of `TestResolve`'s table, fail with the fold reverted to `return a`, verified on this
    lane. Nothing about a viewer is stored by any of this: the dedupe key was already a truncated hash of
    the address, and it is now a hash of a coarser one.

293. **Every ENDING a job writes is pinned to the attempt that holds the row, and every kind has a
    lost-attempt ending** (2026-09-17, lane `attempts` of checkpoint 2, from the cleanup list's lane-worker
    row (2026-09-16, erratum 291); `internal/db/jobs.go`, `internal/db/ops.go`, `internal/worker/pipeline.go`
    and the seven media runs).

    **(a) The four writers erratum 291 left on `state = 'running'` alone.** 291 pinned the three writes a
    run makes WHILE IT RUNS — `SetJobStage`, `SaveCheckpoint`, `CancelJob` — and said in as many words that
    `FailAttempt`, `ReleaseJob`, `RequeueWithBackoff` and `CompleteJob` were still unpinned, because on the
    TRANSCODE path every one of them sits behind the pinned checkpoint and a repaired row is met there
    first. The media kinds have no checkpoint. Nothing preceded their endings, so a run whose row a
    SECOND HAND had taken — an operator's `admin jobs unstick` on a live job (DEPLOY §24.3), a second
    process's automatic repair (§24.6), the boot reconcile — could still end that row on the old
    attempt's word: `fail()` spent the NEW attempt's counter and, at the cap, failed the job while its
    encode was running; `release()` and `noRoom()` put a running attempt's job back on the queue;
    `complete()` marked it `done`. Measured, not reasoned: with the pin reverted,
    `TestEveryKindsEndingRefusesAStaleHandle` shows all seven kinds taking the repaired row's `attempts`
    from 1 to 2, and six of the seven ending it outright.

    The four now take the claim stamp as their second argument — `(ctx, jobID, startedAt, …)`, the shape
    291 gave the other three — and refuse a row that is not that attempt's with `ErrStateMismatch`, a gone
    id with `ErrNotFound`, changing nothing either way. `CompleteJob` became one `attemptWrite` whose
    WHERE carries the kind too (`kind <> 'transcode' AND state = 'running' AND started_at = ?`), so the §5
    rule that only a transcode moves a clip is enforced by the statement rather than by a read before it;
    the other three read the row for its kind, its counters and its clip coupling before they can decide
    what to write, so they test the same predicate in Go, in the same transaction, through
    `heldByAttempt`. The stamp rule is 291's unchanged and is repeated here once because it is what makes
    the pin sound: two claims can never share a stamp, since an unstick needs ≥ 30 s of age and
    `started_at` is whole seconds. `db.ClaimStamp` is that rule's one definition now, in the package that
    owns the row, and the worker's private `claimStamp` is gone.

    **(b) The REPAIR is the one caller that is not pinned.** The boot reconcile, the automatic repair and
    `admin jobs unstick` end a row precisely because they have established that no run of this process is
    holding it — their evidence is age plus the live set, not a claim stamp they could hold — so
    `repairRunningJobTx` passes the sentinel `unpinned` (`-1`, which no Unix-second stamp can be) to the
    two tx-level bodies it shares with the exported endings. It is also what must keep reaching a `running`
    row whose `started_at` is NULL: `staleEnough` deliberately counts that as stale, it is exactly the
    inconsistency a repair exists for, and no pinned write could ever match it
    (`TestTheRepairStillReachesARunningRowWithNoStamp`).

    **(c) The lost-attempt ending, per kind.** Each of the seven media runs (`trim`, `gif`, `social`,
    `replace`, `poster`, `filmstrip`, `full`) gained its own `lostAttempt`, the copy of the one 291 gave
    the transcode: the row is NOT touched, what this attempt uploaded is discarded (a media kind keeps no
    checkpoint, so nothing references it), this attempt's scratch outputs go, the source stays for
    whoever runs the row next, the kind's progress entry is forgotten, and the line is INFO — a repair
    somebody chose to run is an expected ending, not a failure. Two kinds differ in one detail each, and
    both are the kind's existing rule rather than a new one. `replace` discards its ENCODE outputs only
    and keeps the uploaded original, because the job's params name that file and whichever attempt runs
    the row next reads it — the same reason its requeue keeps it; before this pass the mismatch branch of
    its `fail()` took `attempted` whole, which was safe only for the tombstone reading of a mismatch.
    `social` and `full` leave their TIER column alone: it still says `encoding`, and it is the attempt
    that holds the row that will settle it (`SettleTierEncoding`'s guard refuses while any job of the
    kind is queued or running — erratum 237 — so `full`'s `markSkipped` after a refused `complete()` is
    safe without a check of its own).

    On the TRANSCODE path the same three endings now reach `lostAttempt` too, which brought one case the
    ending from the checkpoint never could: a run that has ALREADY checkpointed and is then released
    (a shutdown racing a repair). That checkpoint names this attempt's objects, a checkpointed row is
    RELEASED by the repair rather than failed, and the retry finalizes onto them — so a checkpointed lost
    attempt leaves the bucket alone and says so in its own line. Objects a still newer checkpoint has
    since superseded are bounded orphans under the clip's own prefix, listed by `admin orphans`, which is
    the direction §10.1 already takes. `requeueNoCount` returns the refusal instead of swallowing it, so
    every kind's `noRoom` can take the ending rather than log a requeue that did not happen. A `notify`
    job's whole lost-attempt ending is one line: it writes no object, keeps no scratch and registers no
    progress.

    **(d) Every exit path, and where its pin is.** Per media kind: `complete()` → `CompleteJob`;
    `release()` → `ReleaseJob`; `fail()` → `FailAttempt`; `noRoom()` → `requeueNoCount` →
    `RequeueWithBackoff`; `lostRace()` → `CancelJob` (pinned by 291); and the kind's COMMIT —
    `SwapRendition`, `SetGIF`, `SetSocial`, `SwapSource`, `SetPoster`, `SetFilmstrip`, `SetFull` — which
    is that kind's finalize and is left exactly as it was: it is guarded by the CLIP (still `ready`, still
    on the rendition the job read) and reports a refusal rather than erroring, so a stale attempt's commit
    publishes an object of its own making onto a clip that still wants one, and the newer attempt then
    reads "the job is no longer running" and discards its own. Pinning those seven to the attempt as well
    is a real tightening and a lane of its own; it is a cleanup row rather than widened here. On the
    transcode path: `finish()` → `release()` / `fail()` / `noRoom()` / `lostAttempt()`, `lostRace()`, and
    `FinalizeTranscode`, which was already guarded by the clip and by erratum 102's attempt-key re-read.
    `notify`: `completeNotify`, `releaseNotify`, `failNotify`. `refuseKind` (an unknown kind) fails
    through the same pinned `FailAttempt`. No ending that spends an attempt, returns a row to the queue
    or resolves a job on the WORKER's own word writes on `state = 'running'` alone any more. The eight
    that resolve a row on the CLIP's word are the exception, and are exactly the eight named above: the
    seven kind commits, which still resolve the job on `state = 'running'` alone, and `FinalizeTranscode`,
    which tests no job state at all — in both the clip's own `WHERE` is the guard, and a commit it
    refuses is reported to the caller rather than written.

    **(e) What an operator sees.** One INFO line per kind, the transcode's wording with the kind's name
    in front: `trim job row is no longer this attempt's; outputs discarded, row untouched` (and `gif`,
    `social`, `replace`, `poster`, `filmstrip`, `full`); the transcode's own second form, `job row is no
    longer this attempt's; its checkpoint keeps the outputs, row untouched`, for the checkpointed release
    above; and `notify job row is no longer this attempt's; nothing recorded, row untouched`. None of them
    is WARN or ERROR. Pins: `TestEveryKindsEndingRefusesAStaleHandle` (all seven kinds × all four
    endings, through a handle whose row was unstuck and re-claimed — every one refused and the row byte
    for byte unchanged, then the CURRENT attempt's ending lands),
    `TestATrimWhoseRowWasRepairedEndsAsALostAttempt` (the same from a LIVE run, the unstick fired from
    inside the cut), `TestAttemptPinnedEndingsRefuseAStaleHandle` and
    `TestCompleteJobStillRefusesATranscodeJob` at the db level, and erratum 206's
    `TestTierFieldsSurviveAFinalizeOnlyRetry` and 291's two still green.






294. **The link-out card describes its picture too: `og:image:alt` and `twitter:image:alt` on every
    state that is not `ready`, and §9.1's link-out inventory is 16 tags** (2026-09-17, lane `alt`, from
    the cleanup list's lane-card section). Erratum 103 gave the READY card the one accessibility
    affordance a card has and erratum 177 gave X its half of the same sentence, on the principle that
    half an affordance is not one — and both stopped at the ready card, for the reason 177 wrote down:
    "a processing or failed card has no real frame to describe". The reason was about the FRAME and it
    was right. What it left behind is a card with a 1200×630 picture on it that a reader who cannot see
    it is told nothing at all about, which is the same half an affordance read from the other end.
    177's head now says it is narrowed here.

    **The sentence names the PICTURE and not the clip**, which is the one way it differs from
    `imageAlt`'s. Since erratum 287(f) the placeholder is the wordmark on the Kept dark ground and
    carries no text at all, so there are exactly two things worth telling a reader who cannot see it:
    what is drawn — "The Clippet wordmark" — and the state, which is why this is a link-out card at all
    and is the fact the reader came for. It does not name the clip. The picture is not of this clip and
    never was; `og:title` carries the title two tags above it; and an alt that claimed the placeholder
    showed this clip would be the one thing an alt may not do, which is lie about a picture. It carries
    no host either: the site line is `og:site_name`'s job (erratum 287(a)), and a self-hoster's card
    must not describe its picture in somebody else's domain.

    **Two sentences, because the card has two states.** "The Clippet wordmark: this clip is still
    encoding" for `queued` and `processing`, "The Clippet wordmark: this clip could not be encoded" for
    `failed`. The first two share one exactly as `og:description` gives them one `"Processing…"`: the
    card draws no distinction between a clip nothing has claimed yet and one being encoded, and an alt
    that drew one would be the only surface in the product that does. The word is ENCODING because that
    is the product's own word for the state on the page ("Encoding on the server — the Discord card is
    not ready yet.", erratum 213). `productName` builds both, so the product's spelling has one home.

    **The inventory moved 14 → 16, in the four places that pin it.** §9.1's link-out paragraph; the
    `BuildMeta` golden (`TestBuildMetaLinkOut`, an exact 16-entry map per state, with the alt as the
    state's own value); `TestLinkOutInventoryIsSixteenTags`, which pins the COUNT for its own sake on
    both schemes and all three states the way `TestReadyInventoryIsTwentySevenTags` holds the ready
    card's — a golden that listed tags without counting them would let one more in; and `card_check`'s
    `linkout` branch in `scripts/e2e.sh`, which until now asserted PRESENCE alone and printed "no exact
    card inventory" beside the page's tag count. That branch is exact now: it takes the clip's STATE as
    its last argument (`encoding`, the default, or `failed` — the two values that follow from it are the
    description and the alt), it matches the placeholder by prefix so the asset version's cache-busting
    query is not pinned, and both branches print the same one count line. **The READY card does not
    move**: 27 tags on http and 28 on https, exactly as errata 103 and 177 left it, and a link-out card
    gains nothing on https because it has no `og:video:secure_url` and no URL of its own but the PNG's.

    **What did not change, stated rather than glossed.** `og:video:url` and `video:duration` stay absent
    from a link-out card (`TestLinkOutCardGainedOnlyItsAlts`, renamed from `…GainedNothing`): there is
    no video to point at and no measured duration to state, and a tag whose content would be invented is
    worse than no tag — which is also why the alt does not borrow the ready card's sentence. The
    COLLECTION card (§9.4, `BuildCollectionMeta`) is deliberately untouched and is not this erratum's
    subject: its picture is a member clip's poster when the list has a ready member and there is NO
    picture at all when it does not, so both the sentence and the prior question — is there anything to
    describe — are different ones. It is recorded as this lane's own cleanup nit rather than
    fixed in passing.

    **What proves it live.** `55-owner.sh` step 56 already builds the suite's one deterministic
    not-ready subject — sixty seconds of 1080p60, stream-copied from a fixture, so the clip is certainly
    still encoding when the request lands — for the oEmbed `link` document. Its SHARE PAGE is now kept
    at that same instant, before the state is re-read, and `card_check linkout`'d: every run asserts the
    sixteen tags and both sentences against a real stack, as a HUMAN, because a crawler with no card to
    read is held at 503 with no card tags at all (erratum 213) and that page is step 5's subject. Step
    5's own conditional check of clip E is unchanged; a fast box can race it, which is why it was never
    the pin. The Go pins were proven to fail on the old code by reverting the two emissions: 14 tags,
    want 16, on all three states and both schemes.





295. **`~/Videos/clippet` — the one-container flavour's desktop default** (ROADMAP #42 (a), the owner's
    call of 2026-09-16: `~/Videos/clippet` is a fine default on Windows and macOS;
    lane `drop`. Changed: `compose.fs.yaml`, `cmd/clippet/doctor.go`, `.env.example`, DEPLOY §32.1 and
    §24.1's table. New: `scripts/fsdefault.sh` and `TestDoctorStoreNamesTheHostDirectory` in
    `cmd/clippet/doctor_drop_test.go`. No migration; the `s3` flavour resolves byte-for-byte as it did.)

    **(a) What changed.** `compose.fs.yaml`'s bind was
    `${STORAGE_DIR_HOST:?set STORAGE_DIR_HOST in .env…}` — a REQUIRED variable, which is right for a
    server and wrong for the machine somebody is trying this on for the first time. It now defaults to
    the person's own Videos folder. That folder is already the right place: a capture tool writes
    there, and the store keeps its objects under `clips/` beside its `.clippet-store` marker, so the
    folder's ROOT stays theirs — which is what erratum 296's drop folder then reads. A server still
    sets the variable and nothing about it changes; DEPLOY §32's `/srv/clippet-media` is still the
    example, with the desktop default as §32.1's first sentence.

    **(b) The spelling, measured rather than assumed.** Compose interpolation cannot expand `~`, so the
    default is spelled from the variables a shell already exports:
    `${STORAGE_DIR_HOST:-${HOME:-${USERPROFILE}}/Videos/clippet}`. Three facts came out of running
    `docker compose config` (v2.40.3) on this box in BOTH shells, and each of them decided something:

    - **Nested `:-` works.** Git Bash and PowerShell both resolve it, and both resolve it to the same
      path on Windows — because MSYS converts a path-shaped variable for a native child, so docker.exe
      is handed `HOME=C:\<home>` and the bind source is `C:\<home>/Videos/clippet` in either
      shell. The daemon takes the mixed separators (proven with a throwaway `docker run -v`).
    - **Nested `:?` DOES NOT WORK, and that is the spelling this erratum exists to warn about.**
      `${STORAGE_DIR_HOST:-${HOME:-${USERPROFILE:?…}}/Videos/clippet}` is the obvious way to refuse on
      a machine with no home directory at all. Compose evaluates that guard EAGERLY: it fires whenever
      USERPROFILE is unset — with HOME set and the branch never taken, and even with STORAGE_DIR_HOST
