302. **Sign in with Discord on an instance — the instance's own application, a second key to an existing door**
    (2026-09-17, lane `signin` of checkpoint 2, ROADMAP #44; `internal/config/discordlogin.go`, migration `0019` (0018 is lane `drop`'s; renumbered at merge),
    `internal/db/users.go`, `internal/auth` (the flow cookie), `internal/notify/login.go`, `internal/httpapi/discord_login.go`,
    `internal/web/pages.go`, `web/templates/{login,settings}.html`, `web/static/app.js`, `cmd/clippet/{admin,doctor,serve}.go`,
    `scripts/e2e.d/93-signin.sh`; DEPLOY §19.6; the design of record is in the run's records).

    **Amended 2026-10-19 (erratum 341):** "never a door" holds for THIS feature, the OAuth button — it still creates
    nothing under any mode. The instance's door is now the bot's signed `/signin` (never OAuth, never the plane), under
    `REGISTRATION=members|role:<id>`; the missing recovery story is `admin users password` plus Discord's own — see 341.

    **(a) Whose application, and why.** Each instance registers its OWN Discord application (`DISCORD_LOGIN_CLIENT_ID` +
    `DISCORD_LOGIN_CLIENT_SECRET`, both or none, independent of the bot's three and of `managed`). Not the official application
    brokering identity through `bot.clippet.gg`: that would put our Worker in the login path of every self-hosted box — a
    call-home in the free product §15's first bullet forbids — and would make a compromised or mistaken Worker able to mint an
    assertion for ANY Discord id against ANY instance that trusted its key, which is the failure mode that decides it (the brief's
    "Worker down = nobody can log in" is the softer one: the password path stays). The cost of (a) is one portal visit of about
    two minutes; an own-bot instance reuses its application outright (the OAuth2 client id IS the application id), and a managed
    instance makes a small one. The brokered shape is recorded to its seam in the design file (§10) and not scheduled.

    **(b) The account rule: a second key, never a door.** The callback looks the proven Discord user id up in
    `users.discord_user_id`; found → a session exactly as `POST /api/auth/login` issues one (same row, same cookie, same clamp;
    `GET /api/auth/me` keeps saying `via: session`); not found → **no account is created, under any `REGISTRATION` value** —
    `closed` still means closed, `first` is still bootstrapped by a password, `open` still means "anyone who reaches `/register`",
    not "anyone with a Discord account". A match on username is never a link (the id is the key; the name is display, refreshed
    at every Discord login). Two ways to link, both explicit: the signed-in owner from Settings, **re-entering their password**
    (erratum 108's reason — an unlocked laptop must not silently become a permanent takeover), and the operator's `clippet admin
    users link <username> <discord-id>`. Both refuse an id already linked to another account (409 `discord_taken` never reaches
    the wire: the callback lands on `/settings?discord=taken` naming nobody; the CLI names the other account, since the operator
    sees every account anyway) and refuse a second link on an account that has one (409 `discord_linked`; "unlink first") — one
    explicit state change at a time, never a silent replacement. Unlink (`DELETE /api/auth/discord`, session + CSRF, no password:
    it removes a capability; `admin users unlink`) touches no session. A password change does not unlink; its session sweep
    reaches Discord-issued sessions like any other, because they ARE ordinary session rows. No global users, nothing
    cross-instance, no guild anything: the bot's guild binding (0016) and this link are different tables answering different
    questions.

    **(c) The flow, and its cookie.** `state` + PKCE, both carried in ONE browser-side cookie and NO server-side table: the
    cookie's value is `nonce "." base64url(mode NUL userID NUL next) "." mac` (the third segment is clause (h)'s, from the fix pass), where the nonce (32 random bytes as 43 base64url characters)
    IS the PKCE `code_verifier`, `code_challenge = base64url(sha256(nonce))` and `state = base64url(sha256("clippet-discord-state."
    ‖ nonce))` — domain-separated from the challenge; both public in the authorize URL, both bound to a secret only this browser
    holds. Its name is the session cookie's plus `_discord`, so it **inherits the `__Host-` prefix** on clippet.gg (the reasoning: a
    subdomain-planted flow cookie is the one way to fix a login); flags `Path=/; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Secure iff
    https; Max-Age=600` — Lax and not Strict, because the callback is a top-level GET from Discord's site. The authorize URL is
    built from `config.DiscordAPIHost()` (never a literal) with `response_type=code`, `scope=identify` and nothing else (no
    `email`, no `guilds`, ever), `code_challenge_method=S256`; no `prompt`. **The callback's checks, in order, each refusal a
    one-word verdict on the access line and never a value:** (1) the flow cookie's clearing is queued before anything else, so a
    flow is single-use and a **replayed callback URL is refused at step 2 with no outbound call**; (2) no cookie, or unparsable →
    `no_flow` → `/login?discord=expired`; (3) `state` ≠ the derived state (`subtle.ConstantTimeCompare`) → `bad_state` → the
    mode's page, `?discord=expired` (the page does not distinguish); (4) `error` present → `denied`; (5) `code` absent or over 512
    bytes → `bad_state`; (6) link mode: a live session whose user id equals the cookie's bound id, else `link_session` →
    `/settings`; (7) the exchange — `notify.Login.Identify`: `POST /api/v10/oauth2/token` (form: `client_id`, `client_secret`,
    `grant_type=authorization_code`, `code`, `redirect_uri`, `code_verifier`) then `GET /api/v10/users/@me` as a Bearer, 10 s per
    call, redirects never followed, the body windowed, the secret's spellings scrubbed from any echoed error, the `*url.Error`
    wrapper unwrapped to its cause; the access token is used for that one GET and discarded, the refresh token ignored and never
    stored — `identify` gives the instance no standing capability on anybody's Discord, and it keeps none; failure →
    `exchange_failed` (the scrubbed cause on the app log) → `?discord=failed`; (8) login mode: `GetUserByDiscordID` → `unlinked`
    or `issueSession` + `TouchDiscordUsername`, `login=discord user=<name> client_ip` on the access line → 303 `next` (held to
    `safeNext`'s rule, duplicated in httpapi with a table pin since it cannot import web); link mode: `LinkDiscord` — an
    `UPDATE … WHERE id = ? AND discord_user_id IS NULL`, 0 rows or the partial UNIQUE index → `taken`; ok → `discord_linked=<name>
    discord_id=<id>` → `/settings?discord=linked`. The refusal pages read one line from a closed map; an unknown value renders
    nothing, and with the feature off neither the button nor a notice exists.

    **(d) The routes and the buckets.** Three paths, four handlers, registered ONLY when configured (off = the router's 404, like
    the bot's): `GET /api/auth/discord/start?next=` (anonymous; signed in → 303 `next`; `Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site` → 303
    `/login` — a plain anchor, not a form, because CSP `form-action 'self'` is enforced on a form's redirect chain), `POST
    /api/auth/discord` (`RequireSession`, CSRF, JSON, `{"current_password"}` → `200 {"url"}`; app.js navigates — a script
    navigation, not a request the page makes off-origin), `GET /api/auth/discord/callback` (anonymous, a navigation, never JSON),
    `DELETE /api/auth/discord` (`RequireSession`, CSRF; 204 or 404 `not_linked`). Start, callback and the link POST are in the
    **`auth` bucket** (10/min/IP): the callback performs an outbound exchange and a database write, the POST a bcrypt compare —
    erratum 108's argument; a Discord login costs two tokens where a password login costs one. The two GETs carry no
    `TimeoutHandler` (the callback's two calls have their own budgets). CSRF: the login-CSRF attack on OAuth (an attacker completing
    a callback in a victim's browser with the attacker's code) fails at step 3, because the victim's browser holds no cookie for
    the attacker's state; the link-mode variant additionally needs the victim's password at the start. `Cache-Control: no-store`
    on every navigation answer.

    **(e) The CLI and the doctor.** `clippet admin users link <username> <discord-id>` (15–25 digits; refuses "already linked to
    <other>" and "already linked — run `users unlink` first", exit 1; 2 on usage), `clippet admin users unlink <username>`
    (reports whether there was one), and the `users` listing gains `discord=<id|->`. The doctor's `login` row (between `bot` and
    `repair`, the fifteenth check): off → `discord login: off (… are unset): /api/auth/discord/start is not served and /login
    shows no Discord button`; on → `discord login: on - client <id>, secret (redacted)` plus the **Redirect URI** to paste
    (`<base>/api/auth/discord/callback`, byte for byte), and a WARN when `PUBLIC_BASE_URL` is plain http on any host but loopback
    (Discord accepts an http redirect only there). The secret is a needle from the raw environment before `config.Load` can
    fail, as the bot token is; `config.DiscordLogin.String()/LogValue()` render `client <id>, secret (redacted)`. The boot line is
    `discord login configured client_id=… redirect_uri=…`. Egress: two paths on `discord.com`, a host both allowlists already
    name; the client is built by `internal/notify`'s one construction function (a third caller), so check.sh's stages pass
    untouched and §15 gains a sentence and no name.

    **(f) What the harness proves, and what only a human can** (erratum 257's division). `93-signin.sh` (step 93, `parallel
    lane=4`) boots throwaway containers on private `DATA_DIR` + `SCRATCH_DIR` and proves, with **no outbound call anywhere**: the
    boot line, the anchor on `/login`, the authorize URL (`identify`, S256, the state in the URL EQUALS the state the host derives
    from the cookie's nonce with openssl — the flow cookie is browser-side only, so the harness holds it the way a browser does),
    the flow cookie's flags, cross-site/no-cookie/bad-state refused, the Settings panel following the link, the link POST
    401/200/409, `DELETE` 404/204 with the session untouched, the CLI matrix, the doctor row without the secret; a SECOND container
    with the same configuration answers the minted cookie's callback with the GOOD state and Discord's own refusal
    (`?discord=denied`, the cookie cleared), then the same URL again (`expired`, no exchange), no code and an absurd code; on the
    live stack the OFF state (or ON, whichever doctor reports); and one variable alone refusing to boot naming both. The one
    callback shape the suite never sends is a good state WITH a code, because that reaches Discord. Everything past the exchange
    is `httptest`: `internal/notify/login_test.go` (the token form and `redirect_uri`, the Bearer, a 3xx not followed, the secret
    scrubbed from an echoed 400, a 5xx, a hung server, the window) and `internal/httpapi/discord_login_test.go` (the whole matrix
    against a fake `IdentityProvider`: the OFF state; unlinked under `open`/`first`/`closed` with `CountUsers` unchanged; a
    linked login's cookie with login's exact flags and `via: session`; link mode taken / no session / another session / ok,
    then a login opening that account; unlink; `next` sanitised; the cookie cleared on every outcome; `__Host-` inherited;
    no body, header or log line carrying the code, the state, the verifier or the secret). The LIVE proof — the real portal,
    the real consent screen — is the owner's to run; until then the live half is unproven, as
    the bot's was.

    **(g) Not taken, on purpose.** The Worker-brokered identity (the seam is `DISCORD_LOGIN_CLIENT_ID=managed`, under which
    `start` would 302 to the bot's origin and `callback` would accept a Worker-signed Ed25519 assertion instead of a `code` —
    same cookie, same account rule, same routes; a Pass-lane subject, recorded in the design file and not scheduled); an
    account-creating mode (`REGISTRATION=discord`) until a passwordless account has a recovery story; per-user attribution of a
    bound guild's `/clip` (ROADMAP #33's list); Discord's `email` scope, guild membership checks and `prompt` extras. Three
    deviations from the lane brief, stated: the link POST is a fourth handler (the password at link time); the drop-in is a new
    `93-signin` rather than a "20-auth" extension, which is not a bundle; the exchange is proven by `httptest` rather than a
    stubbed Discord, because the binary cannot be pointed at a fake `discord.com` without a config knob that would weaken §15
    for a test's convenience.

    **(h) The flow cookie is authenticated** (2026-09-17, the fix pass after checkpoint 2's verifier; finding SIGNIN-1, a
    blocker). As built, the cookie was `nonce "." base64url(payload)` with no MAC and no server-side record, `state` is a public
    function of the nonce, and step 6 checked only that the session's user id equalled the cookie's — so the cookie was not proof
    the password was ever checked, it was a string the caller sends. Proved live: a thief holding Alice's SESSION cookie
    hand-builds a link-mode cookie naming her id, derives the state, consents at Discord with their OWN account (the client id is
    public, the redirect URI fixed, the PKCE challenge theirs to compute), replays the callback, and `LinkDiscord(alice,
    attackerDiscord)` succeeds — a second key that survives `changePassword`'s session sweep (erratum 108) and "Sign out
    everywhere else", the two things DEPLOY §19.2/§19.6 answer a stolen laptop with; (b)'s "an unlocked laptop must not silently
    become a permanent takeover" and (d)'s "the link-mode variant additionally needs the victim's password" asserted a property
    the build did not have. **The fix:** the cookie is `nonce "." base64url(payload) "." base64url(HMAC-SHA256(key, nonce "."
    base64url(payload)))`, with `key = sha256("clippet-discord-flow-mac." ‖ DISCORD_LOGIN_CLIENT_SECRET)`; `decodeFlow` verifies
    the MAC with `hmac.Equal` BEFORE reading a field, so a forged, tampered, re-bound or unsigned cookie is `no_flow` →
    `/login?discord=expired` at step 2, whichever mode it claims, with no exchange and no row. The nonce is inside the tag, so a
    payload cannot move under another nonce's state, and the bound user id is inside it, so a real link cookie cannot be
    re-bound. **Why a derived key and not a per-process random** (the verifier offered either): the client secret is exactly the
    value a session thief does not hold, it is never written anywhere (the key is a labelled hash of it, and the secret itself
    still goes to one place), it is the same across a restart (an in-flight ten-minute flow survives one) and on every replica
    of one configuration — which is what lets step 93's SECOND container answer the first container's cookie, the property (c)
    chose and (f) leans on. Rotating the secret invalidates in-flight flows, which is the right answer. **Why not a table:** (c)'s
    "no server-side table" was the design's own decision and it still holds; a MAC is the browser-side proof that decision was
    missing. Login-mode cookies carry the same MAC for consistency (nothing escalates there: a login-mode forgery could only
    make the exchange run with the forger's own code). Pins: `TestDiscordLinkCookieIsUnforgeable` (the unsigned repro, a cookie
    signed under a wrong key, a real login cookie with its payload swapped, a real link cookie re-bound to another account, a
    login-mode forgery — each with a live session for the named account, each `expired`, `IdentityProvider` never asked, no
    link written, and then the genuine cookie linking); it FAILS on the old behaviour (the MAC check neutered: the forged cookie
    landed on `/settings?discord=linked`). Step 93 (h) sends a hand-built link cookie and a tampered real one — both with the
    GOOD state and a code — to the second container and asserts `expired` with `outbound: 0`, the one place the harness sends
    that shape, because step 2 refuses it before step 7 exists. API.md's callback paragraph and DEPLOY §19.6's "on the wire"
    paragraph say it in one sentence each.

303. **The product glue the verification plane owes — one self-describing route, a compose file, a wizard walk and a runbook step, and still no "pass mode"**
    (2026-09-17, lane `glue`, ROADMAP #34 shape P1; `internal/httpapi/instance.go`, `router.go`, `httpapi.go`,
    `cmd/clippet/{main,serve}.go`, `Dockerfile`, `compose.yaml`, `compose.pass.yaml`, `.env.example`,
    `internal/web/{setup.go,pages.go}`, `web/templates/setup.html`, `scripts/e2e.sh`, `scripts/e2e.d/94-instance.sh`;
    API.md, DEPLOY §16/§17.4/§35.5/§36, README; the design of record is `clippet-pass/docs/verification-plane.md`
    — its §4, §8 and amendment 9 — and the sibling change is `clippet-pass` `guard/src/routes.ts`).

    **(a) The two rules this lane is bounded by, and why it does not break them.** A Clippet Pass sells a name on
    the owner's zone pointed at somebody's box, and the control plane that keeps that name honest has to know which release
    is answering. The product's side of it could have been a mode, and is not: **prov §3.4 stays literally true — there
    is no "pass mode" flag and no code path in this binary that branches on the Pass at run time**
    (the provisioning design's §3.4), and **the wizard holds no credential field**
    (the setup-page design's §0.1). What shipped is prose, a compose file, one anonymous route whose body
    is a function of the build and `.env`, and a page of the wizard that prints a block. A route that answers the same
    thing to everybody on every instance is not a flag; a printed `.env` line is not a field. The whole feature is
    unreachable from the app's own behaviour, which is the property that makes it checkable rather than promised.

    **(b) `GET /api/instance`, and its body as a contract.** `internal/httpapi/instance.go`: `200 application/json`,
    `Cache-Control: no-store`, anonymous, GET only (405 + `Allow: GET, HEAD`), registered **unconditionally** — outside
    the `discordConfigured()` block that `/api/bot/claim` lives in, because there is no configuration behind it — and
    under the existing **`claim` rate bucket** (30/min per client address) rather than a limiter of its own, which is
    the owner's standing rule and is right here: the two routes are the same shape of anonymous machine GET. The body is
    exactly four keys, in this order, for ever:
    `{"version":"<main.version>","build":"<40-hex commit>"|null,"media_delivery":"proxy"|"redirect","media_origin":"<scheme://host>"|null}`.
    `version` is `Deps.Version` (`dev` when unset — the field is a release NAME a verifier looks up, and `""` is not
    one); `media_delivery` comes from `Cfg.RedirectsMedia()`, the ONE predicate the media handlers and the CSP already
    share, so the three cannot disagree and the field is total even on a zero-valued Config; `media_origin` is
    `Cfg.MediaOrigin()`, which answers `""` on every proxy instance and is published as `null`, because the field names
    an origin or says there is not one. Nothing else is in it — no clip, account, count, bucket, endpoint, path or
    queue — which is §15's rule for `/healthz`, and `/healthz` itself is unchanged.

    **(c) `build` is the git commit, not the build id — an amendment to the design's §4.** The design wrote
    `"build":"<buildID>"`, meaning `serve.go`'s `?v=` cache-busting id (the version, or `dev-<start36>`). It cannot be
    that: `provision/src/verify.ts acceptRelease` accepts 7–40 hex characters, keeps the first twelve and looks that up
    in the release manifest's `commit`, and refuses anything else as **drift** — so a box answering `dev-1a2b3c` would be
    marked as having lied about its release. So `build` is `git rev-parse HEAD` of the tree the binary was built from,
    plumbed as `var commit = ""` in `cmd/clippet/main.go` (`-X main.commit=`), `ARG COMMIT=""` on the Dockerfile's
    build stage, `COMMIT: ${CLIPPET_COMMIT:-}` under compose's `args:` beside `VERSION`, and `#CLIPPET_COMMIT=` in
    `.env.example`. It defaults to EMPTY and not to a word: `version` can honestly call an unstamped build `dev`, and
    there is no honest stand-in for a commit. **It is validated on the way out** — only `^[0-9a-f]{40}$` is published,
    anything else is `null` — because the value arrives as a build argument, which is where a tag, a `git describe
    --dirty` string or an unexpanded `$(git rev-parse HEAD)` shows up, and publishing a malformed one is worse than
    publishing nothing.

    **(d) Every gate-built stack carries a commit.** `scripts/e2e.sh` step 1 exports
    `CLIPPET_COMMIT="$(git rev-parse HEAD)"` before its `up -d --build`; a shell variable wins over `.env` in compose
    interpolation, which is the same mechanism the run's raised limiters have used since Phase 2. It stamps HEAD even on
    a dirty tree, deliberately — `build` is not a claim that the working copy was clean, it is the commit a release
    manifest is looked up by, and a release is published from a clean tree by the runbook that says so.

    **(e) The release runbook, and the order that is load-bearing.** DEPLOY §17.4 (new, under §17.3 the release gate):
    the version convention is fixed HERE as `CLIPPET_VERSION=YYYY.MM.DD[.N]`, because no tagged release exists yet; the
    version in `.env` and the commit IN FRONT OF THE BUILD, then `e2e.sh` must PASS, then — **before any image or binary
    is published** — `cd ../clippet-pass/guard && CLIPPET=<checkout> sh scripts/test.sh manifest`, run
    `sh scripts/test.sh` in `guard/` **and** `provision/`, commit the four files those two steps wrote
    (`guard/releases/<commit12>.json` + `guard/releases/index.json` + `guard/releases/all.ts` +
    `provision/releases/index.json`), the owner deploys both Workers by hand, and only then the artefact. The order
    is load-bearing and §17.4 says why in one sentence: a customer who updates before the manifest is deployed answers
    with bytes the control plane has never seen, which reads as *foreign*, and a foreign name is disabled on the first
    occurrence with no automatic recovery. Two smaller orderings inside it are load-bearing too, and both were wrong in
    the lane's first draft. The suites run BEFORE the commit because `provision/scripts/build.mjs` syncs
    `provision/releases/index.json` from the guard's — provision bundles the index rather than reading it from KV — so a
    commit taken after the manifest alone leaves a tracked fourth file behind; and the commit goes in front of the build
    rather than into `.env`, because **compose does not run a shell over `.env`**: the `$(git rev-parse HEAD)` of (c)
    is stored there literally, reaches `-X main.commit` as those twenty-one characters, and (c)'s validation then
    publishes `build: null` for the published artefact for ever — the exact failure §36.3 warns about, reached by
    following the runbook. `e2e.sh` re-exports the commit for the stack IT builds, so the gate passes over the mistake
    and only the artefact carries it. §16 gains the second variable beside `CLIPPET_VERSION`, in front of its build for
    the same reason, and keeps its `/healthz` confirmation step exactly as it was.

    **(f) `compose.pass.yaml`**, per `clippet-pass/edge/README.md`'s runbook snippet: the one `edge` service, the pinned
    `:1` tag (`scripts/check.sh` refuses a moving `latest` in any compose file — erratum 292 — and the sidecar's own
    release rule is what moves this one), `CLIPPET_PASS_TOKEN` as a `:?` required variable so selecting the file without
    a token is a loud compose error rather than a sidecar that quietly never attaches, a **named** volume at `/state`
    (the image owns that directory at the uid it runs as; a root-owned bind mount does not, and the box then comes back
    dark from a restart), and `depends_on: app: service_healthy`. Its header is modelled on `compose.tunnel.yaml`'s and
    names the four `.env` lines and the bucket rule. `CLIPPET_PASS_TOKEN` is **not** an app variable and reaches no
    `internal/config` reader, which is exactly how `CLOUDFLARE_TUNNEL_TOKEN` satisfies check.sh's config-name ↔ compose
    parity stage: that stage reads `internal/config`'s own calls, so a variable the app does not read has nothing to
    reconcile.

    **(g) The wizard's third exposure.** `internal/web/setup.go` grows `exposurePass` — *through a Clippet Pass name
    (name.clippet.gg)* — beside the two of erratum 299. Its block is DERIVED, not written: `passBlockFor` takes the
    target's **Cloudflare** block, EXTENDS its `COMPOSE_FILE` line with `:compose.pass.yaml` rather than adding a second
    one (law 2's total-block rule, and its test counts the assignments), rewrites the head line's *on a Cloudflare
    tunnel* to *on a Clippet Pass name*, and appends `PUBLIC_BASE_URL`, `SESSION_COOKIE_NAME=__Host-clippet_session` and
    `CLIPPET_PASS_TOKEN=<paste the token from your Clippet portal>` — a printed LINE, never a field. Deriving it means a
    store option added later is on a Pass name the day it is added. `cloudflareRefusesLocal` is widened rather than
    duplicated, because a Pass name IS a Cloudflare tunnel and erratum 299's terms reason applies word for word; the
    sentence is unchanged. The exposure is **never detected**, only chosen: a Pass name carries `CF-Ray` like any other
    tunnel, and a page that guessed it would print a paid product's instructions at everybody behind a tunnel of their
    own. Nothing about run-time behaviour differs — it is a template of prose and a block.

    **(h) Law 1's one exception, and how the source stays clean.** The Pass block prints `PUBLIC_BASE_URL` as a whole
    secure base on the Pass zone, which is the first absolute URL beyond its own origin this page has ever carried. The
    exception is narrow and argued in the file: the scheme is not the operator's to choose there (a name is served over
    TLS by one edge and nothing else), so a `<scheme>://` placeholder would be a question with one answer and a paste
    that forgot to answer it would not boot. It is not an endpoint the app opens, not a link the page renders and not a
    third party's host — it is the value of THIS instance's own base URL, one line, inside a block. The §15 tripwire
    (`scripts/check.sh` greps `https?://` over every .go and .html under `internal/`, `cmd/` and `web/`, comments
    included) stays satisfied the way that stage's own message says to: the scheme is a constant spelled apart from its
    separator (`passScheme`), and `setup_test.go`'s golden — which the grep exempts, being a test — pins the rendered
    line as bytes. Step 94 re-checks the rendered page for any OTHER absolute URL.

    **(i) The path is spelled, not named.** `router.go` registers the literal `"/api/instance"` although
    `instance.go` holds the same string as `instancePath`, and the reason is the plane: `guard/test/routes.test.ts`
    diffs the product's registrations against the guard's allowlist and resolves a path CONSTANT only for the three
    Discord files it lists by name, so a named route would be invisible to that diff and the diff would pass vacuously
    on the one route it exists to read. A pin asserts the mux recorded exactly `instancePath`, and exactly once. The
    same reader balances parentheses from the registration helper's own name, so that name is not written in a comment
    in that file either — spelled there it reads as a call and swallows the rest of the file, which is how this clause
    came to be written: the diff went from 45 routes to none and said so.

    **(j) The sibling change, in one commit with this one.** `clippet-pass` `guard/src/routes.ts` gains
    `{ m: "GET", p: "/api/instance", c: "json" }` under the health block — without it the guard would answer its own 404
    for the one route the verifier reads. `guard/README.md`'s "does not exist yet" bullet and `provision/src/verify.ts`'s
    "does not exist tonight" comment are corrected; leg B keeps **tolerating a 404**, because a customer on a release
    older than this erratum has no such route and "answered nothing" is not a wrong answer.

    **(k) DEPLOY §36**, the operator's page: what a Pass is (optional, paid, the owner's — first sentence), that the product
    does nothing for it, how to run one, what the plane reads from this instance and what it does with the answers (an
    unmodified release or nothing; a wrong answer disables on the first occurrence; **no** answer only ever flags;
    `MEDIA_DELIVERY=proxy` gets 24 hours then a disable (amended 2026-10-14, verification-plane amendment 17: no clock,
    no disable); an old release gets a banner and is never disabled), the
    cross-reference to §17.4, and the two legal sentences — the Pass's Terms and Privacy are served by the official
    bot's claim page at `bot.clippet.gg/claim/terms` and `/claim/privacy` (drafts, not yet in force until the owner says
    otherwise) with abuse reports to `abuse@clippet.gg`, and a self-hosted operator stays responsible for their own
    content because the Pass is a conduit. README carries one line of the same.

    **(l) What is pinned.** Go, `internal/httpapi/instance_test.go`: the key set IN ORDER read out of the raw bytes
    (a decoded map has no order, and the order is the contract), four keys and no fifth, `no-store`, anonymous with no
    cookie set and no `Vary: Cookie`, 405 + `Allow` on every other method with HEAD answering 200, the route present
    with the bot OFF while `/api/bot/claim` is still a 404 in that state, both delivery shapes with `media_origin` null
    in proxy mode even when an origin is resolved, `build` null across ten wrong shapes and the 40-hex value published
    byte for byte, `version` never empty, the `claim` bucket shared both ways (draining the new route refuses the claim
    route, and a signed interaction still passes), the pattern the mux recorded, and `/healthz` unchanged. Web: the
    Pass block in `setupBlockGolden` as BYTES for all four bucket targets, `config.Load` accepting each one with the
    pass-token line dropped (which is itself the assertion that the app does not read it) and its `__Host-` cookie only
    because the base is https, the rendered walk's one-of-each assignment count, the refusal on both local targets
    under `via=pass`, `via=pass` beating a `CF-Ray` and a bare `CF-Ray` NOT being read as a Pass. E2E step 94
    (`scripts/e2e.d/94-instance.sh`, bundle 25, parallel lane 4): the four keys in order off the wire, `media_delivery`
    against the mode the harness DETECTED from a real media response and `media_origin` against the origin it measured
    from a real 302, `build` against `git rev-parse HEAD` of the checkout step 1 built from — the one assertion that
    proves the whole chain from the shell to the linker — 405 on POST, and the wizard's Pass walk including its
    refusal. Every one of those was proved to fail by reverting the behaviour it names.

    **Amended 2026-10-19 (run 18, lane `passdocs`):** the wizard's Pass block gains a line — every block it prints for
    a tunnel ends with `TRUSTED_PROXIES=172.16.0.0/12` (DEPLOY §4: behind a tunnel every viewer is the tunnel's one
    address), so (g)'s derived Pass block carries it before its three; the golden pins it, steps 92 and 94 count it;
    the closing line points at §16, not §17.4; (f)'s header and §36.2's by-hand lines name `compose.nobucket.yaml`.

304. **`GET /favicon.ico` answers with the companion mark — one ICO, three drawings, a day of cache** (the owner,
    2026-09-17, lane `favicon`; `scripts/lib/mkicons.py`, `web/static/favicon.ico`, `web/static/embed.go`,
    `internal/web/server.go`, `internal/web/static.go`, `internal/ids/reserved.go`, `scripts/e2e.d/70-web.sh`;
    API.md, DEPLOY §28, `docs/brand/README.md`; the sibling change is `clippet-pass` `guard/src/routes.ts` and `guard/scripts/manifest.mjs`).

    **(a) What was missing.** Erratum 301 put the mark in the tab as a `data:` URI on `base.html` and `embed.html`.
    That is the right icon for a browser looking at a PAGE — it is the only one that can carry a
    `prefers-color-scheme` rule, so the mark follows the browser's own light or dark chrome — and a browser that has
    read a page's `<link rel="icon">` never asks for `/favicon.ico` at all. The callers that DO ask are the ones that
    were handed a URL and no page: bookmark managers, several link previewers, Safari's pinned-tab fallback, feed
    readers. Every one of them got the router's HTML 404 where an image was expected. The owner, after the fifteenth
    gate: serve `/favicon.ico` too, since readers expect it.

    **(b) The file, and why PNG-in-ICO.** `scripts/lib/mkicons.py` draws one more asset, `web/static/favicon.ico`:
    an ICO container holding three PNG entries, at 16, 32 and 48 px. PNG inside an ICO is read by every current
    browser and by every Windows since Vista, and it costs this generator nothing — the module already writes PNGs
    with `zlib` and `struct`, while a BMP/DIB entry would be a second encoder, bottom-up, with a 1-bit AND mask
    beside it, for a file three times the size. Shipping an SVG at that path was never on the table: the address
    exists for the client that does not read the page, and such a client expects an ICO.

    **(c) Which drawing at which size** (SUPERSEDED 2026-09-18 — see (i)). 16 and 32 are the PLAIN MITRE, rasterised from the two literal SVG strings
    in the generator — the size rule erratum 301 set (stripes at 64 px and above, the plain cut below) applied to a
    raster for the first time, and the reason the small entries are read out of that markup rather than scaled from
    the unit geometry: a hand-copied polygon list would be a second mitre to keep in step. 48 is the rasteriser's
    own draw of the striped mark, fitted to the same 1/16 inset the two literal cuts have, so the three entries are
    one drawing at three sizes rather than a small mark beside a large one. `flatten` gained an `A` case (circular
    arcs, the SVG endpoint-to-centre conversion) to read the literal lids; nothing else uses it yet.

    **(d) Ink on transparent, no tile.** Every entry is the mark in the LIGHT theme's ink with the green span, on
    nothing. The favicon slot has no tile — the `data:` URI has none either — and a raster that put the manifest
    icons' rounded ink tile behind the same mark would be a second favicon, not this one at another size. The cost
    is the one thing an ICO cannot do: it carries no colour-scheme rule, so on a dark tab strip it is dark ink on
    the chrome. That is accepted rather than worked around, because the client that prefers the `data:` URI is
    exactly the client that has a theme, and the clients this file exists for draw it on a surface of their own.

    **(e) The route, and the cache rule.** `internal/web/server.go`: `mux.Handle("/favicon.ico", page(getOnly(s.favicon)))`,
    beside `/robots.txt` and `/manifest.webmanifest` and for the same reason — one embedded file, identical for every
    caller, no Resolver lookup, no cookie, no `Vary`. The handler reuses the static handler's own table rather than
    embedding a second copy: the ETag is the sha256 the boot walk already took of these bytes (strong, and better
    than the build id — two builds of one icon share it), the media type is a new `.ico` row in `staticTypes`
    (`image/vnd.microsoft.icon` — the IANA registration rather than the older `image/x-icon`; go1.27's own
    `mime.builtinTypesLower` happens to answer that same string, so the row is BELT AND BRACES like `.ttf`'s
    neighbour rather than a fix for an octet-stream, and the first draft of this clause said otherwise and was
    wrong. What it buys: the served type is a property of THIS file rather than of the toolchain's table or of
    whatever `/etc/mime.types` an image ships — Go loads the system database over its builtins at init — and it is
    the string the guard's manifest mirrors for a Pass name. `favicon_test.go` asserts the ROW as well as the
    header, because the header alone still passes with the row deleted), and `http.ServeFileFS` answers HEAD, Range and the 304 on
    `If-None-Match`. `Cache-Control` is **`public, max-age=86400`** where every other static asset gets an hour: an
    hour is right for `/static/` because a template renders `?v=<build id>` onto those URLs, so a replaced file is a
    new URL; `/favicon.ico` is a fixed path nothing writes into a page, a query would bust nothing, and the file
    changes only with a release. A day of staleness buys every browser-shaped client one request instead of one a
    visit. The file is reachable at `/static/favicon.ico` too, with the same ETag and the ordinary hour, because it
    is a file of `web/static` like any other (`embed.go`'s pattern list gains `*.ico`).

    **(f) `reserved.go`'s sentence changes, its list does not.** `favicon.ico` has been in `ids.Reserved` since
    erratum 248, with a comment saying it is NOT a route — it was there because it is what a client asks for
    unprompted. It is a route now; the word stays exactly where it was and the comment says so. The router test that
    walks the mux's own patterns and demands a row per literal is what made this a two-line change rather than a
    silent one.

    **(g) The plane.** `clippet-pass` `guard/src/routes.ts` gains `{ m: "GET", p: "/favicon.ico", c: "static" }`, or
    the guard answers its own 404 for it under every Pass name. The `static` class resolves a manifest file name,
    which only `{file...}` had ever produced, so `matchPath` gained the smallest rule that gives a LITERAL static
    path its own name — its last segment — and `favicon.ico` is in the release's `static` map already, because the
    manifest tool hashes every file under `web/static/`. That tool's `.ico` media type is corrected from
    `image/x-icon` to the registration the product serves, so the guard hands a viewer the type the origin meant.

    **The day in (e) is the ORIGIN's rule, and a Pass name does not carry it.** `guard/src/guard.ts`'s
    `staticHeaders` writes the guard's own policy over every `static`-class response and drops the box's headers,
    so a viewer reaching this file through a Pass name gets `public, max-age=3600` — an hour, the same as every
    other `/static/` byte. That is the plane's choice and not a bug here: the guard caches per name at its own edge
    and will not let a box dictate how long its colos hold something. Nothing about the drawing or the type changes,
    and the ETag survives intact — the guard's is the manifest's sha256 truncated to 32 hex, which is byte for byte
    what `newStaticHandler` computes for the same file — so a conditional request is still one round trip. What a
    self-hosted operator is told in DEPLOY §28 (a day) is what their own origin does; §36's readers get the hour.

    **(h) What is pinned.** Go, `internal/web/favicon_test.go`: 200, the media type, the day of cache, a strong ETag
    equal to `/static/favicon.ico`'s, 304 on `If-None-Match` and 200 on a stale one, HEAD, 405 + `Allow` on POST,
    DELETE and PATCH, the page header set and `nosniff`, the Authenticator never running (a `countingAuth` at zero)
    with no `Set-Cookie` and no `Vary: Cookie`; then the container — the `00 00 01 00` magic, three directory
    entries, their declared sizes, and each payload starting with the PNG signature — and then the drawing, a golden
    over each entry's DECODED pixels (never the compressed bytes, which depend on the interpreter's zlib) with
    probes that say what the golden is of: the stem, the lid, the window between the stems, the green span, the
    transparent corner, and at 48 two of the lid's three cuts. `links_test.go`'s route table gains the row that
    keeps the mux's own pattern list exhaustive, and its "a single segment that is not an id" list swaps
    `/favicon.ico` for `/sitemap.xml`. `scripts/lib/mkicons.py --check` walks the ICO's directory and compares each
    entry's decoded pixels, never the container bytes. E2E step 71 (`scripts/e2e.d/70-web.sh`): 200, the type, and
    the first six bytes read with `od`, anonymously, through the running stack. Every one of those was proved to
    fail by reverting the behaviour it names.

    **(i) All three entries are the striped mark (2026-09-18, erratum 306, lane `stripes`).** Erratum 301's size
    rule, which (c) applied to a raster, is revoked: `draw_favicon` has no size branch left, the 16 and 32 px
    entries are the same `mark_layers(favicon_map(size))` draw the 48 always was, and the two literal mitres they
    were rasterised from are deleted. The container, the route, the day of cache, the ink-on-transparent rule of
    (d) and the three sizes are unchanged; the file grows 1073 → 1258 bytes, the 48 px entry's golden is the same
    string, and (h)'s goldens for 16 and 32 were redrawn. `flatten`'s `A` case, added in (c), has no caller left.

305. **A cleanup that asks the LISTING cannot remove what was written a millisecond ago — the destroyed clip that kept its rendition** (the fifteenth gate,
    2026-09-17, lane `inflight`; `internal/store/store.go`, `internal/store/minio.go`, `internal/store/fs.go`,
    `internal/store/fake.go`, `internal/worker/pipeline.go`, `internal/worker/worker.go`,
    `internal/lifecycle/lifecycle.go`; DEPLOY §10.)

    **(a) What was seen.** E2E step 15 — "expire-while-in-flight: upload F, expire immediately → gone within 150 s
    whatever its state" — failed on clippet.gg on two consecutive runs of a product tree the fourteenth gate had
    passed it on in 11 s. The second of them is the one that names the bug: the row was gone (`api=404`), and ONE
    object stayed under the clip's prefix — `clips/qRh1o9APi3Xv/renditions/main-OoAMnpnh.mp4`, 2,171,720 bytes,
    modified at the instant of the `admin expire`. That is the whole of the uploaded fixture's size (`std-720p30.mp4`
    is 2,171,720 bytes), so it is a COMPLETE remux output, not a truncated one: the object had been written in full.
    `admin orphans --min-age 0` listed the prefix afterwards; `admin jobs --clip` found no job row, because
    `DeleteClipRow` had cascaded it away. Nothing in `internal/worker`, `internal/sweeper`, `internal/lifecycle` or
    `internal/store` had changed between the two gates.

    **(b) The interleaving.** The sweeper tombstoned the clip while its transcode was inside the `store` stage, one
    upload past the rendition. `MarkDeletingIfDue` cancelled the job row, `Worker.Cancel` cancelled the run, the next
    `PutFile` returned the cancelled context, and the run took its lost-attempt ending — which deletes exactly the
    keys this attempt wrote. It deleted them with `DeletePrefix(key)`, on the long-standing argument that a key is its
    own prefix (§20.6). But `DeletePrefix` LISTS first and removes what the listing returned, and a bucket's listing
    is an INDEX rather than the objects: R2's is eventually consistent, so an object whose `PutFile` returned
    milliseconds earlier can be missing from the very next `ListObjects`. The delete therefore removed nothing,
    reported success, and logged `outputs discarded`. `lifecycle.Destroy` then ran its own `DeletePrefix` over the
    clip prefix — the same listing, the same blind spot — counted the original, re-listed, found the prefix "empty",
    and deleted the row. The object became listable seconds later, under a prefix nothing points at any more.
    Two layers of cleanup, both asking the same question, both getting the same stale answer.

    **(c) Why the fourteenth gate passed, and why no E2E run ever caught it.** Nothing about the code decides this;
    the width of the bucket's indexing lag does. The E2E cannot see it at all: it runs against the bundled MinIO,
    whose erasure backend lists from local metadata and is strongly consistent, so on MinIO the cleanup always
    removes what it just wrote. The same MinIO-vs-R2 split is already recorded in the harness — step 83's
    `expect_deleted` note says "on the bundled MinIO the job always wins the race, on R2 it did not" — and this is
    the same difference, one layer down. The lane replayed the destroy 22 times on its own MinIO stack — twelve at
    step 15's own shape (expire the instant the upload returns, the moment varied over a second) and ten with the
    destroy fired at a live run's `encode` stage, all ten of which reached the very ending the leak came through
    (`job row is no longer this attempt's; outputs discarded`) — and leaked nothing, before the fix or after it.
    That is the expected answer on MinIO and not a reassuring one; the pin in (h) is what proves the interleaving.

    **(d) The fix: cleanup is addressed by KEY.** `store.Store` gains `DeleteKey(ctx, key) error` — remove exactly
    this object, and any incomplete multipart upload of it, without consulting a listing; a key that is not there is
    not an error, which is what S3 and R2 both answer anyway. The minio store implements it as `RemoveObject` plus
    `abortIncomplete` on the EXACT key (the one form MinIO also implements, per that function's provider note); the
    fs store unlinks the file and prunes the directories it empties; the Fake removes the entry. The worker's
    `deleteKeys` and `deleteReplacedKeys` — the cleanup every run kind uses for its own uploads — call it. A
    key-addressed delete asks the object instead of the index, so what the run logs is what happened.
    `lifecycle.Destroy`'s prefix sweep is unchanged and still list-driven, because finding everything is exactly what
    a listing is for; it is no longer asked to see a write of a millisecond ago.

    **(e) And the run cleans up whatever ended it.** `jobRun.release()` deleted this attempt's uploads only when the
    reason was `shutdown`, on the argument that a CANCELLED clip's prefix is deleted by `lifecycle.Destroy` a moment
    later anyway. That is the same misplaced trust in (b), in the ordering rather than in the listing, and it made
    one kind of run the odd one out: `trim`, `gif`, `social`, `poster`, `full` and `filmstrip` have always deleted on
    release whatever the reason. It is now `if !j.checkpointed` alone, as everywhere else. In production the
    tombstone always precedes the cancel, so this path was reached through `lostAttempt` and the objects did go; the
    arm was a hole waiting for the first caller that cancels a run without tombstoning the clip.

    **(f) What `Worker.Cancel` now promises.** §10.1 said "no PutFile in flight", meaning no goroutine of this
    process is inside one. That is a statement about this process, and the leak lived in the gap between it and the
    bucket: cancelling a transfer does not un-write it — the client stops waiting while the bucket may already have
    taken the last byte. So the promise is now about the bucket: a `true` return means the run's exit path has
    removed, by key, every object that attempt wrote, including one whose `PutFile` the cancellation cut off. The
    comment trail says so at all three sites — `worker.go`'s package doc and `Cancel`, and `lifecycle.go`'s step
    list, which now also says what step 3 is and is not for.

    **(g) What is NOT closed.** A `PutFile` the bucket commits AFTER the run's key-addressed delete has gone out is
    still an orphan; nothing on this side of the wire can order a delete against a write that is landing. The window
    is one round trip wide instead of one listing-lag wide, and `admin orphans` remains the backstop for it —
    unchanged, and now the only thing that needs to be. Step 15's 150 s budget is NOT the problem and was not
    touched: it is ten sweep ticks at the 15 s interval a gate runs with and two at the shipped 60 s, and in the
    failing runs the row was already gone — the object simply never was. `httpapi.abortUpload` still clears a failed
    ingest's prefix by listing, which has the same shape with a much wider window (a request that has just died, not
    a run mid-flight); it is recorded as a cleanup row rather than changed here.

    **(h) What is pinned.** Go, `internal/worker/inflight_test.go`
    (`TestCancelledRunRemovesItsUploadWhateverTheListingSays`): the `Fake` gains `Unlisted`/`Listed`, which hold a
    key back from `List` and `DeletePrefix` while every key-addressed operation still finds it — the one guarantee a
    bucket does not give and the Fake used to give for free. The test uploads the rendition, hides it from the
    listing, holds the next upload until `MarkDeleting` + `Cancel` cut it, and asserts that when `Cancel` returns the
    object is gone from the bucket and the clip's prefix survives the destroy's own `DeletePrefix` empty. It fails on
    the old code with "Cancel returned with clips/…/renditions/main-….mp4 still in the bucket" beside the log line
    claiming the outputs were discarded — proved by reverting both halves of (d) and (e) and re-running.
    `internal/store/fake_test.go`'s `TestDeleteKeyIgnoresTheListing` pins the store contract: a list-driven delete
    leaves the unlisted object, `DeleteKey` removes it, and a second `DeleteKey` is not an error.

306. **The striped clapper is the only mark, at every size — the size rule revoked, the plain mitre deleted**
    (the owner's call of 2026-09-18: the plain clapper is wanted nowhere in the repository, the striped one
    reads fine small, and no further drawings were wanted — the icon was already chosen; lane `stripes`; `scripts/lib/mkicons.py`, `web/static/favicon.ico`,
    `web/templates/base.html`, `embed.html`, `docs/brand/mark-16.svg` and `mark-32.svg` — DELETED —
    `docs/brand/README.md`, `internal/web/mark_test.go`, `internal/web/favicon_test.go`,
    `scripts/e2e.d/77-design.sh`, `scripts/check.sh`; `web/STYLE.md`, DEPLOY §17.2 and §28, ROADMAP #43.)

    **(a) What is revoked, and what is NOT redrawn.** Erratum 301 (a)'s size rule — stripes at 64 px and above, a
    plain mitre cut on whole pixels at 32 and 16 — is withdrawn on the owner's word, and 304 (c)'s reading of it with
    it. No geometry was designed, chosen or altered here: the mark is the one eight rounds settled on, the unit
    geometry `mark_shapes()` has drawn since 301, and the whole of this erratum is that it is now the drawing at
    EVERY size — the tab included. What makes it read at 16 is the rasteriser's 4 × 4 supersampling, which is the
    same thing that has always made the 48 read; nothing is hand-placed on a pixel grid any more.

    **(b) What was deleted.** `MITRE_16`, `MITRE_32`, `mitre_shapes()` and its three little parsing regexes from
    `scripts/lib/mkicons.py`; `docs/brand/mark-16.svg` and `docs/brand/mark-32.svg` from the repository.
    `brand_svgs()` writes `mark.svg` alone, so `--check` and the module docstring's file table lost two rows each,
    and `check.sh`'s stage line, DEPLOY §17.2's row and STYLE.md now say one SVG where they said three. The mark's
    elements moved into one `mark_elements(fills)` that the brand file and the favicon both build from — that is
    what makes "the same drawing" a fact about the code rather than a claim — and `docs/brand/mark.svg` comes out
    of it byte-identical to what 301 committed, which is the proof the move changed nothing.

    **(c) The favicon a page declares.** `favicon_svg()` emits the unit geometry: the two stems, the lid as ONE
    `fill-rule="evenodd"` path with its three cuts as subpaths, the span capsule — the same four elements and the
    same path data as `docs/brand/mark.svg`, under `FAVICON_STYLE`'s unchanged colour-scheme rule, percent-encoded
    in full into `base.html` and `embed.html` exactly as before (no scheme literal reaches a template). The stems
    stay their own elements and are NOT folded into the even-odd path: the right stem runs a few units up into the
    lid on purpose (301 (c)), and one even-odd fill over both would cancel that overlap and open the joint. The
    viewBox is `-104 -306 1624 1624` — `mark_box()` centred in a square with the same 1/16 inset `favicon_map`
    gives the ICO's entries, derived by `favicon_box()` rather than typed, so the tab and the file are one framing.
    The cost: the `data:` URI grows from 727 to 970 bytes on every page and embed (the lid's path data is most of
    it), paid in the head of every response.

    **(d) The ICO's 16 and 32.** `draw_favicon()` has no size branch left — every entry is `mark_layers(favicon_map
    (size))`, ink on transparent with the green span and no tile, as 304 (d) fixed. The file grows 1073 → 1258
    bytes. The 48 px entry is untouched, byte for byte: its golden hash is the same string it was, which is the
    check that the rasteriser itself did not move. `flatten()`'s `A` case, which 304 (c) added to read the literal
    mitres, now has no caller in either generator; it is kept (it is the reader `mkcard.py` shares) and recorded in
    a cleanup row rather than pulled out.

    **(e) What is pinned.** `internal/web/mark_test.go`: `TestFaviconIsThePlainMitre` becomes
    **`TestFaviconIsTheStripedMark`** and asserts the new URI as XML — the viewBox above, the unchanged colour rule,
    four pieces with three `.p` and one `.s`, the lid's `rotate(-9 0 230)` carrying `fill-rule="evenodd"`, FOUR
    subpaths (the outline and three cuts) and the two `A230 230` corner arcs, the stems in font units
    (`0 230 272 570` and `M1146 18L1418 5V800H1146Z`), the span as the wordmark's `1418 × 200` capsule at
    `y = 1000`, no glyph curve anywhere, and both pages carrying one URI. On the old template it fails at the
    viewBox and at every piece. `internal/web/favicon_test.go`'s `TestFaviconEntriesAreTheMark` carries new goldens
    for the 16 and 32 entries and the same one for the 48; the 32's probes gain two of the lid's CUTS as whole
    transparent pixels — the thing that tells the mark from the mitre — and the 16's do not, because at 16 a cut is
    a third of a pixel wide and the stripes are an antialiased lightening of the lid, which the golden pins and a
    probe cannot. **The goldens were regenerated by drawing them**, not by copying a failure: `python -c` over the
    module's own `draw_favicon(size)`, `sha256` of the concatenated rows — the same bytes `pixels()` hashes in Go —
    and every probe point was read out of the same draw before it was written into the table. E2E step 77 asserts
    the new lid transform on the share page and the embed, and now also `lacks_file` the old `rotate(-9 1 4)`, so
    the deletion is asserted and not merely un-asserted. `mkicons.py --check` and `mkcard.py --check` (§16.1
    stages) cover the eight files the generator writes and the card.

    **(f) What this lane did NOT prove.** No visual pass and no full E2E ran (the brief's rule; no shot photographs
    a tab — `grep favicon scripts/lib/visual.js` is empty), so step 77's two edited lines are proved only by the
    template carrying the exact string they grep for, not by a run; the lane ran `E2E_ONLY=70-web`, whose step 71
    asserts the ICO's route, type and container. Whether the stripes at 16 px please the owner is a question for the

307. **`clippet admin import <dir>`: a folder of old clips walks through the upload path, once**
    (ROADMAP #51, the owner's pick of 2026-09-18: a one-time `clippet admin import <dir>` that walks an
    existing folder of old clips through the same `ingestCore`, idempotent by content hash, as the way
    a person moves off Streamable; run 2, lane `import`. New: `cmd/clippet/admin_import.go` +
    `admin_import_test.go`, `internal/httpapi/importer.go`, `internal/db/imports.go` + migration
    `0020_clips_owner_source_size.sql`, `scripts/e2e.d/95-import.sh` (step 95), DEPLOY §34.4. Changed:
    `cmd/clippet/admin.go` (the dispatch, `adminUsage`, the injectable probe), `internal/drop/drop.go`
    (three helpers exported, no behaviour change), `scripts/e2e.d/README.md`. No HTTP route, so **no
    API.md change and no guard allowlist line**; no new dependency, no new egress, no new `.env`
    variable and no compose row.)

    **(a) The drop folder's sibling, and the line between them.** §34 watches for what arrives NEXT;
    this reads what is there ALREADY. The difference that matters is who owns the folder: the drop
    folder is OURS and may be written in (it moves what it takes into `.clippet-drop/`), and an import
    folder is the PERSON's — so **nothing in it is ever moved, renamed or deleted**, on success, on a
    refusal or on a re-run, and nothing of ours is written into it either: no `.failed.txt`, no staging
    directory. The rule that a destructive action needs an explicit yes is satisfied the
    way `storage migrate` satisfies it, by there being no destructive action at all. That is also the
    boundary 296 (i) drew for ROADMAP #42 (c) — a WATCHED folder is read and never written — reached
    from the other side, and this verb is the one-shot half of it.

    **(b) It is the upload path, for the fourth time.** `internal/httpapi`'s `Importer` is
    `dropIngest`'s sibling and the fourth caller of erratum 253's ingest core: the scratch precheck
    with the size the filesystem already reported, `MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES` through the same capped reader,
    the storage quota, the ffprobe gate, `applyDefaultsCtx` — so an imported clip gets the account's
    own lifetime, link grammar and unlisted-or-not, and its title is the file name without its
    extension (erratum 60). The candidate predicate and the probe gate are the DROP FOLDER's own,
    exported for this (`drop.Eligible`, `drop.ProbeVideo`, `drop.Cause`) rather than written again: two
    ideas of "what is a file we take" would disagree eventually and nothing would notice.

    **What it deliberately does NOT spend: `RATE_UPLOAD_PER_HOUR`.** That bucket bounds what an ACCOUNT
    can push over the network in an hour. This is an operator at the box's own command line moving a
    folder they already own onto their own instance, once — and the limiter would be theatre besides:
    the verb runs in its own process, so its bucket is minted full on every run, which is erratum 292's
    "a knob nobody can act on". Stopping an import of five hundred clips at sixty would leave the
    operator running it nine more times. Every gate that is about the INSTANCE's health is kept.

    **(c) Idempotent by content, with no second memory.** `clips.source_etag` is already the hex sha256
    of the original, computed by the store while writing it at ingest (0001's own column comment), so
    the brief's `import_seen` table was not built: one fact in one place, and deleting a clip really
    does mean that content is no longer here, so re-importing the file is the right answer rather than
    a `seen <id>` pointing at nothing. The question is asked **by size first** — migration 0020 indexes
    `clips(owner_id, source_size)` — and the file is hashed only when this account already owns a clip
    of exactly its size. That is what keeps the FIRST run to one read per file (the hash falls out of
    `PutFile` for free) and the SECOND run to one read and no writes. **The brief's "one read, never a
    second pass" was met this way rather than by hashing through the ingest itself**, which would have
    been one read on a first run and a full spool through `SCRATCH_DIR` of every already-imported byte
    on the second — slower, and on a folder larger than the working disk a re-run would have been
    REFUSED for want of scratch, which is the exact opposite of what idempotence is for.

    **(d) What it prints, and what it exits.** One line per file — `imported <id> <name>`,
    `seen <id> <name>`, `refused <tag> <name>: <sentence>` — then
    `import: N imported, N seen, N refused, N bytes`. Dotfiles and directories are skipped in silence,
    as the drop folder skips them; `--recursive` walks sub-directories (never a dotted one) and
    `--dry-run` prints the verdict it would reach for every file, `seen` included, and creates nothing.
    The exit code is the drop folder's own rule (296 (l)) pointed at a shell instead of at a text file:
    **if fixing something here and running the verb again could change the answer it is THIS
    INSTANCE's refusal and the command exits 1** (`quota`, `scratch`, `storage`, `database`), and if
    the answer would be the same tomorrow it is the file's, it is one line, and the run is a success
    (`not-a-video`, `too-large`, `empty`, `unreadable`). The brief's "exit 0 unless a file errored" is
    that rule made decidable — a folder with holiday photos in it is not an error.

    **(e) Three refusals before it reads anything.** The owner must exist (there is no default account
    and a typo must not become somebody else's library); a file larger than `MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES` is
    refused on the size the filesystem reported, which is the declared-length gate every upload route
    already applies to `Content-Length`; and **this instance's own directories are not a folder of old
    clips** — `STORAGE_DIR`, `DATA_DIR` and `SCRATCH_DIR`, or anything inside or around one, is exit 2
    with a sentence. Without that last guard, `admin import /media --recursive` on `fs` would walk the
    store and re-import every rendition of every clip as a new clip. It is the overlap rule
    `config.storageDir` already applies to the same three directories, which is a refusal an operator
    has met before.

    **(f) Where it runs.** A one-off container beside the live instance — `docker compose run --rm -v
    /path/to/old/clips:/import app clippet admin import /import --owner alice` — which is the shape
    DEPLOY §32 already documents for `storage migrate`. It needs no listener: the clip is created
    `queued` exactly as an upload is and the SERVING instance's worker claims it on its next poll, so
    `Deps.Worker` is the no-op and there is nothing to wake. Pinned by fourteen Go tests and
    `scripts/e2e.d/95-import.sh` (step 95, `parallel lane=4` beside 91-drop, publishing no port at
    all), which runs the verb three times over one folder — dry, real, and again with one file RENAMED
    — and asserts that the second run imports zero and that the folder still holds exactly the three
    files that went into it, byte for byte.

308. **What the product exposes for a Windows operator** (`cmd/clippet/freebytes_windows.go`,
    `cmd/clippet/volumepath.go`, `internal/worker/freebytes_windows.go`, the two `freebytes_other.go`
    stubs, `internal/transcode/{lighttag,posterlabel}.go`, `Dockerfile` `crosswindows`,
    `scripts/check.sh`, `cmd/clippet/admin.go`, `internal/httpapi/{sxcu,token_handlers,dto}.go`,
    `scripts/e2e.d/96-mint.sh`; DEPLOY §9, §16, §19.4, §27; API.md; ROADMAP #48).

    The product ships as a Linux container and that does not change. But the BINARY is also something a
    person runs on Windows — `clippet.exe admin doctor` against a box's own data directory, and, since
    `clippet-pass/docs/desktop-app.md` §9, a desktop shell that drives the same program — and four things
    it needs were missing or unreachable from a shell. Nothing here names a shell, a mode or a Pass:
    every item is equally useful to an operator with a terminal and no browser.

    **(a) Disk statistics on Windows.** `freebytes_other.go` in both `cmd/clippet` and `internal/worker`
    was `//go:build !unix`, so `freeBytes`, `diskUsage` and `sameDevice` had no implementation on
    Windows at all. Two consequences, both silent: `admin doctor`'s and `admin stats`' disk rows printed
    *free space unavailable* on every line, and `httpapi.scratchHasRoom` — which treats a statfs failure
    as "cannot tell, let it through" — skipped the §8.3 precheck outright, so the documented
    `507 insufficient_scratch` could not be produced before the spool ran the disk out. The worker's own
    §10.2 check was skipped the same way, its `-1` meaning "unknown".

    Both stubs are now `!unix && !windows` and each package has a `freebytes_windows.go` of its own,
    over `golang.org/x/sys/windows` (`GetDiskFreeSpaceEx`), which becomes a DIRECT requirement of
    `go.mod`. **Each package keeps its own contract exactly**, because they are not the same contract:
    `cmd/clippet` returns values AND an error and every caller degrades to "unavailable", while
    `internal/worker` returns a NEGATIVE value to mean "cannot tell, skip the check" and an error to
    fail the stage — the Windows files answer as the unix ones do in each, and the uint64 the API
    returns is SATURATED rather than converted, because a wrapped count would be negative and negative
    is the worker's "skip".

    `GetDiskFreeSpaceEx`'s first out-parameter is the reading, not the third: it is the space available
    TO THE CALLER, which is what a per-user quota makes different from the volume's own free space — the
    same distinction `statfs` draws between `Bavail` and `Bfree`, and a precheck must not promise room a
    quota will not give.

    `sameDevice` compares the two paths' **mount points**, via `GetVolumePathName`, and not the volume
    serial from `GetVolumeInformation`. Three reasons, and the first is the one that decides it: only
    the mount point distinguishes a volume MOUNTED INTO A FOLDER from the drive it is mounted on, so a
    data disk at `C:\clippet\data` beside a scratch directory on `C:\` reads as two devices rather than
    one — which is the exact deployment the `same_device` row exists to describe, and the one a
    drive-letter comparison would get wrong. Second, it takes a path and opens nothing, while the serial
    wants a volume ROOT and therefore needs this call first anyway. Third, it answers for a directory
    this process may not be able to open, which is the state `admin doctor` is most often run to
    diagnose.

    **What can be PROVEN here, and what cannot.** A Linux container cannot run a Windows binary, so the
    decision those two calls feed — whether two answers name one volume — is kept in a function with no
    build constraint (`sameVolumePath`, `cmd/clippet/volumepath.go`) and table-tested everywhere: the
    trailing separator and case are normalized away, a prefix is not a match (`C:\data` vs
    `C:\database`), a mounted folder is not its host drive, a UNC share is a volume, and an empty answer
    is never the same volume as anything, itself included. The rest is proven by the compiler — see (c).

    **(b) Fonts beside the binary.** `tagFontCandidates` and `posterFontCandidates` were POSIX-absolute
    lists (`/usr/share/fonts/…`, `/usr/local/share/clippet/fonts/…`), which name nothing on a Windows
    box, so a hand-run binary drew no Light tag and no poster label and said nothing about why. Each list
    now ends with a `fonts` directory BESIDE the executable: `<exe dir>/fonts/DejaVuSans.ttf` for the tag,
    and `<exe dir>/fonts/spline-sans-mono.ttf` then `DejaVuSans.ttf` for the poster label — the project's
    own mono face leading its own half, as the installed list already has it lead. It is a SEARCHED path
    and not a variable, in the spirit of the comment that has always been there: a `LIGHT_TAG_FONT` would
    be one more thing to get wrong for a cosmetic line. It is LAST, so an image that installed a font is
    never overruled by a file dropped next to the binary; `os.Executable` is read ONCE at package
    start-up (`exeFontsDir`) rather than per encode, and a failure simply omits the entries — no
    candidate, no tag, never an error, which is the degradation an image with no font already had.
    Pinned by building both lists with a fake executable directory and finding a font planted there when
    every installed path is absent (the installed paths are re-rooted under an empty directory, so the
    answer is a fact of the test rather than of the host), and by the same probe with one installed font
    present, which must still win.

    **(c) A cross-compile stage.** `go vet` and `go test` only ever see the host's `GOOS`, so the three
    files above are compiled by NOTHING in the gate: a dependency that pulls in cgo, a syscall that is
    not on that platform, or a build tag that stopped covering it would each pass every stage and be
    discovered by whoever next tried to make a Windows build. `scripts/check.sh` gains
    `[check] cross-compile: windows/amd64`, a `Dockerfile` stage `crosswindows` that is a SIBLING of
    `test` and `racetest` off the same `testsrc` parent (erratum 283's shape): it shares their source
    copy, their `gofmt` and their `go mod verify` and costs one link step — **10 s** measured on a warm
    parent. `-o /dev/null`, because what is wanted is the compiler's verdict and never a binary; a real
    Windows build is made on a Windows host. It was proved by putting the old `!unix` constraint back on
    one stub: the stage fails with three `redeclared in this block` errors while every other stage stays
    green.

    **(d) `clippet admin tokens mint`.** A capture token could only be minted by `POST /api/auth/tokens`,
    which needs a browser SESSION — and the two situations a capture token is most wanted in have none:
    a machine being set up by somebody who is not the account's owner, and a box whose browser cannot
    reach the instance. `tokens mint <username> [--name n] [--scopes upload[,read]] [--sxcu]` is the
    second door.

    **STDOUT is the artefact and stderr is for people.** That is the whole shape of the verb:
    `… tokens mint alice > token.txt` writes a token and `… tokens mint alice --sxcu > clippet.sxcu`
    writes an importable ShareX uploader, and neither file may contain a sentence. So the confirmation,
    the usage text and every refusal go to stderr, and the confirmation carries the `ck_<prefix>…`
    display half that `tokens list` prints and never the raw value (erratum 109, amended). `resolveUser`
    grew a writer argument for the same reason — "no such user" is stdout for every other verb here and
    stderr for this one, so a typo cannot end up inside the uploader file.

    **One set of rules, two doors.** `internal/httpapi` exports `CleanTokenName`, `CleanScopes` and
    `NewSXCU`, and the CLI calls all three rather than carrying its own copy of any: the default scope
    set is the route's absent-array default (`["upload"]`, erratum 111), an explicitly empty `--scopes`
    is the route's `[]` and therefore an error rather than "no permissions", the name rule is
    `cleanText`'s 1–64 runes with the route's own control-character rule, and the file is erratum 59's.
    That package stays their home because it owns both contracts and `cmd/clippet` already imports it
    (`doctor.go`, `serve.go`); moving either rule out would split one contract across two packages to
    save an import that is already there. `--sxcu` for a token without the `upload` scope is refused
    BEFORE anything is minted — the route answers `sxcu: null` there, and a file cannot be null on
    stdout, while a destination that cannot upload imports cleanly and answers 403 on the first capture.

    Pinned in `cmd/clippet/admin_tokens_mint_test.go` by driving the route's OWN middleware chain
    (`Resolver.Middleware` → `RequireUser` → `RequireScope(upload)`) over the row the CLI wrote: 204 for
    the minted token, 403 for a `--scopes read` one, 401 after `tokens revoke`. The `--sxcu` document is
    compared field for field against `NewSXCU(urls.New(cfg.PublicBaseURL, …), <its own token>)` — with a
    DIFFERENT build id, so the static `?v=` cache-buster cannot reach the file — and
    `internal/httpapi/token_handlers_test.go` asserts the ROUTE's `sxcu` field is that same call's
    output, which is what makes "one generator" a pin on both sides rather than a claim. E2E step **96**
    (`96-mint.sh`, parallel lane 1) mints on the live stack for an account of its own, uploads with the
    token, drives `POST /api/upload` using only the fields of the `.sxcu` the shell wrote (a deliberate
    `400 missing_video` — the one answer only a request that passed auth, the scope and the CSRF rule can
    get, and it encodes nothing), revokes both, and removes its clip and its account.

309. **`/setup` reshaped: labels are nouns, a verdict is a state word, a rule is said once when it bites, a
    panel is headed by what it is** (2026-09-21, lane `setup2`; the owner's walk of `/setup` — the page read as
