312. **The Light tag's paths escaped for BOTH levels of the filtergraph parser, so a Windows path parses**
    (2026-10-04, lane `wintag`; `internal/transcode/lighttag.go` `escapeFilterValue`, used by the Light tag and
    the poster label alike; amends erratum 214 (b)). Seen on the first real desktop install (Windows, the
    bundled ffmpeg 7.1.5): the first clip that needed a Light copy failed `light: ffmpeg exited 4294967274`,
    `Error parsing filterchain '…drawtext=fontfile='C:\\<home>\\AppData\\Local\\Clippet\\fonts\\DejaVuSans.ttf':textfile='C:\\…\\tag-….txt':…'`.
    Every clip that gets a Light copy failed on Windows; Linux was unaffected.

    **(a) What was wrong.** The value was single-quoted with `\` and `'` backslash-escaped, on erratum 214 (b)'s
    claim that a colon is safe inside quotes — measured on a Linux path, which has no colon. ffmpeg parses a
    graph in TWO levels (ffmpeg-filters "Notes on filtergraph escaping"): the GRAPH level reads the filter's
    argument string and strips one layer of quoting and escaping, then the OPTION level splits what is left on
    `:` and strips a second. The quotes are gone before the split, so `'C:\\<home>\\…'` reached the option
    level as `fontfile=C` followed by `\\<home>\\…` ("No option name near '\\<home>\\…'", exit −22). The same
    rendering also broke on a `'` in a path, on Linux too: `\'` inside quotes is not an escape, so the quote
    closed the string.

    **(b) Measured, not reasoned** (lane scratch `first-name/wintag/measure-windows.md`, every command and exit
    code). One `[0:0]drawtext=fontfile=…:textfile=…:expansion=none:fontsize=16[v]` over a 64×64 lavfi source,
    both paths rendered with each spelling; exit 0 means the graph parsed AND drawtext opened both files.
    Windows argv through PowerShell 7.6, the font the desktop app ships (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\Clippet\fonts\DejaVuSans.ttf`);
    Linux argv through Go's `os/exec` in `clippet-gotest:ffmpeg`. A = the old rendering; B = forward slashes,
    `\:` inside single quotes; **C = the option-level escape (`\`, `'`, `:` each get a backslash) and then
    single quotes, a `'` written close–escaped quote–reopen** — for a quote-free Windows path,
    `'C\:\\Users\\…'`; D = unquoted, forward slashes, `\\:`.

    | ffmpeg | text path | A (old) | B | **C** | D |
    |---|---|---|---|---|---|
    | bundled 7.1.5, Windows | `C:\…\tag.txt` | −22 | 0 | **0** | 0 |
    | bundled 7.1.5, Windows | `C:\…\it's a tag.txt` | −22 | 0 | **0** | −2 |
    | host 7.1.1, Windows | `C:\…\tag.txt` | −22 | 0 | **0** | 0 |
    | host 7.1.1, Windows | `C:\…\it's a tag.txt` | −22 | 0 | **0** | −2 |
    | 7.1.1, Linux (container) | `/w/tag.txt` | 0 | 0 | **0** | 0 |
    | 7.1.1, Linux (container) | `/w/it's a tag.txt` | 254 | 0 | **0** | 254 |
    | 7.1.1, Linux (container) | `/tmp/odd/a:b.txt` | 234 | 0 | **0** | 0 |
    | 7.1.1, Linux (container) | `/tmp/odd/a\b.txt` | 0 | 254 | **0** | 254 |

    C is the only spelling that opens every file on all three binaries. B was the brief's preference and the
    commonly quoted Windows spelling; it is not taken because rewriting `\` to `/` is lossy on Linux, where a
    backslash is a legal filename character and the rewrite opens a different file (the last row). Windows
    needs no forward slashes once the backslashes are escaped for the option level.

    **(c) The rendering.** `escapeFilterValue` escapes inside-out: `filterOptionEscaper` (a `strings.Replacer`:
    `\` → `\\`, `'` → `\'`, `:` → `\:`) for the option level, then the result wrapped in single quotes with each
    `'` written as `'\''` for the graph level — inside the quotes `,`, `;`, `[`, `]` and every backslash are
    literal. No OS branch: the one function is right for both path syntaxes. A Linux path with none of the three
    characters renders exactly as before (`'/usr/share/fonts/…'`), so no Linux argv changes. The function's
    comment no longer claims a colon is safe inside quotes; erratum 214 (b) stands amended by this one.

    **(d) Tests** (`internal/transcode/lighttag_test.go`, pure strings, run on Linux): `TestEscapeFilterValue`
    pins the exact rendering of a Windows path (`C:\<home>\fonts\DejaVuSans.ttf` →
    `'C\:\\<home>\\fonts\\DejaVuSans.ttf'`), a forward-slash Windows path (`'C\:/Windows/Fonts/x.ttf'`, which
    the old table pinned as the broken `'C:/Windows/Fonts/x.ttf'`), a Linux path (unchanged), a path with a
    quote and a space (`/tmp/it's a tag.txt` → `'/tmp/it\'\''s a tag.txt'`), a bare colon (`'a\:b'`) and the
    old separator, bracket, backslash and empty rows (unchanged except `a'b`, which the old table pinned as the
    broken `'a\'b'`). `TestDrawtextFilter`'s and `posterlabel_test.go`'s Linux-path pins are unchanged.
    **Not proven here:** a Light copy encoded end to end by the desktop app on Windows — the measurement
    exercises the exact rendering on both Windows binaries, the encode itself waits for the next desktop build.

313. **The upload card after a pick: the name in its own cell, and the ink on the next step**
    (2026-10-04, lane `uploadcard`; `web/static/app.css` `.drop-status`, `web/static/app.js` `setupUpload`,
    `web/templates/index.html` the drop frame, `scripts/lib/visual.js` `pickedCard`; amends erratum 240's
    one-ink-button rule in `web/STYLE.md`). The owner's screenshot (the first name's walk,
    nits 10–11): after an upload of a long-named file the drop frame drew the name, `Pick a file` and
    `Uploaded — encoding on the server` over one another; and once a file is picked, the pick and the upload
    read alike.

    **(a) What was wrong.** `.readout` is a flex row (`justify-content: space-between`) of two items, the
    name and the `.live` stage phrase, both on the default `flex: 0 1 auto`. Under a long name the two shrank
    in proportion to their content widths, so the phrase lost most of its width and broke onto three lines.
    `.drop-status` is positioned from the frame's BOTTOM, so every extra line grew it upward — over the
    `Pick a file` button, which the frame's `padding-bottom` only clears for one line of readout. The name
    already ellipsised; it was never given a cell to ellipsise in.

    **(b) The cell rule.** The name is `flex: 1 1 auto; min-width: 0` — it takes what the phrase leaves and
    ellipsises inside it; the phrase is `flex: none; max-width: 100%` — it keeps its width, and wraps only when
    the phrase ALONE is wider than the row. The whole name rides on the name cell's `title` (`setName`, used by
    `showPicked` and by the per-file label during a batch; an empty cell carries no `title`). The stacked card
    under 860 px is the same row with more room; nothing there changed. Superseded by erratum 314: the cell
    beside the phrase left an OBS name two characters in the 300 px column, so the name now has a line of its own.

    **(c) The loudness swap.** One solid control on the card (`web/STYLE.md`), and it is the next step: with
    nothing picked `Pick a file` (`data-upload-pick`, new) is `primary` and Upload is hairline — the served
    classes, so the no-script form reads the same before a pick — and once a file is picked Upload is `primary`
    and Pick a file is hairline. `loud()` decides from the batch (`picked`, else `input.files`) and runs at
    the end of `showPicked` (the picker's `change`, a drop, a paste), after the reset that ends a landed batch,
    and once at start-up for a browser that restores a chosen file on Back. A cancel or a failure keeps the
    batch, so Upload stays the solid one beside Try again. No word changed.

    **(d) The frame.** `upload-picked`: the library with a file picked through `setInputFiles` and never sent,
    light, 1280 — one frame, so the visual pass is **103** shots on an unbadged stack. Its `before`
    (`pickedCard`) asserts the swap in both directions, the name cell's text and `title` against the picked
    name, the name's box inside its row; then, with `Uploaded — encoding on the server` put in the live cell
    by hand and taken out again, that the phrase is one line, the name ends before it begins and the readout
    stays below `Pick a file` — at 1280 and again at 390.

314. **The upload card's foot on two lines: the name alone above the stage phrase**
    (2026-10-04, lane `upload2`; `web/static/app.css` `.drop-status` and `.drop`, `scripts/lib/visual.js`
    `pickedCard`, `web/STYLE.md`'s ink paragraph; amends erratum 313 (b)). The owner's screenshot, on a 4K desktop
    after uploading an OBS clip through the desktop app: the drop frame's foot read
    `2…   Uploaded — encoding on the server`.

    **(a) What was wrong.** Erratum 313 gave the name its own cell BESIDE the stage phrase and let it
    ellipsise there. But the drop column is a fixed 300 px (`.upload { grid-template-columns: 300px
    minmax(0, 1fr) }`), so the frame's foot is ≈240 px wide (238 px measured) at every screen width above
    860 px, and `Uploaded — encoding on the server` at 12 px, with its lamp and the cells' 12 px gap, takes
    220 of it: the name's cell was 18 px wide, two characters of `2026-10-04 18-52-11.mp4`. Truncation was
    the wrong shape for a cell that small; the owner's suggestion: a second line.

    **(b) The two-line rule.** `.drop-status .readout` is a column (`flex-direction: column; align-items:
    flex-start`, 16 px lines, no gap). Line 1 is the name alone, stretched across the whole foot (`align-self:
    stretch`), mono, `--text`, one line that ellipsises only when the name is wider than the foot — the whole
    name stays on its `title` (`setName`, unchanged). Line 2 is the `.live` group (lamp + phrase), left-aligned,
    `flex: none; max-width: 100%`, so it wraps only when the phrase alone is wider than the row. An empty name
    is `display: none`, so a foot with nothing picked is the one line it always was. The stacked card under
    860 px is the same frame with more width and takes the same two lines; there is no media-query fork of the
    readout.

    **(c) The frame's room.** The rail, its 4 px margin and two lines are 42.2 px of foot (measured, the
    second line being the live row's 18.2 px) where one line was 22.2; standing 10 px off the frame's bottom,
    that needs `padding-bottom: 54px` to keep the foot's top 1.8 px under `Pick a file` — the same clearance the
    one-line foot had at 34. The room is given only while there is a name (`.drop:has(.drop-status
    .name:not(:empty))`): the resting frame keeps its 34 px and is pixel-identical (the 1280 and 390 crops of
    the upload card at rest hash the same before and after this lane), and a picked frame grows by the second
    line, 153.5 → 173.5 px at both widths (its content already outgrew the 16:9 box by 2.75 px at 1280; the
    `aspect-ratio` stays). Nothing else moved: `loud()`, the rail, the batch's per-file label, the no-script
    form and every word are 313's.

    **(d) The pins** (`pickedCard`, the `before` of the `upload-picked` frame; still one frame, **103** shots).
    Before the long name, ONE new assertion: `2026-10-04 18-52-11.mp4` picked, with `Uploaded — encoding on
    the server` in the live cell, shows WHOLE at 1280 (`scrollWidth <= clientWidth`; on 313's CSS it read
    161 > 18). Then, with the long name and the same phrase, at 1280 and at 390: the name's box spans the
    foot's width, the name sits ABOVE the phrase (`name.bottom <= live.top`), the phrase is one line inside the
    row, and the readout stays below `Pick a file`. 313's "the name ends before the phrase begins" is dropped —
    it was the old shape. Each new pin was proven by revert-and-rerun on the lane stack: on 313's CSS the
    whole-name pin fails (`scrollWidth 161 > clientWidth 18`), with it skipped the span pin fails (`the name's
    box (18 px) does not span the foot (row 238 px)`), with that skipped too the above pin fails (`the name
    (bottom 233.5) is not above the stage phrase (top 214)`); on this CSS all pass.

315. **Three commands: `/upload file:`, `/clip link:` and the message command "Enrich" — and ONE enhanced message
    for all three** (the owner, 2026-10-05 ≈03:35Z, decision (c): the upload with a file attachment is `/upload`, and
    `/clip` is the formal viewing of a clip; then ≈03:50Z, decision (b) on the auto-enrich spike's §6(a): the
    right-click "Enrich"; lane `commands`.
    Changed: `internal/config/{discordbot.go,config.go}`, `internal/notify/{bot.go,reply.go}`,
    `internal/httpapi/discord.go`, `internal/urls/urls.go` (ParseShare restored), `cmd/clippet/{admin_bot.go,serve.go,
    doctor.go}`, `internal/web/meta.go` (a comment), `compose.yaml`, `.env.example`, `scripts/e2e.d/85-bot.sh` step 85,
    the tests beside every one of them; DEPLOY §7, §30, API.md, README. In clippet-pass: `forward/scripts/commands.json`
    (new), `forward/scripts/deploy.sh` (`register`, `check`), `forward/test/register.test.ts` (new), README step 11,
    RUNBOOK. **No migration, no new route, no new egress, no new E2E step number, doctor still 16 checks.** It
    **amends 268** (the reply's grammar becomes the embed), **284** (one name becomes three) and **286** (a `link` option
    returns, on a command of its own); erratum **287**'s card is untouched — it is still what Discord draws under the
    message.)

    **AMENDED by erratum 316 (2026-10-05):** (c)'s embed is GONE. A bot message carrying an embed of its own never
    gets Discord's link unfurl (measured three times on the dev server), so the embed hid the card it was meant to sit
    above. The message is the share link alone, and the clip's page declares the branded card Discord draws under it
    (316 (b), (e)). The rest of this erratum — the three commands, the names, the compatibility — stands.

    **(a) The three commands.** One PUT per guild (`admin bot register`, unchanged in shape: it replaces the guild's
    whole set) now carries three definitions, in this order:
    - **`/upload file:`** — the one command of errata 253–286, RENAMED and otherwise unchanged: the required
      attachment, the deferral, the fetch through the CDN allow-list, the ingest as the bound account, the card-ready
      wait, the follow-up edit. Its description is *"Upload a video. You get a link that plays in Discord."*
      with 268(a)'s clause appended exactly as before (` Bigger files: {host}` when the host is 32 characters or
      fewer — the new lead is one character longer, so the ceiling moved from 33 — and ` Bigger files go on the
      site.` otherwise). The restart sentence a cancelled job leaves names this command now
      (`Clippet was restarting — run /upload again.`): the job is an upload.
    - **`/clip link:`** — a REQUIRED STRING option, `link` (*"A link to a clip on this Clippet"*), and the description
      *"Post a clip of this Clippet as a card."* Parsed, never fetched: `urls.Builder.ParseShare` — erratum 268(b)'s
      parser with 275(b)'s widening (`/clips/{id}`, `/embed/{id}`, the scheme-less form, Discord's `<…>` and
      `||…||` wraps), removed by 286(c) with its only caller and RESTORED byte for byte with its three tests — then
      `ids.Valid`, then ONE read of the row. The answer is `type: 4` on the interaction's own response — no
      deferral, because there is nothing slow to wait for — and PUBLIC: the channel is meant to see it. Every state
      is posted (an encoding clip answers at once with its state in the embed; somebody who pastes mid-encode wants
      the message now), an unlisted clip answers like a listed one (the link is the auth, §9), and ownership is not
      checked, for 268's reason. Two refusals, ephemeral: *"That is not a link to a clip on this
      Clippet."* (another host, another route, a segment that is not an id, an id nobody minted, no link at all) and
      *"That clip is gone."* (the `deleting` tombstone, or a clip whose `expires_at` has passed and the sweeper has
      not reached). 268 answered those two cases with ONE line so as not to be an oracle; the second line is
      call here, and what it adds is only "this id existed and is going" about an id the asker already holds —
      never a listing, never "exists, but not for you".
    - **"Enrich"**, the MESSAGE command (`type: 3`): a message's Apps menu (right-click, or long-press on a phone).
      The interaction carries the picked message in `data.resolved.messages[data.target_id]` — Discord's own
      exception for a message command, which is why this needs no gateway and no Message Content intent (the spike's
      §6(a)). The endpoint scans its `content` for the FIRST link `ParseShare` accepts as a clip here — each
      whitespace-separated token as it stands, then from every `https://`/`http://` inside it (a masked link
      `[text](…)`), each also with closing punctuation trimmed (a link ending a sentence); an id-shaped link of ours
      that names no row is skipped and the scan goes on — and answers exactly as `/clip link:` would for that clip.
      No link of ours: *"No link to a clip on this Clippet in that message."*, ephemeral. A tombstone:
      *"That clip is gone."*. It is routed by `data.type` FIRST and then by name, because Discord keeps message
      commands in a namespace of their own. Its name may carry uppercase and spaces (Discord's rule for type 3 —
      checked against the application-commands page before the rule was written: "may be mixed case and can include
      spaces", 1–32 characters), so it has no description (Discord refuses one on a message command) and no
      options. **Two facts stated rather than discovered:** the answer is NOT a reply to the picked message — an
      interaction callback has no `message_reference`, and a reply would need the bot token and a channel POST,
      which a managed instance does not hold — so the card simply posts next in the channel, as "<user> used
      Enrich"; and Discord's own card on the picked message stays, because the bot asks for no Manage Messages
      (hiding it is the spike's later, opt-in second app). **The message's text is read for the link and dropped:**
      only the clip id found reaches the access log (`discord=enrich clip=<id>`); nothing of the message is parsed
      beyond `content`, stored, or logged (`TestEnrichLogsTheClipAndNotTheMessage`).

    Both link-reading commands are gated by the guild binding exactly as `/upload` is — a server nobody connected may
    not post this instance's clips through this app's name — and answer a DM with the existing lines (the chat
    command's `Run /clip in a server, not in a DM.`; Enrich, which Discord never offers in a DM, the generic
    `Clippet is not available right now.`).

    **(b) Why the `link` option coming back is not the shape 286 withdrew.** 286 withdrew a `link` that sat BESIDE
    the file on the UPLOAD command, where it asked somebody to type a link back at the place it had just come from —
    and could only ever re-post what the person already held. A person pastes a link to SHOW a clip, not to upload
    it; `/clip link:` is that act, on a command of its own, and what it posts is not the bare link the person
    already had but the message of (c), with the instance named and the clip's state in colour. `/upload` keeps 286's
    single required option, and a string option arriving on it is still "no attachment" (that pin is kept).

    **(c) The enhanced message — ONE builder, `notify.ClipMessage`, for all three.** `/upload`'s follow-up PATCHes it;
    `/clip link:` and Enrich return it as their `data`. In Discord's Message shape, with no `flags` (public, and NOT
    `IS_COMPONENTS_V2`, which would forbid `content` and `embeds`):
    - `content` = the share link ALONE. Discord unfurls it under the message into erratum 287's card (site line,
      title, poster with its duration plate, the state-coloured bar); `SUPPRESS_EMBEDS` is never set. The title
      moved out of `content` into the embed — this replaces 268(c)'s `{title} · {m:ss}` line.
    - `embeds` = exactly ONE embed, which Discord draws ABOVE the unfurl: `author` = `{ name: SiteName() (287(a)'s
      host; the product's spelling only for a builder with no host), url: the front door, icon_url:
      {origin}/static/icon-192.png }` — the striped clapper of erratum 306, the smallest PNG every install serves
      (the favicon is an inline SVG with no URL; Discord draws an author icon at ~24 px through its media proxy, and
      the mark does not change with the build, so no `?v=`); `title` = the clip's title through 268's `plainTitle`
      (whitespace collapsed, every markdown active escaped — an embed title renders markdown too) and DROPPED when
      it reads as a link; `url` = the share link, so the title is the link (and dropped with the title);
      `description` = `{m:ss}`, then — short of ready — the reviewed state word (`queued`, `encoding` for `processing`,
      `failed`), joined by ` · `, a missing half simply not printed; `color` = web.CardColor's value as an integer.
    - No `footer` (it would repeat the author line), no `thumbnail`, no `image` (the picture is the unfurl's job), no
      `fields`, no `timestamp`. §15 stands: nothing the bot says is a CTA.
    - **The one-link rule of 268 is kept**: `content` is one link, ours; the embed's `author.url` and `url` are the
      same origin and the same clip — Discord unfurls `content` and never an embed's own URLs, so that is not a
      second card — and a URL-shaped title is dropped. `allowed_mentions` stays the empty parse list.
    - **An embed title past 256 characters makes Discord refuse the WHOLE message** (the follow-up would leave
      "thinking…", `/clip link:` would read "The application did not respond"), and a 200-rune title can double
      under escaping, so `embedTitle` cuts it to 256 — counted in UTF-16 units, between escapes, ending in one `…`.
      This was found writing the builder, not reported; it is pinned.
    - **The colour has ONE source.** §3 forbids `internal/notify` importing `internal/web`, so the three integers
      (`0x0E7C4F`, `0xD98E12`, `0xF0665C`) and the state words are spelled in `internal/notify` and pinned against
      `web.CardColor` for every db state by `TestEmbedColourIsTheCardsColour` in `internal/httpapi` — the package
      that already holds both, and already pins the command names the same way.
    - **Discord caches a card per URL**: a link posted mid-encode carries the link-out card under an amber embed and
      Discord will not re-unfurl it when the clip becomes ready. The bot does not edit its message later (an
      interaction token is good for 15 minutes; an edit loop is not built); a person re-pastes later. DEPLOY §30.4
      says so. How Discord RENDERS a bot message carrying both an embed and an unfurl is measured on the dev
      instance by the owner's hands; this lane builds to the documented Message and Embed objects and the
      E2E pins the JSON.

    **(d) Three names, all settings (amends 284).** `DISCORD_COMMAND_NAME` keeps naming `/clip` — now the LINK
    command — default `clip`; **`DISCORD_UPLOAD_COMMAND_NAME`** names `/upload`, default `upload`, under 284's rules
    word for word (Discord's chat-input pattern, no whitespace around it, an orphan with the bot off is a boot error,
    a managed instance must use the default); and the two **must differ** — one Discord server holds one chat command
    per name, so the PUT would carry one name twice (Discord refuses it whole) and the endpoint could not tell the
    two apart. The refusal names both variables and the shared name: `DISCORD_UPLOAD_COMMAND_NAME: must differ from
    DISCORD_COMMAND_NAME: both name /clip, and one Discord server holds one command per name, so the upload command
    and the link command would replace each other (DEPLOY.md §30.2)`; it is checked only when both names resolved
    cleanly, so a refused name's fallback is never reported as a collision nobody typed.
    **`DISCORD_ENRICH_COMMAND_NAME`** names the message command, default `Enrich` (dev: `Enrich (dev)`): length only
    (1–32 runes), plus our whitespace, orphan and managed rules; it may share a word with a chat command. The boot line
    gains `upload_command=/…` and `enrich_command=…` beside `command=/…`; the doctor's `bot` row reads `commands:
    /upload, /clip and Enrich`; `admin bot` names all three wherever it named one. The managed sentinel still refuses
    `register`, in words that now name the three the official application publishes globally.

    **(e) The one compatibility.** Every server held `/clip file:` before this build, and its picker keeps showing it
    until somebody re-registers (for the official bot, until the owner's `deploy.sh register` and Discord's propagation).
    So a `/clip` that arrives with an ATTACHMENT and no `link` is uploaded exactly as `/upload` would upload it
    (log field `discord_compat=attachment_on_link_command`) instead of telling somebody who attached a video that it
    is not a link. It closes itself when the command is re-published; nothing else is kept for the old shape.

    **(f) The forwarder (clippet-pass).** `forward/scripts/commands.json` is the global body, whole, and
    `deploy.sh register` PUTs that file: `/upload` (with the no-host sentence, ` Bigger files go on the site.` — a
    shared application has no host to name), `/clip link:`, and Enrich with `integration_types: [0]` and
    `contexts: [0]` (Discord reads both for GLOBAL commands only, which is why the instance's GUILD registration

    `interactions.ts` nothing more), so invariant I1's files are untouched. The register is the owner's Discord write,

    It **amends 315** (the message is the share link alone; 315's head says so).)

    **AMENDED by erratum 317 (2026-10-06):** (b)'s heading test is narrower. The title is the masked link when it
    holds none of the characters that can act INSIDE a label (`labelActives`: ``\*_~`|<>[]()`` and `@`); `-` and
    `#` act only at a line's start, which a label never is, so a hyphenated title — every date-and-time title 317
    gives — is the link. The escape table outside a label (`discordMarkdownActives`) is unchanged.

    **(a) The format, as Discord writes it (the documentation is unmerged).** The source is Discord's own
    Link Previews pull request, discord/discord-api-docs #8606 ("Document link previews", opened 2026-09-16 by Discord
    staff, head `48e0eef`, still OPEN and unmerged on 2026-10-05; its pages `developers/link-previews/
    component-embeds.mdx` and `developers/link-previews/overview.mdx`, read raw from the PR's files). The PUBLISHED
    docs (docs.discord.com, read through Discord's docs MCP on 2026-10-05) carry none of it yet; the components
    reference they do carry is the source for each component's fields. What the PR says, quoted:
    - What it is: *"A component embed replaces that preview with a layout you control, built from a subset of the
      same components apps use in messages."* Its changelog entry (dated September 30, 2026 in the PR): *"Component
      embeds are display-only, so nothing sends an interaction, and you don't need an app or a bot to use them."* A
      message carrying one has a new embed `type`, `components`, with a `components` array holding the one Container.
    - **Where it goes, option 1 (ours):** *"Put a `<script id="discord:component-embed"
      type="application/vnd.discord.component-embed+json">` in the page Discord fetches, inside the `<head>`
      element."* *"`application/json` is also accepted."* Option 2 is a `<link rel="discord:component-embed"
      type="application/vnd.discord.component-embed+json" href="…">` to a JSON document *"on the same site"* whose
      `href` *"must be an absolute URL"* on the page's host, a subdomain or its parent — a second fetch inside the same
      ten seconds, and a new JSON route for the guard to learn; not taken (see (d)).
    - **Shape:** *"a JSON object with a single, parent Container component"* — `{"component": {"type": 17, …}}`;
      *"No other component can exist at the top level with the container."*
    - **Limits:** *"For both options, there is a 3,000-byte limit. Escape sequences like `<` also count toward
      it at their full length."* *"A component embed can contain up to 40 components, including the parent Container
      component."* Media Gallery items *"are capped at 10 across the entire embed"*. A media URL *"must use `http` or
      `https` and be a max of 2,048 character in length. Valid file formats for video include `.mp4`, `.webm`, and
      `.mov`. Valid file formats for images include `.png`, …"*. *"The whole fetch, including every image in the
      payload, must finish within 10 seconds."*
    - **Compatible components:** Action Row (1), Button (2), Section (9), Text Display (10), Thumbnail (11), Media
      Gallery (12), Separator (14), Container (17). *"A button must use the link style (`style` of `5`) and may
      contain `id`, `type`, `url`, `style`, `label`, `emoji`, and `disabled` … Any other key invalidates the entire
      payload."* Text Display *"content uses Discord markdown"*.
    - **Media:** *"A video in a Media Gallery shows a preview frame with play controls but does not autoplay."*
      Discord fills in width, height, content type and the proxy URL *"after it fetches the asset"*.
    - **The fallback:** *"Open Graph tags are present, so a standard preview is available when a component embed
      can't be shown"* (a prerequisite) — and the warning that it is NOT universal: *"There are some cases … that can
      cause embed unfurling to completely fail without a fallback, like using more than 40 components or adding an
      invalid `id`."*, *"Using more than 40 components will cause the embed to not render instead of falling back on
      Open Graph."*
    - **What is still changing:** the page opens with *"Link previews are subject to change."*; staff deployed
      *"a bunch of improvements to component embeds"* on 2026-10-03 (the second research sheet). **Which clients draw
      it** — desktop, web, mobile — the PR does not say at all; the measurement in (f) is the only answer we have.
    - **Caching and testing:** *"Discord caches previews for about 30 minutes"*; *"share the URL with a new query
      string, such as `?v=2`"*; *"The Embed Debugger (discord.com/developers/embeds) shows how Discord reads any URL,
      including which tags it picked up and which layout it chose."*

    **(b) What a Clippet page declares.** One Container, six components, built by the pure function
    `web.BuildComponentEmbed(ClipView, badge)` from the same row and the same `urls.Builder` the §9.1 inventory comes
    from:
    - `accent_color` = `web.CardColor(state)` as an integer — erratum 287(c)'s green / amber / red, the same source as
      the `theme-color` bar. It is now the ONLY source: the bot's embed colour of 315 is gone with the embed.
    - a **Section**: one Text Display of three lines — `-# {SiteName()}` (287(a)'s host as Discord's small grey
      subtext), the title as a `###` heading, and the card's description line (`cardDescription`, 287(b)) for a ready
      clip or the link-out card's `Processing…` / `Processing failed` otherwise — and as its accessory a
      **Thumbnail** of the mark: `{origin}/static/icon-192.png`, or, on an instance that wears `INSTANCE_BADGE`,
      `{origin}/static/icon-dev-192.png` (see (d)).
    - a **Media Gallery** with ONE item: for a ready clip `Social(id)` — the Light copy `social.mp4`, the exact URL
      `og:video` names; otherwise the §9.1 placeholder `Static("card-placeholder.png")`.
    - an **Action Row** with ONE link Button (`style` 5): `url` = `Page(id)`, `label` = **`Open`** — the only
      new user-facing string in this erratum.

    **The text is Discord markdown, so it is escaped — and one place refuses escapes.** The host, the title and the
    owner's words go through erratum 268's rule (whitespace collapsed; ``\*_~`|<>[]()#-`` backslash-escaped), which
    Discord consumes in ordinary text. Inside a masked link's LABEL it does NOT: the owner's first real card printed the
    title `Arc_Raiders_2026.01.06_-_00.15.37.07.DVR-…` as `Arc\_Raiders\_2026.01.06\_\-\_…`. A label cannot go
    unescaped either — a `]` ends it, `* _ ~ |` and a backtick format inside it, `<@…>` is a mention — so there is no
    backslash-free encoding that keeps a label both faithful and inert. Hence `titleLine`: the title is the masked
    link `### [title](page)` only when it holds NO markdown-active character at all (its label is then the title's
    own characters and has nothing to smuggle), and otherwise a plain escaped `### title`. A title that reads as a
    link (`://`, `www.`) is dropped, as 315 dropped it, and a description whose owner's words carry one keeps its
    length and quality clause and loses only those words. **"at this link" is the link** (the owner's second finding):
    `descriptionLine` makes exactly the quality clause's closing words `[at this link](page)` — a label with no
    markdown character — on this card only; `og:description` keeps its text unchanged, and the words are one
    constant (`qualityLinkWords`) shared by both.

    The JSON is encoded with `<`, `>` and `&` as JSON unicode escapes, so no text can close the `<script>` element,
    and a payload past 3,000 bytes is not emitted at all (the page carries the §9.1 card alone, the documented
    fallback); the worst case a 200-rune title of `<` and a 200-rune description of four-byte runes reach on a long
    host is 2,948 bytes, pinned by `TestComponentEmbedWorstCaseFits`.

    **(c) `CARD_COMPONENTS=on|off`, ON by default** since the owner's real-channel test (f). `off` serves every page byte
    for byte as before this erratum (pinned). The data block is rendered by `base.html` in `<head>`, after the §9.1
    inventory and before the canonical link, on the share page in both of its shapes and nowhere else (not the
    embed, not a collection, not a 404/503). The §9.1 `og:*`/`twitter:*` inventory and the `theme-color` bar are
    unchanged in both states: they ARE the fallback, and `card_check`'s counts do not move. The crawler hold (213)
    is unchanged — a crawler asking about a clip whose card is still coming still gets the 503 with no card — so
    Discord in practice reads the ready shape and the failed one. The CSP is unchanged: a data block of a
    non-JavaScript type is never executed; the unit test that every page carries no inline script admits exactly
    this one element, by its exact opening tag, at most once.

    **(d) The mark is the instance's** (the owner, on a dev card: the production logo, not the dev one; pick (b) of
    three). `scripts/lib/mkicons.py` draws one more raster from the one geometry: `web/static/icon-dev-192.png` —
    `icon-192.png`'s drawing, size and rounded ink tile with the GREY span the dev Discord application's icon
    already carries (erratum 285's rule: green span = production, grey = any other instance). Nothing is redrawn;
    the generator's `--check` (check.sh stage 06) covers it, `TestMarkAssetsMatchTheGolden` pins its decoded pixels (its
    golden computed from the generator's own `draw(192, GREY, True)` by the same row hash, which reproduces
    `icon-192`'s existing golden for GREEN), E2E step 77 HEADs it, and the card's Thumbnail uses it whenever
    `INSTANCE_BADGE` is set (`TestComponentEmbedMarkFollowsTheBadge`). It is a NEW STATIC PATH — the clippet-pass
    manifest's static table must carry it.

    **(e) The bot's message is the share link alone (amends 315(c)).** `notify.ClipMessage(u, clipID)` returns
    `{"content": <share link>, "allowed_mentions": {"parse": []}}` and nothing else — no `embeds`, no `components`,
    no `flags` — for `/upload`'s follow-up, `/clip link:` and Enrich alike. Removed as dead with the embed: the
    `Embed`/`EmbedAuthor`/`ClipCard` types, `EmbedColor` and its three integers, the state words, `embedTitle` and
    its 256 cut (UTF-16 counting, `escapedPieces`, `utf16Len`), `plainTitle`/`markdownActives`/`looksLikeALink`
    and notify's `formatDuration` copy; `IngestResult` loses `Title`, `DurationMS` and `State`, which only the
    embed read; `internal/httpapi`'s `TestEmbedColourIsTheCardsColour` goes with `EmbedColor`. The one-link rule of
    268 holds trivially. The page's card is the branding now: a bot message and a human paste draw the same card.

    **(f) What the guard needs (clippet-pass, a lane of its own; not edited here).** `guard/src/html.ts`'s hard rule
    *"no <script> but the one whose src is /static/app.js and whose body is empty"* refuses this element outright
    (`e.body` is true, `src` is missing), so a release carrying this erratum served through a Pass name would BLOCK
    every finished clip's page — the default is on. The plane needs, before such a release is served: (1) a
    hard-rule exception for exactly one `<script>` per page with exactly `id="discord:component-embed"` and
    `type="application/vnd.discord.component-embed+json"` and no other attribute; (2) its body judged (the guard reads
    no script body today): valid JSON, at most 3,000 bytes, every `url` on the response's own origin (`absoluteOn`);
    (3) the skeleton signature `script|id,type`, which the manifest tool derives from `base.html` — noting that
    `scan.ts`'s RAW_TEXT path marks the template's interpolated body as non-empty too; (4) the new static path
    `/static/icon-dev-192.png` in the manifest's static table; (5) fixture pages with the element, one with a
    foreign URL in its body. No new route and no new `<meta>`, so `META_URL_KEYS` does not move. Option 2 (linked
    JSON) would instead need a new route class and a JSON body judge, which is why it was not taken. Until then a
    Pass operator sets `CARD_COMPONENTS=off`.

    **(g) The measurement** (recorded in the run's records).

317. **A capture tool's timestamp becomes the title; Cancel covers a run parked behind the one it cancels**
    (the owner's pick (1a) of run 4, 2026-10-06: the timestamp title `2025-06-24 00:23`, after the cards showed raw file names; lane `titles`.
    Changed: `internal/httpapi/upload.go` (`captureTitle`, `captureStamp`, `defaultTitle`), `internal/web/compembed.go`
    (`titleLine`, `labelActives`), `internal/worker/worker.go` (`withRun`, `Cancel`, three registry fields and a test
    hook), the tests beside each, `scripts/e2e.d/47-upload.sh` step 47 (one upload more, `N6`), DEPLOY §9 (the rule,
    once) with §9's ShareX note, §30 and the drop folder's and the importer's sentences pointing at it, API.md. **No
    migration, no new route, no new E2E step number, no new user-facing string.** It **amends 316** (b), as 316's head
    now says.)

    **(a) The title rule** (the reviewed wording, applied exactly). At the ONE fallback — `defaultTitle`, which every
    route that creates a clip without a typed title reaches through the ingest core: `POST /api/clips`, the capture
    link `POST /api/upload`, the bot's `/upload`, `admin import`, the drop folder — when the file's stem (extension
    removed) carries a date `YYYY-MM-DD`, `YYYY.MM.DD` or `YYYY_MM_DD` followed by a clock `HH-MM-SS`, `HH.MM.SS`,
    `HH_MM_SS` or `HH-MM`, with a space, `_`, `-` or ` - ` between them (and `_-_`, which is Game Bar's ` - ` after a
    trim tool made its spaces underscores), the title is **`YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM`**: seconds dropped, the date's
    separators made hyphens, the clock as the file wrote it — no timezone. Text BEFORE the date is kept in front,
    its underscores made spaces and its runs of whitespace collapsed; everything after the clock (`.DVR`, a trim
    range, a duplicate's `(1)`) is dropped. A stem with no such timestamp is unchanged, byte for byte; a typed title
    always wins, and a capture-link title equal to the file's own name is still no title (erratum 60), so it, too,
    reaches the rule. What makes a match (checked in `captureTitle`, since RE2 cannot): the date's two separators
    agree and so do the clock's; the bare `HH-MM` form is hyphenated only; month 01–12, day 01–31, hour 00–23,
    minute and second 00–59; the date does not start inside a longer run of digits and the clock does not run on
    into one. The first timestamp that passes wins; the 200-rune cap applies after.
    - Pinned (`TestDefaultTitleFromACaptureTimestamp`): OBS `2025-06-24 00-23-54.mkv` and its trim
      `2025-06-24_00-23-54-00.00.22.520-00.00.40.483.mp4`, ShareX `2025-06-24_00-23-54.mp4` → `2025-06-24 00:23`;
      Game Bar `Arc Raiders 2026.01.06 - 00.15.37.07.DVR.mp4` and its trim
      `Arc_Raiders_2026.01.06_-_00.15.37.07.DVR-00.02.14.016-00.02.23.033` (with and without `.mp4`) →
      `Arc Raiders 2026-01-06 00:15`; each separator form; and the negatives `2025`, `v1.2.3`, `192.168.0.1`,
      `2025-06-24` with no clock, a lone `HH.MM`, disagreeing separators, month 13, hour 24, a clock running on into
      a digit and a date inside a longer number — each the stem unchanged.
    - **The brief listed `final 2025-06-24 00-23-54 (1)` among the negatives.** The rule it states keeps the text
      before the date and drops the `(1)`, so it gives `final 2025-06-24 00:23`; it was ruled a
      positive and it is pinned so.
    - Three existing pins move with the rule, all capture-link tests whose file names were timestamps:
      `TestCaptureUploadFieldAfterFileIsIgnored` (`Replay 2026-09-04 18-22-13.mp4` → `Replay 2026-09-04 18:22`),
      `TestCaptureUploadTitleEqualToTheFilename`'s first case and `TestMintTokenCarriesSXCU`'s ShareX upload (both
      `2026-09-04_18-22-13.mp4` → `2026-09-04 18:22`).
    - E2E step 47 (bundle `47-upload`) adds ONE upload with no title, named
      `ts<stamp>_2025-06-24_00-23-54-00.00.22.520.mp4`, and asserts the title `ts<stamp> 2025-06-24 00:23`; the clip
      is waited for and deleted with the step's other five.
    - **Where it shows** is everywhere the title already shows — the card, the library row, `og:title` — and the
      component card's heading, where (b) of 316 as built would have made every such title the plain escaped
      heading for its hyphens. Hence the amendment: inside a masked link's label only ``\*_~`|<>[]()`` and `@` can
      act (a backslash Discord prints literally there; the formatting marks; a mention or custom emoji's `< >` and a
      mention's `@`; the link's own brackets), while `-` and `#` are actives only at the START of a line — a list
      item, a heading — and a label never starts one: it follows `### [`. So `2025-06-24 00:23`, `Arc Raiders
      2026-01-06 00:15` and `Clip #3 - the ace` are links with their own characters in the label, and a title with
      any `labelActives` character is still 316's escaped plain heading. `:` was never an active. Pinned in
      `TestComponentEmbedTitleLine` (three links, three plain headings: `]`, `*`, `@`) and
      `TestComponentEmbedTimestampTitleIsALink` (one whole card, with `og:title` carrying the same characters).

    **(b) `TestPosterIsCancelledSynchronously` — the promise, the hole and the claim.** The test failed three times
    (lane `speed2`'s first check, gate 22's attempt 1, once in the cleanup list) with *"Busy is still true after Cancel
    returned"*. Two things were true at once:
    - **The product hole.** `withRun` let a run of a clip PARK behind a predecessor of the same clip (erratum 32: a
      job requeued by `fail()` and re-claimed by another loop). `Cancel` cancelled and waited for the registered run
      only; the parked one took the slot the instant the cancelled one closed `done` — after `Cancel` had stopped
      looking — and ran uncancelled into the prefix and the scratch dir `lifecycle.Destroy` was about to remove.
      **The promise now:** when `Cancel` returns true, no run of the clip is registered or parked. A run that
      registers while a `Cancel` of its clip is in progress starts cancelled (`reasonCancelled`, its context done,
      its own release path); `Cancel` counts parked runs (`waiting`), waits on a registration broadcast (`regCh`,
      closed and replaced on every registration) when it finds the slot empty but a run parked, and loops until
      neither remains — every wait still bounded by its `ctx` (AUDIT #13's false return is unchanged).
    - **The claim was wrong as the test set it up.** The test called `Cancel` on a `ready` clip without
      `MarkDeleting`. The cancelled poster's release then handed its job BACK to the queue (`run_after = now` on the
      harness's frozen clock), and the one media loop claimed it again a moment after `Cancel` returned: a NEW run
      of new work, which no ordering inside `Cancel` can cover — whatever `Cancel` does, it has returned before the
      claim. The only caller supplies the precondition that makes the promise whole: `lifecycle.Destroy` runs
      `MarkDeleting` first, which cancels every job of the clip, and no claim takes a job of a deleting clip. So the
      test now runs Destroy's own order (`MarkDeleting`, then `Cancel`) and asserts, besides `Busy` false, that the
      poster job is the mark's cancelled row (not requeued) and the clip is still `deleting` — the old "clip is
      ready" line could not survive the mark, and what it meant, that a poster ending never moves a clip, is what
      the new line says. `TestCancelWithoutTombstoneReleases` keeps the no-mark release covered.
    - **The deterministic pin:** `TestCancelCoversARunParkedBehindTheOneItCancels` forces the interleaving with
      channels the test owns: a run registered by hand whose `cancel` signals the test, a successor parked in
      `withRun` behind it (the `parkedHook` reports the park — no sleep), `Cancel` started, the predecessor released
      exactly as `withRun`'s exit does (unregister, then `done`), and then: `Cancel` must not have returned before the
      successor's body has exited, and `Busy` is false. With the two product changes reverted (the old single-wait
      `Cancel`, no cancelled start), it FAILS on its first run — *"Cancel returned while a run of the clip was live:
      the run parked behind the cancelled one registered uncancelled"*. With them, under `-race -count=200` over the pin, the poster test and the three other
      Cancel tests: 707 passes and no failure before go test's default 10-minute timeout cut the first run, and a
      second run without the timeout passed 1000 of 1000 (200 × 5 tests) in 956 s; the whole package passed once under `-race`.


318. **`/settings` on the instance: the link defaults from Discord — a one-row panel, a modal, and the settings
    page's own writer** (lane `boxpanel`, run 4, 2026-10-06; run 4's panel contract
    §4/§5 is the specification, and lane `panel` in clippet-pass builds the forwarder's half to the same contract).

    **(a) The command.** `DISCORD_SETTINGS_COMMAND_NAME` (default `settings`; the dev instance `settings-dev`) names a
    fourth command, held to the slash-command rules of errata 284/315: Discord's shape, no whitespace around it, an
    orphan with the bot off is a boot error, a MANAGED instance may not rename it (the official application publishes
    `/settings` globally and its forwarder answers it), and it must differ from `DISCORD_COMMAND_NAME` and
    `DISCORD_UPLOAD_COMMAND_NAME` — erratum 315's must-differ pair extended to the three chat names. The message
    command stays outside the rule (its own namespace). `admin bot register` PUTs FOUR definitions in one call; the
    new one is `{"name","type":1,"description":"This server's Clippet: the connection and the link defaults.",
    "default_member_permissions":"32"}` and nothing else (no `contexts`/`integration_types`: a guild command, erratum
    315's reason). A self-hosted application never publishes `/pass` — there is no Pass without the plane. The boot
    line gains `settings_command=/…`, `admin doctor`'s `bot` row and `bind`/`register`'s output name four commands.

    **(b) Three interactions, every one answered on the response.** (1) The command (type 2) → an ephemeral Components
    V2 panel (`flags` 32832): ONE Container, no accent (the accent is the forwarder's connection signal and this
    panel states no connection), holding a Section — `**Link defaults**` + the contract's sentence, accessory a
    Secondary `Edit` button `cb:defaults` — and the Text Display `**Who may clip**\nServer Settings → Integrations →
    Clippet.` Two top-level components, five in all: inside the contract's strict reading of the limits. (2) A
    MESSAGE_COMPONENT (type 3) `cb:defaults` → the MODAL (callback 9) `cb:defaults:modal`, title `Link defaults`,
    three Labels (type 18), pre-filled from the bound account: `Delete after` → a Radio Group (21) of SIX options —
    `server default · {DEFAULT_CLIP_TTL as the page words it}` (value `default`, the account's third TTL state,
    null), `1 day`, `7 days`, `30 days`, `90 days`, `never` (values 1/7/30/90/0); `Unlisted` (description `New
    clips are unlisted unless you say otherwise.`) → a Checkbox (23); `Link` → a Radio Group of `Compact` /
    `Memorable`. The current value carries `"default": true`. (3) A MODAL_SUBMIT (type 5) `cb:defaults:modal` → each
    Label's one `component` is read by its `custom_id` (`value` for the radios — a string, null refused — and the
    checkbox's boolean; `values[0]` for the fallback's selects; the legacy Action Row shape is walked too); every
    answer must be one of its choices, else ephemeral `That is not a choice here.` and nothing written; then
    `changeDefaults` — the SAME function `PATCH /api/auth/me/settings` now calls (extracted from it by this erratum:
    one reader, one set of closed-set checks via `config.ParseTTLDays` and `db.ValidLinkStyle`, one
    `SetUserDefaults`) — and ephemeral `Saved.` (`{"type":4,"data":{"content":"Saved.","flags":64}}`; `Changes saved.`
    since erratum 330).

    **(c) The gate, on every `cb:` interaction and on the command:** the guild is bound (`msgUnbound`), then proof A —
    `member.permissions` (the decimal bitfield; the ONE member field this endpoint reads) carries ADMINISTRATOR
    (1<<3) or MANAGE_GUILD (1<<5), else ephemeral `You need Manage Server here.`; no member object, an empty or
    non-numeric field is a refusal. `default_member_permissions` hides the command already, but a server's admins
    may widen it and a click is a body: re-checked per interaction (the contract's defence in depth; dev-tests T1
    says a channel overwrite cannot touch MANAGE_GUILD). A `custom_id` that does not start `cb:` (the claim plane's
    `cf:` never reaches a box) is `Clippet does not know that command.` BEFORE the binding is read; so is an unknown
    `cb:` id or a click/submit carrying the other's id. The forwarder relays `cb:` exactly as `/clip` (same hop,
    same 2 s deadline, the sentinel `X-Real-IP`): no new trust and nothing new exposed — no read endpoint for the
    defaults, `GET /api/bot/claim` unchanged.

    **(d) Words and logs.** Every string is the contract's §6 or the settings page's own word for the same choice;
    the TTL label is `Delete after` — the page's label — because the contract's first draft `Keep for` would have
    read "Keep for: never", which erratum 244 records the owner rejecting (withdrawn 2026-10-06). The
    fallback's two Unlisted choices are the clip page's own `listed in the library` / `not in the library`. The
    access log carries `discord=component|modal` and `discord_prefix=cb:|other` — never a submitted value, the
    full custom_id or anything of the member.

    **(e) The fallback (dev-tests T5).** `defaultsModalShape` (internal/httpapi/discord_settings.go) is the ONE
    constant: `modalRadios` (the contract's shape) or `modalSelects` — the same three Labels with String Selects
    (type 3; Unlisted as a two-option select). The submit parser reads EITHER shape whatever the constant says, so a
    modal opened before a flip still saves.

    **(f) The measurement (dev-tests T4/T5, Clippet Dev, `/settings-dev`).** PENDING the owner's look. Set up
    2026-10-06: the dev worktree checked out `boxpanel` (`eb27718`) detached, `DISCORD_SETTINGS_COMMAND_NAME=
    settings-dev` appended to its `.env`, rebuilt (boot line `settings_command=/settings-dev`), and, on the owner's word
    relayed, `admin bot register 222222222222222222` → "/upload-dev, /clip-dev, Enrich (dev)
    and /settings-dev published". The owner was asked: (1) desktop, `/settings-dev` — does the one-row panel render
    (T4)? (2) desktop, `Edit` — does the modal render with the radios and the checkbox (T5)? (3) change all three,
    Submit → `Saved.`, and does dev's Settings → Upload defaults show the new values? (4) the same modal on a
    PHONE (T5 mobile; a screenshot); (5) the web client if handy. The verdicts are relayed; if
    a client cannot draw the radios/checkbox, the swap is ONE constant (`defaultsModalShape = modalSelects`) and
    lane `panel` copies the shape that renders everywhere. The live wire on a lane stack (E2E step 85,
    `E2E_ONLY=85-bot`, PASS 172 s, zero ERROR) shows the panel, the modal, `Saved.` and the settings API reading
    the saved values back.

    **Pins.** internal/config: default, rename, Discord's shape, whitespace, orphan, must-differ against both chat
    names (and NOT against the message command), the managed refusal. internal/notify: the register body is four
    definitions, the fourth pinned key for key, `default_member_permissions` on it alone. internal/httpapi
    (`discord_settings_test.go`, request fixtures in Discord's documented shapes, responses pinned as JSON goldens):
    the panel; its strict limits; the renamed command; the default-name pin (notify ↔ config ↔ loader); the gate on
