    Revert-and-rerun: proof A forced true, the ADMINISTRATOR bit dropped, the shape flipped, `never` re-cased, the
    permissions field dropped from the register body, the must-differ check removed — each turned its pin red;
    the modal's own link-style check removed stayed green, because `changeDefaults` refuses it too (two layers, by
    design). E2E step 85: the first probe answers the panel, the Edit modal (three Labels, radios + checkbox, the
    server-default option marked), a no-Manage-Server click refused, the submit `Saved.` and the account's
    defaults read back through `GET /api/auth/me/settings`; the renamed probe answers `/settings-dev` and not
    `/settings`, and the boot line, doctor and bind name four commands; the managed refusal names four.

    **Amended 2026-10-12 (run 14, lane `settingsui`; the owner's ask: the Link defaults section should print
    what it is set to).** A bound answer of `GET /api/bot/claim` (erratum 279) now carries the bound account's
    defaults beside `bound` and `app_id`: `"defaults": {"ttl_days": N, "unlisted": bool, "link":
    "compact"|"memorable"}` — `ttl_days` the EFFECTIVE term (the account's, else DEFAULT_CLIP_TTL's days — also for a hand-edited term outside the legal set, as an upload falls back; 0 =
    never), `link` through `LinkStyleOr`. A failed defaults read omits the object and keeps the proof. The official
    bot's `/settings` panel (clippet-pass `forward/src/claim/panel.ts`) makes the same GET on every draw of a
    connected panel, beside its name read and under the same 1.5 s deadline (a Connect reuses proof C's own
    answer), and prints the three in its own closed words under "Link defaults" (`7 days · listed · compact link`);
    an old box, a silent one or a wrong shape draws the label alone. The disclosure changes from one bit to one bit
    plus three preferences to anyone who knows a bound guild id and the host — no identity, no content; the
    grammar and the term already show on every link and clip page, the unlisted default is the one new fact.
    Pins: `bot_claim_test.go` (exactly three fields; a fresh account's resolved term; set values read back;
    `claimDefaults` over the instance TTL, nil, never, an illegal stored term (5 → the instance's 30) and an illegal grammar). The review's two follow-ups (the line redrawn after a save; the endpoint back to one bit, an option) are ROADMAP #55.

319. **A webhook on every new clip: one signed JSON document, POSTed to the one URL the operator names — off by
    default** (lane `hook`, run 6, 2026-10-06; ROADMAP #54 pick 6; the reviewed design is
    the reviewed hook design).

    **(a) Configuration.** `CLIP_WEBHOOK_URL` + `CLIP_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, both or neither (`internal/config/clipwebhook.go`):
    one alone is fatal at boot naming the missing one — `is unset but CLIP_WEBHOOK_SECRET is set: the clip webhook
    needs both, or neither` and its mirror. The URL: `http` or `https` (the review settled the design's Q1 as (a): the
    receivers this is for sit on the operator's own network without TLS; the cost is stated in the doctor row and
    DEPLOY §11.1, and https-only is a one-line change), a host, no userinfo, no fragment (a trailing `#` included), a
    query allowed, no length rule. The key: 32 characters or more, no whitespace. **Both values are secrets** and live in
    ONE type with unexported fields, `config.ClipWebhook` (`Configured`/`URL`/`Secret`/`Scheme`/`Host`); its
    `String`/`LogValue` render `<scheme>://<host>` plus `/(path redacted)` when anything follows the host, `(unset)`
    when off. No rejection echoes any part of either value — the scheme error says only `scheme must be http or
    https`, because the two variables swapped parse the key's prefix as a "scheme". `admin doctor` registers both raw
    values as secrets before the load.

    **(b) The queue.** `db.ReadyFields.QueueHook` is an instruction (QueueSocial's precedent) that ONLY
    `FinalizeTranscode` reads: inside the ready commit, independent of the notify bit and of `unlisted`, it inserts one
    `kind='hook'` job with `params_json='{}'` — nothing of the URL or the key is stored. The already-applied path
    (n == 0) inserts nothing, and `SwapRendition`/`SwapSource` ignore the field, so the event fires once per clip, when
    it FIRST becomes ready; a trim or a replacement sends nothing. The pipeline sets it to `Hook != nil` on the fresh
    run and on the finalize-only retry alike (it rides on no checkpoint). `db.KindHook`, `HookMaxAttempts = 5`
    (`limitsFor` pins 5/5 whatever the transcode caps say); the notify loop claims it through its existing EXCLUSION
    filter; `ClipIDsWithLiveJobs` excludes `hook` beside `notify` (it writes no object).

    **(c) Delivery.** `internal/notify/hook.go`: `NewHook` returns nil unless both values are set; the client comes from
    `newHTTPClient` (no redirect followed — a 3xx is a permanent rejection), 10 s per attempt. `Deliver` makes one
    attempt and reuses the notifier's classifier, now the shared `classify` (2xx ok; network/timeout/429/5xx retry, a
    429's `Retry-After` honoured up to five minutes; any other answer permanent) — Discord's `Deliver` calls the same
    function, byte-identical. Headers `Content-Type: application/json`, `User-Agent: Clippet`, `X-Clippet-Signature:
    sha256=<64 lowercase hex>` = HMAC-SHA256 over the exact body bytes, keyed with the secret's bytes as typed, computed
    at delivery. The body, in this order: `event` (`clip.ready`), `id`, `url` (`urls.Builder.Page`), `title` (as typed;
    HTML characters not escaped), `duration_ms` and `expires_at` (the row's nullable columns, number/null and
    RFC 3339/null), `owner` (the USERNAME — already public through the anonymous clip DTO's `owner.username`; never the
    account id), `created_at`, `unlisted`. No clock is in the body (the design's `sent_at` was cut): `id` is the dedupe
    key, and a retry is byte-identical to the first attempt. Never in it: a token, an email, a storage key. **Scrub
    needles**: every spelling of the WHOLE URL and the key always; the path, the escaped path, the raw query, each path
    segment and each query value (raw and escaped) only at 8 bytes or more (`minHookNeedle`; doctor's `minSecretLen`
    precedent — the fixture's `/in` must not strike honest text), longest first; the read window grows to
    `bodySnippet + the longest needle` because the URL has no length cap.

    **(d) The worker.** `runHook` (`internal/worker/hook.go`) is `runNotify`'s twin on the same loop: not configured →
    skip; re-read the clip → gone / `deleting` / not ready → skip (`done`, the note in `last_error`, INFO); the
    owner's username (a missing owner is an empty name, not a withheld event); deliver; complete / release on shutdown
    / fail (retryable → crash class with the Retry-After floor: immediately, +30 s, +60 s, +120 s, +240 s, then
    `failed`; otherwise permanent). WARN, never ERROR; the clip is never written. **An UNLISTED clip is sent**, marked
    `"unlisted": true` — the receiver is the operator's own system; the Discord post still skips it. The notify
    helpers were generalised by a `delivery` descriptor (a noun and a subject) instead of copied: every `discord
    webhook …` and `notify job …` line, its attributes, `NotifyMaxAttempts` and every Detail are byte-identical (E2E
    step 20 and 55-owner pin them); the hook's lines are `clip webhook configured|delivered|skipped|delivery failed;
    requeued|not delivered; giving up|rejected; not retrying` and `hook job …`, and none contains `discord webhook`.

    **(e) The operator's surfaces.** Boot: one INFO `clip webhook configured scheme=… host=…` (host with its port;
    never the path, the query or the key). `admin doctor`: inside the existing `webhook` check (the summary stays `16
    checks`), the Discord rows first and the hook row last, `ok` for http and https alike (a permanent warn for a LAN
    receiver would teach operators to ignore warns) with the plain-http sentence appended for `http`; with the hook
    set, the Discord-unset row becomes `DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL is unset: no clip is posted to Discord` and the `fs`
    `store` row keeps only `on \`fs\` the media path has NO outbound destination` — the sentences they replace would
    be false. With the hook unset every row is byte-identical. `admin jobs --kind hook`; `admin stats`' `jobs:` line
    ends `… full=%d hook=%d)`. §15's list of outbound destinations gains the one URL; README, DEPLOY §11/§11.1/§32
    and the doctor table, `.env.example`, compose.yaml (two passthroughs, both empty by default), check.sh stage 09's
    message and `parseDiscordURL`'s host error (its §15 tail dropped) were trued up. No migration, no route, no UI,
    no API.md change, nothing in clippet-pass.

    **Pins.** internal/config: off by default; five accepted shapes with their redacted forms; seven refusals with their
    exact messages, none echoing the token, the key, the bad scheme or the bad escape; the key rule; both-or-neither in
    both directions without echo; `%v`/`%+v`/slog of the whole Config never carry the path, the query or the key.
    internal/notify: nil when unset or keyless; the body golden (nine keys, order, null/RFC 3339, HTML unescaped); the
    signature recomputed over the received bytes, another key refused, 64 lowercase hex; the classifier table (204,
    400, 404, 301 not followed, 429 with Retry-After, 500, 503) with one request each; timeout and refused retryable
    with no URL in Detail; an echoing receiver gets the URL, the query, the token and the key struck while honest text
    stays; `/in` is not a needle and a 30-byte path token echoed alone is struck; a 1500-byte URL straddling the cut
    leaves nothing. internal/db: QueueHook inserts exactly one job in the ready commit for listed AND unlisted clips,
    with or without notify, none without it, none on the re-finalize; a trim and a replacement with `QueueHook: true`
    insert none; the cap is 5/5 and the backoff 30/60/120/240 s; the media and transcode claims never take it;
    `ClipIDsWithLiveJobs` ignores it. internal/worker: delivered (unlisted marked, owner `alice`, no Discord line);
    five attempts then `failed`, WARN only; a 404 fails once and is never asked again; deleted / deleting /
    unconfigured skips post nothing; unset enqueues nothing and logs no `clip webhook` line; a shutdown releases with
    both counters untouched; no log line or job row carries the token or the key. cmd/clippet: unset leaves the
    `webhook` rows alone; the hook row's exact text for https and http, last, `ok`, `16 checks`, no secret; Discord's
    rows unchanged before it; a half-configured doctor run never echoes the URL; the `fs` store row with and without
    the hook; `hook` valid and last in `jobKinds`; `hook=0)` on the stats line. **E2E step 97** (`97-hook.sh`,
    parallel): (a) no hook job for any clip of THE RUN'S OWN account when the stack's `CLIP_WEBHOOK_URL` is empty
    (run 8, lane `harness9`: it was `admin stats`' whole-database `hook=0` until a stack where the webhook was once on
    kept its old jobs) — tested inside the container without printing the value — else a SKIP line; (b) a throwaway `STORAGE_BACKEND=fs` app container named from the lane port,
    both hook variables set explicitly, no published port, a busybox `nc -lk -e` receiver on its own loopback (an
    applet the runtime image ships; nothing added to the image) answering 500 then 200 and reading exactly
    Content-Length bytes; (c) a minted token uploads a listed and an unlisted clip; the listed one's job is `done`
    after one failed attempt, the unlisted one's on its first; (d) on the host, `$PY` verifies all three signatures
    over the received bytes (and refuses another key), the nine fields and their values, `unlisted` marked, the retry
    byte-identical, and no token, key, `@`, storage key or path in any body; (e) the boot line, two `delivered` lines,
    the requeue line, no ERROR, no token or key in the log; the doctor's three rows and `17 checks` (sixteen until erratum 321's `backup` row); the URL without
    the secret refuses to boot (exit 2) naming the missing variable. The container is removed by a trap armed before
    it exists.

    *Amended run 8 (lane `nits9`):* a rejection body is read, scrubbed and only then cut, as before, and when the
    read FILLED its window the window's tail is struck too if it is the start of a needle (`scrubWindow`,
    `strikeCutNeedle` in internal/notify) — a receiver that echoes the URL after a run of leading whitespace the trim
    removes, or as the last, cut-off one of several echoes, left that prefix in the snippet; the Notifier had the
    same two gaps and takes the same cure. Pins: `TestHookURLCutAtTheWindowEdgeIsStruck`,
    `TestTokenCutAtTheWindowEdgeIsStruck`. DEPLOY §11.1 says the key is used trimmed of surrounding whitespace.

320. **The upload form: `/upload` answers a modal — Title, Delete after, Tags — while the upload already runs, and
    the link is a follow-up** (run 6 lane `form`, 2026-10-06; ROADMAP #33 "Wish (3)"; the owner's ask of 2026-09-15: while
    the bot shows "thinking", let the person set the title and tags; run 6 decision 3a). The design is the
    reviewed form design.

    **(a) The flow.** With `DISCORD_UPLOAD_FORM=on` (the default; `off` | `on`, anything else a boot error; inert
    without a bot, so no orphan rule; allowed on a managed instance) a bound `/upload` that passes every refusal
    is answered `type 9` — a modal, `custom_id` `cb:form:<32 hex>`, title "Your clip is uploading", four
    components: a Text Display ("Cancel keeps the defaults."), and three Labels — `Title` (a short Text Input,
    `max_length` 200, not required, pre-filled with `defaultTitle(filename)` only when that is at most 200 UTF-16
    code units: a modal Discord rejects would leave the command unanswered and the link undeliverable), `Delete
    after` (a Radio Group: `default · {what this upload gets}` selected — the bound account's TTL default when it
    has a legal one, else `DEFAULT_CLIP_TTL`, the order `applyDefaultsCtx` applies — then `1 day` … `never`) and
    `Tags` (a short Text Input, description "comma separated; a-z, 0-9 and -", `max_length` 329). The job starts
    behind it at once with `ClipJob.Followup` set; nobody waits on the form. (Amended by erratum 325: the job
    also posts a private "Uploading…" while it runs and deletes it at the end — a dismissed form had left the
    person told nothing.) A full table (256 open forms) or
    `off` is the deferral, byte for byte as before (`{"type":5}`), and the full table logs one warn line.

    **(b) Delivery.** After a modal there is no `@original` to edit, so EVERY message a `Followup` job ends in —
    the link, a refusal sentence, the restart sentence and the panic recovery's sentence — goes through ONE
    `deliver()`: `POST /api/v10/webhooks/{app}/{command token}` ("Create Followup Message"), the same body the
    edit sends, public, no Authorization header, the token `PathEscape`d and scrubbed, one retry on the edit's
    retryable set (429, 5xx, 404 — a fast failure can arrive before Discord has processed the modal). The
    deferred path still PATCHes. internal/notify's header lists four calls (six since erratum 325: the redraw's
    PATCH and the `Uploading…` line's DELETE, both on follow-ups this binary posted).

    **(c) The table and the submit.** An in-memory table on the handler, keyed by a 128-bit `crypto/rand` nonce,
    holding the guild, the clip id once the ingest attaches it, a held submit, and two flags; nothing about the
    member and no interaction token. Fifteen minutes (the token's life), swept lazily on every open, lost on a
    restart. The nonce is the credential — Discord shows a modal only to its invoker and the nonce is never in a
    channel or a log — so `member.user.id` is NOT read (the bot still reads nothing about who ran a command); the
    submit must come from the same server. The `cb:form:` MODAL_SUBMIT is routed in `discordPanel` after the
    prefix log field and BEFORE `panelGate` (an uploader needs no Manage Server); a type-3 click on a `cb:form:`
    id is not special and meets the gate. **One submit per form**: the box checks no timestamp window on signed
    bodies, so a submit that passes validation consumes the entry (clip attached → written now; not yet → held,
    and `attach` writes it and removes the entry); a failed entry is answered once and removed; every later
    submit with that id, an unknown or malformed id and another server's are all "That form has expired.".
    Failure reaches the table from notify, not from the ingest wrapper: `ClipJob.Failed` (nil-safe, panic-safe)
    is called by `runClip` on ANY error BEFORE the `/clip failed` line — a refused host, a CDN non-200 and a
    declared size all return before `Ingest` is called — by the panic recovery, and by a job refused during
    shutdown. Validation: title (`cleanText`, 200 runes) and delete-after (the six values) first, a refusal
    applies nothing and keeps the form (both reachable only by a forged body); then tags (`SplitTags` +
    `db.CleanTags`) — bad tags never block the rest: title and delete-after are applied, the tags are left as
    they were, the form is consumed and the answer is a fixed sentence. No answer echoes what was typed (not
    `BadTagError.Error()`, which quotes the tag). The write is `db.UpdateClipMeta`, the web PATCH's writer; a
    delete-after recomputes `expires_at` from now, as PATCH does.

    **(d) The words** (the review's, final): "Saved." (`Changes saved.` since erratum 330) · "Saved without the tags. A tag must be 1-32 characters of a-z,
    0-9 and -, starting with a letter or a digit." · "Saved without the tags. A clip may carry at most 10 tags."
    · "That form has expired." · "That clip could not be uploaded." · "That is not a choice here." · "Not saved: a
    title is at most 200 characters, with no control characters." · "That clip is gone." · "Clippet is not
    available right now."; every one ephemeral. The boot line gains `upload_form=on|off`; `admin doctor`'s `bot`
    check gains one line for each state.

    **(e) Logs.** The access log carries `discord_prefix=cb:form:` and `form=saved|saved_without_tags|expired|
    failed|refused`, never the nonce or a value; the two app-log lines a write failure can produce carry the clip
    id and the error only (`discord bot: upload form not applied`).

    **(f) Authority, stated.** With the form on, whoever may run `/upload` chooses the lifetime of their OWN
    upload, `never` included, although erratum 318 put the account's link defaults behind Manage Server; that is
    the owner's ask, and DEPLOY §30.5/§30.9 say it in plain words; `DISCORD_UPLOAD_FORM=off` restores the account's
    defaults for every upload. No forwarder change (the forwarder relays the box's 2xx JSON unchanged and routes
    every `cb:` id but its own to the box), no re-registration, no migration.

    **(g) Not built** (the review's nits, for a later lane; *2026-10-27: the forwarder's two items — the never-resolving
    public deferral and the deprecated-rule edge — were built in clippet-pass lane `v1-forward` (`settle()`), the double link's box half
    in lane `v2-followup` (below); the amendment of 325 (e) says the same*): the forwarder's row-16 public deferral that never
    resolves for a box slower than 2 s on a submit (pre-existing for `cb:defaults`, now reachable by any
    uploader while the box encodes); the web upload page's `server default · …` has must 5's untruth when an
    account default is set; DEPLOY §30.5's "nothing is ever posted publicly except the clip's message" is untrue
    for a failure after the first answer; a follow-up retried after a lost response can post the link twice; the
    edge where the forwarder's deferral wins relies on Discord's deprecated follow-up-edits-the-loading-message
    rule. **T-form** (the owner's hands, on dev): (a) send the form with a new title →
    the link posts and the card shows it; (b) dismiss → the link posts with the file-name title; (c) send the form
    AFTER the link has posted → "Saved.", and the clip's page shows the new title. (Amended by erratum 325: that
    card is no longer an accepted edge — a late submit that changes the title redraws it, by editing the link to
    `?v=2`; T-form 2 re-tests all three.) If (a)/(b) fail to post, the
    flip to `off` is the one `oneOf` default in internal/config.

    **(g) amended 2026-10-27 (run 23, lane `v2-followup`; the cleanup list's run 23 wave 1 row, REVIEW F3 of the clippet-pass
    gate): "a follow-up retried after a lost response can post the link twice" — the box's half, BUILT.** The
    forwarder's half landed the same day in lane `v1-forward` (clippet-pass `forward/src/forward.ts` `settle()`: one
    message per interaction token on its own paths, a retry edits). The box talks to Discord directly, so its own
    link follow-up is held here: `internal/notify/bot_linkid.go` keeps the LINK follow-up's message id — the `id`
    Discord answers the POST with, read by `messageID()` — per interaction token, keyed by the token's SHA-256 (the
    table never holds the credential), in memory, capped at 1024 entries with the oldest evicted, each gone with the
    token's fifteen minutes (counted from the hold). `followupLink` is the link's way out (`deliver` with a clip id —
    a link owed no redraw and a duplicate's answer — and `deliverLink` on the form path): on a token that already
    holds a link id it PATCHes `webhooks/{app}/{token}/messages/{id}` with the same body (one retry on the retryable
    set, as every edit) and never POSTs again; otherwise it posts and holds the answered id. Only the link is held:
    the ephemeral `Uploading…` (325) and the not-applied line (326) keep their own POST, their own id and their own
    delete, and a failure sentence is never a link. The single POST's retry now tells its failures apart
    (`retryableError.lost`): an HTTP 429, 5xx or 404 means Discord answered and the body did not land — the retry
    posts, as before; a TRANSPORT failure (no answer read — the response may have been lost after Discord stored the
    message) still retries once, because a lost link is worse than a rare duplicate, under its own WARN line
    `discord bot: follow-up response lost; retrying — the link may appear twice` (`clip`, `after`, the scrubbed
    `reason`; never the token) — `… the line may appear twice` for a non-link line — and the retry's id is the one
    held. Discord's webhooks take no idempotency key, so the earlier message cannot be found by key; that one case
    stays a logged, rare duplicate. The paths that could reach a second link follow-up on one token, traced: the
    retry inside the POST (exists — classified as above); a second link after a first on one job (no such path today:
    `runClip` ends in exactly one `deliver`/`deliverLink`; the guard covers any later one); the panic recovery after
    the link (posts nothing and leaves the form's table alone — a link, never a second one, and no sentence under it;
    the amendments below); the redraw (always a PATCH of a held id,
    never a POST); a restart's re-delivery (none: a bot job is a goroutine, never re-queued — erratum 293's attempts
    are the worker's jobs, and the holder is forgotten with the process); a duplicate interaction (the forwarder's
    dedupe belt answers a repeat from its cache and forwards once; a self-hosted endpoint gets one delivery). Pins
    (`internal/notify/bot_linkid_test.go`, each seen failing with its change reverted): a link follow-up on a held
    token is exactly one PATCH of that id with the link's body and no POST; `deliver` then `deliverLink` on one
    token is one POST then one PATCH of the answered id; 503 then 200 is two POSTs and the retry's id held, under the
    ordinary retry line; a hijacked, closed connection is one retry POST under the lost-response line with the clip
    id and no token, the retry's id held; the table's cap (oldest evicted, a re-hold never evicts, a full table of
    expired entries swept) and expiry; the two ephemeral lines POST and hold nothing even with a link id held. The
    erratum 325 pins (`bot_redraw_test.go`) stay green unchanged. No forwarder change, no migration, no
    configuration. (Amended 2026-10-29, lane `prenits`, the cleanup list's run 23 wave 2 row: the panic recovery posts no
    `SentenceFailed` on a token that already holds a link id — the panic came after the link, in the in-job redraw,
    and the sentence would sit under a working link; pinned by `TestBotPanicAfterTheLinkPostsNoSentence`, the
    token with none still by `TestBotFollowupPanicDeliversByPost`. A deferred job whose link is held for a redraw
    holds `@original` as its link id once the reply is the link, so its recovery never edits the sentence over it;
    pinned by `TestBotDeferredPanicAfterTheLinkKeepsTheLink`. Amended again 2026-11-03, lane `failedlink`: on such a
    token the recovery skips `job.Failed` too — the clip exists, so the upload form's table is not told "no clip"
    (a duplicate's entry would otherwise answer a later submit as failed); pinned by the same two tests, the token
    with none by `TestBotPanicBeforeTheLinkTellsTheTable`.)

    **Pins.** internal/config `TestUploadForm`. internal/notify (`bot_followup_test.go`): the link as a POST with no
    Authorization and ClipMessage's body, no PATCH; `Failed` before the failure line on a CDN non-200 with the
    ingest never called; not called on success, nil allowed; one retry on a 404; the panic delivered by POST and
    `Failed` called; the interaction token scrubbed; the restart sentence a follow-up. internal/httpapi
    (`discord_form_test.go`): the modal golden; the `default ·` label from the instance default, a 7-day and a
    1-day account default; the pre-fill omitted at 150 emoji (300 UTF-16 units) and kept at 200 ASCII; `off` and a
    full table `{"type":5}` with a deferred job; submit-before-attach and attach-before-submit each written once,
    the second submit expired; `default` keeps the lifetime; a failed entry answered once then expired, a held
    submit dropped by a failure; bad tags and eleven tags keep the rest and echo nothing; five forged refusals
    write nothing and keep the form; unknown, malformed, empty and another server's ids expired without consuming
    it; unbound and DM keep their lines; an ordinary member's submit served, `cb:defaults` and a click on a
    `cb:form:` id still gated; a deleted clip; the logs carry no nonce or value; the table's 15-minute edge and its
    sweep; attach racing submit 500 times, written exactly once (under `-race`); and two whole paths through a
    real `notify.Bot` against httptest Discord + CDN — a CDN 403 posts the failure as a follow-up and the submit
    answers the failed sentence, then expired; a successful fetch posts the link and the clip carries the form's
    title, delete-after and tags. E2E step 98 (`98-form.sh`, parallel): a `--network none` probe of the app's
    image (fs storage, no compose volumes) answers the modal, the failed sentence once, then expired, an unknown
    id expired, the panel gated, the failure as a follow-up, nothing typed on the log, doctor's line; a second
    probe with `off` answers `{"type":5}`.

321. **Timed backups of the database, OFF by default and enabled nowhere** (lane `backup`, run 6, 2026-10-06;
    ROADMAP #40 item 4; the reviewed backup design). The owner's call: built, not enabled yet — no backups
    of any server while iterating.

    **(a) Off, and enabled nowhere.** Three variables: `BACKUP_EVERY` (a Go duration, 10 s at least, no ceiling),
    `BACKUP_DIR` (a container path) and `BACKUP_KEEP` (default 30, at least 1). ON only when the first two are both
    set (`Config.BackupOn`); one without the other is a boot error naming the missing one — a backup that is half
    configured and silently does nothing is the worst state it can be in. `BACKUP_KEEP` is read ONLY when both are
    set, so commenting out the pair never turns the third line into a boot error. `BACKUP_DIR` takes
    `STORAGE_DIR`'s three shape sentences (absolute, clean, not `/`; the shape check is now one helper, `absDir`,
    with STORAGE_DIR's messages unchanged) and may not equal, sit inside or contain `SCRATCH_DIR` (the janitor
    removes things there) or `STORAGE_DIR` (the drop watcher ingests its root), with sentences of its own; `DATA_DIR`
    itself or a child of it is allowed (rotation touches minted names only, and `clippet.db` is not one). The only
    files outside Go, tests, docs and bundle 99 that name the variables are `compose.yaml` (three rows, each
    `${VAR:-}`) and `.env.example` (three COMMENTED lines). No overlay, no `/setup` change, nothing in clippet-pass.

    **(b) The verb's code, not a second implementation.** `cmd/clippet/backup_schedule.go` runs ONE goroutine,
    started beside the served-bytes loop right after the listener — not in the storage-gated chain, because a
    database snapshot needs no bucket. A run calls `(*admin).backupInto(BACKUP_DIR, BACKUP_KEEP)` — the code of
    `admin backup <dir> --rotate N` (erratum 149): the minted name, `VACUUM INTO` a `.part-` file, 0600 before the
    rename (erratum 96), rotation that only considers minted names. `backupInto` now also returns a
    `backupOutcome{File, Bytes, Kept, Removed, StaleParts, RemoveErrs}`; the verb ignores it and prints exactly
    what it printed. The loop never calls the verb's front door `backup(args)` (a missing path there is a FILE
    destination) and never creates `BACKUP_DIR` (an unmounted volume fails loudly instead of filling the container
    layer): a `BACKUP_DIR` that does not stat as a directory is a failed run.

    **(c) When.** The directory is read for scheduling ONLY at boot: the anchor is the newest minted name whose time
    is not after now (a name in the future — a clock once wrong, a copied-in file — is ignored, so it cannot stall
    the schedule); no anchor, or anchor + `BACKUP_EVERY` already past, runs at once, else the first run is one
    interval after the anchor, so a restart never resets the clock. After EVERY run — written, skipped or failed —
    the next is that run's start + `BACKUP_EVERY`: one rule, no retry storm. Runs are strictly sequential.

    **(d) The skip, and why it never replaces the last result.** A run is skipped when `BACKUP_DIR` holds a `partRE`
    file younger than `stalePartAge` (an hour): by the verb's own rule a run may still be writing it — a manual
    `admin backup` into the same directory — or it is what a failed run left (the verb leaves the `.part-` behind
    on a failed VACUUM, DEPLOY §15.5). Because of the second case a skip never replaces the last real result: it
    logs one line and moves the next run (the status file's `next` included), and `last.result` is `ok` or
    `failed` only — else a full-disk failure would read `ok` in doctor one interval later. The rule also
    rate-limits a persistently failing target to one attempt an hour; the stale part is removed by the next run
    that gets through.

    **(e) One log line per run.** INFO `backup scheduled` (`every dir keep next`) at boot; then per run INFO
    `backup written` (`file bytes kept removed took next`), INFO `backup skipped` (`reason next`) or ERROR
    `backup failed` (`err next`, plus `file` when the snapshot itself was written). The reason is the verb's own
    last STDERR line, verbatim — never the last combined line, which after a rotation removal failure is the
    `rotate:` summary — except two fixed sentences: `BACKUP_DIR <dir> is not a directory`, and `the snapshot was
    written, but N older file(s) could not be removed` (result failed, file and bytes still recorded).

    **(f) Bounded and contained.** Each run gets `context.WithTimeout(loopCtx, adminTimeout)`, the verb's own ten
    minutes, because `db.Backup` runs on the rw pool's single connection; a panic inside a run is recovered and
    recorded as a failed run (`panic: <value>`), and the loop goes on. Verified by test: a cancel interrupts a
    VACUUM in flight (a ≈200 MiB database: 488 ms uncancelled, 27 ms to `context canceled` when cancelled at
    20 ms). Shutdown awaits the loop under the SAME single 5 s deadline as the sweeper chain (one deadline, not
    5 + 5), before the served-bytes flush and `database.Close()`, with its own WARN `backup did not stop within
    budget`; nothing is written after cancel.

    **(g) The status file.** `DATA_DIR/backup-status.json`, 0600, tmp + rename, exactly
    `{"dir","last":{"at","result","file","bytes","reason"},"next"}` (RFC 3339 UTC; `file` the full path; `last`
    absent until a run has happened). Not in `BACKUP_DIR`: it would count in rotation's `untouched=`, and the
    backup directory may be the thing that is broken. At boot the existing file's `last` is carried over when its
    `dir` is this `BACKUP_DIR`, else dropped. An unreadable or malformed file is absent, to the loop and to doctor.
    A failed write is one WARN `backup status not written` and never fails or repeats the run.

    **(h) `admin doctor`'s `backup` row** (after `repair`; 17 checks). Off: one ok line, in every run, like every
    feature row. On: the settings; a `BACKUP_DIR` that is not a directory is a FAIL that ends the row; else the last
    run (`ok`, or `failed` at warn with the reason through `safe()`) or `no run recorded yet`, then `next:` — `next:
    was due …` when that time is past. Doctor never lists the directory for it. *Amended run 8 (lane `nits9`):* it
    write-probes `BACKUP_DIR` — one empty dotted temp file, removed at once; a failure is a FAIL `… cannot be
    written to: every run fails until it can (<reason>)` that ends the row — and writes nothing else.

    **(i) The known cost.** The snapshot holds the rw connection while it is written: milliseconds for a metadata
    database on a local disk, as long as the mount hangs on one that hangs (DEPLOY §15.6 says so).

    **(j) Not built, on purpose.** Media (the brief). `BACKUP_DIR` takes POSIX paths only, so the native Windows
    server (the desktop app) cannot turn timed backups on. A crash mid-snapshot leaves its `.part-` file: a run in
    the hour after it is skipped. No cross-process lock, no off-box copy, no restore automation (§15.4).
    *Amended run 8 (lane `nits9`):* a skipped run is retried after `min(BACKUP_EVERY, 1h)` — when the part that
    caused it turns stale — not a whole interval on, so a restart inside that hour costs an hour, not a day; a run a
    clean SIGTERM cancels logs `backup cancelled` at INFO (never `backup failed` at ERROR), its own `.part-` is
    removed by the verb (`writeSnapshot` removes it when its context was cancelled), and the status keeps the last
    real result; serve.go asks the stopped loop first, so an overrun sweeper chain no longer makes a false `backup
    did not stop within budget` WARN half the time; `TestBackupCancelInterruptsVacuum` builds 32 MiB, not 200.
    Pins: `TestBackupSkipRetriesWithinTheHour`, `TestBackupCancelledRunIsNotAFailure`, the verb half in
    `TestBackupCancelInterruptsVacuum`, doctor's `/proc` row in `TestDoctorBackup`.

    **Pins.** internal/config: off by default, `BACKUP_KEEP` alone accepted and unused, both half-pairs, the floor,
    malformed and non-positive durations, keep ≥ 1, the three shape sentences, equal/inside/containing both
    SCRATCH_DIR and STORAGE_DIR, `/data` and a `DATA_DIR` inside it accepted, STORAGE_DIR's sentences unchanged.
    cmd/clippet: the boot anchor (missing/empty dir, old, young, future-named), three runs at keep=2 (two files,
    decoy kept, 0600, both restore, one record per run with its fields, the status shape and mode), a restart
    carrying the result and the clock, a missing dir (failed, nothing created, the reason), a skip after a failure
    (one record, nothing written, `last` still failed, `next` moved; the stale part then removed), the verb's
    stderr line, a recovered panic, the reason wording, the loop stopping on cancel, the VACUUM interrupt; doctor:
    off, on + missing dir FAIL ending the row, no status, ok, failed warn with redaction and `was due`, another
    dir's record and a malformed file. E2E step 99 (`99-backup`): the stack's own doctor prints the off line; a
    `--rm` probe (private DATA_DIR/SCRATCH_DIR, S3_ENDPOINT on a closed port) shows the half-pair refusal, `no run
    recorded yet`, three written runs within 40 s, two snapshots plus the decoy at 0600 that both restore, a skip
    beside a fresh `.part-`, doctor's last `ok` and `next:` after it, and a clean SIGTERM.
    *Amended 2026-10-19 (lane `snapshot`, erratum 343):* the copy this erratum's verb makes is now also the copy that
    follows the clips into the bucket — `writeSnapshot` into SCRATCH_DIR, then `PutFile` to `{P}_clippet/db.sqlite` —
    ON by default on `s3`, independent of these three variables, with `admin restore --from-store` as the automated
    restore (j) said did not exist; `writeBackupStatus` became `writeJSONAtomic`, shared with the snapshot's status file.
    (k) *Amended 2026-10-27 (run 23 lane `v1-owner`; D-security row 10, the cleanup list's privacy-class `[backup]` row):*
    the `.part-` file is CREATED 0600 — `os.OpenFile(O_CREATE|O_EXCL, 0600)`, empty — before `VACUUM INTO` writes it
    (SQLite writes into an existing EMPTY file and opens rather than creates it; `db.Backup` now accepts dst when it
    is an empty regular file and still refuses one with a byte in it), and the chmod after the vacuum is gone: until
    now SQLite made the file at the process umask (0644 in the image) and erratum 96's chmod ran only after a
    SUCCESSFUL vacuum, so the file holding every password and token hash was world-readable for the whole write and
    after any failure. And EVERY failure of the vacuum removes the part, not only a cancel (b, d and j said a failed
    VACUUM leaves it): only a process killed mid-write still strands one, 0600 from its first byte, which (d)'s
    skip and rotation still handle. The bucket snapshot (343) goes through the same `writeSnapshot`. Pin:
    cmd/clippet `TestBackupPartIsPrivateFromCreationAndGoneOnFailure` (the part exists, empty, 0600 when the vacuum
    starts — the test seam `admin.beforeVacuum`, nil in production; a byte written into it makes the vacuum fail with
    an error that is not a cancel, and nothing is left) — seen failing with each half reverted.
    **Amended by erratum 348 (a) (2026-10-27):** timed backups stay off by default, but they are no longer the only
    backup a folder home can have — the database snapshot is on by default on `fs` too — and `admin doctor`'s
    `snapshot` row WARNs when both are off. `BACKUP_DIR` still may not overlap `STORAGE_DIR`.

322. **The inbound URL: `POST /in/{token}` drops a clip on the box** (lane `inhook`, run 6, 2026-10-06; ROADMAP #54
    pick 5; the reviewed inbound-URL design). Free and on every instance;
    a Pass only makes the box reachable.

    **(a) The credential.** An `api_tokens` row holding the scope `inbound` ALONE, raw value `ci_` + 43 base64url
    (32 random bytes, `ids.InboundToken`; `ids.IsInboundToken` is the shape), stored as its sha256 like a capture
    token, display prefix the 8 characters after `ci_`. No migration: revoke (`/settings`, `admin tokens revoke`),
    `last_used_at`, the list and the cascade on account delete are the table's. `auth.ScopeInbound` is a separate
    constant: `auth.Scopes` stays `[upload, read]` and `ValidScope("inbound")` is false. `CleanScopes` recognises the
    set {inbound} (duplicates collapsed) BEFORE its general loop and returns `[inbound]`; `inbound` beside anything
    else falls through to the loop and is the 400 `scopes must be a non-empty subset of upload, read; or inbound
    alone` (`httpapi.ScopesRule`, also the CLI's refusal). Both mint doors call ONE helper, `httpapi.NewTokenValue`,
    which picks `ci_` iff the cleaned set is `[inbound]` and builds the URL with `urls.Builder.Inbound` from
    PUBLIC_BASE_URL — never from a request's Host. `POST /api/auth/tokens` answers it with `token` (the `ci_` value),
    a new `url` field (absent for every other token) and `sxcu: null`; `admin tokens mint --scopes inbound` prints
    the URL alone on stdout, `ci_<prefix>…` on stderr and in `tokens list`, and refuses `--sxcu` with the existing
    sentence.

    **(b) It can do nothing else.** The Resolver never sees it (`bearerToken` admits only `ck_`; the hash covers the
    prefix) and `resolveToken` treats a row holding `inbound` as not found. The route is NOT under the Resolver: no
    cookie and no Authorization header is read, and there is no CSRF check (no browser credential is in play). The
    principal it installs FAILS CLOSED: `Principal{User, Via: ViaToken, TokenID, Scopes: [inbound]}` — no new `Via`
    value, because `HasScope`, `OwnerReader` and `RequireSession` treat anything that is not `ViaToken` as a browser
    session; this one gets 403 from `RequireSession`, `RequireScope(upload|read)` and `RequireSessionOrScope`, and
    `OwnerReader` is false (auth test).

    **(c) The route.** `serve.go` mounts `/in/` on the API handler; `router.go` registers the SPELLED path (the
    guard's route diff reads literals): `/in/{token}` → POST only → `h.inboundCredential(noRoute,
    closeUnlessRead(chain(h.inbound, uploadRate, uploadIPRate)))`. The credential check is OUTERMOST: shape (no
    database read for a value of the wrong shape) → `GetTokenByHash` → live and scopes exactly `[inbound]`, else
    `noRoute` — the very handler value the API's `/` catch-all is registered with, so a miss is `POST /api/nope`
    byte for byte (status, every header, body; a Go test diffs them with a small body, a declared length past the
    close threshold and a chunked one — a miss carries no `Connection: close`, because closeUnlessRead has not run).
    A database error is the usual 503. `h.inbound` writes `last_used_at` FIRST (after both limiters, so a holder of
    a leaked URL already answered 429 buys no write) and then runs `h.capture` — the capture route's whole body
    minus its 201, extracted from `captureUpload` so the two cannot drift — and answers 201 `text/plain;
    charset=utf-8` with the share URL and `\n`, or, when `Accept` NAMES `application/json`, `/api/upload`'s
    UploadDTO. Every refusal past the credential (400/413/415/429/503/507) is `/api/upload`'s JSON envelope. Files
    only: there is no field that makes the server fetch an address. `in` joins `ids.Reserved`
    (`TestEveryAPISegmentIsReserved`), which changes the release manifest's `reserved` list.

    **(d) Rate limits — "per token AND per address".** The account's `uploadRate` bucket (`u:<user id>`) and
    `uploadIPRate`, both AFTER the credential. The account bucket IS the per-token limit the brief asks for: it
    bounds every URL and token of that account together, so a URL can never buy more than its account has; a
    per-token bucket would either give each URL its own extra budget or need a new limiter (the owner's no-new-limiter
    rule). A miss costs one sha256 and one indexed read, the cost of `GET /{id}`.

    **(e) The secret never reaches a log.** `httpx.LogPath` is the one spelling of a request path in a log line: the
    CLEANED path `/in` or under `/in/` is `/in/{token}`; otherwise every run of `ci_` + 43 or more of `[A-Za-z0-9_-]` (at least 43 since run 8: an exact count let a crafted `ci_<40>ci_<43>` leave the real body)
    anywhere in the path is `{token}`. It does not depend on reaching the handler: AccessLog wraps the ROOT mux,
    which answers `//in/ci_…` with its own redirect before any handler, and `/IN/ci_…` or `/api/in/ci_…` reach other
    handlers. AccessLog, Recover and `web.renderFailure` use it; a pin test refuses a non-test line naming
    `URL.Path` beside a `"path"` key without it. The access line carries `inbound=<row id>` (not a secret). A
    reverse proxy's own access log and cloudflared at `--loglevel debug` are outside the process: DEPLOY §9 says so.
    Referer: the route renders nothing and links nothing.

    **(f) The page.** `/settings` → API tokens: a `Kind` row FIRST in the mint form (`.seg`, `Token` · `Inbound
    URL`), its hint showing both shapes on the configured host (erratum 264); `Inbound URL` hides the scopes row,
    posts `scopes: ["inbound"]`, and switches the Name placeholder, the button and the shown-once line (the words
    live in the template as `data-` attributes beside the words they replace); the whole URL is shown in the
    existing `<code data-new-token-value>`; `form.reset()` returns the form to Token. The list shows `ci_<prefix>…`
    for a row whose scopes are `inbound`. No CSS change.

    **(g) The guard (clippet-pass `guard/`).** The row `{ m: "POST", p: "/in/{token}", c: "upload" }` with
    `{token}` = `^ci_[A-Za-z0-9_-]{43}$`; on that route ONLY, any upstream 404 is answered with the guard's own 404
    page, outcome `offroute`, body drained, nothing reported — an older box answers the route with its HTML 404
    (otherwise a stranger-raisable `type` violation), and a wrong token on a Pass name answers like an off-route
    path there. `guard/wrangler.toml` turns the platform's invocation logs off (`[observability.logs]
    invocation_logs = false`): their message is `<Method> <URL>`, which held every request URL — unlisted clip links
    included — so the old "never logs a path" comment was untrue. Whether the guard's own `{name, outcome, ms}` line
    still carries the request URL in stored metadata is UNPROVEN until a deployed probe: no document may claim a
    Pass name keeps no inbound URL in logs. The guard's supported-manifest route diff fails until the release that
    ships this route builds its own manifest (`scripts/release.sh`); until the guard deploys, a Pass name 404s `/in/`.

    **Pins.** internal/ids (shape, length, refusals); internal/auth (the principal fails closed; the Resolver refuses
    an inbound row by Bearer and by hash; `TokenPrefixOf` both prefixes); internal/httpx (LogPath's table; AccessLog
    and Recover through a real mux for `/in/ci_…`, `//in/ci_…`, `/in/ci_…/x`, `/IN/ci_…`, `/x/ci_…`; the logged-path
    pin); internal/httpapi (`CleanScopes`; the mint's `url` from PUBLIC_BASE_URL under a hostile Host; the miss
    matrix — malformed, too long, unknown, revoked, `ck_` upload and read tokens, a deleted account's row, a mixed
    row, a `ck_` with an inbound body, percent-encoded — byte-equal to `POST /api/nope` for three body framings, with
    a cookie and a Bearer riding along; the text and JSON hits; the 429 after the credential writing nothing; the
    507; the access line); cmd/clippet (`tokens mint --scopes inbound`, its refusals, `tokens list`); internal/web
    (the Kind row first, the hint, the `ci_` row). E2E step 100 (`100-inhook.sh`, parallel).

    *Amended run 8 (lane `nits9`):* the redaction's count is `{43,}` (e) and the root mux's answer is "its own
    redirect" (Go 1.27 sends 307); `acceptsJSON` reads `application/json;q=0` as not JSON; `ScopesRule` and the
    `--scopes` flag help are built from `auth.Scopes`; the two set tests are `auth.IsInboundSet` and
    `auth.IsAutoFetchSet`, which the mint door, the admin verb and the settings page's `tokenLead` all call
    (app.js keeps its own `tokenLead`). Pins: `TestLogPath`'s crafted row, `TestAcceptsJSON`,
    `TestScopesRuleWording` (the wording; the derivation is a refactor with no revert-proof).

323. **Enrich takes a video attachment: with no link to a clip here in the picked message, its first video is
    uploaded through `/upload`'s own path — for the message's poster or a member who may manage the server**
    (lane `enrichvid`, run 6, 2026-10-06; the other half of the owner's pick (4): attachment rescue off by default, and
    through an independent bot so the permissions are not conflated: the second app `Clippet Auto` (clippet-pass
    `rescue/`) only replies "use Apps → Enrich on the video", and Enrich — the official bot's message command,
    erratum 315 — does the work on the box). The design note is in the run's records. Amends 315's
    addendum (Enrich read the text alone) and 320(c)'s "the bot still reads nothing about who ran a command".

    **(0) The switch, OFF by default.** `DISCORD_ENRICH_UPLOAD` = `on` | `off`, default `off`, parsed exactly as
    `DISCORD_UPLOAD_FORM` (any case, empty = the default, anything else a boot error naming the variable, inert
    without a bot, allowed on a managed instance; `Config.EnrichUpload`). Off, `discordEnrich` is byte for byte what
    it was before this erratum: a message with a video and no link of ours gets the no-link line, its attachments
    and both ids are not looked at, nothing is fetched and no `enrich=`/`not_poster` field is logged. Everything
    below is the `on` state. Why off: the owner asked for the feature as a setting that is off by
    default, and Enrich has its own row under Discord's Server Settings → Integrations — a server that limited
    `/upload` to a role would otherwise, on upgrade, silently let every member upload through Enrich. compose.yaml
    passes it (`${DISCORD_ENRICH_UPLOAD:-off}`), `.env.example` carries it commented, DEPLOY's table and §30.2 list
    it; the boot line gains `enrich_upload=on|off`; `admin doctor`'s `bot` check gains one line after the form's
    (the reviewed wording): "enrich upload: on - Enrich on a message with a video uploads it, for its poster or Manage
    Server; DISCORD_ENRICH_UPLOAD=off stops it" / "enrich upload: off - Enrich answers links only;
    DISCORD_ENRICH_UPLOAD=on lets it upload a video", the command's configured name in place of `Enrich`.

    **(a) Order.** `discordEnrich` reads the text first, unchanged: a live clip of ours is posted, a tombstone is
    "That clip is gone.", and either way nothing is uploaded. Only when no link names a row here is the message's
    FIRST attachment with a URL that reads as a video (`isVideo`: `/upload`'s own `ContentTypeFor(content_type,
    SanitizeExt(filename))` → `video/…`) taken; later videos are ignored, images and files skipped. No video →
    today's "No link to a clip on this Clippet in that message.", unchanged.

    **(b) Who may**, on the box, from the signed body alone (`mayEnrichUpload`): `hasManagePermission(member)`
    (erratum 318's proof A, reused: ADMINISTRATOR | MANAGE_GUILD), or `member.user.id` non-empty and equal to the
    message's `author.id`. Anybody else: ephemeral "That video is not yours. You need Manage Server here.",
    `reject=not_poster`, no job — so nothing is fetched. Decided before the size check, so a stranger learns
    nothing about the file. On top of Discord's per-command permissions — which for Enrich are its own row, not
    `/upload`'s (DEPLOY §30.4 says so to the operator).

    **(c) One path.** `discordUpload`'s tail is now `startUpload(…, att, form bool)`: the not-a-video and too-large
    refusals, `Bot == nil`, the form (erratum 320) only when `form`, then `{"type":5}` and the `ClipJob` with the
    bound account's `botIngest`. `/upload` and the old `/clip file:` pass `form=true`; Enrich passes `false` — the
    person picked a message and asked for a link — so its clip takes the file name as title and the account's
    defaults, exactly `/upload` with `DISCORD_UPLOAD_FORM=off`, and its message is the edit of the deferred reply
    (erratum 316's bare link). No second fetcher and no second allowlist: a non-CDN URL is refused by
    `notify.fetchAndIngest`'s `ValidAttachmentURL` before a socket, the edit saying `SentenceFetch`, as for
    `/upload`. A managed instance needs nothing more (the edit is on the interaction token; the forwarder relays a
    type-2 body's bytes and the answer unchanged, I4/I5).

    **(d) Privacy.** `discordMessage` now parses `content`, `author.id` and `attachments`; `discordMember` adds
    `user.id`. The two ids are compared and dropped — never stored, never logged; of the attachments only what
    `/upload` keeps of its own is kept (the clip, its title from the file name). The access log gains the outcome
    word `enrich=upload` — set only once `startUpload` reports the job handed over, so a refused upload carries
    its own `reject=` alone — or `reject=not_poster`; the app log's job lines are `/upload`'s. DEPLOY §30.4/§30.5/§30.6
    and API.md's interactions body and rows say so.

    **(e) Not built.** A reply threaded under the picked message (an interaction answer has no
    `message_reference`); more than one video per Enrich; anything in clippet-pass; a migration. A box on
    an older build answers a video Enrich with the no-link line.

    **Pins.** internal/config `TestEnrichUpload` (off by default, on/off in any case, empty = off, four bad values
    refused naming the variable). internal/httpapi `discord_enrich_test.go`: with the switch as config.Load leaves
    it (off), the poster's, a stranger's and a manager's Enrich on a video → the no-link line, no job, `reject=no_link`
    and no `enrich=`/`not_poster`, a link still answered; every test below runs with it on. A too-large Enrich upload
    logs `reject=too_large` and not `enrich=upload`. The poster defers one job carrying the attachment, the
    token and the bound account's ingest, never a form even with the form on, and the ingested clip is the bound
    account's, titled by the file name; a manager (Manage Server, Administrator, both) on another's video, and a
    manager with no user; a stranger, no user, no author, two EMPTY ids, no permissions, no member, a stranger on an
    oversized file → the refusal and no job; a link wins over a video (and a tombstone), links naming nothing here
    do not; the first video after an image and a URL-less one, a video typed by extension, image/text/nothing →
    the no-link line, a stranger on an image → the no-link line; too large, unbound, no bot; managed; the access log
    carries the outcome and no id, URL, text, name or file name; through a REAL `notify.Bot` with httptest Discord +
    CDN, the whole path (one CDN fetch, the PATCH of `@original` with the bare link, no POST, the clip the bound
    account's) and serve's own `ValidAttachmentURL` refusing the stub's own http URL with zero CDN hits, a stranger
    reaching neither half. Each rule proved by revert-and-rerun. E2E step 85 (`85-bot.sh` (l)): a `--network none`
    probe of the app's image with `DISCORD_ENRICH_UPLOAD` unset first — the poster's Enrich on a video is the no-link
    line and starts no job — then the same probe re-created with `DISCORD_ENRICH_UPLOAD=on`: the poster's and a manager's Enrich on a video deferred (a job each), a stranger's
    refused with no job, a link beside a video answered with the link and no job, an off-CDN video deferred and
    refused by the allowlist; exactly three jobs; no member or author id on the log.

324. **The Clippet Auto URL: `POST /in/auto/{token}` makes the box fetch ONE Discord attachment into the URL's
    account — one press in Discord, and no video byte through a Worker** (lane `onepress`, run 7, 2026-10-06;
    the owner's pick: Auto does 1b. The design is the reviewed one-press design in the records,
    the review winning where they differ). Free and on
    every instance; nothing is configured — a box with no such row answers every `/in/auto/…` like a missing
    route. The other half (the Clippet Auto row's three modes, the sealed URL, the press) is clippet-pass.

    **(a) The credential: erratum 322's, with its own shape and scope.** An `api_tokens` row holding the scope
    `autofetch` ALONE, raw value `ca_` + 43 base64url (`ids.AutoFetchToken`/`IsAutoFetchToken`; the two path
    secrets share `pathSecret`/`isPathSecret`), stored as its sha256, display prefix the 8 characters after
    `ca_` (`auth.TokenPrefixOf` knows all three prefixes). No migration. `auth.ScopeAutoFetch` is outside
    `auth.Scopes`; `resolveToken` treats a row holding `inbound` OR `autofetch` — alone or beside anything — as
    not found (`pathScoped`). `CleanScopes` recognises {autofetch} as it recognises {inbound} (`onlyScope`); a
    mixed set is the 400 `ScopesRule`, now "scopes must be a non-empty subset of upload, read; or inbound alone;
    or autofetch alone" (the CLI prefixes it as before). `NewTokenValue` picks `ca_` and builds the URL with
    `urls.Builder.AutoFetch` (PUBLIC_BASE_URL + `/in/auto/` + the secret); `POST /api/auth/tokens` answers it in
    `url`, `sxcu: null`; `admin tokens mint --scopes autofetch` prints the URL alone on stdout and inbound's
    stderr line with `ca_<prefix>…` and `scopes=autofetch`, and refuses `--sxcu` with the existing sentence.

    **(b) One credential check for both routes.** `inboundCredential` BECAME `scopedCredential(shape, scope,
    miss, next)`: the shape, `GetTokenByHash`, and the set test EXACT (`isOnly`: one element, that scope), else
    `noRoute`. `router.go` registers the spelled path `/in/auto/{token}` → POST only →
    `h.scopedCredential(ids.IsAutoFetchToken, auth.ScopeAutoFetch, noRoute, closeUnlessRead(chain(h.autofetch,
    uploadRate, uploadIPRate)))`, beside `/in/{token}` which now calls the same function with the inbound pair.
    So a `ci_` value on `/in/auto/`, a `ca_` value on `/in/`, a revoked or unknown one and a hand-written row
    holding either path scope beside another are each `POST /api/nope` byte for byte; GET/HEAD are the route's
    one 405 for every value. The access field is named by the scope (`autofetch=<row id>`). `in` was already in
    `ids.Reserved`; two segments under `/in/` collide with neither `/in/{token}` nor a share id.

    **(c) The instruction, and the order.** Body ≤ 4 KiB, JSON only, unknown fields refused, nothing trailing:
    `{"guild_id","url","filename","content_type","size"}` — guild a 17–20 digit snowflake, url 1–2048 bytes,
    filename 1–255 bytes, content type ≤ 127 (may be empty), size ≥ 1, no control characters. After the limiters (the ONLY charge:
    `attachmentIngest(userID, charge=false, …)` never spends the account's bucket a second time —
    `botIngestWith` is the same body with `charge=true`): 415 `unsupported_media_type` → 413 `too_large` (the
    body) → 400 `invalid_request` "instruction must be JSON: guild_id, url, filename, content_type, size" → 400
    `attachment_host` "url is not a Discord attachment" → 403 `not_bound` "that server is not connected to this
    account" → 415 `not_video` "that file is not a video" → 413 `too_large` (`/api/upload`'s own message, the
    declared size) → 503 `unavailable` "Discord is not configured on this instance" (no bot). **Attachments
    only:** `attachment_host` is config's shared `ValidAttachmentURL` (https, no userinfo, the two CDN hosts
    exactly, ASCII only — a host byte ≥ 0x80 is refused BEFORE the case fold, because `strings.ToLower` is
    Unicode and U+0130, raw or `%C4%B0`, folds to an ASCII `i` while net/http dials the IDNA form, a different
    domain (the fix pass, measured by the box review); its path rule untouched, because `/upload` legitimately
    sees other paths) AND, here only, the escaped path
    `^/attachments/[0-9]{17,20}/[0-9]{17,20}/[^/]{1,512}$` whose last segment is not `.`/`..` in any spelling:
    the URL is chosen by whoever holds the credential, not signed by Discord, and the two hosts also serve
    avatars, icons and stickers. No socket is opened before it. `not_bound` is ONE answer whether the server is
    unbound or bound to another account (`GuildBinding` → `UserID` = the token's user). Then `last_used_at`.

    **(d) The job: the one fetcher.** `notify.Bot.Fetch(Attachment, Ingest) (<-chan FetchOutcome, error)` — the
    `DiscordBot` interface's second method — runs `fetchAndIngest` (allowlist, declared-size refusal,
    no-redirect client, the stream capped) with no interaction, in a goroutine counted in the Bot's WaitGroup
    under the lock Shutdown closes with, under the Bot's own context and job budget — never the request's — and
    its outcome channel is buffered 1, so a job outliving its request never blocks; a panic is recovered as
    `Clip`'s; once Shutdown has begun it is `ErrClosed` (503 `unavailable` "the instance is restarting; retry
    shortly"). A client already gone when the request arrives starts nothing because the credential's and the
    binding's database reads run on its context and refuse; the handler has no check of its own. The handler
    returns on the first of: the outcome; the
    hold, `Deps.AutoFetchBudget` (100 s, under a proxy's 125 s read timeout) → 202 exactly `{"state":"working"}`,
    the job carrying on into the library; the client hanging up. The card wait inside the ingest is the capture
    wait cut to what is left of the hold. 201 is ALWAYS `/api/upload`'s `UploadDTO` as JSON (no text mode, no
    `Accept` negotiation). Failures by the sentence the fetcher or the ingest chose: fetch → 502 `fetch` "the
    attachment could not be fetched from Discord"; too large → 413; not a video → 415 `not_video`; scratch → 507
    `insufficient_scratch` "not enough scratch space for this upload" (`/api/upload`'s words); (busy cannot
    occur: with `charge=false` the ingest never spends the bucket); quota → 507 `storage_quota`; cancelled → 503; else 500
    `failed` "the upload failed".

    **(e) Logs.** No line on this path carries the URL (a signed CDN link is a bearer link to the file), the file
    name or the guild id: the access line has `/in/{token}`, `autofetch=<row id>`, `auto=upload` once the job
    started, and `reject=`/`clip=`; `Fetch`'s job lines — success, failure and panic — carry `autofetch=<row id>`,
    the clip id, a closed outcome word (`ok|fetch|too_large|not_video|busy|full|quota|timeout|restart|failed|panic`)
    and the duration, never an error's text. `httpx.LogPath` rule 1 already writes `/in/auto/…` as `/in/{token}`;
    rule 2's expression is `c[ia]_` + 43 and its short-cut tests BOTH prefixes, so `/IN/AUTO/ca_…` and
    `/x/ca_…` are scrubbed too.

    **(f) The page.** The Kind control gains a third option, `Clippet Auto URL`, and the hint a third part
    (`· Clippet Auto URL: <code>{host}/in/auto/ca_…</code>`), drawn ONLY on an instance that answers the
    official bot (`DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN=managed`; `settingsPage.AutoFetch`) — Clippet Auto reaches a box only
    through the official bot's `/settings`. Not tiering: the official bot is free for every instance, and the
    API and the shell mint the URL anywhere. Its words live in the template (`data-placeholder-autofetch`
    "Discord server", `data-label-autofetch` "Create URL", `data-once-autofetch`); `app.js` posts
    `scopes: [kind]`, hides the scopes row for either path kind, shows the URL whole, and lists `ca_<prefix>…`
    (`rowLead`). No CSS change.

    **(g) Not built.** A box-side switch (no minted URL = off); a probe of the URL at save; any call from the box
    to Discord's API on this path; more than one attachment per instruction; box-side dedupe by attachment id.
    **The guard** (clippet-pass, release cycle 3 — not this lane's): the row `{ m: "POST", p: "/in/auto/{atoken}",
    c: "upload" }` with `{atoken}` = `^ca_[A-Za-z0-9_-]{43}$`, erratum 322 (g)'s upstream-404 rule extended to it,
    and the platform's invocation logs and traces OFF before either `/in/` row ships (a fetch's log message is
    `<Method> <URL>`); a manifest built before this release lacks the row, so a Pass name 404s `/in/auto/` until
    the release that ships it.

    **Pins.** internal/ids `TestAutoFetchToken`; internal/auth (the principal fails closed; Bearer `ca_…` and
    rows holding `autofetch` alone or beside upload/read/inbound are not found; `TokenPrefixOf`); internal/httpx
    `TestLogPathAutoFetch`; internal/notify `bot_fetch_test.go` (fetch → ingest → outcome with no API call; the
    failure word; an unread outcome never blocks; Shutdown waits for a running Fetch and the job sees the Bot's
    context; `ErrClosed`; a panic recovered; no URL, file name or panic value on any line); internal/httpapi
    `autofetch_test.go` (`CleanScopes`; the mint's `url` under a hostile Host; the miss matrix on BOTH routes for
    three body framings with a cookie and a Bearer riding along; Bearer `ca_` → 401; GET/HEAD alike for every
    value; every refusal in order with zero fetches, the pairs answered by the earlier rule, the media host's
    attachment path accepted; through a REAL `notify.Bot` with an httptest CDN: the 201 (one hit, the clip the
    URL's account's, titled by the file name, JSON whatever `Accept` says, `last_used_at`, the access line);
    the bucket at exactly one charge after a 201, a 502 and each post-credential refusal; a CDN redirect → 502
    and not followed; a slow job → 202 at the injected hold and its clip lands; a hung-up client leaves no job
    behind Shutdown; a request on a context cancelled from the start reaches no fetch, refused by the credential
    read; U+0130 in the host, raw and `%C4%B0`, 400 `attachment_host` with zero fetches); internal/config
    `TestAttachmentAllowlist` (the U+0130 hosts, raw, `%C4%B0` and on the media host, refused); cmd/clippet `TestTokensMintAutoFetch`; internal/web
    `TestSettingsTokensPanelAutoFetch` (absent with no bot and with an own-token bot, drawn after Inbound URL on
    a managed one, the `ca_` row). E2E step 101 (`101-autofetch.sh`, parallel): the shell mint; misses on both

    server 403 with no job, an on-CDN attachment reaches the fetcher and fails as 502 `fetch`, one

325. **The upload form says `Uploading…`, and a late title redraws the card** (run 7 lane `form2`, 2026-10-06;
    the owner's T-form on dev, 2026-10-06 ≈19:00Z, recorded in the run's dev tests; the pick (b) at ≈20:45Z:
    the link still posts at once, and a late submit redraws the card). Amends erratum 320 (a), (b) and (g).

    **Why.** Erratum 320 shipped two defects the owner's test showed. (1) A short clip is posted BEFORE the title is typed:
    a 59 MB clip's link posted 16 s after `/upload-dev`, the Submit came 6 s later; the title was saved (the page
    and `og:title` showed it) but the card in the channel was drawn from the file name, and Discord caches a URL's
    card for about thirty minutes, so even `/clip-dev` of that link showed the old card. (2) A dismissed form is
    silent: Discord sends the app nothing when a modal is closed, and the modal replaced the "thinking…"; the owner saw
    nothing for the 24 s an 83 MB upload took, ran the command again, and got two clips.

    **The Discord fact the redraw rests on (measured 2026-10-06 20:49Z,** on a channel webhook
    in the owner's test server — follow-ups are webhook-backed): POST the bare link → the message's `embeds` held one
    `components` embed for the URL after 1.8 s; PATCH `content` to the same link plus `?v=2` → `embeds` was `[]` in
    the PATCH's own answer, and one `components` embed for the `?v=2` URL was there 1.8 s later; the dev app logged
    one fresh GET of the page 0.4 s after the edit. The message was deleted.

    **(a) `Uploading…`** `ClipJob.Uploading` (set by `openUploadForm`, so only with the form on and the table not
    full — the deferral's "thinking…" is the feedback otherwise; ignored on a deferred job): `runClip` posts ONE
    ephemeral follow-up, `{"content":"Uploading…","flags":64,"allowed_mentions":{"parse":[]}}`, on the command's
    token, in its own goroutine BESIDE the fetch (the first follow-up after a modal can meet the one-second 404
    retry, and the upload never waits on a courtesy line), and a deferred call deletes it by the id Discord
    answered (`DELETE /webhooks/{app}/{token}/messages/{id}`) once the job's last message is out — the link, a
    failure sentence, or (the deferral runs first, then the recovery posts) a panic's. A line that will not post
    is one log line (`the uploading line was not posted`) and the job is unchanged; one that will not delete is
    one log line and stays. The word is the review's, the one Clippet Auto uses; it is the only new user-facing string.

    **(b) The redraw.** A submit that lands AFTER the clip exists (the table's `formWrite`) and CHANGES the title —
    `UpdateClipMeta` succeeded, the title differs from the one read just before the write — calls
    `DiscordBot.Redraw(clipID)` (the interface's third method; never blocking, as property 5 needs). internal/notify
    keeps, per clip a form job posted a link for, the interaction token and the follow-up message's id
    (`linkTable`: in memory, 256 entries at most — full holds nothing more, never an error —, expiring fifteen
    minutes after the job started, i.e. the token's life); the entry is made BEFORE the link's POST, so a submit
    landing while the POST is in flight is marked and the job redraws as soon as Discord answers (`after_post`).
    The redraw PATCHes that message on the interaction token
    (`/webhooks/{app}/{token}/messages/{id}`): `content` = the share link plus `?v=2`, and the empty mention list —
    no embed, no component, no flag —, one retry on the retryable set. ONE redraw per upload (a form takes one
    answer; the entry is removed on use). No redraw when the title is unchanged or blank, when the submit came
    before the link (held, written by `attach` before the link is posted, so the card is drawn right the first
    time, as before), when the submit was refused or the upload failed, after a restart (the table is gone: the
    title is still saved, the card keeps the old title — 320's old behaviour, now only after a restart), or past
    fifteen minutes. The submit's own answer is unchanged ("Saved." and its variants); a failed edit shows nothing.
    `formEntry` still holds no token: the token and the id live only in internal/notify, which never logs them.
    Only the interaction-token routes, so a managed instance (`DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN=managed`) redraws exactly as one
    with its own token. internal/notify's header lists six calls.

    **(c) `?v=2` is a share link everywhere.** The page at `/{id}?v=2` is the page at `/{id}` (the router never
    read a query): the canonical, `og:url` and the component embed all name the BARE link, so the query lives in
    that one message only. `ParseShare` already read past a query, so `/clip link:` and Enrich resolve the edited
    message's link to the clip and answer with the bare link — now pinned.

    **(d) Logs.** `discord bot: card redraw clip=<id> outcome=edited|failed|none|after_post|restart|panic` — the
    clip id and an outcome word, nothing typed, no token, no error text. Nothing typed into the form is logged, as
    before.

    **(e) Edges, stated.** On the official bot, if the box answers the modal after the forwarder's two seconds,
    Discord saw the forwarder's deferral (320 (g)): the first follow-up then edits the "thinking…" under Discord's
    deprecated compatibility rule, ignoring the ephemeral flag — so `Uploading…` replaces the public "thinking…",
    the link posts as a new message, and the delete removes that first message. Only the owner's re-test can show two
    things: (1) that an ephemeral follow-up after a modal is drawn and can be deleted on a real interaction (the
    documented routes say yes; the measurement above used a channel webhook); (2) the redraw on a real
    interaction follow-up, and that it wears Discord's "(edited)" mark. T-form 2 is in the run's dev tests.

    *Amended 2026-10-27 (run 23 lane `v1-forward`, in clippet-pass; D13):* the edge above no longer arises. The
    forwarder settles every public "thinking…" itself (`forward.ts settle()`, 20 s): when the box answers a command
    with the upload form past the two seconds, the forwarder edits the "thinking…" to `Uploading…` and deletes it,
    which ends Discord's loading state — so the box's follow-ups (the `Uploading…` line, the link) are ordinary new
    messages, and nothing leans on the deprecated first-follow-up-edits-the-loading-message rule any more; should
    that rule still fire first, the box's own delete of its line removes the same message and the link posts beneath
    either way. The two things only a re-test could show were shown by T-form 2 (2026-10-06, dev). 320 (g) carries
    the forwarder's half and, from lane `v2-followup`, the box's half (one link per interaction token).

    **Pins** (each failed with its change reverted). internal/notify `bot_redraw_test.go`: the line ephemeral, its
    exact body, on the hook path, deleted by its own id after the link and after a failure sentence, no
    Authorization and no PATCH; a line Discord refuses changes nothing; no line on a deferred job or a form job
    without the flag; the redraw's exact path and body, once (a second ask edits nothing and logs `none`), the
    same on a managed bot; nothing posted → no call; a redraw during the link's POST waits for it; a refused edit
    is one `outcome=failed` line without the token and no retry on a 400; the table's bound and fifteen minutes;
    `messageID` takes a snowflake only. internal/httpapi: the form job carries `Uploading`, `off` and a full table
    do not; a redraw is asked exactly for a late CHANGED title (not the same title, a blank one, a refused submit
    or a held one); the whole path through a real `notify.Bot` (`Uploading…` posted once and deleted by its id,
    the link bare, a late submit PATCHes that message to `?v=2`, once); `/clip link:` and Enrich on
    `{origin}/{id}?v=2`. internal/urls `ParseShare` of `?v=2`. internal/web `TestRedrawQueryLeavesTheCardBare`.
    E2E step 98 (no new step): the `--network none` probe's log shows the line tried and not posted, no redraw for
    a failed upload, no interaction token; the `off` probe tries no line.

    **Amended 2026-10-19 (erratum 340):** while the fetch runs the line is edited every five seconds to `Uploading… 120
