326. **A byte-identical upload within one account answers the existing clip** (run 7 lane `dedupe`, 2026-10-07;
    The owner, 2026-10-06 ≈23:35Z: a storage owner never wants two full copies of one file; the pick (a) — same
    account, same bytes, any age → the existing link — subject to the review's opinion, which is the design;
    the two picks on it 2026-10-07 ≈00:52Z: the web keeps `Upload anyway`, and the form path's line is
    `Already in your library. The form was not applied.`). No migration.

    **(a) The check, in the ingest core.** `spoolBody` hashes the spool as it writes it
    (`io.MultiWriter(disk, sha256)`, the disk first so a disk error is still one) and returns the hex beside the
    size. Right after the spool — before the probe and before any byte reaches the store — `ingestCore` asks
    `liveCopy(owner, size, sum)`: `ClipsWithSourceSize(owner, size)` through migration 0020's
    `(owner_id, source_size)` index (it now also reads `state` and `expires_at`), narrowed by `dedupeMatch`
    (`queued`, `processing` or `ready`, and `expires_at` NULL or in the future; `failed`, `deleting` and
    expired-not-yet-swept never match) and compared by hex in Go, newest first. A match answers THAT clip with
    `existing = true`: the spool is removed, and there is no row, no object, no job — so no webhook either
    (erratum 319 fires at the ready flip of a new clip). One INFO line, `upload deduped clip=<id> bytes=<n>`, no
    file name; nothing else is logged (the access line of an HTTP route carries `existing=true`). On a new clip
    the store's `PutResult.SHA256` is compared with the spool's hash and a difference is one WARN (they are one
    function over one file). The storage quota (277) is still asked first, before any byte is read, so an
    instance at its cap refuses a duplicate too. **Never across accounts**: every lookup is `WHERE owner_id = ?`,
    there is no global hash index, no route takes a hash, and no answer of any shape is given about another
    account's bytes — that would be an oracle over unlisted clips, whose only protection is the id. The race
    (two identical uploads in flight at once) is not closed: neither sees the other, two clips, no error.

    **(b) The opt-out `duplicate=allow`.** `uploadMeta.allowDuplicate`. On the capture grammar (`/api/upload`,
    `/in/{token}`, the share target) it is one more text field before the file, `duplicate`; on POST /api/clips it
    is ONE text part allowed between the `metadata` part and the `video` part (any other part there is still
    `missing_video`). Only the value `allow` opts out; any other value leaves the check on. *Amended run 8 (lane
    `nits9`):* empty is "not sent" (the check stays on) and any other value is the 400 `invalid_request`
    `duplicate must be allow` on both multipart grammars, before the file is read. The Clippet Auto
    instruction (`/in/auto/{token}`, erratum 324) takes an optional `"duplicate": "allow"`; another value is the
    grammar's own 400. The bot's own paths (`/upload`, `/clip file:`, Enrich) never set it.

    **(c) Every path's answer.** POST /api/clips → **200** (never 201) with the existing clip's `ClipDTO` (its own
    tags) and `"existing": true`; the request's title, description, unlisted, TTL and tags are not applied. The
    capture grammar, the inbound URL and the Clippet Auto URL → 200 with the existing `UploadDTO` and
    `"existing": true` (the inbound URL's text answer is the existing link with 200); the card-ready wait applies
    as before, since the clip named may still be encoding. `existing` is absent on every other answer. The share
    target 303s to the existing page. The bot's `/upload`, `/clip file:` and Enrich post the existing link exactly
    as a new one (`notify.IngestResult.Existing`; erratum 316's card draws itself); a duplicate's link is never
    held for a redraw. **The form trap** (the opinion's §3): behind the upload form the modal's fields are NEVER
    applied to the existing clip — the ingest hook gets `existing` and skips `applyHeldForm`'s write; a submit
    already held is dropped; a submit that arrives later is answered `Already in your library. The form was not
    applied.` and not written (`formNotApplied`; so no `Redraw`); and the job (`ClipJob.Form`) posts that same line
    as an ephemeral follow-up before the link, so the person who sent the form first (and was answered "Saved.")
    is told too. The drop folder leaves the file where the person put it, records the decision with the existing
    clip's id (0018's memory unchanged: `touch` it to be asked again), and writes `<name>.failed.txt` — the one
    sibling the watcher already skips — whose whole text is `already here <link>`. `admin import` keeps `seen <id>`:
    `Importer.Duplicates` is now `liveDigests`, the core's own question (so a failed or expired clip of the same
    bytes is no longer `seen`, and the file is imported), and a duplicate the core finds after the verb's
    pre-check is printed `seen` as well. The web (`app.js`) learns 200: a duplicate adds no row and the batch
    carries on; at its end the status reads `Already in your library.` with a link to each existing clip (its own
    title), and `Upload anyway` (index.html, beside Try again) sends exactly those files again with the opt-out.
    *Amended run 8 (lane `nits9`, the owner's pick B a):* the note is `<name>.clippet.txt` (`drop.NoteSuffix`, skipped
    by the watcher, `admin import` and doctor's counts as `.failed.txt` is; a later success or duplicate removes
    the other note). *Also amended run 8:* the line is said ONCE — the job posts it only when the duplicate dropped
    a submit already answered "Saved." (`IngestResult.SubmitDropped`); a submit that arrives later hears it from
    its own answer alone.

    **(d) The harness.** Every multipart upload site of the E2E (`scripts/e2e.sh`, `scripts/e2e.d/*.sh`: 56) sends
    `-F duplicate=allow` just before its file part, because the suite uploads the same fixtures many times under
    one account and means a new clip each time; the Go tests' `multipartBody` does the same unless given
    `dedupeOn`, and `runIngest` feeds distinct bytes per call. The visual pass's faces test uploads the fixture
    through the form under an account that already holds it, so it now meets `Already in your library.` and
    clicks `Upload anyway` — the live proof of the web half. Bundles 85, 98 and 101 never ingest (no network) and
    100's two uploads carry the opt-out. E2E step **102** (`102-dedupe.sh`, parallel; the suite is 102 steps / 33
    bundles): the same file twice → one id, 200 + `existing` on the web, capture and inbound grammars, `1 clips`,
    one transcode job, the same object count, one `upload deduped` line per answer with no file name; the opt-out
    → new ids on both grammars; a second account → its own clip; a drop-folder duplicate in a `--network none`
    probe → stays, with `already here <link>`.

    **Pins** (each failed with its change reverted). internal/httpapi `dedupe_test.go`: the same bytes twice → the
    same id, 200 + existing, no new object, row or job, the second request's fields unapplied, the one log line
    without the file name, the spool removed (reverting the check fails seven tests; reverting the 200 fails
    three); `duplicate=allow` on both grammars → a new clip, another value → the check (reverting either grammar's
    read fails it); never across accounts (widening the lookup's `owner_id` fails it); processing and ready
    match, failed and expired do not (`dedupeMatch` → always true fails it); the spool's hash equals the store's
    and the clip's `source_etag` (removing the hash writer fails it and eight others); the inbound URL's 200 text
    and JSON; the Clippet Auto URL's 200, opt-out and 400 (forcing 201 fails it); the upload form applies nothing,
    late or held, and asks no redraw (removing the form guard fails it); the drop folder's note and the file left
    (removing the drop branch fails it); `Importer.Duplicates` skips a failed clip (reverting to the raw lookup
    fails it). internal/notify `bot_dedupe_test.go`: a Form duplicate posts the ephemeral line and the link and
    holds nothing (disabling the branch fails it); a deferred duplicate is the edit alone.

    **Unverified, stated.** That ShareX accepts a 200 where it got 201 (its custom-uploader treats any success
    status as success as far as the builder read; nothing here was run against ShareX). Whether Discord's client
    re-encodes a video it posts (then two posts of one file are different bytes and the bot path rarely matches).

327. **The Clippet Auto URL's box nits: a cap on running fetches, the declared size as the truth, a long file name
    clipped, the second bucket per URL** (run 8 lane `nits9`, 2026-10-07; the one-press review's
    NIT 2–6, 8–10, the re-check's NIT 8 and the SEAM; erratum 324 is otherwise unchanged).

    **(a) At most two running fetches per account.** `autoFetchInflightMax = 2`, a per-mount in-memory count
    (`handler.autoInflight`) keyed by the URL's account, taken after every other refusal (so a refused instruction
    never holds a slot) and released when the JOB ends, not the request: a relay goroutine reads the job's one
    outcome, frees the slot and hands the outcome on (buffered; a request that stopped waiting leaves nothing
    blocked). A third press while two are downloading is the bucket's own envelope — **429** `rate_limited` `too
    many requests; retry later`, `Retry-After: 10`, access field `reject=inflight` — so no new words. Honest use (a
    person pressing buttons) never meets it; a leaked URL can no longer start an hour's bucket of downloads at once.

    **(b) The declared `size` is the truth.** It chose the early 413 and the scratch-room pre-check, so the stream is
    bounded at it (`capReader(body, size)` around the route's ingest): a download that runs past the size stated
    is the 413 `too_large` an over-cap stream already was. A lying SMALL size can no longer skip the early refusal.

    **(c) A file name over 255 bytes is CLIPPED, never refused** (the SEAM: Clippet Auto passes Discord's own name,
    and a presser cannot shorten it): `clipFilename` cuts on a rune boundary to 255 bytes, keeping an extension of
    up to 16 bytes; the grammar's bound on `filename` is now the 4 KiB body's. The title is the clipped name's stem.

    **(d) The second upload bucket is keyed by the URL** (`tokenKey`: `t:<row id>`), not the address: every press
    reaches a box from Clippet Auto's egress, so `RATE_UPLOAD_PER_HOUR_PER_IP` per address was one cap for every
    server's presses at once. The account bucket is unchanged and still runs first.

    **(e) The outcome switch.** A restart during the CDN GET is a restart: `fetchAndIngest` returns a bare
    cancellation when its job's context was cancelled (the shutdown is the only thing that cancels one), so the route
    answers **503** `unavailable` + `Retry-After: 5` and the log word is `restart` — and a deferred `/upload` cut the
    same way edits in the restart sentence, not `SentenceFetch`. The unreachable 429 arm (`SentenceBusy`, never
    chosen: the route's ingest has `charge=false`) is deleted; were it ever chosen it is the generic 500. A hung-up
    client's access line is the 400 `client_disconnected` every route's hang-up writes (`writeClientGone`), not a
    200 nothing was written for. The `Fetch` panic line carries `panic_type=<the value's Go type>` and never the
    value. Every arm has a test (a stub bot returning each sentence, and `ErrClosed`).

    **(f) ASCII-only folds** beside `ValidAttachmentURL`'s: `parseDiscordURL` (DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL) and the clip
    webhook's shown host fold ASCII case alone (`config.asciiLower`), so a U+0130 host fails the webhook allowlist
    and a clip webhook's host is shown as it is dialled.

    **(g) The job's command on its log lines.** `notify.ClipJob.Command` (`/upload`, an old `/clip file:`'s `/clip`,
    `Enrich`) is a `command=` field on the job's lines; their messages keep the `/clip` wording the E2E greps.

    **Pins** (each failed with its change reverted): internal/httpapi `autofetch_nits_test.go` —
    `TestAutoFetchEveryOutcomeArm` (the deleted 429 arm), `TestAutoFetchDeclaredSizeBoundsTheStream`,
    `TestAutoFetchCapsAnAccountsRunningJobs`, `TestAutoFetchRestartDuringTheGetIsA503`,
    `TestAutoFetchClipsALongFileName`, `TestAutoFetchSecondBucketIsKeyedByTheURL`, `TestAutoFetchHangUpIsNotA200`;
    the 202 row of `TestAutoFetchChargesTheAccountOnce`; internal/notify `TestARestartDuringTheCDNGetIsARestart`,
    `TestFetchRecoversAPanic`'s type, `TestJobLinesNameTheCommand`; internal/config the U+0130 rows of
    `TestDiscordWebhookRejections` and `TestClipWebhookAccepts`.

328. **A clip can be sound** (run 8 lane `audiocore`, 2026-10-07; the owner's D1a, D2a, D4a, D5a, D7a, D8a of
    the audio research's Part 4 — the whole "a" suite taken — and the decisions on the round-2
    research's strip findings; the card — the waveform, the
    audiogram, the card tags — is erratum 329's). Migration **0021**; E2E step **103**.

    **(a) The kind, decided by the probe.** `clips.kind` `video`|`audio` (0021, default `video` = the backfill),
    with `audio_codec`, `sample_rate`, `bit_depth` (NULL for a lossy codec) and `channels`, all NULL on a video.
    `transcode.ParseProbe` grows a SECOND branch, taken only when the file has NO non-cover video stream: a file that
    has one is judged by the video gate exactly as before, whatever is wrong with it, so the audio branch is never a
    weaker way in (`TestParseProbeAudio` pins a zero-dimension video with sound still refused). The branch has its
    own closed `allowedAudioFormats` — mp3, wav, w64, flac, aiff, caf, ogg, the ISO-BMFF family, matroska/webm
    (admitted only for the codecs (b) moves into a clean box), wv, tta, ADTS aac, ac3, eac3, amr, asf — the same kind of allowlist as `allowedFormats` (a playlist with sound is
    still `unsupported container (hls)`). `attached_pic` streams set `CoverArt` and are never a video. Refused, all
    in the permanent `not_a_video` shape the gate answers **415** with: two or more audio tracks — **refused, not
    "take the first"** (a voice and a backing track in one file are two things; publishing one of them silently is
    publishing something nobody chose) —, a `dsd_*` codec in any box and the `dsf`/`iff` demuxers (D8a), Monkey's
    Audio (ffmpeg has no muxer for `ape`, so its tags could not be stripped by a copy), more than eight channels or
    none, no duration. `store.ContentTypeFor` takes an `audio/*` part type as well as `video/*` and the extension map
    learns `.mp3 .m4a .flac .wav .ogg .oga .opus .weba .aif .aiff .caf .amr .wv` — a first opinion only: for an
    audio clip the strip's container decides the stored type, and a VIDEO whose first opinion said sound (`clip.m4a`
    sent as `audio/mp4`) is stored under its extension's video type or octet-stream, never an audio one.

    **(b) The strip, at ingest — the stored "original" of an audio clip is never the upload.** Between the probe
    and the PutFile, `ingestCore` runs `Deps.Strip` (`transcode.StripVerified`): a `-c copy` of the ONE audio stream
    (`-map 0:<index>`, never `-map 0` — cover art is a stream) into the container `transcode.StripTargetFor` names,
    with `-map_metadata -1 -map_chapters -1 -sn -dn -fflags +bitexact -flags +bitexact`, the mp3 muxer's
    `-id3v2_version 0 -write_id3v1 0`, the wav muxer's `-rf64 auto`, the mp4 muxer's `+faststart`, always to a FILE
    (the mp3 muxer's Xing/Info frame is written only into a seekable output). The container is the source's own
    except: the ISO-BMFF family becomes an MP4 (`.m4a`, `audio/mp4`) — raw PCM, which the mp4 muxer refuses, stays
    a `.mov` (`audio/quicktime`) —, ADTS AAC becomes an MP4 too (which is what makes it play), Wave64 becomes a WAV,
    and **Matroska/WebM is never written back**: its muxers keep a per-stream `DURATION` tag and the format's
    `encoder=Lavf` under every strip flag (measured, ffmpeg 7.1.1), so Opus/Vorbis in Matroska or WebM (a browser's
    MediaRecorder, `audio/webm;codecs=opus`) is moved into an Ogg (`.ogg`, `audio/ogg` — and it then PLAYS as its
    Original, D7a), FLAC into a flac, ALAC into an MP4, little-endian PCM into a WAV and big-endian PCM into an AIFF;
    every other codec in Matroska is refused (415). StripVerified then PROVES its output: it probes as the same one
    audio stream in the same codec, with no tag beyond an MP4's structural boxes, no `encoder` tag anywhere (stricter
    than the video remux's fixed point, which allows that key) and no picture (`CheckStripped`), and on every
    lossless source (PCM, FLAC, ALAC, WavPack, TTA, MLP/TrueHD) the decoded samples hash EQUAL to the upload's
    (`ffmpeg … -c:a pcm_s32le -f hash -hash sha256`, `pcm_f32le` for float — the hash muxer's default s16 would hide
    a 24-bit loss); any miss is a 415, nothing stored. The raw bytes are removed the moment the strip is proven; the
    strip replaces them as `source.<ext>` on the spool (the worker's hand-off), and its size and sha256 are the row's
    `source_size`/`source_etag`. So the owner's "Download original" is the strip too: the round-2 research found the
    ORIGINAL download to be the leak (a WAV's `bext`/`iXML`/`LIST`/`id3 ` chunks, a phone's ISO-6709 location, a
    FLAC's vendor string and base64 picture), and it is closed at the one place every path passes. A scratch
    precheck runs first (the two files coexist), so a full disk is the scratch 507, not a 415 for a good file.
    `Deps.Strip` nil REFUSES every audio upload (503), never stores one unstripped. The strip is reproducible
    (`+bitexact`: no creation time, no encoder string, a fixed Ogg serial), so the duplicate check (erratum 326) is
    asked AGAIN after it, on the stripped size and hash: the same file twice is one clip. The strip runs in the API
    process, bounded by a 10-minute budget and by the upload limiters (there is no semaphore of its own).

    **(c) The tiers, as built** (`transcode.MakeAudioPlan`, on the probe of the STORED file; no new job kind — the
    transcode run branches on `ProbeResult.Kind`, `internal/worker/audio.go`):

    | stored file | Original | Full (`full_codec`) | card copy |
    |---|---|---|---|
    | MP3 in mp3 | plays | — | always |
    | AAC in a faststart MP4 | plays | — | always |
    | Opus or Vorbis in Ogg (D7a) | plays | — | always |
    | FLAC in flac (integer) | plays | — | always |
    | integer PCM ≤ 24-bit (WAV/W64/AIFF/CAF), ALAC, WavPack, TTA, TrueHD, FLAC in another box (D1a) | download only | `flac`: bit-exact; the PCM hash of source and Full must match or the clip FAILS | always |
    | float PCM, integer PCM > 24-bit (D2a) | download only | `flac24`: `-sample_fmt s32 -bits_per_raw_sample 24`; the peak is measured first (`astats`) and above 0 dBFS the Full is written with `volume=-(peak+0.01)dB` so no sample saturates; never hashed, never called lossless | always |
    | anything else — WMA, AC-3, E-AC-3, AMR, MP3/AAC in another box (D8a) | download only | `aac`: 256k in a faststart MP4 | always |

    The Full's key is `renditions/main-{r8}.flac` or `.m4a` (`store.AudioRenditionKey`) under `audio/flac` /
    `audio/mp4`; the verifier's audio verdict (`CheckAudioOutput`) is no video stream, exactly one audio stream, the
    expected codec, a positive duration. The CARD COPY of this lane is the ink tile — `web/static/card-placeholder.png`,
    the card a still-encoding clip shows, read from its one source — looped at 2 fps under the sound, H.264 + AAC-LC
    48 kHz in a faststart MP4 at the picture's own 1200×630, `-t <probed seconds> -shortest` (whichever ends first: a
    container that claims a thousand hours over one minute of sound must not loop a picture for a thousand hours),
    stereo only past two channels, AAC fitted to `SOCIAL_MAX_BYTES` like the video Light (95 % of the cap over the
    duration, less 16k for the picture) and clamped to 96k–256k — a long clip keeps a card at 96k past the cap,
    because an audio clip has no other MP4 a card could point at; `SOCIAL_MAX_BYTES=0` still gets the 256k card. Its
    encode is followed by a `-c copy` pass with the tags dropped (`CleanMP4Args`): the ffmpeg CLI writes the H.264
    track's encoder ("Lavc libx264") into the mp4's compressor name for any stream it ENCODES, whatever `-metadata`
    says, and a copy writes none (measured, ffmpeg 7.1.1). It must come out at exactly the picture's size with one AAC
    stream and `moov` first. Every audio encode is held to `outputBudget`'s ceiling with no plan term — max(2 ×
    source, `MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES`) — as ffmpeg's `-fs`, and a file that REACHED it fails `output_too_large` rather than
    being published truncated (the duration an encode runs for is the container's claim, which the uploader
    controls); the scratch room asked for is the plan's estimate (AAC at its bitrate, FLAC at the PCM it encodes),
    capped at that budget. The poster is the same picture as a JPEG (`transcode.AudioPoster`). An audio clip's
    `width`, `height`, `fps_num`, `fps_den` are NULL (FinalizeTranscode writes a zero as NULL; a video's are never
    zero); `duration_ms` is the sound's, `has_audio` true; the card copy's size is on `social_width/height`, as every
    card copy's is. `probe.json` carries the plan under `audio`.

    **(d) Serving it: ONE new route, `GET /api/clips/{id}/audio`.** `db.PlayObject` — the stored original when it
    plays, the Full otherwise — under its REAL media type (the stored `source_content_type`, or `audio/flac` /

    extension>`; a video answers 404. For an audio clip `/video.mp4`, `/light.mp4` and `/social.mp4` serve the CARD
    COPY (never a fall-back to bytes that are not an MP4; no card copy is the ready-row 503), so every card tag,
    `CardReady` and the embed page are unchanged. `/original` follows `db.OriginalIsTheClip` as for a video: a

    fields, and carry a `label` (`Original · FLAC|MP3|AAC|Opus|Vorbis`, `Full · FLAC`, `Full · FLAC 24-bit`, `Full ·
    AAC`; app.js shows it as given, plus the size). **The verification plane's guard (clippet-pass) pins every route

    answers this route 404** — the page's `<audio>` then fails there while `/original` and the card still work

    **(e) Every `width > 0` site touched, and the picture routes.** `resolutionText` (the library row) says `audio`

    player is an `<audio>`); the watch page's player region holds the card picture as an `<img>` above `<audio
    controls preload="metadata">` playing `/audio` (app.js's player keys, loop, remembered mute, quality switch and
    view beacon accept either element); `EmbedCode` is sized by the card copy; `meta.go`'s `socialDims` already reads
    the card copy and `cardQualityLine` says nothing for a clip with no picture; the DTO's tier fields above; `admin
    ls <id>` prints a `kind:` row (a row and not a column: the E2E's sweep reads the listing by position). Trim, both
    GIF routes, `filmstrip.jpg`, the chosen card frame and the replacement answer **409** `not_for_audio` (`Not for
    audio.`) after the route's own lookup or ownership check and before anything is queued, and the page renders none
    of their controls. **Replacement: a video is replaced by a video** (an audio file sent to a video clip's replace
    is the 415), and **an audio clip cannot be replaced in this lane** — the replacement path has its own spool,
    worker run and swap, and teaching it the strip, the audio tiers and the audio facts is a lane of its own
    (a cleanup row, run 8). GIF: no.

    **(f) The paths.** Web upload (the picker accepts `video/*,audio/*` and the audio extensions), `/api/upload`,
    `/in/{token}` and `/api/share` (the PWA `share_target` accepts `["video/*", "audio/*"]`), the drop folder
    (`drop.ProbeVideo` admits an audio result) and `admin import` (its own `strip`, `transcode.StripVerified`) all
    reach the strip through `ingestCore`. The bot's first opinion `isVideo` is `isMedia` (`video/` or `audio/`), so
    `/upload`, the Clippet Auto URL and Enrich (by erratum 323's rule) take an audio attachment — a Discord voice
    message is one `audio/ogg` attachment and is an upload like any other — and the bot posts the bare link (D5a,
    unchanged). The self-host bot's `/upload` attachment option gains `"file_types": ["video", "audio"]` and the
    description `The video or audio to upload`; the official bot's registration (clippet-pass `scripts/commands.json`)
    needs the same change, which is that repo's. The refusal everywhere is `notify.SentenceNotVideo` = `That file is
    not a video or audio Clippet can play.`; the HTTP 415's message `the file is not a playable video or audio file`;
    the drop folder's and import's `this instance cannot read a video or audio stream out of it`; the Clippet Auto
    URL's `that file is not a video or audio file`. The doctor is unchanged. Two words the brief did not give, settled by
    the review: `Original · Vorbis` (the grammar `Original · <codec>` extended to the fifth playable codec) and `Audio`

    **Pins** (each failed with its change reverted, then restored). internal/transcode `audio_test.go`: the branch

329. **An audio clip's card: the drawn waveform, the audiogram, the card tags** (run 8 lane `audiocard`,
    2026-10-07; the owner's D3a — a drawn waveform of the clip —, D5a, D6a of the audio research's Part 4,
    and the round-2 research's verdict: draw the picture yourself and let ffmpeg do the motion). Migration **0022**; E2E step **104**; visual 111 shots. Builds on 328, whose
    card copy was the ink tile under the sound.

    **(a) The peaks, from ONE streamed pipe.** (AMENDED by erratum 332: the bars are now each bar's LOUDNESS —
    RMS over both channels of a stereo source, through a 0.6 gamma, floored at −30 dBFS RMS — and the bucket
    starts at one frame instead of the probed length's share; the payload, the drawing and the stored bars of
    older clips are unchanged. What follows is the reading as 329 built it.) `transcode.WavePeaks` runs `ffmpeg -nostdin -i IN -map 0:a:0 -ac 1
    -c:a pcm_s16le -f s16le -` (the stored original, its NATIVE rate — a resample's lowpass would change the
    peaks) into a `PeakWriter`, an `io.Writer` that keeps max |s| per bucket in constant memory: 4,096 fine
    buckets sized from the probed length, halved (pairs merged by max) whenever they fill, so a container that
    understated its length costs resolution and never memory. `showwavespic` is NOT used: it queues every
    decoded frame until EOF (≈691 MB for an hour of 48 kHz stereo, the research's §1(a)1). The 70 bars are the
    max of the fine buckets each covers, divided by the clip's own peak but never by less than −20 dBFS (3,277
    of 32,768) — the loudest moment of a clip is a full bar, and a near-silent file (hiss, a room tone) is drawn
    at its real share rather than blown up — and quantised to 0..255. The s16 decode saturates a float sample
    past full scale, so a +3 dBFS file's bars are full; |−32768| is taken in an int32. The bars ride the row
    as `clips.peaks` (0022, two lowercase hex digits a bar, exactly 140 characters; `transcode.EncodePeaks`/`DecodePeaks`, the
    latter refusing any other shape) and the checkpoint, so a finalize-only retry commits the bars this attempt
    drew.

    **(b) The drawing, the standard library only** (`internal/transcode/waveform.go`: `image`, `image/png`,
    `image/color`, `image/draw`; no `x/image`, no new binary). The frame is 1280×720 — the card frame, the
    audiogram's own size — with the bars in a 1120×400 band at (80, 160): 70 bars 10 px wide at a pitch of 16,
    centred (the run is 1,114 px, 3 px short of each side), mirrored about y = 360, never shorter than 10 px —
    a bar as tall as it is wide is a DOT, so silence is a dotted baseline. Each bar is a rounded rectangle
    (radius half its width) rasterised ANALYTICALLY: its signed distance at the pixel's centre mapped to a
    1-px ramp, which is the antialias. `WavePoster` paints the bars over the ink tile `#17181C` in the dark
    palette's `--muted` `#A9A59C`; `WaveStencil` is the same tile, opaque, with each bar cut out as a HOLE
    (alpha 1 − coverage). The palette is the colour law's (web/STYLE.md, the research's mapping): the PLAYED
    colour is the dark `--time` `#F0B24A`, amber = happening, and not green — green means "you can paste
    this", and the card's own edge already says that. Each colour is one constant (`WaveRestHex`,
    `WavePlayedHex`, `WaveGroundHex`); the owner has not seen the picture, and a change after that look is one line.
    No time readout (the player has one), no decoration.

    **(c) The poster** (`posterAudio`, the run's `poster` stage). The waveform as a **PNG** — flat colour and
    hard edges, which a PNG keeps exactly and a JPEG rings around — at a key of its own,
    `…/poster/poster-{r8}.png` (`store.PNGPosterKey`), stored under `image/png`; `poster.jpg` serves it under
    that type (`transcode.PosterContentType`, the key's extension decides, for the bucket, the route and
    `og:image:type` alike). The standard library writes no text chunk, and the label pass writes a PNG back
    with `-c:v png` and the bitexact flags, so nothing names a program or a time. On it: the clip's DURATION
    plate in the top-right, exactly erratum 287's (`drawPosterLabel`, which never fails a poster), and the
    companion MARK in the bottom-left — `web/static/icon-192.png`, the manifest icon `mkicons.py` draws, halved
    by a 2×2 box filter (≈55 px, the plate's height) and laid on ink-only (its rounded tile IS the ground
    colour, and its antialiased rim is left as the ground), its ink's left edge on the first bar's, centred in
    the band's bottom margin. That corner is the one the card leaves free: the top-left is the embed overlay's
    (287 moved it there for the plate), the top-right the plate's, and the bottom band is the native
    controls' only while a player is paused in a browser, never on Discord's card at rest. The mark and the
    plate are on the POSTER only — the picture a reader sees before pressing play, as a video's plate is —
    never in the audiogram, which is a picture of the clip and carries no brand (no watermarks). The poster is
    `og:image` (1280×720, its measured size), the page's picture above the `<audio>`, and the library's tile.
    The brief named `mkcard.py` for where the placeholder puts the mark: the placeholder puts it LARGE on the
    left, which a 1,120-px band rules out, so the mark comes from the icon and sits small in the free corner.

    **(d) The audiogram — the card copy** (the run's `light` stage, two passes: the stencil exists BEFORE the
    encode, because one process that drew it from the sound it is also encoding would buffer the whole sound).
    The research's filtergraph 2, as built (`AudioLightArgs`; DUR the probed seconds as a literal, e.g.
    `312.480000`):

        ffmpeg -nostdin -i IN -loop 1 -framerate 30 -i stencil.png -filter_complex
          "color=c=0xA9A59C:s=1280x720:r=30:d=DUR,format=gbrp[rest];
           color=c=0xF0B24A:s=1280x720:r=30:d=DUR,format=gbrp[done];
           [rest][done]overlay=x='80+1120*t/DUR-w':y=0:eval=frame:format=gbrp[field];
           [1:v]format=gbrap[st];
           [field][st]overlay=0:0:shortest=1:format=gbrp,
             scale=out_color_matrix=bt709:out_range=tv,format=yuv420p,
             setparams=color_primaries=bt709:color_trc=bt709:colorspace=bt709[v]"
          -map [v] -map 0:a:0 -t DUR -shortest
          -c:v libx264 -preset veryfast -crf 18 -g 150 -keyint_min 150 -sc_threshold 0 -r 30
          -color_primaries bt709 -color_trc bt709 -colorspace bt709
          -c:a aac -b:a {fitted}k -ar 48000 [-ac 2 past two channels]   |   -c:a copy
          -map_metadata -1 -map_chapters -1 -sn -dn -fflags +bitexact -flags +bitexact [-fs budget]
          -movflags +faststart -f mp4 enc.mp4

    then 328's tag-dropping `-c copy` pass. Two flat fields, two overlays and one conversion a frame; the only
    per-frame expression is the overlay's x, so the played edge IS the playhead, reaching the band's right
    edge exactly at DUR. The composite is in planar RGB and converted ONCE, explicitly BT.709 limited range
    and stamped so, so a browser's decode of frame 0 is the poster's colours. **30 fps constant** — taken off
    the list of variables (the research's §2 found no source on how Discord's phones treat a 1–2 fps card;
    E1 decides, and may try 10) — with a keyframe every 5 s. `-map 0:a:0`, never `-map 0` (cover art is a
    stream). `-t DUR` AND `-shortest` (328's rule: the container's claimed length is the uploader's).
    **CRF 18, not the research's 30**, measured here: at 30 the picture cost 22 kbps but a 10-px bar's chroma
    (4:2:0) came out up to ~20 levels off the poster (the amber went yellow, the grey blue); 18 holds the bars
    within ~6 levels at ~120 kbps. **The sound (D6a):** AAC 256k at 48 kHz, fitted to `SOCIAL_MAX_BYTES` as
    the video Light is — (95 % of the cap × 8 / DUR) − the picture's allowance, now **160k** (measured ~120),
    clamped 96k–256k (328's floor; a long clip keeps a 96k card past the cap) — or the sound AS IT IS
    (`-c:a copy`, `transcode.AudioLightCopies`) when the file the card is made from (the Full when there is
    one, the stored original otherwise) is already AAC in ≤ 2 channels and its bytes plus the picture's
    allowance fit 95 % of the cap. An MP3 is always re-encoded: the card's verifier takes AAC alone. The run
    checks the result as 328 did, now against 1280×720: exactly one H.264 stream at the frame's size, exactly
    one AAC stream, faststart, `-fs` not reached. **No loudness normalisation** (the research's §5.4: never
    Original or Full, which are faithful; the card none by default) — a decision the owner can reverse: a two-pass
    LINEAR `loudnorm` (measure, then apply) on the card's AAC only. The encode's seconds per minute of sound
    are logged (`encode_s_per_audio_min`); measured on the lane's CPU image at
    `APP_CPUS=1` (the lane stack's default): **28.5 s per minute of sound** (an 8-s MP3: 3.8 s; a 100-s 24/96 WAV:
    47.6 s), against the research's UNVERIFIED 3–9 s; it was 38 s before the encode was pinned to the worker's
    thread count (`-filter_threads`/`-filter_complex_threads`/`-threads`, erratum 215's rule — the audio argv
    of 328 had none). On the host's single thread the planar-RGB composite costs ~35 % more than a yuv one
    (6.7 s against 4.3 s a minute; x264 alone 2.9 s): the lever if the cost matters, at the colour price (d)
    measured.

    **(e) The card tags** (`meta.go`). For an audio clip `og:type video.other`, `og:video` the audiogram
    (`social.mp4`, unchanged), `og:image` the poster with `og:image:type image/png` and its measured
    1280×720, `twitter:player` as today, **plus** `og:audio` = `/api/clips/{id}/audio` and `og:audio:type` =
    the type `/audio` serves (`db.AudioPlayType`, now the ONE definition the route and the tag share: the
    stored original's type when it plays, the Full's by extension otherwise). iMessage reads `og:audio`;
    Discord ignores it (the research's §3/§4) — harmless. A video's inventory (§9.1's count) is untouched:
    the two tags are on an audio card only. `og:image:alt` / `twitter:image:alt` say what the picture is —
    `The waveform of the audio clip: {title}` (`The waveform of an audio clip` untitled) — rather than "a still frame". The
    component embed's Media Gallery item is the audiogram exactly as a video's is its card file, and
    `CardReady` is the audiogram's readiness (it is made inside the run that flips `ready`).

    **(f) The page, the embed and the library.** The share page's picture above the `<audio>` is the poster,
    in a frame (`.audio-wave`) carrying `data-peaks` (the row's hex) and `data-wave` (the geometry,
    `1280,720,80,160,1120,400,10,6,10`, from transcode's constants — app.js has none of its own); app.js
    (`setupWaveform`) lays the same 70 bars over it as an SVG in the played colour and clips it with
    `clip-path: inset(0 X% 0 0)` from `timeupdate`/`seeked`, the edge running across the band exactly as the
    audiogram's does — the card's audiogram, on the page, with no library and nothing fetched. A row with no
    readable peaks renders no attributes and no layer. It also sets `navigator.mediaSession.metadata` (the
    title, and the poster URL on our own origin as artwork) so a phone's lock screen shows the clip — local
    JavaScript, no call anywhere. **The embed** (`/embed/{id}`) plays the AUDIOGRAM (`embedVideoURL`: the card
    copy at `/video.mp4`, not the `/audio` the share page plays) in the same `<video>` with the waveform
    poster — the decision the brief left: it keeps the embed's one shape, the overlay with its face at ready
    and its hiding while playing (erratum 274), where `<audio>` + the poster would have needed a second embed
    layout. The library's tile is the poster.

    **(g) A defect in 328, found by this erratum's E2E and fixed here.** Every STEREO MP3 was refused 415 by the
    strip's own proof: ffmpeg's mp3 muxer writes its own Xing/Info frame and, for a stereo stream under
    `+bitexact`, fills its LAME field with the bare string `Lavf`, which ffprobe reports as the stream's
    `encoder` and `CheckStripped` refuses (328's step 103 used a mono MP3, which gets none). The frame must stay
    (it gives a VBR file its duration and its seeking), and the string is the muxer's own with no version —
    the uploader's `LAME3.100`/`Lavc61.19` is already gone — so `hasEncoderTag` now treats exactly `Lavf` on an
    mp3 stream in an mp3 file as structural; any other value, or `Lavf` anywhere else, is still refused.
    Pinned by `TestStrippedStereoMP3IsNotAName` and, on real ffmpeg, "a stereo mp3 strips".

    **What was taken from the research and what was not.** Taken: the shape ("draw it in Go, ffmpeg does the
    motion"), the streamed s16le peaks, the stencil over a sliding field (filtergraph 2), the palette, the
    1120×400 band, the two passes, `-t DUR`, 30 fps and the 5-s GOP, `-map 0:a:0`, the strip flags and
    bitexact, the copy-when-AAC, no loudnorm, the page's two layers with `clip-path`, the Media Session.
    Built rather than dropped in: BBC `audiowaveform` (a GPL binary in the image for a picture Go draws),
    `mdlayher/waveform` (archived), wavesurfer.js (the page needs 40 lines, not a library), the ffmpeg
    `showwaves*` and spectrum family (stock visualisers, off-palette, and `showwavespic`'s memory). Not taken:
    filtergraph 1 (the filters-only poster: no rounded bars, gaps or minimum height), the research's CRF 30
    (above), `-tune stillimage`/`animation` (the picture moves; neither measured better), a time readout, the
    voice-message `waveform` (D5c, NOT built — the same peaks would serve it), `/api/clips/{id}/peaks.json`
    (no new route: the peaks ride the page).

    **Pins** (each failed with its change reverted, then restored). internal/transcode `waveform_test.go`: the
    bar heights of a steady sine (all 255), silence (all 0), a sine then silence (35 full, 35 empty), a
    saturated +3 dBFS float and the most negative sample alone (all 255 — `a = -a` on an int16 fails it), a
    −40 dBFS sine at 26 (dropping the floor makes it 255); streaming byte by byte and a 4,000× understated
    length in bounded memory; the geometry; the rasteriser (a bar's centre grey, the gap ink, a silent bar a
    DOT, an antialiased cap); the poster IS the stencil over the rest colour within one level everywhere; the
    mark in the bottom-left margin, ink-left on the first bar, ≈55 px, green span (dropping it fails); the PNG
    poster with no text chunk; the hex form; the PNG label argv (and a JPEG's unchanged). `audio_test.go`:
    the audiogram argv — the filtergraph verbatim, `-t … -shortest`, CRF/GOP/30 fps, BT.709, `-map 0:a:0`,
    the copy branch (no `-ar`), the thread pin —, the fitting with the 160k allowance, `AudioLightCopies`, the
    stereo MP3's `Lavf` (dropping the allowance fails it).
    `audio_ffmpeg_test.go` on real ffmpeg: the peaks of a linear ramp rise; the audiogram passes the card
    verdict (one H.264 1280×720 at 30 fps, one AAC, faststart, no tag), lasts the sound within a frame, frame 0
    inside the last bar is the poster's grey, half way an early bar is amber and the last still grey, near the
    end a late bar is amber; a 44.1 kHz AAC is carried as it is; the labelled poster is still a PNG with a
    plate. internal/worker: the row's peaks, the `.png` poster under `image/png`, the peaks read once before
    the encode, the poster drawn from the 70 bars with the mark and the duration; a WMA's AAC Full copied into
    the card, an MP3 re-encoded; the checkpoint carries the peaks. internal/httpapi: `poster.jpg` serves the
    PNG as `image/png` (a video's stays `image/jpeg`); the row keeps the bars. internal/web: the audio card's
    tags (`og:audio`, `og:audio:type`, `image/png`, 1280×720, the waveform alt; no `og:audio` on a video), the
    component embed's gallery item, the page's `data-peaks`/`data-wave` and Media Session attributes (none
    for a malformed row), the embed playing the audiogram.

    E2E step **104** (`104-audiocard.sh`, parallel; the suite is 104 steps / 35 bundles), on fixtures it makes
    itself in its own context directory (an MP3 with tags and a cover, a WAV 24/96, a 28.8 MB WAV, all with a
    rising envelope): the poster a PNG of 1280×720 under `image/png` with no tag; the audiogram through
    `probe_check` (the video Light's checks of 62-tiers), no tag, the sound's length within a frame, frame 0
    the poster's grey and a played bar amber; the big WAV's audiogram under 25 MiB; the card tags with
    `og:audio`; the page's 70 peaks; the component embed's gallery item; the embed's `<video>`. Visual
    (`scripts/lib/visual.js`, phase 6): `watch-audio` (both themes, both widths), `watch-audio-played` (the
    amber layer clipped to 60 %, asserted) and `library-audio` — eight shots, the pass is 111.

330. **The bot redraws a link whose card was not ready when it posted; `Changes saved.`** (run 8 follow-up lane
    `latecard`, 2026-10-08; the owner's test of release cycle 4, 2026-10-08 00:15Z, on clippet.gg in a real server, an
    `/upload` of a 4:11 WAV). Amends erratum 325 (b), (c) and (d); the word amends errata 318 (b) and 320 (d).

    **Why.** The log:

    ```
    00:15:25 discord bot: /clip command=/upload clip=TSRk4eW0SYJZ card_ready=false took=36.163s
    00:15:27 audio card copy encoded clip=TSRk4eW0SYJZ encode_s=30.62 encode_s_per_audio_min=7.3
    00:15:29 clip ready clip=TSRk4eW0SYJZ
    ```

    The bot waited its card budget (`captureWait()`, through `awaitCardReadyCtx`), posted the bare link with
    `card_ready=false`, Discord read the page two seconds before the audiogram existed, and the message stayed a
    bare link: Discord never reads a URL again by itself. DEPLOY §30.5's "Discord's own retry picks it up" was
    false (the crawler hold of erratum 213 keeps a crawler off a card that is not ready; it brings nobody back).
    An audiogram costs ≈7 s per minute of sound on the reference box (erratum 329's encode, libx264 on the CPU)
    after the Full, so most music lands this way; a long video whose Light copy outruns the budget was always the
    same race.

    **(a) What is held.** internal/notify's `linkTable` (erratum 325) now holds a link for every reason its card
    may still change — a form job's link for the title, and ANY link posted while `IngestResult.CardReady` was
    false: `/upload` with or without the form, an old `/clip file:`, Enrich's upload (the deferred reply, held as
    `@original`, the message `editOriginal` writes), and — through the new `DiscordBot.HoldReply(token, clipID)`
    — the type-4 reply of `/clip link:` or Enrich on a link to a clip whose card is not ready (`postClip`, before
    the response is written; access-log field `card_ready=false`). A link owed nothing is not held. The table is
    keyed by clip and holds every link of it (the upload's and a `/clip link:` of it are two), the same bound
    (`linkTableMax`, 256 links) and the same life (`linkLife`, the token's fifteen minutes from the command); a
    restart forgets it. Each reason redraws a link at most once; a link owed nothing more leaves the table.

    **(b) The worker says when a card becomes ready.** `worker.Deps.CardReady func(clipID string)`, wired in
    serve.go beside the clip webhook (erratum 319), to `Bot.CardReady` only when the bot exists — nil is a no-op
    that reads nothing. `w.cardReady` re-reads the row (under the exit budget, surviving a cancelled context)
    and calls the hook only when `db.CardReady` is true; the bot decides whether anything is owed, so a card
    reported ready twice redraws nothing twice, and a clip nothing of the bot's waits on costs one map lookup (a
    DEBUG line). Never a poll. The sites, from what `db.CardReady` reads — the state, the poster, `light_state`,
    the card file: `runJob` once a job of a kind that writes one of them has ended (`cardInput`: `transcode` —
    the ready flip, FinalizeTranscode, which is also where an audio clip's audiogram lands —, `social` — SetSocial,
    and its skip, lost-race and capped-failure endings through SettleTierEncoding / FailAttempt; the post-hoc Light
    copy of erratum 211 is such a job —, `poster` (SetPoster), `full` (SetFull), `trim` (SwapRendition) and
    `replace` (SwapSource), the last three because they may re-promise a card copy), deferred so it runs after
    the job's own commit and, for a transcode, after the run has left the registry; and `repairOnce` after it
    repairs a job of one of those kinds (a card copy failed at its cap settles `light_state`, erratum 236). The
    boot reconcile is not a site: the bot's table is empty after a restart. A gif, a filmstrip, a notify and a
    hook job write nothing the card reads. The hook runs on the worker's goroutine and must not block —
    `Bot.CardReady` takes a lock and starts one goroutine of the Bot's own, counted for Shutdown.

    **(c) The redraw is counted.** Discord ignores an edit whose content is unchanged, so `redrawQuery` is now
    `redrawQuery(v)`: the first redraw of a clip's links is `?v=2`, the next `?v=3`, … — one counter per CLIP
    while any of its links is held, so two messages of one clip never get the same URL for different pages. A
    late card then a late title (or the reverse) is two PATCHes, `?v=2` then `?v=3`. A redraw asked for while the
    post is in flight is made by the job once Discord answers (`after_post`), as in 325 (b). The page ignores any
    `v` (325 (c), pinned for `v=3`); `ParseShare` reads past it.

    **(d) Never.** No card redraw for a link whose card WAS ready at post (nothing is owed), for a duplicate's
    answer (erratum 326: never held, deferred or form), after the link left the table (fifteen minutes, or a
    restart — then the link stays bare, and a later paste of it draws the card).

    **(e) Logs.** `discord bot: card redraw clip=<id> reason=card|title outcome=edited|failed|none|after_post|restart|panic`
    (`reason=card+title` for one edit owed both while the post was in flight); `none` for a card is DEBUG.

    **(f) The word.** The owner, 2026-10-08: "Saved." must not read as "the video is saved" — `Changes saved.`
    (the reviewed case) is the answer of the upload form's submit and of `/settings`' modal (`msgSaved`, one constant);
    the variants "Saved without the tags. …" are unchanged. DEPLOY §30.4 ("Discord draws a card once per link"),
    §30.5 (the false sentence replaced, the form's words) and §30.9, API.md's interactions table, E2E step 85's
    `bt_answer saved` and comments follow.

    **Pins** (each failed with its change reverted, then restored). internal/notify `bot_latecard_test.go`: a held
    `/upload` link — deferred (`@original`), on a managed bot, and the form's follow-up — whose card becomes ready
    is PATCHed once to `?v=2` with `reason=card outcome=edited`, a second word edits nothing; a ready-at-post link
    is never PATCHed (deferred or form); a late card then a late title is `?v=2` then `?v=3`, and the reverse; a
    duplicate is never held; a card ready during the post is redrawn after it; `HoldReply` PATCHes `@original`
    once; a shut-down bot says `restart` and a new bot holds nothing; the table holds every link of a clip, each
    at its own version; the table's bound and expiry (rewritten for the new table). internal/worker
    `cardready_test.go`: the hook at the ready flip, when a promised card copy's job settles (and not before), after
    a repair settles it, never for a failed clip, and no hook reads nothing. internal/httpapi: `/clip link:` and
    Enrich hold a not-ready clip's reply (token and clip) and never a card-ready one or a refusal; the whole path
    through a real `notify.Bot` (the link posted before the card, `CardReady` → `?v=2`, a late title → `?v=3`, two
    PATCHes); `/clip link:` of `?v=3`; `Changes saved.` byte for byte. internal/urls `ParseShare` of `?v=3`.
    internal/web `TestRedrawQueryLeavesTheCardBare` for `v=2` and `v=3`. No migration, no new E2E step.

331. **The tiered test system: T0 on every commit, T1 once per lane, T2 when it is owed, T3 after a deploy** (run 9,
    2026-10-08; lanes `t0`, `gatestack`, `retry`, `select`, `settle`, `pool` and `tiers`; `scripts/t0.sh`, `scripts/t1.sh`,
    `scripts/select.sh`, `scripts/gate.sh`, `scripts/smoke-public.sh`, `scripts/lib/{gocheck,gatestack,transient,e2e-registry,
    sleeplint}.sh`, `scripts/lib/navretry.js`, `scripts/check.sh`, `scripts/e2e.sh`, every drop-in header, `internal/worker` and
    `internal/transcode` (two seams); §16.3 and erratum 245 amended). Until this run there was one tier, and it was the
    expensive one. Every change paid for `check.sh` (the whole Go suite twice, once under `-race`), the full E2E through the
    public edge on https://clippet.gg, and 111 screenshots. Two investigations of gates 2–28
    (the toil investigation's report and proposal) counted 70 attempts. 42 of them failed, and only 2 of those failures
    were product defects. Gate 28 alone held the box exclusively for 52 minutes, for one 25-file lane. The owner's picks, in
    order:
    - 1a: fixes 1 → 2 → 3 first.
    - 2a: the full suite only for a release, a shape change or a nightly slot.
    - 3a: `-race` in T2 and the nightly only.
    - 4a: the rest in the proposal's order.

    (a) **T0 — every commit, no stack: `bash scripts/t0.sh`** (lane `t0`). It runs, at once:
    - `gofmt -l` over every Go file git knows.
    - `go vet`, with and without `-tags ffmpeg`, on the CHANGED packages (`T0_BASE`, default `main`).
    - `go test -tags ffmpeg ./...` through `scripts/lib/gocheck.sh`, in the Dockerfile's `testdeps` image. The checkout is
      mounted read-only and the named volume `clippet-gobuild` is Go's build and test cache. `CHECK_JOBS` defaults to 4.
    - `check.sh CHECK_ONLY=cheap`: every stage but the Go one, including the E2E self-test and the sleep lint (h).

    It prints one line per step and `T0 PASS|FAIL` last. Three things were deleted from the default path:
    - `-count=1` and the cold container. A fresh container had no cache, and that was the only reason they existed.
    - `-race`. `CHECK_RACE=1` races `GOCHECK_RACE_DEFAULT`: the twelve packages whose non-test code starts a goroutine,
      runs a ticker loop or holds a mutex its callers share. `CHECK_RACE=all` races every package. A list races that list.
    - The duplicate pass. With a race pass, the two passes are complementary: a raced package's untagged tests run only
      under `-race`, and only its tagged-only tests run in the `-tags ffmpeg` pass. The only tests in both are the two whose
      own body reads `raceDetector`.

    The shards are now a function of the tree and the committed `scripts/lib/go-weights.txt`, never of `CHECK_JOBS`. A
    shard's `-run` expression is part of Go's cache key, so T0 at 4 jobs and check.sh at 16 share one cache. `CHECK_ONLY=<ids>|cheap`
    and `CHECK_DIR` are new knobs on `check.sh`. `gocheck.sh --selftest` is a stage of it.

    **Measured** (lane `t0`'s logs):
    - An unchanged tree: 122 s cold → **30 s** cached, all 63 shards answered `(cached)`.
    - Tests per default run: 3451 (1702 race + 1749 tagged) → **1749** in one pass.
    - `CHECK_RACE=1`: 1751.
    - A diff that reaches `internal/httpapi`: 67–99 s at 4 jobs. The ≤ 60 s target holds for a quiet, unchanged tree, not
      for a diff that fans into httpapi. A comment-only edit stays cached, because Go keys a result on the linked binary.

    (b) **T1 — once at a lane's end, ≤ 5 min, on the lane's OWN stack: `bash scripts/t1.sh`** (lane `tiers`). The steps, in
    order, each on one line with its seconds:
    - **select**: `scripts/select.sh` over the diff against `T1_BASE` (default `main`), plus the working tree.
    - **t0**: the whole of T0.
    - **race**: `-race` over the changed packages ∩ `GOCHECK_RACE_DEFAULT`, through gocheck.sh with that list. Skipped, and
      said, when the intersection is empty.
    - **tagged**: T0's one pass is `-tags ffmpeg`, so the tagged tests already ran there. With a race pass, gocheck's
      complementary plan runs the raced packages' tagged-only names again in its `-tags ffmpeg` half.
    - **cross**: the windows/amd64 cross-compile, when a `cmd/` file or a `*_windows.go` file changed (run 10, lane
      `nits10`: whenever any Go file, `go.mod` or `go.sum` changed — 2 s image + 2–4 s build warm; cleanup row Run 9 R8).
    - **e2e**: `E2E_ONLY=<the selection>` on the lane stack.
    - **visual**: `VISUAL_ONLY=<the phases of the touched pages>` when `web/` or `internal/web/` changed.
    - **down**: `down -v` of the lane stack, but only when t1 found it down and brought it up. `T1_KEEP=1` keeps it.

    `T1 PASS|FAIL` is the last line. The selection decides how far T1 goes:
    - **A shape path** stops T1 before anything runs, with `this diff needs T2: <path>`. That is `compose*.yaml`,
      `Dockerfile*`, a migration, `internal/config/**`, `internal/store/**`, `cmd/clippet/serve.go`, the harness core
      `scripts/e2e.sh` / `scripts/lib/*`, or `go.mod`/`go.sum`. No slice of the suite proves a shape change.
    - **`all`** (a CORE, uncovered or unknown path) runs the whole suite after a warning and its estimate.
    - **`none`** runs no bundle.

    Knobs:
    - `T1_WHY=1` prints every path's reason.
    - `T1_ONLY=<bundles>` is a fixer's slice: it replaces the selection.
    - `T1_VISUAL=<phases>|none|all` overrides the page map.

    T1 refuses (exit 2, before anything runs) in these cases:
    - The compose project is `clippet`, `clippet-dev` or `clippet-gate`. A checkout with no `.env` resolves to
      `compose.yaml`'s `name: clippet` and is refused too.
    - `PUBLIC_BASE_URL` is not a loopback origin of the lane's own, or uses port 8480, 8481 or 8576.
    - `COMPOSE_ENV_FILES` is set.

    `T1_SELFTEST=1` pins every one of these decisions against planted inputs, and check.sh's stage `t1` runs it.

    **Measured** on this lane's stack (`clippet-tiers`, :8581), each run from its own planted diff:
    - A comment in `internal/notify/bot_redraw.go` selected `./internal/notify` and `85-bot` alone. `T1 PASS` in **147 s**: t0 35 s, race 19 s over 91 tests, `85-bot`'s `E2E PASS (PARTIAL)` 83 s with the stack brought up from nothing, then the stack and its image removed (160 s on the run before).
    - A docs-only diff selected `none` and ran in **35 s**. The first run on a new tree took 65 s, with 16 of 63 shards still to fill Go's cache.
    - A whitespace change in `compose.yaml` stopped at once with `this diff needs T2: compose.yaml`, in **1 s**.
    - For scale: latecard's lane paid 380 s plus gate 28's 3144 s. The proposal estimates ≈ 2.5 min for the same diff
      under T1.

    (c) **The change map and the namespace registry** (lane `select`; R3 and fix 6). Every drop-in carries two more header
    lines within its first 60, right after its schedule markers. The format:

        # e2e-namespace: account=<suffix>[,…]|- prefix=<VARPREFIX>[,…]|- buckets=<auth|upload|uploadip|view|poll|bot|claim>[,…]|-
        # e2e-covers: <glob> …        (one or more lines, over internal/ cmd/ web/)

    `scripts/e2e.d/CORE` lists the product files every bundle stands on, and a change to one selects `all`.
    `scripts/e2e.d/GO-ONLY` lists the files no bundle proves, each with the Go test that does (or `@cross-compile` /
    `@not-built`), and a change to one selects nothing. The E2E self-test now refuses:
    - a duplicate, core or malformed account suffix, or one that is minted but not declared;
    - a duplicate prefix, a prefix that starts another bundle's, or a declared prefix the file never uses;
    - a variable assigned inside another bundle's prefix;
    - two bundles draining one bucket without `apart`;
    - a non-test product file that no row covers;
    - a glob that matches no file.

    `bundle_account` now registers only a suffix its bundle declares. Four renames were needed to pass: 104-audiocard
    `AC_` → `AG_`, 33-account `D_PASS` → `AC_DPASS`, 51-admin `BK_NAME` → `AD_BKNAME`, and the core's `T_EXP*` →
    `TTL_*`. Gate 27a's `_ac` collision is the class this closes. `select.sh` prints `T2 | all | none | a,b,c`. `--why`
    gives each path's reason, `--go` gives the packages, and `--plan` gives everything. The bundles come out longest first
    by the last recorded run.

    (d) **Retry once, by policy, with a reason log** (lane `retry`; R4). `scripts/lib/transient.sh`'s
    `transient_sig <log> [ctx]` reads a pool bundle's log from its last `[e2e] FAIL step` line. It answers one signature,
    or nothing:
    - `curl-7/28/35/52/56`, when that curl was the failing request.
    - `edge-502` or `edge-520…524`, only with the edge's own evidence: a cf-ray, `server: cloudflare`, or Cloudflare's
      error body.
    - `pw-closed`, `pw-reset` or `pw-timeout`.
    - `docker-125`.

    An assertion's `got 'NNN'` is never classified. A classified failure re-runs that bundle ONCE, in the same run, with
    `E2E_ATTEMPT=2`. `bundle_user_` then mints `e2e_<epoch>2_<suffix>`, which is still inside erratum 272's sweep
    regex. The retry leaves a record:
    - The first attempt's log is kept as `bundle-<stem>.1.log`.
    - `.e2e/retries.txt` gets `stem, signature, first-attempt seconds, utc`.
    - The closing banner always prints a `retried:` line.

    A second failure is a failure, and an unclassified one is never retried. `E2E_RETRY=0` turns the policy off. The
    visual pass retries a navigation once on the same Playwright signatures (`scripts/lib/navretry.js`; `VISUAL_SELFTEST=1`
    tests both with no browser). This replaces the old "recreate the tunnel, rerun". It was proven on injected
    bundles: all four signatures were retried once, and an assertion's `got '200'` was not. It costs the E2E self-test
    4–6 s.

    (e) **The gate on a stack of its own, and the key-diff rule** (lane `gatestack`; fix 2 and fix 7). `bash
    scripts/gate.sh` with no `BASE` is T2. It runs on the compose project `clippet-gate`:
    - `http://localhost:8576`, with MinIO on :9576.
    - `MEDIA_DELIVERY=redirect` against that MinIO, and the gpu flavour as production runs it (`GATE_GPU=0` drops it).

    - Its own `.e2e/gatestack/<project>.env`, made from `.env.example`'s active lines plus the gate's values, with the
      production secrets blank. The checkout's `.env` is never read for values.

    Stage 0 is the **key-diff**: the gate refuses to start when a key the reference `.env` sets is missing, or when an
    undeclared key is extra. Only names are compared, nothing right of the `=`, so the gate stack cannot quietly be a
    different shape from what it claims to prove. Stage 1 passes `CHECK_RACE=all`. The visual pass runs only when `web/`

    Phase 4 of the visual pass was 121 s of a watch whose stop condition never fired. It now ends 1.5 s after the embed

    (g) **The settle hook and the stall clock: two seams, nil in production** (lane `settle`; F1/F2, R1/R2).

      LAST in `runJob`, as the first `defer`: after the card hook, the untrack and every log line of the run. It is also
      called after `repairOnce`'s summary line for each repaired row. A nil hook is a no-op, and a panicking hook is one
      log line.
    - `transcode.EncodeOptions.StallClock`, a `Clock{Now; NewTimer}` with `Timer{C; Stop; Reset}`. Nil is the wall
      clock.

    `cmd/clippet/serve.go` sets neither. The worker tests wait on the settle (`h.until`, `h.awaitJob`, `h.settledAfter`)
    instead of polling the wall clock. The stall tests feed progress through a FIFO and advance a fake clock, so they
    have no sleep and no wall budget. `TestPosterIsCancelledSynchronously` checks the instant the run has SEEN its cancel.
    It passes at `-cpu 1,2,4,16`, which makes the GOMAXPROCS cap of lane `pool` safe. Each seam is pinned by a mutant:
    - the settle moved before the untrack;
    - the settle moved before `Repairs.Record`;
    - `stallDisableFrac=1.01`;
    - Cancel not waiting for the run.

    - transcode 4.7 → 0.5 s.
    - The four named worker tests at `-race -count=50`: 162 → 87 s.

    `time.Sleep(` in tests:

    - sweeper 2 → 1

    Store's 9 stay, each the subject of its test.

    (j) **When each tier is owed.**
    - **T0**: every commit.
    - **T1**: once, at a lane's end. It is the lane's whole proof. A lane no longer runs `check.sh`, a full E2E,
      `visual.sh` or `gate.sh`.
    - **T2**: only at a release (DEPLOY §17.4 step 1, `GATE_RELEASE=1`), for a shape change (T1 says so), in the nightly

332. **The audio card's bars are loudness, not peaks** (run 10 lane `wave`, 2026-10-08; the owner's look at the card of an
    unmastered heavy EDM/dubstep WAV: a short quiet intro, then every one of the 70 bars full — "is this waveform really
    just full fat?"). It was: 329(a) drew each bar as the PEAK sample of its slice over the clip's peak, and a bar of a
    4-minute track is ≈ 3.6 s, inside which heavy electronic music — mastered or not — has a near-full-scale kick or snare,
    so every bar after the intro was full. Peaks answer "did anything clip here"; the card answers "where is the music
    loud", which is the ENERGY of each slice — the picture a DAW's overview or SoundCloud's draws. No migration, no new E2E
    step.

    **(a) The measure** (`internal/transcode/waveform.go`). `PeakWriter` keeps, per fine bucket, max |s| (kept, not drawn:
    the reading a clipping indicator or a peak-based near-silence test would want), the SUM OF SQUARES of every sample of
    every channel as an exact `uint64`, and how many samples that sum holds. One square is at most 32768² = 2^30, a merge
    adds two halves' sums and counts, and a bucket holds at most the stream's samples ÷ 4,096 (a merge leaves 4,096 buckets
    of the new size behind it), so a bucket cannot overflow below 2^34 samples — 2^46 samples a clip; a bar's sum, which spans many buckets, is taken in `float64`. `Heights` draws each
    bar's RMS, √(Σs² ÷ n), over the clip's loudest BAR's (not sample's), the divisor floored at `rmsFloor` = **−30 dBFS
    RMS** (1,036): 329's −20 dBFS peak floor moved down by the ≈ 10 dB a loud bar's RMS sits under its peak (the brick
    fixture measures 6–11 dB, a sine 3 dB), so the same material is floored at the same loudness — a −40 dBFS
    tone draws at 41 % of the band, a −60 dBFS RMS hiss at 13 %, nothing quiet is stretched to full. The share is drawn
    through a perceptual curve, **h = 255 × (rms ÷ top)^0.6** (`waveGamma`): a passage 20 dB under the loudest is a
    quarter of the band instead of a tenth, so a quiet intro reads as quiet, not as silence. The alternative, a 40 dB
    decibel scale, was rendered beside it on the brick fixture: it lifts the intro further (a third of the band) but
    flattens the loud bars — a breakdown 4 dB under the drop drew 223 against 247, where the gamma draws 180 against 234 —
    and a rising sound's top bars land within a level of each other. A bar of pure silence is still 0, the dot 329(b)
    draws.

    **(b) The antiphase row** (the cleanup row `[audio/card] the peaks pipe downmixes with -ac 1`). `PeaksArgs(in, channels)`
    decodes STEREO (`-ac 2`, interleaved) when the probe reports two channels or more (a 5.1 source to its stereo pair) and
    mono otherwise; the writer counts FRAMES into buckets and sums the energy of every sample of both channels. A downmix
    sums L and R, so a file whose channels are each other's negative (karaoke tricks, "8D" mixes, some vinyl rips) mixed to
    silence and drew a dotted line under an audible clip; the RMS over both channels is the mono mix's only when they are
    correlated. The buffers are the same size.

    **(c) The overstated-duration row** (the cleanup row `[audio/card] a container that grossly OVERSTATES its duration`). The
    bucket was sized from the probed length's share of 4,096; a container that overstated it gave a few huge buckets and
    every bar repeated one. The bucket now starts at ONE frame and doubles whenever the 8,192 slots fill — the claimed
    length is never read (`NewPeakWriter(channels)`): any clip past 4,096 frames ends with 4,096–8,192 buckets after
    ⌈log2(frames ÷ 8,192)⌉ merges of 4,096 buckets each (15 for an hour at 48 kHz, ≈ 61 k bucket moves against the hour's
    173 M samples). The memory is still bounded by `peakFineBuckets`. A WAV cannot overstate on ffmpeg 7.1 (its demuxer
    measures a data chunk that outruns the file from the file's size); a FLAC's STREAMINFO total is believed, so the
    fixture is a FLAC.

    **(d) What stays.** The payload (70 × uint8, `clips.peaks`, `data-peaks`; the name `peaks` stays), the drawing (329(b):
    the geometry, the palette, the poster, the stencil, the audiogram), the page and `app.js`. EXISTING audio clips keep
    their stored bars and their encoded cards: no migration, no recompute, and `admin` gets no verb (a later lane if the owner
    wants the live clips redrawn).

    **(e) The pins.** `internal/transcode/waveform_ffmpeg_test.go` makes three fixtures with lavfi: `edm.wav` (20 s: 2 s of
    a −30 dBFS sine, then a 20-ms full-scale 50 Hz square burst every 0.25 s — every 0.29-s bar holds one — over a −6 dBFS
    bed that falls to −18 dBFS from 10 to 14 s): the intro's bars are under 40 % of the band, the brick's are NOT all
    ≥ 250 and the breakdown's are under the drops' lowest (the peak reading: every bar after the intro 255);
    `antiphase.wav` (stereo, R = −L): every bar > 200 (the peak reading: 0); `longheader.flac` (a 10-s rising tone whose
    STREAMINFO claims 3,600 s): 70 distinct bars (the peak reading: 12, in steps). Untagged: `TestPeakWriterStereo` (the
    `-ac` per channel count, antiphase = in phase = full bars, a frame never split across buckets) and 329's pins moved to
    the new reading (`TestWavePeaksPinnedHeights`' −40 dBFS tone is 104, not 26). E2E step 104 uploads `edm.wav` and reads
    the bars the page draws (`data-peaks`): the intro under every brick bar, the brick not all full.

333. **Clippet Auto on the box: the instance watches its own Discord server** (run 14 lane `autobox`, 2026-10-11; the owner's
    decision of ≈20:30Z: the Durable-Object gateway in clippet-pass `rescue/` is NOT shipped — an outbound WebSocket on a
    Durable Object is evicted every 15 minutes and nobody runs a gateway bot that way). Auto becomes a feature of the
    clippet server itself — the box each operator already runs — and later the SAME Go code runs as one hosted process on a
    VPS for paid users who want zero setup. Off by default; a different thing from §30's bot (DEPLOY §30.10). No
    migration, no new E2E step.

    **(a) The configuration** (`internal/config/discordauto.go`). `DISCORD_AUTO_MODE=off|prompt|auto` (unset = off),
    `DISCORD_AUTO_TOKEN` (the bot token of an application the OPERATOR made — the §30 app itself, or a new one beside
    `DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN=managed`; never `managed`; the bot token's charset; a secret, redacted in `String`/`LogValue` and
    registered with the doctor's redaction), `DISCORD_AUTO_SECONDS` (5–60, default 10), `DISCORD_AUTO_NOTICE=on|off`
    (default on). With the mode UNSET the other three are orphans (a boot error naming the variable); `off` WRITTEN OUT is
    a deliberate off — the token may stay and nothing reads it. prompt|auto needs §30's bot configured (own or managed):
    Auto acts only in servers `admin bot bind` bound, and fetches through that bot's fetcher. With off the binary builds
    no client, starts no goroutine and opens no socket.

    **(b) The package** (`internal/autobot`, usable by a hosted process: it imports nothing of this repository). Four
    seams: a `Dialer` and a `Caller` (built in `internal/notify/auto.go`, still the one package that builds a network
    client, §15), a `Host` (`Bound`, `Applicable`, `Upload`; `internal/httpapi/autobox.go`), and the clock. The gateway
    (`gateway.go`): `GET /gateway/bot` (the IDENTIFY budget, read before the first IDENTIFY and before every IDENTIFY
    that follows a session that did not hold; logged; at zero, waited out), the socket on
    `?v=10&encoding=json` with no compression, IDENTIFY with GUILDS | GUILD_MESSAGES | MESSAGE_CONTENT (33281), the
    heartbeat on Discord's interval with the first beat jittered and an un-ACKed beat a zombie, op 1 answered at once,
    RESUME on op 7 and on a dropped socket (closed with 4000 so the session survives), op 9 waited 1–5 s then RESUME or a
    fresh IDENTIFY, IDENTIFYs never closer than 5 s and a daily ceiling of its own — never more than 500 in any 24 h,
    the next one waited until the window rolls (Discord terminates every session and RESETS the bot token past 1000 a
    day) —, failures backed off 1 s → 5 min doubling, where an op 9 or op 7 on a session that did not hold is a failure
    too and only a session that HELD resets the backoff (it reached READY or RESUMED and lived 60 s: an op 9 loop, a
    READY → op 9 loop and a READY → drop → RESUME → op 9 loop each settle at one cycle per 5 min, ≤ 288 IDENTIFYs a day,
    where the build's first cut sent ≈17,000 — the fix pass's finding F1), three failed opens in a row forget the resume URL, 4004/4010–4014 and a REST 401 HALT (logged once; nothing
    reconnects until a restart), a clean 1000 on shutdown. The REST manners (`rest.go`): Discord's buckets learned from
    `X-RateLimit-Bucket/Remaining/Reset-After` per route key; an exhausted bucket and a global limit are waited out; a 429
    is waited `retry_after` and tried ONCE more; no wait longer than 60 s. The library is `github.com/coder/websocket`
    v1.8.15: pure Go (no cgo, so the static binary and the Windows cross-compile stand), zero dependencies of its own,
    context-first, concurrent-write-safe, and its dial takes an `*http.Client`, so the socket rides notify's one
    construction site (no redirect followed). The URL is checked by `config.ValidGatewayURL` (wss; `gateway.discord.gg`
    or a regional `gateway-….discord.gg`; no userinfo, port, path or non-ASCII) before every dial — the §15 list gains
    that one host family, named by Discord itself.

    **(c) The modes** (`modes.go`; `brief-auto2.md`'s design, ported from `rescue/src/dispatch.ts`). Only MESSAGE_CREATE
    and INTERACTION_CREATE are read; the guild id first, and a guild NOT BOUND here is dropped with nothing else read and
    nothing logged. A bot's message, a webhook's and our own are ignored; "applicable" is POST /in/auto's own rule
    (`autofetch.go`: the instruction grammar, the CDN allowlist and attachment path, a video or a sound, under
    `MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES`), the first applicable attachment of the message. **Prompt**: ONE reply under the video — no text,
    one button `Upload to Clippet` (custom id `auto:go`), `fail_if_not_exists`, no ping — deleted after
    `DISCORD_AUTO_SECONDS` unless pressed. A press by the poster or Manage Server / Administrator → `Uploading…` to the
    presser alone → the upload → the link posted as the bot's own NEW message → the original deleted → the reply deleted,
    in that order, each once; anyone else gets `Only the poster or someone with Manage Server can do this.`. **Auto**: no
    reply; the upload, the link, the original deleted. The original is never deleted unless the link posted. **The
    notice**: `Videos posted here become Clippet links.` as one `-# ` subtext line under the link, unless
    `DISCORD_AUTO_NOTICE=off`. **Manage Messages**: a 403 on the delete is never retried — Prompt says `Clippet Auto needs
    Manage Messages to remove the original.` to the presser (a follow-up, ephemeral), Auto says it to the channel once a
    day per server. A failed upload tells the presser the bot's own sentence for it (`notify.Sentence*`) or `That video
    could not be uploaded.`; Auto logs it. One upload at a time per server, at most 10 waiting; the 11th is a log line.
    Why the reply is visible: Discord's Create Message takes only SUPPRESS_EMBEDS, SUPPRESS_NOTIFICATIONS,
    IS_VOICE_MESSAGE and IS_COMPONENTS_V2 as flags, and EPHEMERAL is "only visible to the user who invoked the
    Interaction" — a message the bot posts on its own has no invoker, so it cannot be ephemeral; it is short-lived
    instead.

    **(d) The two doors, one function.** A press arrives as INTERACTION_CREATE on the socket when the Auto app has no
    Interactions Endpoint URL, and at `POST /api/discord/interactions` when it has one (the §30 app used for both).
    `autobot.(*Auto).Press(ctx, raw)` is the ONE function: it answers the callback body and a start func the door runs
    once the answer is delivered (the socket: after the callback route answered 2xx — a press whose answer did not reach
    Discord uploads nothing; the endpoint: after the response is written). A press on a reply this process does not hold
    (a restart forgot it) is acknowledged and the reply removed. Only a reply authored by the bot user READY named, of
    the application READY named, in a bound guild, is acted on.

    **(e) The upload** (`internal/httpapi/autobox.go`, `autofetch.go`'s `fetchAttachment`, now shared): the SAME job POST
    /in/auto/{token} runs, in-process — the bot's fetcher (Discord's two CDN hosts, https, no redirect, the declared size
    as the truth), the bound account, its link defaults, charged to its upload bucket (this door has no route limiter) —
    and the link is `URLs.Page(id)`. The fetch job's log lines name the tag `gateway`.

    **(f) The doctor** gains `auto` (18 checks): off calls nothing; on, ONE read-only probe — `GET /users/@me` answers

334. **Hosted Clippet Auto: one process on Fly.io, dispatching to the boxes** (run 14 lane `autohost`, 2026-10-11; the owner's
    decisions of ≈23:30Z: the host is Fly.io — one `shared-cpu-1x` 256 MB Machine, the free stopped standby, Fly's
    shared egress IP first and a static one only if Discord ever bans it —, the account is the owner's company's, nice
