    run once for every server that turned Auto on in the official bot's `/settings`, as `cmd/clippet-auto` — a second
    binary, built by clippet-pass `autohost/` from a clone at a tag (the product's Dockerfile and release are
    unchanged). The clippet-pass `rescue/` Durable-Object Worker is DELETED; its sealed URL and its instruction live on
    here. No migration, no new E2E step: `cmd/clippet-auto/**` and `internal/notify/autohost.go` are GO-ONLY rows (their
    unit tests are the proof); `internal/autorule/**` joins `101-autofetch`'s map.

    **(a) The configuration** is the environment and nothing else — no file, no volume: `DISCORD_AUTO_TOKEN` (the Auto
    app's, `222222222222222222`), `AUTO_PLANE_URL` (the claim Worker's `/claim` base, https), `AUTO_PLANE_SECRET` (the
    bearer of its `/auto` routes), `AUTO_SEAL_PRIVATE` (the P-256 private JWK that opens the sealed URLs; the claim
    plane's `AUTO_SEAL_PUBLIC` — both renamed from `RESCUE_SEAL_*` — holds the public half), `AUTO_LISTEN` (`:9091`,
    internal), `AUTO_DEADMAN_URL` (optional, https), `AUTO_LOG=json|text` (json). A missing secret is exit 2 with the
    variable named; `String` prints no secret. `GOMEMLIMIT` defaults to 200 MiB in code on the 256 MB Machine.

    **(b) The rule in one place** (`internal/autorule`, new). The instruction type, its grammar, THE decoder POST
    /in/auto/{token} runs (`Decode`: one object, no unknown field, nothing after it, the grammar; the body cap comes back
    as `*http.MaxBytesError`), the attachment-URL rule and `IsMedia` moved out of `internal/httpapi` (`autofetch.go`'s
    type is now an alias; `isMedia`, `discordAttachmentURL` and `duplicateAllow` call through), and `Applicable` — the
    grammar, the URL, a video or a sound, at most a cap. The hosted process applies `config.DefaultMaxUploadBytes` (the
    4 GiB default, now a named constant `MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES` reads) because it cannot read a box's own value; the box
    answers its own 413 past a lower one.

    **(c) `internal/autobot` gains the hosted seams, the box's behaviour unchanged with them zero.** `ModeGuild`: every
    server's mode, seconds and notice come from the Host (`GuildSettings.Settings`, asked after `Bound`); a Prompt reply's
    timer and a link's notice are the server's own. `Config.Sessions` (a `SessionStore`): the session — `session_id`,
    `seq`, `resume_gateway_url` and the newest message id seen — is read once as `Run` starts and written on every change
    at most once a second and once more as `Run` ends, so a restarted or standby process RESUMEs (Discord replays the
    gap; a RESUME costs none of the 1,000 IDENTIFYs a day); with a store a shutdown closes the socket 4000 (resumable),
    never 1000. `Config.Backfill`: after a fresh IDENTIFY (no session, or a RESUME refused), each bound server's channels,
    as its GUILD_CREATE lists them and read only after `Bound` says yes, are read back with `GET
    /channels/{id}/messages?after=…&limit=50` from the newest message seen or ten minutes back, whichever is later, and
    what is found goes through the live path; a message id is acted on once (a backfill never repeats a live one; the
    dedupe runs only with a store or a backfill, so the box is unchanged). `Config.Observer`: told each gateway moment
    (identify, resume, up, down, reconnect, beat, ack with its round trip), each decision (video, offer, press, link,
    backfill — with the guild, the channel and the original's id, the mode, the outcome and the upload's duration),
    each 429 from Discord's REST and the queue's depth; never a token, a URL, a file name or content.

    **(d) The plane-backed Host** (`cmd/clippet-auto/plane.go`). `Bound` = `GET /auto/guild/{id}` says Auto is on there
    with a route; the answer — on or off — is cached 60 s, so a change in `/settings` is seen within a minute (plus KV's
    own propagation); a plane that stops answering keeps the last answer it gave, a server never asked is off.
    `Applicable` = autorule's. `Upload` = the sealed URL opened for (guild, route host) — never cached —, its shape
    re-checked against the CURRENT route (https, that host, no port, query, fragment or userinfo, `/in/auto/ca_` + 43,
    printed back exactly), the instruction POSTed (`notify.HostedClient.Box`: two headers, `content-type` and
    `user-agent: clippet-auto/1`, never an Authorization, no redirect, 110 s over headers and body, 8 KiB read and only
    for 200/201/403/502), and only a root share link of the route's own host is posted (`https://<host>/<1–64
    [A-Za-z0-9_-]>`). The box's refusals become the presser's line — run 7's settled words: 404 `This server's Clippet
    Auto URL no longer works. Set it again in /settings.`, 403 in the box's envelope `…is from the wrong account…`, 413,
    415, 429 `This server's Clippet has hit its upload limit. Try again later.`, 507, 202 `Still uploading…`, no answer
    or a 5xx `This server's Clippet did not answer.`, anything else `That video could not be uploaded.`; never a retry.
    The seal (`seal.go`): blob `0x01 ‖ ephemeral P-256 (65) ‖ IV (12) ‖ AES-256-GCM`, key HKDF-SHA256(ECDH, salt
    ephemeral ‖ recipient, info `clippet-onepress-v1`), AAD `v1|<guild>|<host>`, base64url ≤ 1024, shape-checked first;
    `crypto/ecdh` + `crypto/hkdf` — this file opens and cannot seal.

    **(e) Presses** arrive on the socket: the Auto app has NO Interactions Endpoint URL (clippet-pass `autohost/README.md`
    says so); a press while the process is down fails with Discord's "This interaction failed", which the standby makes
    rare. A halt (4004/4010–4014, a REST 401) does NOT exit: a restart would IDENTIFY into the same refusal, so the
    process stays up with `/healthz` at 503 and says why once.

    **(f) Observability** (the owner's ask). One JSON line per decision on stdout — `ts`, `level`, `event`, `guild`,
    `channel`, `msg_id`, `outcome`, `ms` (and the mode) — beside autobot's own lines; never a token, a message's text, a

    only while Discord's REST reads answer.

    **(g) Three more destinations, in `internal/notify/autohost.go`** (still the one package that builds a client, §15):
    the plane (the bearer, 10 s, 64 KiB), a box (above) and the dead-man (a bare GET, 10 s). Every transport failure is
    one error with no URL in it.

    **(h) Pins** (each fails with its change reverted): `cmd/clippet-auto` — the instruction's exact shape through

    **Amended 2026-10-12 (lane `autofix`, the audit of the live process;
    no new env name, the box's behaviour unchanged — every change below is behind a hosted seam, or touches only
    malformed input or memory).** **F1** a failed session Save backs off — `SaveEvery` (1 s), doubling, at most
    300 × `SaveEvery` (5 min), a 2xx resets it, one WARN per failed try (with `retry_in`), never one per tick; a Save the

    admits them — clippet-pass `forward/src/claim/auto.ts`, which must be DEPLOYED FIRST: the old one answers the new

    `GET /users/@me` + `GET /applications/@me` once through the REST manners — so a RESUME-started process acts on a

    waits for that call when there is none. **F4** the hosted client has its own transport (`newHostedTransport`):
    no proxy, response headers ≤ 64 KiB, TLS handshake 10 s, response headers 110 s, dial 10 s, and a dialer `Control`
    that refuses any resolved address that is not public — loopback, RFC 1918, IPv6 ULA (Fly's 6PN), link-local,
    CGNAT, 0/8, unspecified, multicast — for the plane and a box alike. **F5** the REST route keys are pruned (past 256,
    at most once a minute: every bucket whose reset has passed, every route left pointing at nothing). **F6** `GET
    /auto/guilds` (read before the first IDENTIFY, then every 5 min) pre-filters `Bound`: a server not on a list
    younger than 15 min makes no GET of its own; a message from an unlisted server re-reads the LIST at most once a
    minute for the whole process, so a server that just turned Auto on is still seen within the minute. **F7** every id
    in a REST path is a snowflake and an interaction token carries no `/ \ ? # %`, space or control byte, checked
    before the call. **F8** a panic in one upload ends that job, not the process (`runRecovered`). **F10** `GET
    /auto/guilds` is read up to 1 MiB (≈ 10,000 servers, the plane's own ceiling); every other plane answer keeps 64
    KiB. F9 (digest pins), F11 (by design, (f)) and F12 (inherent) are not this amendment's. Pins: `internal/autobot/
    autofix_test.go`, `internal/notify/autohost_test.go`, five in `cmd/clippet-auto/auto_test.go`; each was seen
    failing with its fix reverted.
    **Amended 2026-10-12 (lane `autonits15`):** a waiting Prompt reply reads its server's settings again when its

    **Amended 2026-10-15 (lane `autoroute`):** `auto_guilds_bound` counts `GET /auto/guilds`' additive `routable` list

    **(amended 2026-10-19, lane `autoskip`; route by person, the reviewed build spec §3, signed off by the owner):** `GET
    /auto/guild/{id}`'s record gains `skip` — the server's members who route their uploads to their own box, as

    `autobot.Settings.Skip`. Each answer REPLACES the set (the 60-s cache holds it with the rest of the record; never

    metric) — never the poster's id. A poster put on the list while his Prompt reply waits uploads nothing: a press

    `TestUnlistedPosterActs`, `TestSkipDroppedLetsNextThrough`, `TestSkipAddedWhileAReplyWaits`) and

    replaces —, `TestSkipDecisionIsDebug`).
    **(amended 2026-10-26, lane `nits22`; the cleanup list's run 15a N1/N2, run 14 the backfill's one-second double):** the
    session's last writes. `Shutdown` saves the session FIRST — synchronously, whatever the debounce or the backoff —
    right after it cancels, before it waits for any job, and again after the jobs only if it changed; `Run`'s own last
    save (`flushLast`) writes only a session that differs from the last one a Save wrote, so a stop with nothing moving
    writes it ONCE (it could write twice: Shutdown's, then `flushLast`, which wrote whenever a session was held). Since
    `last` moves when a video is SEEN, a clean stop — even one whose upload runs past Shutdown's context, after which
    the hosted process exits — never leaves the last second unsaved for the next start's backfill to act on again; the
    double remains only for a process that DIES inside the 1-s debounce. The act's save (`savedAfterAct` as an upload
    job ends) runs in a tracked goroutine off the server's upload queue, so the server's next upload never waits
    behind a Save to the plane (up to 5 s); refused once Shutdown began, which saves what changed itself. Pins:

    of every REST READ — each GET: the backfill's channel reads, `/gateway/bot` before a socket, the identity fetch on a
    RESUME. A read FAILED when it did not complete or answered anything but 2xx; a 429 is the REST manners' own wait
    and counts as neither. Each 60-s tick (`restReads.tick`) withholds the ping when the minute held a read and its
    LAST one failed, pings when the last one answered, and still pings a minute with no read at all (idle is healthy);

    failed` (`event=deadman outcome=withheld`) on the first withheld tick, one INFO `dead-man ping resumed`
    (`outcome=resumed`) on the first ping after — never a line a minute. The WRITES (a notice, a delete, an
    interaction's answer) are left out: their refusals are facts about one server (a deleted message, a missing

    followed by idle minutes withholds ONE ping, which a dead-man's grace longer than a minute absorbs — the 347 (e)

335. **`admin storage migrate` between two buckets, with a manifest, a stop file and a byte cap; `/setup`'s steps-only view**
    (run 15 lane `migrate2`, 2026-10-12; ROADMAP #56, the owner's picks 1a–6a of the storage build brief §1).
    What changed for a user: the desktop app's Storage screen can move clips from one bucket to another while links keep
    playing, keep a copy on the PC, and open one provider's console steps — all through the product's own verb and page,
    and the product is never told the app exists. For a self-hoster the same verb gains bucket to bucket and three flags;
    every line it printed before keeps its exact shape. No migration. E2E step **105** (`105-migrate2.sh`, parallel;
    the suite is 101 steps / 42 bundles); 92-setup gains the steps view.

    **(a) Bucket to bucket.** `MIGRATE_S3_ENDPOINT`, `MIGRATE_S3_BUCKET`, `MIGRATE_S3_ACCESS_KEY`, `MIGRATE_S3_SECRET_KEY`
    (required together), `MIGRATE_S3_REGION` (default `us-east-1`), `MIGRATE_S3_FORCE_PATH_STYLE` (default false),
    `MIGRATE_S3_KEY_PREFIX` — read by **`config.LoadForMigrate` only** into `Config.MigrateS3`; `Load` never reads them,
    so `serve` and its doctor neither use nor mention them (`compose.yaml` passes the seven empty, erratum 292's rule, so
    a `.env` line is not inert). `--to s3` on an `s3` instance: with the four set the destination is that bucket, opened
    on S3's clock; with none set, today's refusal (`--to s3 is the store this instance already uses …`, exit 2); with
    some set, `admin storage migrate: --to s3 needs MIGRATE_S3_ENDPOINT, MIGRATE_S3_BUCKET, MIGRATE_S3_ACCESS_KEY,
    MIGRATE_S3_SECRET_KEY in this environment; <missing> unset` (exit 2). `--to fs` ignores them. The from line names
    the destination `s3 (<bucket> at <endpoint>)` — never a key. `MIGRATE_S3_KEY_PREFIX` unset is `S3_KEY_PREFIX`'s
    value (the brief said empty; changed because the database names every object by its whole key, prefix included,
    so a destination under another prefix holds objects the switched instance's rows do not name); a prefix of its
    own re-roots each key under it.

    **(b) `--manifest <path>`.** A text file, one line per verified object, `<key>\t<size>\t<sha256>`, appended after
    every `copied` and every hashed `skip` (a zero-byte object records the empty hash). On a re-run an object whose key
    is in the manifest at its size and whose destination `Stat` size matches is skipped WITHOUT hashing:
    `migrate: skip <key> size=N (in the manifest)`. A line for a key the plan no longer holds is ignored. A missing file
    is an empty manifest; an unreadable file or a malformed line is fatal, `admin storage migrate: --manifest <path>: …`
    (exit 2), before the plan — never a silent trust.

    **(c) `--stop-file <path>` and `--max-bytes N`.** Both are read BETWEEN objects (after one finishes, before the next
    starts, and before the first). The stop file is `stat`ed; `N` counts the bytes placed this run plus the bytes
    skipped, and the run stops before the object that would cross it (the copy stays a mirror of at most N). On either:
    `migrate: stopped reason=stop-file copied=N skipped=N bytes=N (H) failed=N remaining=N` / `… reason=max-bytes …`,
    exit **3**, nothing removed, no marker written; `remaining=` is the objects not yet attempted. A negative
    `--max-bytes` is the usage (exit 2).

    **(d) The steps-only view.** `GET /setup?view=steps&store=<id>` renders only the option's `Head` (+ `Caveat` as the
    head hint), the `<ol class="walk">` with its dated hints and `labels read <walksRead>` — no chooser, no Reached, no
    Now, no block, no `data-setup-cmd`, no STOP, no refusal, no Check now (the section is `data-setup-steps`, so app.js
    wires nothing). `view=steps` without a valid `store` renders the ordinary page. The gate is `/setup`'s own (`authed`,
    the zero-users exception) — nothing new is exposed. With `SETUP_WIZARD=off` (default `on`; set by the desktop app on
    every instance it runs, which does the setup there — the owner's call 2026-11-02, built 2026-11-03) every other `/setup`
    answers the ordinary 404 to everyone, before and after the first account, and `/settings`' Storage head drops its
    `where clips live` link, while this view stays as it is, behind the same gate (`TestSetupWizardOff`).

    **(e) The lines that stay exactly as today**: `migrate: from … to …`, the two plan lines, the NEVER line,
    `--dry-run: nothing was copied`, `copied`, the verified `skip`, `FAILED`, `done`, the `did NOT arrive verified` line
    + exit 1, `.clippet-store written in …`. Pre-run errors stay on stderr with exit 2 (`--to`, missing variables, the
    manifest) or `a.fail` exit 1 (a store that does not answer). The exit codes: 0 done, 1 failed, 2 refused, 3 stopped.

    **(f) One more row (the owner, 2026-10-12 ≈19:45Z).** The API-tokens Name field's placeholder for the Clippet Auto URL
    kind (`data-placeholder-autofetch`) read `Discord server` and was taken for a prompt for an id; it is
    `the server it is for`.

    **(g) Pins** (each fails with its change reverted): `cmd/clippet/admin_storage_test.go` — bucket to bucket (both
    stores named, no key printed, the source unwritten, the destination opened with MIGRATE_S3_*), the key prefix
    re-rooted, the three refusals, the manifest round trip (the second run makes no `GetRange` on either Fake), the
    manifest refusals, the stop file between objects, `--max-bytes` before the object that would cross;
    `internal/config/config_test.go` — `Load` never asks for a `MIGRATE_S3_*` name, `LoadForMigrate` reads all seven
    with their defaults and shapes, the four required together; `internal/web/setup_test.go` — `TestSetupStepsView`;
    `internal/web/inbound_test.go` — the placeholder.

    **(h) Windows paths (run 15d lane `uncpath`, 2026-10-14).** `absDir` (STORAGE_DIR, BACKUP_DIR) takes a UNC share
    (`\\server\share\…` or `//server/share/…`) beside the drive-letter path, held slashed with its two leading slashes

336. **No directory fsync on Windows; the `fs` store's ping takes a real object's path** (run 15 lane `winsync`,
    2026-10-15; the desktop app's first real Move of four clips from R2 to a folder on a Windows GPU box wrote every object at
    full size and reported every one `migrate: FAILED <key>: writing it to the destination: … Access is denied.`). On
    Windows `os.File.Sync` on a DIRECTORY handle fails with ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED (errno 5): the handle `os.Open` gives a
    directory has no write access and FlushFileBuffers refuses it. `syncDir` (erratum 276's directory fsync after
    PutFile's rename) forgave only EINVAL/ENOTSUP/ENOSYS/ErrUnsupported, so on Windows PutFile returned an error AFTER
    the object was in place — the Windows `fs` store (`STORAGE_BACKEND=fs`, the desktop app's This PC or a NAS home,
    errata 276 and 335) had never been able to write, while the doctor's `store` row read `writable`, because its ping
    only created and removed a temp file. Fix: `syncDir` is split by build tag — `internal/store/fs_sync_other.go`
    (`!windows`) keeps the body unchanged, so Linux behaves exactly as before; `internal/store/fs_sync_windows.go` is a
    no-op whose comment says why (NTFS journals the rename; the object's bytes are made durable by the temp file's own
    Sync before it). No other directory sync exists under `internal/` or `cmd/` (Download's rename, the ingest file and
    minio.go's spool sync FILES). The `fs` ping now renames its probe file inside STORAGE_DIR and runs `syncDir` on the
    root before removing it, so a store whose writes fail after the file is made fails `/readyz` and the doctor's
    `store` row (`… is not writable by this process`), whose words are unchanged. Proven on a Windows GPU box with a temporary
    `cmd/fsprobe` cross-compiled for windows/amd64 (PutFile, Stat, GetRange, DeleteKey on a scratch folder): main's code
    → `putfile … sync …\probe\abc: Access is denied.` with the 4096-byte object on disk; the fix → every step ok; the
    new ping over main's `syncDir` → `store: ping: STORAGE_DIR … is not writable: sync …: Access is denied.` The probe
    was deleted before the commit; a Linux test cannot show the Windows error, so the pins are `fs_test.go` unchanged and
    green and the windows cross-compile stage.

337. **A verified copy without the read-back; parallel parts; progress per byte** (lane `fastcopy`, 2026-10-16; the owner's
    2026-10-15 move of 1.2 GB from a folder on a Windows box to Cloudflare R2 through `admin storage migrate`). Three costs, one
    lane. (a) **One stream.** `PutFile` hands minio-go a TeeReader (the sha256 pass), which has no ReadAt, so every object
    over 16 MiB went up on minio-go's SEQUENTIAL multipart path — one 16 MiB part after another, ≈300 Mbps on that line.
    Now `PutObjectOptions{ConcurrentStreamParts: true, NumThreads: STORAGE_UPLOAD_THREADS, PartSize: 16 MiB}`: the
    buffers are filled from the stream one after another and uploaded at the same time, from any io.Reader, so the
    TeeReader is untouched. **`STORAGE_UPLOAD_THREADS`** (`internal/config`, `S3Config.UploadThreads`; default **6**,
    `1`–`32`, anything else a boot error naming it; a `compose.yaml` row and `.env.example`; DEPLOY §7's table; S3 only,
    `fs` ignores it; a bucket-to-bucket migrate's destination takes the instance's value with S3's clock). Memory is about
    N × 16 MiB per running upload, held only while it runs; `1` is minio-go's sequential path, the store before this
    erratum. `SendContentMd5: true` puts a Content-MD5 on every part and on the single PUT, so the provider refuses a part
    that arrived different at write time. **The watchdog, which this change would otherwise have broken:** on the
    parallel path minio-go's `Progress` hook sees the FILE being read into the part buffers, and with every buffer in
    flight the file is not read again until a part finishes — a 16 MiB part on a slow uplink would have tripped
    `STORAGE_IDLE_TIMEOUT` while bytes moved the whole time. `wireTransport` (minio.go) wraps the client's RoundTripper
    and touches the watchdog of the PutFile a request belongs to (carried on the request context) for every byte of
    request body sent; requests without it pass through. (b) **The read-back.** `migrateVerify` read every object back IN
    FULL through the destination and hashed it — the copied ones and the ones already there — 1.2 GB down for 1.2 GB up.
    Cloudflare's R2 documentation states its S3-API ETag rule, and AWS documents the same for plaintext and SSE-S3
    objects: one PUT's ETag is the object's MD5; a multipart object's is the MD5 of the concatenated binary part MD5s
    followed by `-N`, every part but the last the same size. B2's and MinIO's rules are not established by any document
    read. `internal/store/etag.go`: `ETagHasher` (an io.Writer beside the sha256 in the SAME pass), `ExpectedETag(r, size,
    partSize)`, `UploadPartSize` (= the store's 16 MiB; an object of exactly one part is a single PUT, minio-go's own
    threshold), `NormalizeETag`, `ETagMatches` (empty never matches). `store.PutResult` gains `ExpectedETag` and
    `StoredETag` (the provider's answer to the write) and `Verified()`; `fs` leaves both empty (erratum 276: no ETag). The
    `Fake` now answers the S3 shape from Stat/List/PutFile, and `Fake.OpaqueETags` makes it answer each object's sha256 —
    the shape of a provider with no documented rule, and what the Fake reported before. **The migrate's rule,
    provider-agnostic:** after a copy, the destination's `Stat` ETag equal to the one predicted from the scratch copy's
    bytes (the pass that took the sha256) verifies the object with no read-back; otherwise today's full read-back runs. An
    object already at the destination at the same size: the SOURCE is read once for the manifest's sha256 and the
    expected ETag together, the destination is HEADed, a match skips it verified without reading the destination, a
    mismatch is today's read-back (and a hash mismatch still falls through to a re-copy). A provider whose ETag is not
    MD5-shaped — or an object uploaded earlier at another part size, or a directory — simply never matches and is read
    back, which is the safe side. MD5 is adequate for what this defends against (a part that arrived different between
    two of the operator's own stores); the sha256 is still the object's identity and the manifest's format is
    unchanged. NO `x-amz-checksum-*` work: R2's HeadObject returning one is not documented, and minio-go's `Checksum`
    option needs `TrailingHeaders`, whose acceptance by R2 is not established. **Measured on MinIO**
    (`minio/minio:RELEASE.2025-09-07T16-13-09Z`, the `-tags integration` test on a throwaway container): the 40 MiB
    parallel upload's ETag `…-3` and a 70 kB single PUT's both MATCHED the prediction (PutObject's answer and StatObject's
    alike), so on the bundled MinIO the migrate takes the ETag proof too; nothing depends on that. (c) **Progress per
    object only.** The migrate passed `nil` progress to Download and PutFile. Now `migrate: progress <key> <bytes>/<size>`
    prints on stdout at most once a second per object (the admin's clock, `migrateProgressEvery`) and once at the end of
    the leg with `<bytes>` = `<size>` unless the last line already said it; never the same number twice. ONE leg per
    object — the one that crosses the network: the write into a bucket, or the read out of a bucket into a directory
    (bucket to bucket, the write) — so an object's bytes only ever grow; a skip prints none. **The contract** (the desktop
    app reads these lines; DEPLOY §32.3 lists them): `migrate: progress <key> <bytes>/<size>`, `migrate: copied <key>
    size=N sha256=H (etag proof)` / `(read back)`, `migrate: skip <key> size=N (already at the destination, verified
    sha256=H) (etag proof)` / `(read back)`; `skip … (in the manifest)`, the mismatch line, `FAILED`, the plan, `done` and
    `stopped` lines are unchanged. Pins: `internal/store/etag_test.go` (the expected ETag against the formula written out
    independently — empty, single, exactly one part, one byte past it, exactly three parts, five plus a remainder — chunked
    writes, the literal MD5 of `hello`, a short stream refused; `ETagMatches`; the Fake's two shapes);
    `internal/store/minio_parallel_test.go` against a fake bucket speaking the multipart API (two parts in flight at once,
    every part's Content-MD5 matching its bytes, the object reassembled, the prediction equal to the ETag the bucket
    computed; the single PUT's Content-MD5; `STORAGE_UPLOAD_THREADS=1` one part at a time; a slow uplink over an
    unbuffered net.Pipe that outlasts the idle timeout without the wire pausing for it); `internal/config` (the default,
    `1`, and `0`/`33`/`six` refused by name); `cmd/clippet/admin_storage_test.go` (copy and skip on the ETag proof with
    zero destination reads and one source read per skip; `OpaqueETags` → every skip and the copy read back; the progress
    lines and the throttle; the bucket-to-bucket destination's thread count); `storage_fs_test.go` (into a directory:
    the read leg's progress line, every copy read back). The E2E's `105-migrate2` exercises the proof against the stack's
    MinIO and now covers `internal/store/etag.go`; no line an E2E bundle pins changed.

338. **The harness runs on WSL** (lane `wslgate`, 2026-10-18; the owner's push: stop fighting Git Bash's process cost and
    move the harness). On the Windows GPU box Git Bash spawns one process in ≈45 ms (500 × `/bin/true` = 22.8 s)
    and WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04 on ext4 in ≈1.3 ms (0.65 s); the E2E, check.sh's cheap stages and two load-dependent timing pins were
    one disease. The Docker daemon, the GPU, the volumes and the image cache are the SAME from either side (Docker Desktop's WSL
    integration), so nothing about a stack moves — only the host the harness's processes start on. (a) **The re-run.**
    `scripts/lib/wslexec.sh` (POSIX sh: `t0.sh` sources it under dash): `scripts/gate.sh` (gate mode only), `t0.sh` and `t1.sh`
    typed in Git Bash re-run themselves inside WSL when `MSYSTEM` is set, `CLIPPET_WSL` is not `0`, `CLIPPET_IN_WSL` is unset,
    `wsl.exe` is on PATH and WSL's home holds the clone (`CLIPPET_WSL_CLONE`, default `dev/clippet`; `CLIPPET_WSL_DISTRO`, default
    `Ubuntu`); otherwise they run where typed, with a one-line note on Git Bash. The call is `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 wsl.exe -d Ubuntu
    --cd ~ --exec bash -l <the checkout's wslexec.sh via /mnt/c> wsl-enter …`, backgrounded and waited on so a trapped INT/TERM
    is relayed (`wsl-kill`: TERM to the run's own process group, `setsid -w`, whose EXIT traps then run — gate.sh now traps TERM
    and INT into `exit` for that reason). Values cross only by NAME through `WSLENV` (`GATE_*`, `E2E_*`, `CHECK_*`, `VISUAL_*`,
    `T0_*`, `T1_*`, `SELECT_BASE`, `PW_VERSION`, `CLIPPET_VERSION`, `BASE`). (b) **The same commit.** The invoking checkout must
    be clean (`git status --porcelain`; refused otherwise — WSL runs the commit, never a working tree; the owner's open pick between
    "refuse" and "a snapshot commit" for t0/t1 defaulted to refuse); WSL detaches the clone, mirror-fetches
    `+refs/heads/*:refs/heads/*` and the tags from the Windows repo (so WSL's `main` IS the Windows main for select.sh, the
    T0/T1 base and the visual decision), refuses a commit it cannot see (one on no branch or tag), and detaches the run directory
    at it, asserting HEAD and a clean tree. The run directory: the clone for the gate; a detached worktree of it named after the
    invoking checkout's folder for t0/t1 (`clippet-<lane>` under the WSL clones' folder; `clippet-main` for the main checkout,
    never the gate's clone). A lock per run directory (`flock -n`) refuses a second run; a Git Bash gate (`CLIPPET_WSL=0`) refuses while a WSL gate
    holds the clone. (c) **The `.env` files.** The reference `.env` (the Windows main worktree's — production's secrets) is NEVER
    copied into WSL (the lane's review, G1: the first build copied it into the clone on every t0/t1, which never read it,
    and left a byte-equal copy `0755`). The gate reads it IN PLACE over `/mnt/c`: `wsl-enter` exports
    `GATE_REF_ENV=<main worktree>/.env`, which `gatestack.sh keys` and `gate-key`'s `env=` read by name only, so a
    `release-cycle --bump-env` edit is what the next gate sees. The clone's own `.env` is a GUARD, rewritten on every run kind
    (mode 600, no secret): `COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME=clippet-never`, `CLIPPET_IMAGE`/`CLIPPET_GPU_IMAGE` of that name and
    `PUBLIC_BASE_URL=http://refused.invalid` — compose.yaml's `name:` is `clippet`, so without a project line a bare compose there
    IS production; with it, a project nobody runs, and `clippet-app:local` is never re-tagged. gate.sh's `envfile` reads the
    guard's origin as "this checkout's stack", so its mode stays `gate`; check.sh's stage 01 there validates compose.yaml alone
    (the reference's COMPOSE_FILE names the tunnel file, whose token the guard does not carry). `GATE_REF_ENV` and
    `GATE_WIN_ROOT` never cross WSLENV (wsl-enter sets both). A lane checkout's `.env` is copied into its WSL worktree (mode
    600) when its `COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME` is a lane's own (`clippet-<lane>`, never `clippet`, `clippet-dev` or `clippet-gate`);
    no value is printed. (d) **The records.** gate.sh's LAST act in WSL is a silent copy of the run's `.e2e/gate-<utc>/` and, on GATE PASS, of
    the `.e2e/checkpoints/gate-green.txt` THIS run wrote (`commit=` HEAD, `proved=` not before the run's start) into the Windows
    checkout that typed the command — so clippet-pass's release cycle (`cd <clone> && GATE_RELEASE=1 bash scripts/gate.sh`, its
    `tail -1` = `GATE PASS`, and `--gate-cached` reading the record and `<dir>/gate.log`) needed no change; a copy failure is on
    stderr and fails the gate; on FAIL only the dir goes back; `GATE_COPY_VISUAL=1` copies `.e2e/visual/`. `gatestack.sh gate-key`
    reads the same tree (git objects) and the same key names from either side, so the Windows checkout's key equals the record's.
    Every other checkpoint (durations, the Go stage's, the E2E resume) is the WSL side's memory. (e) **What inside WSL refuses.**
    gate.sh's own and foreign modes (a BASE other than the gate stack's): the gate's clone is a scratch clone, never a
    stack — refused before anything is made. The guard `.env` keeps a bare `docker compose`, `e2e.sh` or `visual.sh` there off
    project `clippet`, but the only ways in remain gate.sh (COMPOSE_ENV_FILES) and t1.sh (a lane worktree's own `.env`).
    A relayed TERM/INT ends gate.sh through its EXIT trap: it first waits (≤ 120 s) until no other live member
    of its process group is left — the E2E's own EXIT-trap hand-back RECREATES the app, and the first build's teardown ran
    under it and left the app, the network and two volumes up (G4, measured) — then the gate stack is torn down, a `GATE FAIL
    … ended by TERM` line is said, and the run's `.e2e/gate-<utc>/` is copied back; t0.sh/t1.sh remove their testdeps image and containers on
    a signal in three passes, because the TERMed `docker run` client can leave the daemon's create to finish after the first
    `rm` (G3, measured). (f) **The Linux branches.** A root container's directory in a
    WSL bind mount cannot be removed by the user (measured): `gocheck.sh` chowns its `/out` back at exit (`GOCHECK_CHOWN`, passed
    by check.sh, t0.sh and t1.sh on Linux), the visual container chowns `/out` after the pass, and `E2E_CLEAN=1` removes a
    root-owned entry through busybox instead of dying under `set -e`. Under WSL's mirrored networking a closed loopback port TIMES
    OUT (curl 28) instead of refusing (curl 7): the three readiness polls (gate_ready_, gs_ready_, t1's) are bounded per curl and by
    the clock, `curl__` carries `--connect-timeout 10`, and the smoke self-test waits 20 s for its stub's port, refuses an empty port
    by name and bounds its curl (the cold first WSL check.sh hung >3 min there). **Linux's pipes lose a race Git Bash always won**:
    `dc config | grep -q …` and an `awk … exit` / `head -1` on compose's output give SIGPIPE 141 under pipefail when the reader
    leaves early — the first WSL gate's step 1 died of it; the config is now read whole and searched as a here-string
    (`dc_config_has_`), and 20-pages' `dc logs | grep -q` poll likewise. `lane-teardown.sh` removes the lane's WSL worktree too
    (`wsl-teardown`, refused while a run holds it). (g) **ffmpeg 6.1.1** (Ubuntu's) builds every fixture; the 11 testclips' ffprobe
    summaries equal the 7.1.1-made ones and the 104 brick is byte-identical (the survey); the stack-side comparisons were proven by
    this lane's gate (below). No binary was added. (h) **Measured (2026-10-18, this PC).** The gate typed in Git Bash as the release cycle types it (`GATE_RELEASE=1 bash
    scripts/gate.sh` in the lane worktree): GATE PASS in 484 s wall (481 s inside WSL: check 11 s — the Go stage skipped on the
    checkpoint its first attempt proved in 42 s with `-race` over `./...` —, the E2E 360 s for 41 bundles with no retry and 2802 app
    log lines with zero ERROR/panic, the visual pass 106 s for 111 shots), against 927 s at gate 41 (its record) and the 983 s on Git Bash the same day
    (check 85, E2E 879, no visual); the Windows checkout's `gate-key` equal to the copied record's, line for line. T0 on one tree,
    warm: 18 s typed in Git Bash (re-run in WSL; 14 s inside) against 91 s with `CLIPPET_WSL=0`; `CHECK_ONLY=cheap` check.sh 11 s;
    the E2E self-test 12 s, its pool pin's third slot starting 0.01 s after the first against a 4.5 s window (three runs). The
    host-ffmpeg-sensitive bundles (41-social, 43-watch, 62-tiers, 67-capture, 103-audio, 104-audiocard) passed on 6.1.1.
339. **The register notice names the instance's host** (lane `regline`, 2026-10-18; the owner's sentence, signed off verbatim).
    `/register` with registration closed said `Registration is closed. Ask the operator for an account.` — on a Pass name or a
    friend's box "the operator" names nobody a visitor knows. It now reads `Registration is closed. Ask whoever runs <host> for
    an account.`, where `<host>` is `urls.Builder.Host()` (erratum 268's: PUBLIC_BASE_URL's host and port, no scheme; config
    clears the path) carried as `authPage.Host` from `register()` — no second parser. The `<noscript>` hint and `/login`'s
    `Accounts are made by the operator.` are unchanged (not signed). Pinned by `TestRegisterClosedNamesTheHost`
    (internal/web/web_test.go: a Pass-shaped host, `clips.example`, `localhost:8481`, the whole `<p>` asserted).
340. **The fetch measures itself and the `Uploading…` line counts the bytes** (lane `fetchline`, 2026-10-19; the owner's go,
    the design is option a of run 17's review decision; the sentence is the owner's, signed off).
    A 263 MB `/upload` took 64 s, ≈55 s of it ONE GET from Discord's CDN, and said nothing while it ran; no line measured
    the fetch alone (`took=` is the whole job). (a) **The GET** in `fetchAndIngest` (shared with Clippet Auto, erratum
    324) sends `Range: bytes=0-` and accepts a 200 or a 206 whose `Content-Range` starts `bytes 0-` (the whole file, so it
    streams exactly as a 200); any other status is still `SentenceFetch`. A cold miss on `bytes=0-` is today's full pull.
    (b) **The line.** The body is wrapped in a counting reader (`fetchMeter`, under the size guard's LimitReader), and ONE
    Info line is logged when the fetch ends, success or not: `discord fetch bytes= seconds= mb_s= proto= status=
    accept_ranges= ttfb_ms= clip=` — `seconds` to the body's end (the spool, probe and card wait after the last byte are
    not Discord's), MB = 10⁶, one decimal; `proto` is `resp.Proto`, `accept_ranges` the header ("" when absent), `clip`
    only when known. Never the URL, never a header that could carry a signature. It decides whether a parallel ranged
    fetch (option b) is worth building: only on `status=206` with `accept_ranges=bytes` on a real ≥ 100 MB upload.
    (c) **The count.** `runClip` hands `fetchAndIngest` an edit; while the body runs a goroutine fed by the meter edits
    every five seconds (the first at five, never sooner) — the form's private `Uploading…` follow-up by its id
    (`PATCH …/messages/{id}`, once Discord has named it; a tick before that passes), the deferred path's `@original` — to
    exactly `Uploading… 120 of 263 MB`: received and declared size (the response's length when Discord stated none) in
    whole MB, 10⁶ bytes — the decimal unit the storage line's GB is (internal/cost); the web's sizes are binary MiB and
    are not this sentence —, never past the total; no rate, no time, no percentage. One attempt per edit, no retry; a
    refused edit (a 429 among them) makes the next tick rest; the fetch never waits on an edit; the goroutine stops when
    the body ends and is joined, its edit in flight cancelled, before the job's last message, so no count lands after
    the link; the delete of the line and the link's edit are unchanged. Clippet Auto gets the line and no edit (nobody
    waits). One edit per five seconds is an order of magnitude under any per-route bucket the bot has met. (d) **Docs.**
    DEPLOY §30.4's "10 MB without Nitro" is the reviewed sentence without numbers; §30.5 names the count; §30.7 a row for the
    line. **Pins** (internal/notify `bot_progress_test.go`): `TestFetchLineOn200And206` (the Range asked; 200, 206, a 206
    elsewhere and a 403, each one line with its fields and no URL, signature, file name, guild or token),
    `TestProgressSentence`, `TestWatchFetchCadenceAndSkip` (the ticker is a channel the test feeds: one 5 s ticker
    asked, no edit before a tick, the exact sentence, the tick after a 429 rests, nothing after the body ends),
    `TestUploadingLineCountsTheBytes` (the follow-up edited by its id, a 429 fails nothing, the link posted and the line
    deleted), `TestDeferredCountEditsOriginal`, `TestAutoFetchLogsAndNeverEdits`; `TestFetchFailureIsOneWordOnTheLog`
    now reads the status off the fetch line and keeps it off the job's. No E2E change: the fake Discord in steps 98 and
    101 has no network, so no fetch gets a body to count.
341. **`/signin` — the bot is the door** (lane `signin`, 2026-10-19; the owner's go; the design is option a of run 17's
    review decision on logging in to a Pass box). Erratum 302 made Sign in with Discord "a second key to an
    existing door, never a door" because a passwordless account had no recovery story and the only Discord identity on offer
    was OAuth — the box's own application, a portal walk per owner, impossible on a Pass box. **302's "never a door" is
    AMENDED:** the door is the bot's signed interaction, never OAuth and never the plane. A `/signin` is Discord's own Ed25519
    signature over a body that already carries the guild, `member.user` and `member.roles`, verified by the BOX (on a managed
    box the forwarder relays bytes it cannot forge, erratum 279) — the plane gains no power to mint a login, which is why the
    brokered option ("the plane vouches") stays rejected. The recovery story 302 said was missing is (e) below plus Discord's
    own account recovery. (a) **The command.** `/signin`, no options, a FIXED name (`config.SigninCommandName`, pinned
    against internal/notify's registration; the three configurable chat names may not take it), published by `admin bot
    register` beside the four (the official bot's forwarder registers it in clippet-pass). From a signed interaction: a
    server, not a DM, and a BOUND one (the other commands' refusals, word for word); then the mode (c); then, under
    `role:<id>`, the role among `member.roles`. Then ONE token, `cs_` + 43 base64url (`ids.SigninToken`, 256 bits), stored
    as its sha256 with the guild, the member's id, username and display name (`global_name`, else the username) and an
    expiry of 300 s (migration **0023**, `signin_tokens`; the expired rows go when the next is minted). The answer is
    ephemeral + SUPPRESS_EMBEDS (flags 68) and exactly `Sign in to <host> · this link works once, for five minutes.` and,
    on its own line, `<PUBLIC_BASE_URL/login/discord/cs_…>` (`<host>` = `urls.Builder.Host()`, erratum 339's helper).
    Refusals, ephemeral: `Discord sign-in is off on this Clippet.`; `This server limits sign-in to a role you do not
    have.`; the unbound line. Nothing of the member and never the token on the log (`discord=signin signin=link|off|no_role`).
    (b) **The link** (internal/web `signin.go`, at `auth.SigninLinkPrefix` + the token). GET renders the login page's shape
    (the wordmark, `Sign in to <host> as <name>`, one primary `Sign in`) and CONSUMES NOTHING — Discord's crawler fetches
    what a bot says (erratum 316), so a GET must be free of effect; `Referrer-Policy: same-origin` (not `no-referrer`,
    which would send the form's POST with `Origin: null`). The form's POST refuses a cross-site caller (the CSRF rule's two
    headers, `auth.CrossSite`, with no session to compare: a forged POST would sign the victim into the forger's account),
    then consumes the token in one transaction (of two POSTs exactly one wins) and requires the guild still bound. Then the
    account whose `discord_user_id` is the member's is opened; if none, one is CREATED in the same statement that links it:
    the Discord username normalised to §14 (lowercase, `[a-z0-9_]`, every other character `_`, 3-32 bytes) and suffixed
    `_2`, `_3`… on a collision — `_`, not the brief's `-`, because `-` is outside §14's charset and the password form could
    never type it — with NO password (the empty hash bcrypt refuses every password against, so the password login answers
    it with its ordinary `invalid_credentials`). A username match is never a link. The session is a password login's:
    `auth.CreateSession` + `auth.SetSessionCookie`, the same row, cookie, TTLs and Signed-in browsers row; the browser
    lands on `next` (safeNext) or `/`. A used, expired or unknown link lands on `/login?discord=link`: `That sign-in link
    expired. Run /signin again.` (a `loginNotices` key shown only while the door is open). The route is the 404 page unless
    the door is open — the bot configured AND a Discord mode — so a token minted before a restart into another mode opens
    nothing. `httpx.LogPath` writes the path `/login/discord/{token}` and a `cs_` run anywhere as `{token}`. (c) **The
    modes.** `REGISTRATION` gains `members` (any member of a bound server) and `role:<id>` (one role id, a snowflake checked
    at boot); `/register` and `/login`'s `Open` read both as closed; the boot line names the mode; `admin doctor`'s
    `login` row has a first line for `/signin` (on, or off with the mode, or a WARN for a Discord mode with the bot off);
    `/login` carries `Members of the connected server: /signin in Discord.` under the form when the mode AND the bot are
    on. A member who leaves keeps the session until it ends (`admin sessions revoke` sooner) and their clips; the box

342. **A person-scoped server binding — route by person, the box's half** (lane `person`, 2026-10-19; the owner's sign-off of
    run 17's reviewed spec, with the member's command renamed `/connect`). Until now a binding (erratum 255)
    meant "every member of this server uploads into this account", and the origin proof (erratum 279) asked one question:
    "did this box consent to this guild?" A member who runs his own Clippet wants his OWN uploads in a server to reach HIS
    box while everyone else's go to the server's — and with the proof as it was, a server's admin could aim the WHOLE server
    at that friend's PC (Change passes the proof), and a stranger could aim himself at a box he has no shell on. The plane's
    half (the `u:<user>:<guild>` route, `/connect`) is clippet-pass lane `routeperson`; this is what the box must know.
    (a) **The column.** Migration **0024**: `discord_guilds.scope TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'server' CHECK (scope IN ('server',
    'person'))`. Every binding that existed is a server binding; `guild_id` stays the primary key (one account per server per
    box: two friends on one self-host want two boxes, not two rows). `db.GuildBinding` gains `Scope` and `DiscordID` (the
    account's linked id, 0019, through the join that already reaches `users`); `db.BindGuildScope` writes the scope it is
    given (`ON CONFLICT` updates `user_id, scope`), `BindGuild` is its server form, and a change of scope on the same account
    reports `rebound`. (b) **The CLI.** `admin bot bind <guild-id> <username> --person` (beside `--no-register`) is refused
    while the account has no Discord user id: stderr `admin bot bind: <user> has no Discord user id - run `clippet admin
    users link <user> <discord-id>` first`, exit 1, nothing stored; stdout gains ` (person)` after the account; a rebind
    without `--person` makes the server every member's again. `admin bot ls` ends each row with a fourth column, `server` or
    `person`. `admin users unlink` is refused while a person binding names the account — a person binding without an id
    would refuse every member, silently: `admin users unlink: <user> has a person binding (guild <G>) - run `clippet admin
    bot unbind <G>` first`, exit 1. (c) **The proof.** `GET /api/bot/claim?guild_id=G[&user_id=U]`: a `user_id` that is
    present and not a snowflake is 400 `invalid_user_id` on either scope. A server binding answers as before plus
    `"scope":"server"`, with or without U. A person binding answers 200 `{"bound":true,"app_id":…,"scope":"person"}` — no
    `defaults`: the server's `/settings` row reads the SERVER route's box — only when U equals the account's linked id;
    every other ask (no U, another U, an account unlinked since) is the empty 404 an unbound guild answers. The log field
    `bot_claim` is `bound` / `unbound` / `person` / `not_person`; the asked id is compared and dropped, never logged or
    echoed. An OLD box ignores `user_id` and answers a 200 without `scope`, which the plane refuses for a person route —
    safe in the cycle's order (plane first). (d) **The invoker check.** `guildBinding`, after the row is found: on a person
    binding, an interaction with no member, no user, or a user id other than the linked one is answered ephemerally
    `Not your Clippet.` (`msgNotYours`, the reviewed wording) before anything is fetched, log field `discord_guild=not_yours`.
    Every caller of `guildBinding` inherits it (`/upload`, `/clip link:`, Enrich, the form's clicks, `/settings`,
    `/signin`); a server binding never reads the invoker. (e) **Docs.** DEPLOY §30.8 step **3b "Just me"** (`admin users
    link`, `admin bot bind … --person`, then `/connect` → **Connect my Clippet** in the server), the operator-learns line
    `With a person binding, the bot's operator also keeps your Discord user id beside that server's record.`, the stale
    "repeated weekly" canary sentence struck (no weekly canary exists); §30.3's command count corrected to five.
    **Ships inert:** no row has `scope='person'` until an operator types `--person`. **Pins:** internal/db
    `TestGuildBindingScope`, `TestMigrate0024KeepsTheBindingsItFinds` (a 0016-shaped row upgrades as `server`; 0016's own
    upgrade test now applies 0024 after it); internal/httpapi `TestBotClaimPersonAnswers` (the whole table),
    `TestBotClaimLogsTheAnswerNeverTheID`, `TestPersonBindingRefusesEveryOtherInvoker`, `TestPersonBindingPassesTheLinkedMember`,
    `TestServerBindingPassesEveryMember`, and `TestBotClaimAnswersOneBooleanPerGuild`'s four fields; cmd

343. **The database snapshot follows the clips into the bucket** (lane `snapshot`, run 17, 2026-10-19; the owner's pick (a), the
    reasoning in run 16's multihost review §3 "A stale DB": the foundation is worth building alone). The bucket holds bytes
    without names; every clip's id, title, owner and TTL lives only in `clippet.db`. Now a box whose home is a bucket keeps
    a copy of that file IN the bucket, so the bucket alone can rebuild the instance on any PC.
    (a) **Where.** `{S3_KEY_PREFIX}_clippet/` is the instance's RESERVED prefix (`store.ReservedDir`, `ReservedPrefix`,
    `IsReserved`), beside `clips/` and never inside it: `{P}_clippet/db.sqlite` (the copy, `application/vnd.sqlite3`),
    `.sha256` (lowercase hex and a newline, written LAST) and `.meta` (`{written_at, commit, clips, bytes, sha256, born}`,
    written FIRST). Every reader of the clips prefix — `admin orphans`, the sweeper's per-clip DeletePrefix, `admin stats`'
    bucket line — cannot reach it by construction; `orphans` also skips `IsReserved` keys in words. `admin objects
    _clippet` lists it under a heading of its own (`_clippet` is in neither id grammar). The displayed storage reading (the
    sweeper's, so /healthz, the panel, the advisory WARN) adds its size (`Sweeper.WithExtraBytes`); the hard cap
    (`STORAGE_BUDGET_HARD`) reads clip rows at the upload and never it, so the snapshot cannot be why a clip is refused.
    (b) **Settings.** `DB_SNAPSHOT=on|off`, ON when empty on `s3`; on `fs` the word is still checked and the result is
    always off (a folder home sits beside the database; nothing is built). `DB_SNAPSHOT_EVERY`, 10 m, 5 s at least. Two
    compose rows, two commented `.env.example` lines. The boot line carries `db_snapshot=on|off`.
    (c) **The copy is erratum 321's.** `cmd/clippet/snapshot.go`'s `writeOnce`: `db.Born` (the applied_at of the lowest
    migration — new, read-only, no migration); the owner check; `(*admin).writeSnapshot` (`VACUUM INTO` a `.part-`, 0600,
    renamed) into `SCRATCH_DIR/.db-snapshot-<id>.sqlite` — a dotted FILE, which neither scratch janitor reads; its sha256;
    `db.Inspect` (restore-check's integrity check) on it; `PutFile` of the meta, the copy (the parallel-parts path, its
    `PutResult.SHA256` checked against the hash) and the sidecar; the scratch copy and anything SQLite left beside it
    removed. `writeBackupStatus`'s body became `writeJSONAtomic`, shared with the snapshot's status file.
    (d) **Never another database's.** The meta's `born` is the database's identity — `VACUUM INTO` and a restore carry it,
    two databases created apart do not share it. A write whose bucket meta names a different `born` is refused
    (`errForeignSnapshot`, naming both times, S3_KEY_PREFIX and `admin restore`): a fresh PC booted against the bucket
    before its restore would otherwise replace the one copy that can bring the instance back with an empty database. No
    meta is an unclaimed slot; a meta without `born` is overwritten.
    (e) **When.** One goroutine (`dbSnapshotter.Run`), started in the background chain after the storage ping, waited for
    at shutdown under the sweeper's single deadline before the database closes. Triggers: a clip's card becoming ready
    (erratum 330's `worker.Deps.CardReady`, now composed with the bot's when both exist) and a clip row destroyed (new
    `lifecycle.Deps.Destroyed`, fired after the row is gone — the owner's DELETE and the sweeper's expiry alike). Users,
    tokens, sessions and settings are NOT tracked; a day with no tracked change still uploads once (`snapshotIdle`). `Touch`
    is a non-blocking send into a channel of one — never on the request path. Debounce: at most one upload per
    `DB_SNAPSHOT_EVERY` after the last one, with a TRAILING write (a burst is one upload when the window closes). At boot:
    an upload at once when the sidecar's LastModified is older than the debounce or there is none, or the status file says
    the last process stopped with a change `pending` (a stop with one pending records it). A failure is one WARN `db
    snapshot failed` (`err retry`) and a retry one interval on; a panic is a failure; nothing is refused; a cancel at
    shutdown is INFO. Lines: INFO `db snapshot on` (`key every due_now`) at boot, INFO `db snapshot written` (`key bytes
    took`). `DATA_DIR/snapshot-status.json` (0600, tmp + rename): `{last_ok, bytes, failed_at, reason, pending}`.
    (f) **`admin restore --from-store [--yes]`** (`admin_restore.go`), routed before the database is opened (a new PC has
    none): refused on `fs` (exit 2) and without `--from-store`; takes `DATA_DIR/serve.lock` EXCLUSIVE — refused while a
    server holds it (exit 1, nothing changed); a filesystem that cannot lock is a sentence and the verb goes on. Downloads
    the copy into `SCRATCH_DIR/.db-restore-*/`, reads the sidecar (missing → refused), compares the hash (mismatch →
    refused, both values named), inspects it (not OK → refused), prints `snapshot / written (age, commit) / integrity /
    schema / rows / current`, and a meta whose sha256 is not the sidecar's says the later write did not finish. Without
    `--yes` it is a dry run. With it: the copy lands beside the database as `.part-<id>` (0600, synced), `clippet.db` and
    its `-wal`/`-shm` move aside as `clippet.db.before-restore-<UTC>` (+ the same suffixes, so the aside copy opens whole and
    no stale WAL is replayed into the snapshot), the part is renamed in. The scratch area is removed either way.
    (g) **The lock** (`datalock*.go`, new). Every `clippet serve` takes `DATA_DIR/serve.lock` SHARED for its life (flock on
    unix, LockFileEx on Windows; two servers over one database stay a supported shape — 37-library and 73-ops run two);
    the restore takes it exclusive. A server that finds it held exclusive refuses to boot (`boot: DATA_DIR is held by
    admin restore`); one that cannot lock at all boots with a WARN. 321's restore was by hand (§15.4) and had no lock
    check; this is the first.
    (h) **`admin doctor`'s `snapshot` row** (after `backup`; 19 checks): `off (folder home)`, `off (DB_SNAPSHOT=off)`,
    `never: …`, `on · <age> · <size>` (the sidecar's LastModified, the copy's size, from Stat only), or a FAIL — the status
    file's failure newer than its success, through `safe()`, or the store's own words. It writes nothing. `/healthz` gains
    nothing.
    (i) **Docs.** DEPLOY §15's top (the first line of defence, what the database carries — so the bucket's keys ARE the
    instance — and the recovery recipe), §24.1 (nineteen checks, the row), §31.2 (stored bytes), §33 (the reserved prefix,
    never served).
    (j) **Not built, on purpose.** No history in the bucket (one copy, overwritten; the timed backups keep history); no
    tracking of user/token/setting writes beyond the daily upload; no automatic restore at boot; the hard cap does not
    count the snapshot. Two instances on one bucket MUST differ in S3_KEY_PREFIX (the second's snapshot is refused, every
    attempt a WARN).
    **Pins.** cmd/clippet `snapshot_test.go`: `TestSnapshotDebounce` (fake clock: the boot upload, a burst of 50 → one
    trailing upload at the window's close, nothing a second before it, a lone change after a quiet at once, the daily
    upload), `TestSnapshotTouchNeverBlocks` (100 000 Touches during a stuck upload), `TestSnapshotFailureIsAWarnAndARetry`,
    `TestSnapshotBootRule` (a recent copy, an old one, `pending`, a stop recording it), `TestSnapshotWriteOnce` (meta → copy
    → sidecar, the sidecar is the object's sha256, the meta's clips and born, a sound database, scratch empty, the key
    prefix), `TestSnapshotNeverOverwritesAnotherDatabase`, `TestDoctorSnapshotRow` (the four shapes and a Stat failure),
    `TestReservedPrefixInObjectsAndOrphans`, `TestRestoreFromStore` (dry run on a new PC, refused under a held lock, `--yes`
    0600, the aside copy whole, a bad sha changes nothing, no snapshot, the usage, `fs`), `TestDataLock`,
    `TestFolderHomeHasNoSnapshot`; internal/sweeper `TestSweepLeavesTheReservedPrefix` (and the Destroyed hook per row),
    `TestBudgetCountsTheExtraBytes`; internal/config `TestDBSnapshotDefaults`, `TestDBSnapshotRefusals`; the doctor
    count pins 18 → 19 (Go and E2E 51, 73, 88, 90, 97). E2E step **107** (`107-snapshot.sh`, parallel; 106 is lane `signin`'s `106-botsignin`): the stack's own
    doctor row `on ·`; a `--rm` probe on its own prefix with `DB_SNAPSHOT_EVERY=5s` — `db_snapshot=on` on the boot line,
    the boot upload, one clip and the debounced upload after its card, `objects _clippet` (heading, three objects),
    `orphans` silent on it, doctor `on ·`, restore refused under the running server, then into a NEW data directory a dry
    run (sha256 ok, `clips=1`, no database made) and `--yes`, after which `admin ls` shows the clip and its title.
    **Amended by erratum 348 (a) (2026-10-27):** (b)'s "always off on `fs`" and (f)'s refusal on `fs` are withdrawn —
    the snapshot is ON when empty on both backends and on a folder home lands under the media folder's own
    `_clippet/`; `admin restore --from-store` reads it from either store; (h)'s `off (folder home)` shape is gone and
    `off (DB_SNAPSHOT=off)` is a WARN when timed backups are off too. `TestFolderHomeHasNoSnapshot` became

344. **The chunked web upload: one file as a run of requests, one ingest** (lane `chunked`, run 18, 2026-10-19; the owner's
    picks: chunked, in 50 MiB chunks; the reasons in run 17's records). Cloudflare
    refuses any one request body over its plan's cap — 100 MB on Free and Pro — with a 413 of its own, before the guard
    Worker or the tunnel sees it, so a friend's 2 GB web upload to a `*.clippet.gg` name never reached the box (nothing in
    its log). The edge's own error-413 page names the remedy first: send the upload as smaller requests. The terms forbid
    circumventing a limit; following the limit's documented remedy is not that, and the CDN video clause is about serving
    out, not uploading in (`chunked-tos.md` §2).
    (a) **The routes** (`internal/httpapi/uploads.go`), one family: `POST /api/uploads` opens a session from one JSON object
    — `{size, name?, type?, duplicate?}` plus the one-shot's metadata document (`title`, `description`, `unlisted`,
    `ttl_days`, `tags`, `link_style`) — and answers **201** `{id, size, chunk_bytes, received: 0}`; `PUT
    /api/uploads/{uid}/{index}` carries ONE chunk; `POST /api/uploads/{uid}/finish` assembles and ingests; `GET
    /api/uploads/{uid}` answers `{…, received, finishing?, clip?}` for a resume; `DELETE /api/uploads/{uid}` abandons
    (**204**). `{uid}` is 32 lowercase hex characters (16 random bytes), never a clip id, so neither id space can name the
    other. Credential, scope and CSRF are `POST /api/clips`' (`RequireUser` + the `upload` scope + CSRF; an `upload`
    token may speak them). A session is its owner's alone: another account's, an unknown and an expired one are the same
    **404** `not_found` (`no such upload`).
    (b) **The one-ingest rule.** Finish calls `ingestCore` — the function `POST /api/clips`, `/api/upload`, the bot and
    the drop folder call — with a new field of `ingestSource`, `Spooled`: the assembled file's path INSTEAD of a body.
    `adoptSpool` hard-links it into the spool's `source.{ext}` (a copy where the filesystem cannot link) and hashes it
    there; from then on the upload is the one-shot's, by the same code — the duplicate check (erratum 326, so the other
    door's identical bytes answer `existing`), the quota, the probe, the audio strip, `PutFile`, the transaction, the
    worker's hand-off — and its errors go through the same `writeIngestError` and its 201/200 body is the same
    `ToDTO`. There is no second ingest. The metadata document is checked by ONE function, `checkMeta`, which the
    one-shot's `readMetadata` now calls too: at the open (to refuse early) and again at the finish (the defaults are the
    account's NOW, as a one-shot sent now would get).
    (c) **The open asks every gate that can be asked before the bytes**: both upload limiters (one upload is one token
    from each bucket, however many chunks — the chunks, the finish, the GET and the DELETE carry no limiter, the owner's
    no-new-limiter rule: each is bounded by a session the open paid for), `checkMeta`, `size` against
    `MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES` (**413** `too_large`), the scratch precheck for that size (`declaredScratchNeed`, **507**), the
    storage quota (`storageQuota`, the same function and sentence — the finish asks it again inside the core). So a file
    the instance would refuse is refused in one small request, not after it was sent.
    (d) **A chunk** is exactly its length: `chunk_bytes`, the last one the remainder; `Content-Length` is required
    (**411** `length_required`) and must equal it (**400**); the body is read through `MaxBytesReader` at that length.
    Chunks go in order: an index already received is **200** and its body is never read (a retry of a lost answer); one
    past `received` is **409** `out_of_order` carrying `received`; the sum is enforced per chunk by construction (every
    length is fixed by `size`, which passed `MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES` at the open). Each chunk asks the scratch disk for its own
    length plus `SCRATCH_MIN_FREE_BYTES` (**507**). The route is `long` and `closeUnlessRead`-wrapped like every upload
    body; `bodyWillBeRead` comes off only for a chunk that will be read.
    (e) **The store** (`internal/chunks`, new; no migration, nothing in the database): `$SCRATCH_DIR/.chunks/{uid}/`
    holds `session.json` (owner, size, chunk_bytes, received, name, type, the raw metadata document, created; once
    finished the clip id and `existing`), written whole through a synced temporary file and a rename, and `data`, written
    at each chunk's own offset and synced BEFORE `received` counts it — a crash between the two re-asks the same chunk.
    `.chunks` is outside both janitors' rules (neither `ids.Valid` nor `.upload-`), so the boot janitor, which removes
    every row-less spool, leaves a half-sent upload alone and a restart of the box between two chunks loses nothing.
    One in-process lock per session serialises its writes; two sessions never wait on each other. `Expire` removes a
    session 24 hours after its open, finished or not (`chunks.MaxAge`), skipping one whose lock is held; the sweeper
    calls it beside the scratch janitor (`Sweeper.WithUploadSweep`; one INFO `sweep: expired upload sessions` when it
    removed any). `clippet serve` builds ONE store and hands it to both (`httpapi.Deps.Uploads`).
    (f) **The finish outlives its client.** The core runs under `context.WithoutCancel`: a 4 GiB file's hash, probe and
    store can outlast the edge's wait for an answer (the edge then answers the browser and drops the connection), and a
    finish that died with its connection would throw the upload away at its last step. A second finish waits on the
    session's lock and answers the recorded clip; GET shows `finishing` meanwhile and `clip` after. A FAILED finish
    keeps the file (it was linked, not moved), so a transient 503 is simply sent again; on success the session's `data`
    is removed once `session.json` records the clip. A DELETE during a finish answers 204 at once and the session goes
    when the finish returns — the clip it makes is made, as with a one-shot cancelled after its last byte.
    (g) **The knob**: `UPLOAD_CHUNK_BYTES`, default **52428800** (50 MiB), bounded **5242880 … 95000000** at boot
    (`config.MinUploadChunkBytes`/`MaxUploadChunkBytes`): "the edge's cap minus headroom". 50 MiB leaves room under 100 MB
    for the headers; the floor stops a value that only multiplies requests; the roof keeps a value meaning "as big as it
    goes" under the two cheapest plans' cap. It changes how many requests, never what is accepted. One compose row, one
    commented `.env.example` line, DEPLOY §7's row and its "Why chunks" paragraph.
    (h) **The web** (`web/static/app.js`): the upload form carries `data-upload-sessions="/api/uploads"` and
    `data-upload-chunk` (the knob); a file larger than ONE chunk takes `sendChunked`, every other file the one-shot POST
    exactly as before. Both end in the same `answer` (the 201, the 200 + `existing`, an error's message) and the same bar,
    which counts bytes across chunks (`uploading N%`, then `saving…`). A chunk that fails on the network or with a 408,
    429 or 5xx is tried again after 1, 2, 3 s, each time from where GET says the session is; the fourth failure in a row
    is `Upload failed: network error (<name>)`. A finish whose answer is lost (a network error, a 5xx — the edge's own
    524 among them) is followed by GET every 3 s until `clip` appears, or by another finish when nothing is running.
    Cancel aborts the chunk in flight and DELETEs the session; a refused finish DELETEs it too, so Try again starts a
    fresh one. No sentence on the page changed. The Discord `/upload`, the drop folder, `/api/upload`, `/api/share` and
    the inbound URLs are untouched.
    (i) **The guard** (clippet-pass `guard/src/routes.ts`): the five rows, class `upload` like `POST /api/clips` (JSON or
    `text/plain` relayed; no deadline, because a chunk is a transfer), `{uid}` matched as 32 lowercase hex and `{index}`
    as a decimal of at most six digits with no leading zero; `test/routes.test.ts` diffs them against this router.
    (j) **Not built, on purpose.** No parallel chunks (in order keeps the store one file and one offset, and an upload's
    speed is the uplink's, not the request count's); no tus protocol (four plain routes say it); no direct-to-bucket
    multipart (it only exists for a bucket home and adds a download back before the transcode — `chunked-tos.md` §4); no
    per-account cap on open sessions (the upload limiter bounds opens, the per-chunk scratch check bounds the disk).
    (k) **Every give-up lets the session go** (run 23 lane `v1-owner`, 2026-10-27; cleanup row R18-6). (h)'s client DELETEd
    on Cancel and on a refused finish only; three lost chunks in a row, a refused chunk and a finish whose answer never
    came (the loop is bounded — 200 GETs 3 s apart, ten minutes — not "until `clip` appears" as (h) said) left the
    session and its stored chunks for the sweeper's expiry, and Try again started beside them. Now one `letGo` in
    `sendChunked` DELETEs the session (when one was opened) on every exit that is not the 201/200: `lost` and `end` both
    call it, so no give-up can forget it. A DELETE while a finish still runs is the server's already-defined case (the
    session goes when that finish returns; the clip it makes is made). No sentence changed. Pin: the visual pass's
    `domChunkGiveUp` (phase 2c) drives the library's upload card with every `/api/uploads` request answered by the test
    on its own page (the served page's chunk size cut to 1000 bytes, a 2500-byte pick): a refused chunk (413) and three
    lost chunks (503, GET answering 503) each DELETE their session exactly once — seen failing with the change reverted.
    The never-answered finish is the same `lost` and is not driven (ten minutes of the loop).
    **Pins.** internal/chunks `chunks_test.go`: `TestSessionArithmetic`, `TestValidID`,
    `TestPutInOrderIdempotentAndFinish` (out of order with `received`, a repeated chunk never read, a wrong length, an
    index past the end, a short body, finish refused while incomplete, the file handed over whole, a second finish not
    re-running the ingest, a chunk after the finish), `TestFinishFailureKeepsTheFile`, `TestOwnerOnly`,
    `TestDeleteWhileFinishing`, `TestExpire` (old and finished go, young stays, a locked one waits, litter goes);
    internal/httpapi `uploads_test.go`: `TestChunkedUploadIsTheOneShotsIngest` (three chunks → 201, the stored original
    and the row are the file's, the one-shot door then answers `existing`, the chunked door answers the one-shot's clip as
    `existing`, `duplicate=allow` at the open opts out), `TestChunkedOpenGates` (size, `MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES`, the metadata
    document, the JSON gate, anonymous, the scratch precheck, another account's 404s, bad indices, 411, an `upload`
    token, DELETE), `TestChunkedOpenQuota`, `TestChunkedFinishFailureKeepsTheSession`; internal/config `TestDefaults`
    (52428800) and the two bound refusals. E2E step **109** (`109-chunked.sh`, parallel, account `ck`; the suite is 105
    steps / 46 bundles): the stack's own chunk size off a probe session (then DELETE → 404), a fixture of exactly 2.5
    chunks (the small clip plus one MP4 `free` box), out of order 409, a repeated chunk, an early finish 409, finish 201
    → ready → the original's sha256 is the fixture's, then `POST /api/clips` of the same file answers that clip with
    `existing`.

345. **The default stack is the folder store; the bundled bucket is withdrawn** (lane `folder22`, run 22, 2026-10-25;

    before this erratum (the reference stack's, clippet.gg's: a bucket, no `STORAGE_BACKEND` line) keeps its bucket on

346. **`admin objects` writes: the test harness needs no S3 client** (lane `objects2`, 2026-10-26; the owner's pick (3a), the
    first two bullets of the cleanup list's "Run 22 storage" section; `cmd/clippet/admin_objects.go`, `cmd/clippet/admin.go`,
    `internal/store/{store,minio,fake}.go`, `scripts/e2e.sh`, ten drop-ins, `compose.e2e-bucket.yaml` (was `compose.e2e-minio.yaml`),
    `scripts/lib/gatestack.sh`, `scripts/t1.sh`; DEPLOY §24; **no migration, no new step, no new doctor check**).
    Until now every WRITE the harness made into a bucket went through `store_mc`: `mc` in a one-off `bucket-init`
    container — since run 22 Pigsty's `pgsty/mc` build of a client whose upstream left, pinned by digest beside the
    RustFS server, with the stack's credentials copied out of `.env` into its environment (281 (f)). The verb that
    already answered the READ questions (281) now answers the writes, so the harness talks to its bucket only through
    the binary it tests, with S3_* exactly as the app reads them.
    (a) **Five forms beside `objects <id> | _clippet [--count]`**, each routed past the database like the read form:
    `objects init` creates the configured bucket when `BucketExists` says it is missing (`store.BucketMaker`, an
    optional interface the minio-go store and the Fake implement) and prints `bucket <name> created` or `bucket <name>
    already exists`; it sets NO policy — a new bucket is private, an existing one is left as it is (`mc anonymous set
    none` on a bucket just made was already that state); a bucket another account owns is an error; on `fs` it prints
    that there is nothing to create and opens nothing. `objects put <key>` stores stdin (spooled to a temp file,
    because the Store's write is `PutFile`) and prints `stored <key> <size>`; `objects rm <key>` is `DeleteKey` (a key
    that is not there is not an error, erratum 305's contract); `objects rm --prefix <p>` is `DeletePrefix`;
    `objects --prefix <p> [--count]` is the read form's listing from the bucket's root. **Every key and prefix in
    these forms is ROOT-RELATIVE** — S3_KEY_PREFIX is not prepended — because what the harness writes is mostly not
    this instance's: a probe container's `-e S3_KEY_PREFIX=e2e-<word>-<epoch>/` replaces the stack's prefix, so its
    objects sit beside the stack's key space. The forms work on `fs` too, as the read form does.
    (b) **The refusals, all before the store is opened** (exit 2, one stderr line `admin objects<form>: refused: …`;
    the tests assert the store was never opened): a key outside the app's own alphabet (`[A-Za-z0-9._-]` with `/`
    between parts; no leading or trailing slash, no empty, `.` or `..` part); `put` with no stdin; and for `rm
    --prefix` the harness's `store_rm_prefix_ok_` moved into the product (`probePrefixRefusal`): an empty prefix, `/`
    or a dot-path is the whole bucket; anything not `^e2e-[a-z0-9]+-[0-9]+/$` is not a test probe's prefix; and a
    prefix that overlaps this instance's own S3_KEY_PREFIX in either direction is refused. With S3_KEY_PREFIX empty
    the instance's space is the app's own top-level names (`clips/`, `_clippet/`, `doctor/`), none of which has the
    shape. The harness keeps its own copy of the check so a refused EXIT trap prints a line instead of spending an
    exec.
    (c) **The harness**: `store_mc`, `store_mc_derive_`, `store_scrub_` and `SM_EP`/`SM_AK`/`SM_SK`/`SM_PATH`/
    `SM_ROOT`/`SM_B` are gone; `store_obj <args…>` is `dc exec -T app clippet admin objects <args…>` with stderr kept
    for the failure message, and `SM_PREFIX` (derived the same way) is what a caller prepends when it means the
    stack's own space. 51-admin's three plants are `put`, its two removals `rm`; the probe tidy-ups of 37, 47, 55,
    73, 89, 90, 92, 105 and 107 are `rm --prefix`; 73-ops's two counts and 92-setup's one are `--prefix … --count`.
    No credential crosses a command line or a second container any more. check.sh's stage 13 drops the six names.
    (d) **The bucket is made by the app**: the overlay's `bucket-init` service and its `pgsty/mc` pin are deleted,
    and the app depends on the server alone. The E2E's step 1 runs `admin objects init` right after `dc up -d
    --build` and before it waits for `/readyz` (a live ping that asks for the bucket, so it answers 503 until it
    exists; the boot ping loop retries for 30 s, well past the init); `gatestack.sh up` and t1's visual-only bring-up
    do the same. A non-fatal NOTE in step 1 if it fails — the readiness wait then fails with the store's own word.
    `gatestack.sh pins` passes with one image left; its self-test now pins that the overlay names exactly one image,
    RustFS, by digest.
    (e) **The rename** (the section's second bullet; its own commit): `compose.e2e-minio.yaml` is
    `compose.e2e-bucket.yaml`, its service `minio` is `s3` and its volume `minio_data` is `s3_data`; the overlay's
    S3_ENDPOINT default, gatestack's generated `.env`, 88-fsstore's fallback and 92-setup's endpoint check follow

    `GATE_MINIO_PORT` — because `.env` files and the records carry them; the `minio-go` module is the S3 client and
    keeps its name; 91-drop's `http://minio:9000` stays, being an endpoint that must NOT answer. A lane `.env` whose
    `COMPOSE_FILE` names the old file must name the new one. Records before this erratum keep the old names.
    Tests: cmd/clippet `TestAdminObjectsInit`, `TestAdminObjectsPut`, `TestAdminObjectsRmKey`,
    `TestAdminObjectsRmPrefix` (every refusal, both directions of the key-space overlap, a prefix beside a non-empty
