347. **The hosted Clippet Auto end to end: one test-only knob, one mock, bundle 110** (lane `autoe2e`, 2026-10-26; the
    last size-M cleanup row, "Run 14 [autohost] the hosted process has no E2E bundle", with lane passnits4's plan;
    `cmd/clippet-auto/main.go`, `internal/notify/autohost.go`, `internal/notify/auto.go`, `scripts/e2e.d/110-autohost.sh`,
    `scripts/e2e.d/110-autohost/main.go`, `scripts/e2e.d/GO-ONLY`, `scripts/select.sh`; DEPLOY §30.11; **no migration,
    no compose or Dockerfile change, no doctor check**; E2E step **110**, the suite **106 steps / 47 bundles**).
    Until now `cmd/clippet-auto/**` and `internal/notify/autohost.go` were GO-ONLY rows: the process had only ever met
    Discord, the plane and a box as in-process fakes. Bundle 110 runs the binary the tree builds against all three.
    (a) **How it reaches no real host — DNS and trust, not configuration.** The plan asked for a knob that would point
    the API host, the gateway allowlist and the https-only plane URL at a mock. None is needed: on a private docker
    network (`--internal`, no route out) the mock answers under the REAL names — network aliases `discord.com`,
    `gateway.discord.gg`, `gateway-e2e.discord.gg`, `cdn.discordapp.com` — and two names under the reserved `.test`
    domain (RFC 6761: no public resolver answers for it), `plane.clippet.test` and `box.clippet.test`, all over TLS
    with a certificate from a CA the mock makes at start. The two clippet processes trust that CA through
    `SSL_CERT_FILE`, Go's own variable, and nothing else in them changes: `config.DiscordAPIHost`, `ValidGatewayURL`,
    the attachment allowlist, https and certificate verification are production's, so the bundle proves them too.
    The ON-BOX path (Clippet Auto in `clippet serve`, erratum 333, and the box's own fetch from the CDN) has no
    address check of its own, so the same network serves it with NO knob at all — the cleanup list's `105-autobot` row can
    use this mock as it is.
    (b) **The one knob, `AUTO_TEST_ENDPOINTS=1`, and what it changes.** The one thing DNS cannot steer is the hosted
    transport's dial check (erratum 334, amended 2026-10-12, audit F4): it refuses any address that is not public
    AFTER resolution, and the mock is on a private address. The knob sets `notify.HostedDeps.AllowTestNames`: a
    dial to a name under `.test` skips that check (`notify.TestName`, read from the dial's own `host:port` BEFORE
    resolution — the one thing about a name no resolver can steer); every other name, and every IP literal, keeps
    it whatever it resolves to. Nothing else reads the knob. Production's dial to `bot.clippet.gg` or a box goes
    through the guarded dialer exactly as before, with or without it.
    (c) **The guard: a process with the knob on is refused at start (exit 2, before any connection)** unless ALL of
    (1) `DISCORD_AUTO_TOKEN` is NOT shaped like a Discord token — a real one is three dot-separated segments whose
    first is the base64 (either alphabet, padded or not) of the bot's 17-20-digit user id; any other token is one
    Discord never issued, which its gateway closes with 4004, so a process with the knob on can hold no real session;
    (2) `AUTO_PLANE_URL`'s host is a `.test` name — never production's plane, whose bearer and records stay out;
    (3) `AUTO_DEADMAN_URL` is unset — a test pings nothing real. Any value but `1` is refused too. The token rule was
    chosen as the strongest the code could have: the process has no token-shape check of its own, and the box's
    (`isBotToken`) is an alphabet and a length, which a test token also passes; the user-id segment is the one
    property every real token has and a made-up one does not. The refusals, verbatim:
    `AUTO_TEST_ENDPOINTS must be 1 or unset`;
    `AUTO_TEST_ENDPOINTS needs a DISCORD_AUTO_TOKEN that is not a Discord token (a test's mock gateway; never production)`;
    `AUTO_TEST_ENDPOINTS needs an AUTO_PLANE_URL under the reserved .test domain (a test's mock plane; never production's)`;
    `AUTO_TEST_ENDPOINTS refuses AUTO_DEADMAN_URL: a test pings nothing real`.
    On, the FIRST line the process logs is one WARN: `AUTO_TEST_ENDPOINTS=1: a name under .test may reach a private
    address. This process is a test's, never production's` (`event=test_endpoints outcome=on`), and the start line's
    config says `test_endpoints=true`. The doctor is not involved (the hosted process has none).
    (d) **The mock and the bundle.** `scripts/e2e.d/110-autohost/main.go` (Go, the module's `coder/websocket`) is
    ONE program playing the gateway (HELLO, IDENTIFY checked, READY with a regional `resume_gateway_url`, two
    GUILD_CREATEs, a video MESSAGE_CREATE in server A — Auto, notice on — and in server B — Prompt, notice off —, the
    poster's INTERACTION_CREATE press on the offer, op 7; then RESUME expected on the resume host with the last
    sequence, RESUMED and the server-A message delivered a second time; on the third socket, after a restart, RESUME
    at the saved sequence), Discord's REST (records every call with its Authorization verdict and answers it), the
    CDN (each video's own file, by Range), the plane (`/auto/guilds` with `routable`, `/auto/guild/{id}` with a URL
    SEALED to the process's key exactly as clippet-pass seal.ts seals, `/auto/session` load and save, the bearer
    checked) and the box's edge (a tunnel's part: `box.clippet.test` proxied to the box's plain listener). It is
    test-only: `scripts/` is outside the Docker build context, so the product image never contains it, and nothing
    under `cmd/` or `internal/` imports it (check.sh's call-site and URL tripwires scan those two and `web/` only). The
    bundle builds it and `clippet-auto` in the Dockerfile's `testdeps` stage with the checkout mounted read-only and
    the `clippet-gobuild` cache (T0's own build; 6-11 s warm), and runs three throwaway containers of the APP's image
    (the 101-autofetch pattern: the project's compose label and `clippet-e2e-` names): the mock, a box (`clippet
    serve` on private directories and an fs store, `DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN=managed`, `PUBLIC_BASE_URL
    https://box.clippet.test`, its own account bound to both servers, a Clippet Auto URL minted) and the process. It
    first runs the built binary with the knob into each refusal; then asserts from the mock's record and the
    process's log: IDENTIFY with the token and intents 33281; the fresh IDENTIFY's backfill reading the two text
    channels only; each instruction as Discord named the attachment, with `clippet-auto/1` and no Authorization; the
    box fetching each from the CDN once and answering 201 with two different links; Auto's link with the notice and
    the original removed; Prompt's offer (`auto:go`, a reply), the private `Uploading…` without the bot token, the
    link, the original and the reply removed; the act's save carrying `last` = the newest video and the identity;
    op 7 → RESUME on the regional host at sequence 6, the duplicate event making no third upload; the stop saving
    sequence 8 with `last` kept and exiting 0; the restart reading the session back and RESUMEing at 8, never
    IDENTIFYing; no call the mock does not know, no other host, no failure line; the knob's WARN first, once per
    start; no token, bearer, seal key or box URL in the log; both clips served by the box. Parallel; no account on
    the stack; prefix `AH_`; the trap removes the containers, the network, the build tag and the scratch files and
    keeps the record and the log as `.e2e/autohost-record.txt` / `autohost-auto.log` (no secret in either: asserted).
    (e) **What it found: the hosted backfill never reached Discord.** `notify.AutoClient.Call` built its URL with the
    whole path in `url.URL.Path`, so the backfill's `GET /channels/{id}/messages?after=…&limit=50` (erratum 334) went
    out as `…/messages%3Fafter=…` — another resource; Discord's 404 made the backfill skip every channel, silently,
    since the process first ran. The query now goes in `RawQuery` (`strings.Cut` at the first `?`). Only the hosted
    process backfills (`Backfill` is false on the box), so only it was affected. Pinned by `TestAutoClientCallQuery`
    (seen failing before the fix: the path arrived as `/api/v10/channels/123/messages?after=456&limit=50` with an
    empty query).
    (f) **The map.** The bundle's covers take `cmd/clippet-auto/**`, `internal/notify/autohost.go`,
    `internal/notify/auto.go`, `internal/autobot/**`, `internal/autorule/**` and `internal/httpapi/autofetch.go`; the
    two GO-ONLY rows are deleted. `select.sh` maps a change under `scripts/e2e.d/<stem>/` (a drop-in's own program)
    to that drop-in, and classifies `scripts/box-tidy.sh` as a harness tool (`none`; it answered `all` before).
    Tests: cmd/clippet-auto `TestTestEndpointsGuard` (the four refusals in eight cases, the knob off loading a real
    token as before, the WARN first and only when on), `TestDiscordTokenShape` (11 cases); internal/notify
    `TestHostedTransportTestNames` (14 names, the dial routing, a loopback IP literal still refused with the knob),
    `TestAutoClientCallQuery`.
    (g) **The on-box bundle, 111-autobot: the same mock, no knob** (the cleanup list's `105-autobot` row, the lane's last item;
    `scripts/e2e.d/111-autobot.sh`, prefix `AB_`, covers `internal/httpapi/autobox.go`, `internal/autobot/**`,
    `internal/config/discordauto.go`, `internal/notify/auto.go`; E2E step **111**, the suite **107 steps / 48
    bundles**). Clippet Auto inside `clippet serve` (erratum 333) is proved by the process the tree builds against the
    mock of (d): a throwaway box of the app's image on the private network with `DISCORD_AUTO_MODE`, a
    `DISCORD_AUTO_TOKEN` that is a test's (the box checks an alphabet and a length, which it passes; it carries no
    Discord user id), `DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN=managed` (Auto acts in the servers that bot's `admin bot bind` bound and

    not set. The mock gained four settings whose defaults are bundle 110's run, re-run green after the change:
    `MOCK_MODES` (each scripted server's mode, default `auto,prompt`), `MOCK_SCRIPT=hosted|box` (`box` skips the
    session-save wait, the duplicate event after RESUME and the third socket — the box keeps its session in memory,
    so a restart IDENTIFYs afresh and a duplicate is acted on twice by design: there is nothing of those to assert),

    counter across sockets (110's run still RESUMEs at 6 and saves 8). The box's mode is global, so the bundle runs
    two passes, each with a fresh mock scripting ONE server and a fresh box whose account is bound BEFORE it serves
    (the mock posts the video right after READY): `auto` with the notice on (the link with
    `-# Videos posted here become Clippet links.`, the original removed, nothing offered, no callback) and `prompt`

348. **The folder home's backup, the wizard that never refuses, and the first-run nits** (run 23 lane `v1-folder`,
    2026-10-27; PLAN D1, D2, D14 — decided by best practice on auditor A's findings 2–11;
    D2 is the owner's verdict of 2026-10-14 on the tunnel-video question).
    (a) **The database snapshot on a folder home** (D1, A-3: on the default install the database had NO backup — timed
    backups off, the snapshot forced off on `fs`, `restore --from-store` refused, doctor green, and the database in the
    `app_data` volume rather than in the folder everything suggested was the instance). `DB_SNAPSHOT` is honoured on
    `fs` exactly as on `s3` — ON when empty (`config.snapshotBlock`); the copy is erratum 343's, written through the
    folder store under the same relative keys, `{P}_clippet/db.sqlite`, `.sha256`, `.meta`, so the media folder's own
    `_clippet/` holds it and **backing up the folder is the whole backup**. The store marker `.clippet-store` sits at
    the folder's ROOT and the snapshot under `_clippet/`: two names that cannot meet (pinned on a real folder store). The
    owner check (343 (d)) works unchanged on a folder, so a fresh database booted over a restored folder cannot replace
    its copy. `admin restore --from-store` reads the snapshot from whichever store is configured — the fs refusal is
    gone; on a folder home the recipe is the folder put back, bound as `STORAGE_DIR`, and the verb. The drop folder
    (erratum 296) skips directories, `admin orphans` and the sweeper read `clips/` only, and `admin storage migrate`
    copies clip prefixes only (the target's own snapshot is written by its next server), so nothing else meets the new
    directory. `admin doctor`'s `snapshot` row reads the folder like a bucket (`never: the media folder holds no …`,
    `on · <age> · <size>`) and is a **WARN** — not green — when the snapshot is off AND timed backups are off, one line
    naming `DB_SNAPSHOT` and `BACKUP_EVERY`/`BACKUP_DIR`: an instance with no backup of any kind. The harness's
    probe-prefix sweep (`probe_prefix_tidy_`/`probe_prefix_swept_`) runs on a folder stack too (`store_obj
    --any-backend`): a probe on its own `S3_KEY_PREFIX` now writes `<prefix>_clippet/` into the shared folder.
    (b) **The wizard never refuses folder + tunnel or Pass** (D2, A-2; erratum 299's refusal WITHDRAWN). The folder

349. **The owner: the first account owns `/setup`, `Check now` and the Storage panel** (run 23 lane `v1-owner`,
    2026-10-27; the plan's D3 after the review's triage of the 1.0 audits (auditor B's §(1));
    `internal/db/migrations/0025_owner.sql`, `internal/db/users.go`, `internal/web/pages.go`, `internal/httpapi/setup.go`,
    `web/templates/setup.html`, `web/templates/settings.html`, `cmd/clippet/admin.go`, `scripts/e2e.sh` step 3,
    `scripts/e2e.d/92-setup.sh`; DEPLOY §2, §19.4, §31.5, §35.1; API.md; **migration 0025**, no new variable, no doctor
    check). Errata 297 (d) and 270/277 opened the wizard and the instance-wide Storage panel to every signed-in account
    because §14 had users and nothing else. On a household instance that is the friend reading the bill and the
    provider's setup walk; for 1.0 those two surfaces belong to the account that set the instance up.
    (a) **Who the owner is, durably: a column, not a derivation.** `users.owner` (0/1). "The lowest id" names nobody
    (ids are random text); "the oldest `created_at`" ties at one-second resolution and changes silently when an account
    is deleted. A column is one fact an operator reads (`admin users`: `owner=yes`, the LAST field, so the E2E's and the
    visual pass's sweeps, which read the name by position, and the Discord checks, which grep `discord=<id>` as a
    substring, are untouched) and moves (`admin users owner <username>`, one transaction: the old flag cleared, the new
    set). Three pieces of SQL keep it right on EVERY path with nothing in Go to forget: trigger `users_owner_first`
    makes an inserted row the owner when the table has none — `REGISTRATION=first`/`open`, `admin users create`, Sign
    in with Discord, `/signin` alike; trigger `users_owner_next` hands the role to the oldest remaining account
    (`created_at`, then rowid) when the owner is deleted (`admin users prune` is the one verb that deletes a user; one
    statement that removes the owner AND the next in line still lands on the oldest survivor), so an instance with
    accounts always has an owner and its setup page is never locked to everybody; the partial unique index
    `users_one_owner` makes two owners impossible. The migration backfills the oldest existing account — on an
    upgraded instance, whoever registered first; the operator whose first account was a test one runs `admin users
    owner`. (A VACUUM may renumber rowids on a table without an INTEGER key; that only reorders accounts made in the
    same second, and only for the backfill and the deleted-owner rule.)
    (b) **The owner's surfaces — every handler that needed only "signed in" for an instance-wide answer.** `GET
    /setup` (the page and its steps-only view, `?view=steps`), `POST /api/setup/check` and the Storage panel of
    `/settings`. Enumerated from the router and the page mux: every other session route answers about the caller's own
    account (settings, stats, tokens, sessions, password, Discord link, clips, collections, uploads). A member gets:
    on `/setup` **403**, `private, no-store`, the heading and one sentence, `Only the account that set up this Clippet
    can see this.` (`ownerOnlyLine`; PROPOSED copy, run 23's report) and nothing the page reads — no backend, no clip
    count, no chooser, no Check now; on `/settings` the Storage panel's head and that sentence, with none of its
    figures computed; from `Check now` **403** `not_owner` with the same sentence, before any probe or cache read. An
    `IsOwner` read error is the page's ordinary backend failure (503), never a guess. The owner's experience is
    unchanged, and anonymous on an instance with no account is still let in (297 (d)'s first-run door; shut under
    `SETUP_WIZARD=off`, erratum 335 (d)).
    (c) **Deliberately NOT the owner's.** The library's budget line (erratum 157): a member needs to know whether the
    next upload fits. `/healthz`'s budget figures: an anonymous probe, unchanged. The bot's `/settings` (erratum 318):
    Discord's Manage Server permission is its gate, and it edits the BOUND account's defaults. A member's clip pages,
    uploads, library and settings are untouched.
    (d) **The E2E.** Step 3 reads whether the run's account is the stack's owner (`admin users`, which changes
    nothing; the pure `owner_of_listing_`) and records `E2E_IS_OWNER=1|0` — it never stops the run and never prints
    a remedy that moves the role (on clippet.gg or dev the owner is a PERSON, and `admin users owner <the run's
    account>` there would hand the owner's `/setup` to a throwaway account). On a stack step 1 swept the
    run's account is always the owner. When it is not, a NOTE says so (for the owner's pages: a fresh stack,
    `docker compose down -v`), and 87-storage (the Storage panel and the cost line that follows it), 92-setup
    (sections 2–6: the owner's page and `Check now`) and 94-instance (the Pass walk) stand down behind
    `E2E_IS_OWNER` with a printed NOTE — the `store_has_bucket` pattern. 92-setup gains (1b): a member gets 403 and
    the sentence on `/setup` and its steps view, the Storage panel's sentence and no figure, and `Check now` 403
    `not_owner`; the member is a second account (`bundle_account so`) when the run's account owns the stack — which
    then keeps the figures — and the run's account itself when a person does (the refusal a real member meets).
    The E2E self-test pins `owner_of_listing_` on planted listings, that the three bundles name `E2E_IS_OWNER`, and
    that no script prints `admin users owner` for the run's account.
    **Pins.** internal/db `instance_owner_test.go`: `TestFirstAccountIsTheOwner` (CreateFirstUser and CreateUser),
    `TestOwnerSurvivesItsDeletion` (the next oldest; the owner and the next in one prune; an emptied table's next first
    account), `TestSetOwnerMovesTheRole` (one owner after every move, an unknown name changes nothing, a hand-written
    second owner refused by the index), `TestOwnerMigrationBackfillsTheOldest` (0001–0024, four accounts, 0025: the
    oldest by `created_at`, not the lowest id); cmd/clippet `TestAdminUsersOwner`; internal/web
    `TestSetupIsTheOwnersPage`, `TestSettingsStoragePanelIsTheOwners`; internal/httpapi `TestSetupCheckIsTheOwners`
    (no store call for the member). Each seen failing with its change reverted (the triggers removed; each handler's
    check disabled).

350. **`admin storage migrate` and `admin orphans --delete` outlive the invocation's ten minutes** (run 23 lane
    `v2-migrate`, 2026-10-27; the cleanup list's `[admin, S]` row from lane winexpose's section; `cmd/clippet/admin.go`,
    `cmd/clippet/admin_storage.go`; DEPLOY §32.3; no new variable, no doctor check, no migration). Every admin verb ran
    under `adminTimeout`, ten minutes for the WHOLE invocation. DEPLOY §32.3's own worked example — 412 clips, 44.9 GiB —
    does not copy and verify in ten minutes on any disk, so a big library's migrate, and the desktop app's Move that
    drives it (clippet-pass `core/src/migrate.rs`), ended in `migrate: N object(s) did NOT arrive verified` with nothing
    wrong. `admin import` had taken a context of its own for this reason (erratum 307); these two now do the same.
    (a) **`storage migrate` has no whole-run deadline, and every object has one.** The verb's context is
    `context.Background()`'s, cancellable and undated; the stop file and the byte cap (erratum 335) are still how a run
    is stopped, between objects. Each object's copy and verify — the destination stat, the source read, the write,
    the ETag proof or the read-back — runs under `STORAGE_TRANSFER_MAX` (6 h by default), the ceiling the store already
    gives one transfer, so an object that fits on a bucket fits here; on a directory, whose transfers have no clock of
    their own (DEPLOY §32.2), this is the one. (`STORAGE_TRANSFER_MAX=0` is a BOOT error — the loader refuses a non-positive duration, config.go `l.duration`;
    the review of 2026-10-27 struck the lane's "0 = no cap" claim, which held only through the test seam). An object that hits its deadline is `FAILED <key>: …: context deadline exceeded` and the run goes on to
    the next object; the exit codes and every line's shape are unchanged.
    (b) **`orphans --delete` has no whole-run deadline either.** On a large store it is one DeletePrefix after another;
    each store call keeps its per-operation timeout (`STORAGE_OP_TIMEOUT`, floored for the CLI), and the verb is
    idempotent. `orphans` without `--delete` only reads and keeps the ten minutes.
    (c) **`admin backup` keeps the ten minutes.** It is one `VACUUM INTO` of the database, which holds rows and no
    media; the database of a large library is megabytes, not gigabytes, so it has no such hole.
    **Pins.** cmd/clippet `TestMigrateOutlivesTheInvocationBudget` (a 5 ms invocation budget, four objects at 20 ms
    each, all copied), `TestMigrateObjectDeadlineFiresOnAHungObject` (a read that never returns fails that object
    alone under a 50 ms object deadline; the other three copy; the run ends), `TestAdminOrphansDeleteOutlivesTheInvocationBudget`
    (a 5 ms budget, a 20 ms delete, deleted). Test seams `adminEnv.timeout` and `adminEnv.objectTimeout`, zero in
    production. Each seen failing with its change reverted (the invocation context kept; the per-object deadline
    removed — that test's own 10 s guard fired; the orphans context kept).

351. **The Light copy encoded from a PRODUCED file addresses that file's streams** (lane `lightidx`, 2026-10-29;
    `internal/transcode/plan.go` `Plan.ForProducedFile`, `internal/worker/pipeline.go` `light()`; no new variable, no
    doctor check, no migration). `light()` reads the best file the run has — the Full the encode wrote, or the remux on
    the fast path — but rendered the graph with the UPLOAD's stream indices, the ones the probe read. A produced file
    always lays out the video first, then at most one audio track (`encodeArgs` maps `[v]` then `[a]`; `RemuxArgs` maps
    the video index, then the one audio index), so an upload whose audio track comes first — the owner's phone recording,
    audio 0, video 1, rotation 90, 20 s, on a Pass box through the GPU path — put `[0:1]` on the video pad of a file
    whose stream 1 is the audio: ffmpeg `Stream specifier ':1' in filtergraph description … matches no streams`,
    `clip failed … permanent`, the Original played, the card never came. Every such clip since the remux fast path
    (erratum 200) failed the same way; the test-clip matrix has no audio-first file, so nothing caught it.
    **The fix.** `Plan.ForProducedFile()` is the plan for a produced input: `VideoIndex` 0, `AudioIndexes` `[1]` and
    `AudioSingle` when the plan has any audio (a Merge of two upload tracks is ONE track in the produced file), `AudioNone`
    otherwise; the picture's decisions (W, H, FPS, the rotation, the tonemap, the duration) hold, because they are the
    picture's and the produced file carries the same picture. `light()` uses it exactly when its input is `j.outPath`;
    the two-output pass (erratum 217) reads the upload and is untouched. **Pins.** `TestForProducedFileAddressesTheProducedLayout`
    (video 1 / audio 0 → `[0:0]` on the video pad, `[0:1]aresample`; the upload's own plan untouched) and
    `TestForProducedFileReadsAMergeAsOneTrack`; T1's bundles 7, 41, 62, 103 on the lane stack. **Not done:** an
    audio-first fixture in the test-clip matrix (an E2E bundle would have caught this; a cleanup row).

352. **A source turned by its Display Matrix comes out turned, and matrix-free, on the CUDA graph** (lane `cudarotate`,
    2026-10-29; `internal/transcode/encode.go` `Plan.cudaBranch`/`cudaRotationInputArgs`, `hwaccel.go`
    `cudaScaleTo`/`hwWhyMirror`, `plan.go` `Plan.MatrixTurn`/`MatrixMirrored`/`ForProducedFile(remux)`, `probe.go`
    `matrixMirroredOf`, `internal/worker/pipeline.go` `light()`; `scripts/testclips.sh` `rotated90-audiofirst`, E2E
    step **112** (`112-rotated.sh`; the suite 108 steps / 49 bundles); DEPLOY §27's GPU flavour paragraph; no new variable, no
    doctor check, no migration). Found after erratum 351's fix on a Windows GPU box: the same phone recording (coded 626×1234,
    a Display Matrix of rotation 90, displayed 1234×626) came out of the LIGHT copy on the GPU path as 1234×626 frames
    holding the UNTURNED picture squeezed sideways, AND still carrying the rotation-90 matrix — so every player turned
    it again: a portrait, distorted card. The remuxed Original (626×1234 + matrix) was right.
    **The cause, proven.** ffmpeg's autorotate inserts its `transpose` at the graph's input only for SOFTWARE frames;
    on device frames (`-hwaccel_output_format cuda`) it inserts nothing, the frames reach `scale_cuda` unturned (626×1234
    squeezed into the plan's display-oriented 1234×626), and because nothing applied the matrix ffmpeg copies it to the
    output. Reproduced on the Mac with the same mechanism on VideoToolbox frames (`scale_vt` → 616×312 + matrix 90).
    The CPU graph was always right: autorotate turns, and its output carries no matrix. The Full of a turned source on
    CUDA (the two-output pass of erratum 217) had the same defect.
    **The fix.** The plan carries `MatrixTurn` — the clockwise quarter turn autorotate gives a matrix-rotated source,
    `(360 − Rotation) mod 360` in the probe's ffprobe convention (rotation 90 → 270 → `transpose=2`; −90 → 90 →
    `transpose=1`; 180 → `hflip,vflip`) — and `PreRotate` keeps its legacy-tag meaning. The CPU graph never reads it
    (its argv is byte-identical for every source, pinned, and so is the NVENC-only fallback of erratum 265, which
    decodes on the CPU). On the CUDA graph a turned plan renders, single and per branch of the two-output pass:
    `-display_rotation:v 0` before `-i`; `scale_cuda=<coded W>:<coded H>` (the plan's W×H swapped for a quarter turn);
    `,hwdownload,format=yuv420p,<turn>`; then the tag's `drawtext`, so it sits in the corner the viewer sees. Measured
    on 7.1.1 and 8.0.1: `-display_rotation:v 0` replaces the matrix with the identity, so ffmpeg neither autorotates
    nor writes a matrix to the output; `-noautorotate` stops the first and NOT the second (the output kept rotation 90).
    A matrix that also MIRRORS the picture (a negative determinant; autorotate then uses `cclock_flip`/`clock_flip` or
    a lone flip) is refused the card (`hwWhyMirror`) and takes the CPU graph. `ForProducedFile` now says which produced
    file it reads: the remux carries the upload's matrix, so the turn rides with it; an encoded Full is already turned,
    tone mapped, deinterlaced and square and carries no matrix, so every head flag is OFF for it (unreachable today —
    `light()` reads a produced file only after the remux — but a Light from a Full must never turn twice).
    **The direction, pinned.** `TestMatrixTurnMatchesAutorotate` (ffmpeg tag) makes three matrix-rotated sources with
    `-display_rotation` on a stream copy (audio-first at 90, −90, 180 — `-metadata:s:v:0 rotate=90` on an mp4 writes
    NO matrix in 7.1.1, so it cannot make this fixture), encodes each on the software path, and runs the CUDA argv this
    package renders with only the card's pieces swapped for their CPU twins (`scale_cuda…hwdownload` → `scale`, no
    `-hwaccel`, libx264 for NVENC): both outputs are W×H with no Display Matrix, SSIM(explicit, software) ≥ 0.9
    (measured 0.994–0.995) and SSIM against the software output turned by a half ≤ 0.7 (0.512) — the other quarter
    turn would land there. Unit pins: `TestCUDAMatrixTurnGraph` (the owner's clip's exact graph), `TestCUDADualMatrixTurn`,
    `TestCUDAUnturnedGraphUnchanged`, `TestCPUArgvIgnoresMatrixTurn`, `TestHWAccelForMirroredMatrix`,
    `TestForProducedFileRotation`, `TestMakePlanMatrixTurn`, `TestMatrixMirroredOf`. **E2E step 112** uploads the new
    phone-shaped fixture (coded 720×1280 at 60 fps, matrix 90, audio stream 0 — the cleanup list's audio-first row, closed) twice:
    as is (remuxed, the Light from the remux: 1280×720) and as a small HEVC of the same shape (coded 360×640, 2 s: one
    pass writes the Full and the Light, both 640×360), and requires every fetched file to be landscape with no matrix. **Only the GPU gate proves the card:** `scale_cuda` and NVDEC frames
    exist only on the PC, where step 112 runs on `TRANSCODE_HWACCEL=cuda`; on the Mac it proves the software path.

353. **The public tree** (run 25, lane `pub-design`, 2026-11-06; the repository is public from the day of the
    flip, on the owner's word; no migration, no route, no setting). Until this erratum the product and the records
    of building it shared one private repository, and the records were written for the people building it: a
    hand-off, a state ledger, a cleanup list, a credentials file, the run records and the build brief under `docs/`,
    the workflow scripts, the per-session journals they point at, and this document's §17–§19 (the Phase 4 fit,
    the build plan and the risk list, written before the first commit). Publishing that history would publish
    names, machine paths, account identifiers and a business's numbers, and so **the public tree is a fresh root
    cut from the product paths**, not a flip of the existing repository's visibility.
    **(a) What the public tree is.** `cmd/`, `internal/`, `web/`, `migrations/`, `scripts/` (the harness, without
    the workflow scripts), the compose files, the Dockerfile, `DESIGN.md` (this document, with §20 whole), `DEPLOY.md`,
    `API.md`, `web/STYLE.md`, `ROADMAP.md` as a public index (one row per number), the brand assets a self-hoster
    needs (`docs/brand/mark.svg` and its generator; not the Discord and app-icon tiles), and the files a stranger
    expects at the root: `README.md`, `LICENSE`, `SECURITY.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md`,
    `THIRD_PARTY.md`, `CHANGELOG.md` and a short `CLAUDE.md` for contributors. Everything else — the ledgers, the
    run records, the build brief, the credentials file, the audit, the workflow scripts, the full roadmap with its
    discussion, the moved §17–§19 — lives in a **private records repository** beside it, and nothing in the public
    tree points into it by path. The history is the records repository's; the public tree's history begins at the
    cut.
    **(b) What was scrubbed, and what was kept.** Every person's and every model's name, every machine path, every
    session or temporary-folder identifier and every pointer into the records are gone from the public documents and
    from every comment under `cmd/`, `internal/`, `web/` and `scripts/`: a person's decision reads *the owner's*,
    a review's wording reads *review*, and a sentence somebody said is replaced by the decision it carried, in plain
    words, on the same date. Real account names, the real Pass host and the real Discord application ids in
    fixtures became neutral fictions with every assertion and count unchanged. **Kept, everywhere:** dates, lane
    names, migration numbers, DEPLOY section numbers, the product hostnames (`clippet.gg`, `bot.clippet.gg`,
    `get.clippet.gg`, and `dev.clippet.gg` as the dev instance), and every erratum and roadmap number — a number is
    never reused or renumbered, and the numbering note below stands as written. Scrubbing a comment never changes
    the behaviour the comment describes.
    **(c) The citation key.** A comment, a script, DEPLOY.md, API.md or STYLE.md cites a decision as **`§20 erratum
    N`** (a numbered entry of this section, a clause as `283 (h)`) or **`ROADMAP #N`** (a `### N.` heading of
    `ROADMAP.md`), and never by a person's name. `scripts/check.sh` stage **19** proves every cited number resolves:
    a single number must be an entry, a range `A–B` is a bundle's allocation and resolves when `A` is an entry and
    `B` is no higher than the newest (an allocated number a bundle did not need stays unused, as the numbering note
    says). Its self-test plants a dead erratum and a dead roadmap citation beside live ones and requires exactly
    the dead ones named.
    **(d) The two tripwires.** `scripts/check.sh` stage **`pii`** scans the tree for the *shapes* of what must not
    be there — a Windows or macOS home path, a personal mail domain, a private package name, an account or zone
    identifier beside the words that name one — and, when a private deny file is present (`PII_DENY_FILE`, read in
    CI from a repository secret written to a temporary file), for the *values*; it prints `path:line pattern #k` and
    never the matched text. **gitleaks** runs over the tree with the repository's `.gitleaks.toml`, which allows the
    fixtures and placeholders the tests carry by exact path and nothing else. Both run in T0 and in CI.
    **(e) The licence.** `LICENSE` is **FSL-1.1-Apache-2.0** — source-available: every self-host, fork and
    modification is permitted; offering the software as a competing hosted service is not; each release converts
    to **Apache-2.0** two years after it is published. There is no contributor licence agreement; a contribution
    carries a Developer Certificate of Origin sign-off (`Signed-off-by`), described in `CONTRIBUTING.md` and
    checked in CI. The product name and the mark are not covered by the licence (`docs/brand/README.md`).
    **(f) The seam a stranger hits first.** `compose.pass.yaml` pulls the Pass sidecar image from a public registry
    path; until this erratum that package was private and published by hand (ROADMAP #58), so a reader following
    DEPLOY §36 got a pull refusal. The release cycle now publishes the image at every release that moved it, as
    `:<version>` and `:1`, so the compose file a self-hoster is handed works without an account anywhere.

> **Numbering note (2026-09-07 roadmap run).** Errata 99–164 were allocated in ranges to nine parallel builder bundles (A nits 99–104, B account 105–112, C library 113–120, D media 121–126, E watch page 127–134, F upload 135–142, G operator CLI 143–150, H owner extras 151–160, I docs 161–164). A number a bundle did not need stays unused; numbers are never re-assigned. A pass that must record something after its range is spent AMENDS the erratum that owns the subject rather than borrowing another bundle's number (errata 101 and 104(c) were amended this way by bundle A's fix pass); for any future parallel run, allocate each bundle 2–3 spare numbers up front for exactly this case, as a protocol line in the run brief rather than in this document.
